opportunities.title: CVPR 2027 Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full papers for CVPR 2027 are due 16 November 2026 (11:59 pm AoE) with supplementary material by 23 November; no travel funding is stated on the call.
opportunities.description:
CVPR 2027, the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, is calling for papers. CVPR is the largest and most selective annual meeting in computer vision, and its proceedings are published openly by the Computer Vision Foundation.

Paper enrolment closed on 10 November 2026 and full papers were due by 16 November 2026 at 11:59 pm AoE, with supplementary material due a week later. Reviews come out on 25 January 2027, authors can respond during a rebuttal week, and final decisions are released on 25 February 2027.

For African researchers in computer vision, machine learning and robotics, CVPR is the venue with the widest reach, and submitting authors also take part in reviewing, which is a valuable way to join the community.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in the CVPR 2027 proceedings on the CVF open-access site and the chance to present at the conference.
requirements: Paper must have been enrolled by 10 November 2026
All co-authors need up-to-date OpenReview profiles (new profiles without an institutional email can take up to two weeks to approve)
Authors must serve as reviewers when asked
Dual-submission rules apply from 16 November 2026 to 22 February 2027
documents: Paper PDF following the CVPR author guidelines
opportunities.selection_process: Double-blind peer review followed by an author rebuttal period, then final decisions by the area chairs and programme chairs.
opportunities.about_provider: CVPR is co-sponsored by the IEEE Computer Society and the Computer Vision Foundation (CVF), a non-profit that organises major computer vision conferences and makes their papers freely available.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit through the CVPR 2027 conference group on OpenReview by the deadline, which is fixed and will not be extended.
opportunities.notes: Rules on the use of large language models in writing and reviewing were still being finalised when the call was published.

opportunities.title: Cancer Genomic Epidemiology (course bursary, Mar 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bursaries are available for researchers and clinicians attending this course at the Wellcome Genome Campus, 15-18 March 2027.
opportunities.description:
Wellcome Connecting Science is running a four-day residential course on cancer genomic epidemiology, subtitled Understanding Mutational Signatures of Cancer to Inform Prevention, at the Wellcome Genome Campus in Hinxton, near Cambridge, UK, from 15 to 18 March 2027. It is organised with the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) of the WHO and the Wellcome Sanger Institute.

The course is for early and mid-career scientists in genomics, epidemiology, clinical or public health who want to learn how mutational signatures in tumour genomes can reveal causes of cancer and guide prevention. Places are limited and awarded on merit, with preference for applicants working on related projects.

The course fee covers accommodation and meals, and merit-based bursaries can halve the fee, which helps African researchers in cancer epidemiology attend. The organisers can also provide letters for UK visa applications.
opportunities.benefits: Course fee £810, including accommodation and all meals. Limited merit-based bursaries reduce the fee by up to 50%.
requirements: Early or mid-career scientist in genomics, epidemiology, clinical or public health
Supporting statement from a scientific or clinical sponsor
Preference for applicants working on related projects
documents: Online application form (including the bursary request, if needed)
Sponsor's supporting statement as a PDF from a supervisor, line manager or head of department
Bursary justification from the applicant and sponsor
opportunities.selection_process: Places and bursaries are awarded on merit by a committee, usually within a month of the deadline. The committee's decision is final.
important_dates: Application and bursary deadline: the page gives both 16 November and 23 November 2026, so apply by 16 November to be safe
opportunities.about_provider: Wellcome Connecting Science is the training and events arm of the Wellcome Sanger Institute, funded by Wellcome. It runs courses and conferences in genomics and biomedical science on the Wellcome Genome Campus and worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the event's applicant portal on eventsair and upload your sponsor's statement; applications without it are not considered. Tick the bursary option in the same form if you need fee support. The fee is requested only after acceptance.
opportunities.notes: Contact events@sanger.ac.uk or courses@wellcomeconnectingscience.org with questions. Many nationalities need no UK visa for short courses; the organisers can send a visa support letter.

opportunities.title: DAAD ERP Study Scholarships for Graduates of Economics and Business Administration 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Economics and business graduates (degree within six years) from eligible developing countries can apply by 16 November 2026 for a fully funded DAAD master's scholarship in Germany starting October 2027.
opportunities.description:
DAAD's ERP Study Scholarships fund graduates in economics and business administration from developing and transition countries to complete a master's degree at a state or state-recognised university in Germany. The programme is financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy.

The scholarship lasts 18 to 24 months (three or four semesters) and starts in October 2027, possibly preceded by a two-month German course. Applicants must apply to three host universities at the same time as applying to DAAD, and selection committees in the home countries choose the scholars in February and March 2027.

The application window closes at midnight (CET) on 16 November 2026, so this is a last-minute opportunity for African economics and business graduates who already have their documents ready.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 992 per month, a study allowance of EUR 460 a year, health, accident and personal liability insurance, a travel allowance on request, and possibly a two-month German course before the master's. Family allowances are not paid.
requirements: Bachelor's (or equivalent) in economics or business administration by the start of the scholarship
Final degree exams no more than six years before applying
Not living in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline
Proof of the language of instruction (German or English, e.g. IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, Cambridge) no older than three years
Must apply to three German host universities at the same time
documents: Admission letter from a host university, or proof it will follow
Form 'Information about your preferred master programmes'
One recent recommendation letter from a university teacher
All university transcripts with grading explanation
opportunities.selection_process: Selection committees in the applicants' home countries choose the scholars in February to March 2027. Incomplete applications are not considered.
important_dates: Application period: 1 June to 16 November 2026 (portal closes 24:00 CET)
opportunities.about_provider: The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) is Germany's national organisation for international academic exchange and one of the world's largest scholarship funders. This programme is sponsored by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE).
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the DAAD portal, complete the online application for the ERP Study Scholarships and upload all documents under 'Attachments' before midnight CET on 16 November 2026. Certified copies are only needed if you are awarded.
opportunities.notes: The portal is only visible while the application period runs. Apply to your three preferred master's programmes in parallel.

opportunities.title: HKBU Admission Scholarship Scheme for Overseas Applicants 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-local undergraduate applicants to HKBU for 2027/28, including holders of African school qualifications, are considered automatically for awards of up to full tuition plus HKD 52,500 a year.
opportunities.description:
Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU) considers every non-local undergraduate applicant with international qualifications for its Admission Scholarship Scheme for Overseas Applicants. There is no separate form: the award is decided when the admission offer is made, for students entering in 2027/28.

The scheme has three tiers. A Full Scholarship covers all tuition (HKD 240,000 a year) plus HKD 52,500 in living subsidies; a Tuition-waiver Scholarship covers full tuition; and a Half Scholarship pays half of the Full award. Awards can be renewed for the normal length of study if results stay good.

African qualifications such as WASSCE, the Cameroon GCE A-Level or Baccalauréat, Egypt's Thanaweya Amma and the Ethiopian University Entrance Certificate are accepted for entry, so strong African school leavers can be considered.
opportunities.benefits: Full Scholarship: 100% tuition (HKD 240,000 a year) plus HKD 52,500 living subsidies. Tuition-waiver Scholarship: 100% tuition. Half Scholarship: 50% of the Full Scholarship. Renewable for the normal study period subject to good results.
requirements: Non-local applicant entering an HKBU undergraduate programme in 2027/28
Strong school results (reference scores include A-Level AAA for a full award and AAB for a half award, IB 37/35, SAT 1430/1360)
Meet HKBU's general entry and English language requirements
Accepted African qualifications include WASSCE, Cameroon GCE A-Level/Baccalauréat, Egypt Thanaweya Amma (70% average) and the Ethiopian University Entrance Certificate
opportunities.selection_process: Holistic: academic results, interview performance and non-academic achievements are all considered. Awards are competitive, subject to quota and reviewed every year.
important_dates: Admission offers released from late December 2026
Applicants without an offer by late January 2027 move to the Main Round
opportunities.about_provider: HKBU is a public university in Hong Kong with six faculties and schools offering 23 undergraduate programmes taught in English. It handles admissions directly and has not authorised any agents.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online to HKBU for undergraduate admission (non-JUPAS route). All non-local applicants are considered automatically for the scholarship, so no extra application is needed.
opportunities.notes: Reference scores are past figures, not guarantees. HKBU also offers faculty-level admission scholarships and a few bursaries for non-local students.

opportunities.title: Marlène and Paolo Fresco Fellowship for African Studies (Jan-Jun 2028)
opportunities.provider: Villa I Tatti, Harvard University Center for Italian Renaissance Studies
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Six-month residential fellowship in Florence for PhD holders researching African-Mediterranean exchange (c. 1250-1750), with USD 5,200 a month plus relocation support and housing where possible.
opportunities.description:
Villa I Tatti, the Harvard University Center for Italian Renaissance Studies in Florence, offers the Marlène and Paolo Fresco Fellowship for African Studies, a six-month residential postdoctoral fellowship for the spring term of January to June 2028. It supports research on exchanges between Africa and the Mediterranean world between about 1250 and 1750, with a preference for projects on early modern links between Africa and Italy.

Fellows live in the Florence area, spend at least three days a week at I Tatti and work on their own research alongside a community of scholars, with access to the centre's library and collections. They cannot teach or hold other fellowships during the term.

This is an unusual opportunity for African historians with a PhD whose work touches on Africa's historical ties with Italy and the Mediterranean.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of US$5,200 per month, a one-time relocation supplement of up to US$1,800, and a rent-free apartment (utilities charged) or a housing subsidy.
requirements: PhD already awarded (not pursuing a second PhD)
Fluent in English, Italian or French
Solid background in African history
Research on Africa-Mediterranean exchange c. 1250-1750, ideally Africa-Italy
No other fellowship, award or teaching during the term
Must live in the Florence area and be at I Tatti at least three days a week
Not previously appointed at I Tatti (former Graduate Fellows excepted)
documents: Online application in English or Italian
Two recommendation letters in English, French or Italian, uploaded by referees
important_dates: Application deadline: 16 November 2026 (midnight, Cambridge MA time)
opportunities.about_provider: Villa I Tatti is Harvard University's research centre for Italian Renaissance studies, located in the hills outside Florence. It hosts postdoctoral fellows each year and holds a major library and art collection.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through I Tatti's SlideRoom portal and ask your two referees to upload their letters online by 21 November 2026. Only one type of I Tatti fellowship can be applied for in an academic year.
opportunities.notes: The fellowship cannot be deferred and can be held only once.

opportunities.title: Princeton PIIRS Fung Global Fellows Program 2027/2028
opportunities.provider: Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies (PIIRS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career scholars with a PhD awarded after 1 September 2017 who hold a faculty or research post outside the USA can apply for a year in residence at Princeton on the theme Democracy in Crisis?
opportunities.description:
The Fung Global Fellows Program at the Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies (PIIRS) brings a small group of early-career scholars from outside the United States to Princeton University for a ten-month residential fellowship. The 2027-2028 cohort will work under the theme Democracy in Crisis?, with fellows appointed as Visiting Research Scholars.

Fellows spend the academic year on campus pursuing their own research, taking part in a shared seminar and contributing to the intellectual life of PIIRS. They must hold a faculty or research post outside the US and return to it afterwards.

African social scientists and humanists who earned their PhD after September 2017 and whose research engages with democracy, governance or political change are well placed to apply.
opportunities.benefits: A ten-month residential appointment at Princeton as a Visiting Research Scholar. The page does not list the stipend amount.
requirements: PhD or equivalent, generally received after 1 September 2017
Faculty or professional research appointment outside the US, with a plan to return
Current PhD students and postdocs are not eligible
Research related to the theme Democracy in Crisis?
Able to obtain a suitable US visa (H-1B processing is not available)
documents: Cover letter of up to 1.5 pages
Research proposal of up to 3 single-spaced pages
One writing sample of up to 50 pages
Three referees, who are invited by email to upload letters
opportunities.selection_process: Selection is based on the strength of the project, its fit with the theme, the applicant's scholarly record, their likely contribution to the programme, and work experience outside the US. Finalists have a virtual interview.
important_dates: Finalist interviews: mid-December 2026 to early January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: PIIRS is Princeton University's institute for international and regional studies. It supports research and teaching on global issues and runs the Fung Global Fellows Program for international early-career scholars.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit all materials in English through the programme's Interfolio page (apply.interfolio.com/191685) before the portal locks at the deadline. Supplementary materials are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: Late applications are not accepted. Interfolio's helpdesk handles technical problems.

opportunities.title: TWAS-SISSA-Lincei Research Cooperation Visits Programme
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Funded research visits to SISSA in Trieste for researchers aged 40 or under who are nationals of a least developed country, hold an MSc or higher and hold a research position in an LDC.
opportunities.description:
The TWAS-SISSA-Lincei Research Cooperation Visits Programme funds three-month research visits to centres of excellence in Trieste and Udine, Italy, for scientists from the world's least developed countries. It is run by UNESCO-TWAS together with the Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei and SISSA, and paid for by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation.

Visitors work with a host laboratory on a joint project linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Host institutions include SISSA, ICGEB, INFN, OGS, the Universities of Trieste and Udine, IOM-CNR, Area Science Park and Elettra. The deadline, originally 31 October 2026, was extended to 16 November 2026.

Many African countries are on the least developed countries list, so researchers under 40 in those countries who hold a research post at home are the main target group.
opportunities.benefits: Travel costs and living expenses for a three-month research visit in Trieste or Udine, Italy (amounts not stated).
requirements: National of a least developed country
MSc or higher
Holds a research position in a least developed country
Aged 40 or under on 31 December of the application year
Not already in the host country; part-time visits not eligible
Must show the intention to return home after the visit
Only one TWAS/OWSD programme per calendar year
documents: Statement of scientific interests and SDG-related plans for the home country
Invitation letter from an eligible host lab confirming a 3-month visit
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee assesses applications on scientific merit. Applications must be in English, and only the fields listed on the form are considered.
opportunities.about_provider: UNESCO-TWAS, The World Academy of Sciences, promotes scientific capacity in developing countries through fellowships, grants and exchanges. SISSA is an international school for advanced studies in Trieste and the Accademia dei Lincei is Italy's national academy of sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact a potential host supervisor in Trieste or Udine early and obtain an invitation letter, then apply through the TWAS online form (onlineforms.twas.org/apply/310). Questions go to exchanges@twas.org.
opportunities.notes: Women scientists are encouraged to apply. Unsigned recommendation letters are not accepted.

opportunities.title: The Web Conference 2027 Short Papers Call (Dublin, May 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Short papers for the ACM Web Conference in Dublin (12-14 May 2027) are due 16 November 2026 with abstracts by 9 November; no travel funding is stated on the call.
opportunities.description:
The ACM Web Conference 2027, the long-running conference formerly known as WWW, is accepting short papers for its research track. The conference takes place at the Dublin Royal Convention Centre in Ireland, with workshops, tutorials and Web4All on 10 and 11 May 2027 and the main conference from 12 to 14 May 2027.

Short papers are limited to four pages including references and appendices, written in English in the ACM double-column template and reviewed double-blind. Each author can submit up to seven papers per submission type, and work already under review or published at another peer-reviewed venue is not allowed, although preprints are fine.

The conference is one of the top venues for research on the web, search, social media, data mining and online systems, and African researchers in these areas can use the short-paper track to present focused results to a global audience.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of accepted short papers in the conference proceedings and the chance to present at the Web Conference 2027 in Dublin.
requirements: Maximum 4 pages including references and appendix
ACM double-column template, single PDF, in English
Anonymous submission for double-blind review
Abstract must have been registered by 9 November 2026; no author changes after that
No concurrent submission to another peer-reviewed venue
Maximum 7 submissions per author per type
documents: Up-to-date OpenReview profile for every author
opportunities.selection_process: Papers are peer reviewed double-blind by the programme committee. Deadlines are strict and no extensions are given.
opportunities.about_provider: The ACM Web Conference is an annual international conference on the future of the World Wide Web, run under the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM), the world's largest computing society.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit through the Web Conference 2027 group on OpenReview before the deadline. Make sure all co-authors have current OpenReview profiles, and do not use placeholder abstracts.
opportunities.notes: Preprints are allowed and need not be cited. The full-paper deadline is end of day Anywhere on Earth.

opportunities.title: USask SIOS Financial Need Scholarship for International Students (Winter 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Continuing USask international or refugee students in second year or above, in good standing, who face unexpected financial hardship.
opportunities.description:
The University of Saskatchewan runs a financial need scholarship for its international and refugee students, funded through the Saskatchewan Innovation and Opportunity Scholarship (SIOS). It is meant for students who are already studying at USask, are in good academic standing, and face an unexpected money problem that threatens their ability to continue or finish their degree.

This round covers the 2027 Winter term within the 2026-27 academic year, and awards are made until the available funds run out. It is not an entrance award: students in their first year cannot apply, while those in second year or above, at undergraduate or graduate level, can. For African students already enrolled at USask, it is a practical safety net when family support or sponsorship falls through mid-degree.
opportunities.benefits: A need-based award whose amount is not published; it is paid straight into the student's university account and may be held back until the student proves they will register for the next term.
requirements: Current international or refugee student at the University of Saskatchewan
Second year of study or higher (first-year students are not eligible)
Undergraduate or graduate student
Good academic standing
Facing unforeseen financial barriers to continuing or completing studies
Past recipients may reapply, but first-time applicants are prioritised
documents: Completed Financial Need Calculator and application in PAWS
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reviews the financial need shown in the PAWS calculator and gives priority to students who have never received this scholarship before. Awards continue until funds are exhausted.
important_dates: Decisions emailed through PAWS: by 11 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Saskatchewan (USask) is a public research university in Saskatoon, Canada. Its Student Finance and Awards office manages scholarships and bursaries for domestic and international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Log in to PAWS and open the Scholarships and Bursaries channel (paws2.usask.ca/awards), start a new application for award year 2026-2027, choose the Fall and Winter terms and select the SIOS International Student Scholarship. Complete every section of the financial need calculator and submit before the deadline; if the calculator still shows 2025-2026, complete it anyway.
opportunities.notes: Questions go to USask Student Finance and Awards through its online help portal. The listing's list of eligible African countries does not appear on the official page: all current international students are eligible.

opportunities.title: University of Sydney Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships Scheme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: AUD 5,000 to 60,000 tuition awards for international applicants with an unconditional offer for a bachelor's or coursework master's; Semester 1 2027 Round 3 closes 16 Nov 2026 and Semester 2 rounds close 15 Feb, 22 Mar and 3 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
The University of Sydney Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships Scheme rewards high-achieving international students starting a bachelor's or coursework master's degree. Awards range from A$5,000 to A$60,000 and are given once, in the first year of study, without a separate application.

Students are considered automatically if they hold an unconditional offer by the close of a selection round. For Semester 1 2027 the final round closes on 16 November 2026, with extra consideration for IB and International UAC students after their December results. For Semester 2 2027 there are rounds closing on 15 February, 22 March and 3 May 2027.

African students applying to Sydney do not need to do anything extra beyond securing an unconditional offer early, which makes this a useful award to aim for when planning a 2027 start in Australia.
opportunities.benefits: One-off awards of A$60,000 or A$40,000 (paid over one year in two instalments), or A$20,000, A$10,000 or A$5,000 (one semester). Recipients of a Sydney International Student Award can receive at most A$40,000.
requirements: International student as defined by Australian law
Applied for, but not yet started, a bachelor's or coursework master's degree at Sydney
Unconditional offer by the round deadline
Not receiving an Australian Government scholarship
Not a previous recipient of this scholarship
documents: No separate application; the admission application is used
opportunities.selection_process: Recipients are selected on academic merit from their admission application and nominated by a selection committee.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Sydney is Australia's first university, founded in 1850, and a member of the Group of Eight research-intensive universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to an eligible Sydney degree and meet all conditions so that you hold an unconditional offer before the relevant round closes. You will be considered automatically and contacted if selected.
opportunities.notes: To keep split payments, recipients must have a semester average of at least 65 and no outstanding fees. Accepting another Sydney scholarship worth over A$20,000 a year ends this award.

opportunities.title: EMBO | EMBL Symposium: Mechanisms of Drug Resistance and Tolerance in Bacteria, Fungi and Cancer 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers at any career stage can submit an abstract by the deadline to attend this hybrid meeting at EMBL Heidelberg (9-12 March 2027). Financial assistance (registration fee waiver, travel grant up to EUR 1000 from outside Europe, childcare grant) is requested with the abstract.
opportunities.description:
EMBO and EMBL are holding the second edition of their symposium on the mechanisms of drug resistance and tolerance in bacteria, fungi and cancer at the EMBL Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg, Germany, from 9 to 12 March 2027, with an option to join online. The keynote speaker is Eduard Batlle, and the meeting brings together researchers from around the world.

The programme covers how microbes and tumour cells survive drugs, with talks, poster sessions and an online platform. Only on-site participants can submit abstracts, and abstract selection is also how financial support is allocated.

EMBO and EMBL offer limited fee waivers, travel grants of up to €1,000 for people travelling from outside Europe, and childcare grants, so African researchers in microbiology, infectious disease or cancer biology can apply for support by submitting an abstract.
opportunities.benefits: Registration fees: on-site €750 (academia), €650 (PhD students), €950 (industry); virtual €240, €190 and €290. Financial help: limited registration fee waivers, travel grants covering transport, accommodation and visa costs up to €400 from within Europe or €1,000 from outside Europe, and childcare grants (priority to early-stage researchers).
requirements: Researchers working on drug resistance or tolerance in bacteria, fungi or cancer
Abstract submission is for on-site participants only
Financial help requires explaining why the lab cannot fund attendance
documents: Short statements on funding need and career impact for financial assistance
opportunities.selection_process: Abstracts and grants are chosen together on scientific merit, place of work or study, financial need and career impact. Results come about three weeks after the abstract deadline.
opportunities.about_provider: EMBL (European Molecular Biology Laboratory) is Europe's intergovernmental life-sciences research institute, with its main site in Heidelberg. EMBO is an organisation of leading life scientists that funds fellowships, courses and meetings.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the EMBL events portal and submit an abstract by the deadline. On-site applicants receive an emailed link to apply for financial help after registering. The fee is paid up front even when a waiver is later granted, and travel costs are reimbursed after the meeting against receipts sent within two months.
opportunities.notes: Contact events@embl.de with questions. Hotel rooms are held until 9 February 2027 with booking code EES27-05.

opportunities.title: Hoover Fellows Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Salaried one- to three-year early-career position at Stanford's Hoover Institution for scholars with a PhD in a policy-relevant field completed by 1 September 2027, open to any nationality.
opportunities.description:
The Hoover Fellows Program at the Hoover Institution, Stanford University, recruits early-career scholars to spend between one and three years doing policy-relevant research and publishing. The 2027 position is a research post with no teaching load, based on the Stanford campus in California.

Fellows are expected to produce scholarly work on public policy in fields such as economics, history, international relations, national security, political science and public policy. The salary is high for a postdoctoral-level role and comes with a yearly housing allowance.

The page sets no nationality restriction, so African PhD holders or candidates finishing by September 2027 whose work speaks to policy questions can apply.
opportunities.benefits: A 12-month base salary of US$169,950 to US$230,000, plus a US$20,000 annual housing allowance.
requirements: PhD or equivalent in a relevant field (economics, history, international relations, national security, political science, public policy, etc.)
Degree completed by 1 September 2027
Research agenda relevant to public policy
documents: Cover letter or statement of interest describing academic background and experience
One or more recent publications, working papers or draft book chapters
Research plan of no more than two pages
opportunities.about_provider: The Hoover Institution is a public policy research centre at Stanford University that hosts fellows working on economics, governance, security and history, and runs a large archive and library.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application online through Hoover's SurveyMonkey Apply portal (hoover.smapply.us) and arrange three recommendation letters. Questions go to hooverfellowship@stanford.edu, which is checked only periodically.
opportunities.notes: The page body describes appointments of one to three years.

opportunities.title: ITU Internship Programme WSIS Forum 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students or recent graduates under 30 from any ITU Member State (including all African countries) can apply for this unpaid six-month WSIS Prizes internship in Geneva by 17 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
The International Telecommunication Union is recruiting an intern to work as a Junior Project Officer on the WSIS Prizes, the awards contest that runs alongside the World Summit on the Information Society (WSIS) Forum 2027. The intern supports the organisation of the prizes and the Forum itself from ITU headquarters in Geneva.

This is a full-time, on-site placement of about six months, running from 18 January to 16 July 2027 (vacancy notice no. 2446). It suits students or recent graduates in fields such as communications, international relations, development studies or digital media who want first-hand experience of how a UN agency runs a major global event.

Citizens of any ITU Member State may apply, which includes every African country, so this is an open door for African students who can fund a half-year stay in Geneva. Note that the internship is unpaid.
opportunities.benefits: This internship is unpaid. The intern (or a sponsoring institution) must cover medical insurance, travel to Geneva, accommodation and living costs. The benefit is six months of practical work experience at UN agency headquarters.
requirements: Citizen of an ITU Member State
Under 30 years of age (exceptions possible for PhD candidates)
Currently enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate or postgraduate programme, or graduated no more than six months before the start date

Studying in development studies, international relations, business administration, communications, public relations, economics, digital media, international development, political science, sociology or a related field
Excellent English; a second ITU official language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) is an advantage
No prior work experience required
Available full-time in Geneva from 18 January to 16 July 2027
documents: Online application through the ITU careers portal
Proof of university enrolment or a copy of the graduation certificate
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are screened against the criteria in the vacancy notice. Shortlisted candidates may be asked to complete tests or assessments and a competency-based interview by video or teleconference, and reference checks are made for final candidates. ITU does not charge any fee at any stage.
opportunities.about_provider: ITU is the United Nations specialised agency for information and communication technologies. It allocates global radio spectrum and satellite orbits and develops the technical standards that let networks and technologies connect worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Open the vacancy notice on the ITU careers site and use the Apply now button to create a profile and submit your application with your CV and enrolment or graduation proof. Submit before midnight Geneva time on 17 November 2026.
opportunities.notes: Unpaid: plan your funding for Geneva before applying. Be wary of anyone asking for money: ITU states it never charges recruitment fees.

opportunities.title: McKinnon-Walker Research Fellowship (PhD)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Domestic and international PhD applicants with a confirmed UOW supervisor whose research can benefit Pacific Islander, Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander peoples can apply by 17 November 2026 for a fellowship worth over AUD 200,000.
opportunities.description:
The McKinnon-Walker Research Fellowship is a PhD scholarship at the University of Wollongong (UOW) in New South Wales, Australia, for outstanding candidates whose research could benefit Pacific Islander, Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander peoples. Two fellowships will be awarded for students starting in 2027.

The fellowship was created in 2024 with a AUD 5 million gift from Suzanne Walker and the late Emeritus Professor Ken McKinnon AO, a former UOW Vice-Chancellor. It is worth over AUD 200,000 in total, combining a generous stipend for 3.5 years, a tuition waiver for up to four years, project money and professional development.

International students may apply, though applicants from Pacific Islander, Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander communities are especially encouraged. African researchers whose work fits these communities and who have a confirmed UOW supervisor can be considered.
opportunities.benefits: Total value over AUD 200,000: a stipend of AUD 55,537 per year for 3.5 years, a tuition fee waiver for up to 4 years, AUD 20,000 in project funding, and professional development such as workshops and mentoring.
requirements: Applying for (or in the first year of) a UOW PhD starting in 2027; domestic and international applicants eligible
A confirmed UOW supervisor
Honours Class II Division 1 or higher with research thesis, a research master's, or a coursework master's with substantial thesis (average 75+ or GPA 3.2/4)
IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with 6.5 in each band (or equivalent)
Research that can benefit Pacific Islander, Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander peoples
documents: HDR admission application with a 3-4 page research proposal
One-page statement on leadership, service and community contributions
One-page statement on which communities the research will benefit and how
Email from your supervisor supporting the application (all fellowship documents combined in one PDF)
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates are assessed on academic excellence, research quality, the relevance of the research to Pacific Islander, Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander peoples, leadership and service. Two fellowships are awarded.
important_dates: Deadline for HDR admission and fellowship application: 17 November 2026
2027 PhD start: Autumn session from 1 March 2027 or Spring session from 26 July 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Wollongong is a public research university in New South Wales, Australia. The fellowship spans its faculties of Engineering and Information Sciences, Science, Medicine and Health, and Arts, Society and Business.
opportunities.how_to_apply: New applicants must apply for PhD admission through the UOW HDR portal by 17 November 2026, then email the single fellowship PDF to graduate-research-school@uow.edu.au by the same date. Current first-year UOW PhD candidates only need to send the PDF.
opportunities.notes: UOW only accepts PhD applications with a confirmed supervisor, so secure one before the deadline.

opportunities.title: DPH 2027 Digital Public Health Conference Call for Papers (London)
opportunities.provider: UCL Centre for Digital Public Health in Emergencies
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide working on digital public health can submit papers or abstracts.
opportunities.description:
DPH 2027, the 12th International Digital Public Health Conference, will take place in London from 15 to 17 June 2027, hosted by the UCL Centre for Digital Public Health in Emergencies, with a student day on 14 June. The main track invites research papers and extended abstracts on digital technologies, data and AI for public health.

Accepted work is published only if the presenting author registers and attends in person. African researchers can look at the external travel support listed on the conference's grant page, such as the Connect Africa scholarships for researchers at certain African institutes.
opportunities.benefits: A chance to present and publish research at an international digital public health conference; the conference itself does not fund travel, but its grant page lists outside schemes.
requirements: Original research on digital public health
Full papers of 4 to 8 pages in IEEE double-column format, anonymised, or extended abstracts of up to 1,000 words excluding references
Presenting author must register and attend in person in London
documents: Anonymised full paper or extended abstract
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are peer reviewed, with notifications on 28 January 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The UCL Centre for Digital Public Health in Emergencies studies how digital data and tools can improve public health, particularly during crises. University College London is one of the UK's leading research universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare an anonymised paper or abstract in the required format and submit it through the conference's EasyChair site before 18 November 2026. Contact support@dphconf.org with questions.
opportunities.notes: Check the grant schemes page for travel support aimed at researchers from Africa and other low- and middle-income regions.

opportunities.title: Keystone Symposia Scholarships: Myeloid Cells (C3), Killarney 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and postdocs from any country can get up to USD 1,500 to present a poster at the Keystone Myeloid Cells meeting in Killarney, Ireland (15-18 March 2027) by applying by 18 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
Keystone Symposia offers scholarships to graduate students and postdoctoral fellows who want to attend its conference "Myeloid Cells: Orchestrators of Immunity in Health, Disease and Therapy" and present their research. The meeting takes place in person from 15 to 18 March 2027 at the INEC Killarney Convention Centre in Killarney, Ireland, with livestream and on-demand options also available. It is organised by Julie Helft, Matthew Collin and Christine Moussion.

The scholarship is a reimbursement of up to USD 1,500 for the costs of attending in person. To be considered, you must submit a poster abstract to the meeting and apply for the scholarship by the same deadline, so this is really a combined abstract-plus-funding call.

There is no nationality restriction, which makes it a practical route for African early-career immunologists to present work at a leading international meeting and connect with researchers in the field.
opportunities.benefits: Up to USD 1,500 towards the cost of attending in person, which can cover airfare, ground transport, lodging and part of the registration fee. It is paid as a reimbursement against receipts after the meeting; some airfare restrictions may apply depending on the funding source.
requirements: Graduate student working towards a higher degree at an academic institution, or postdoctoral fellow (PhD, MD or DVM) within 8 years of the degree at the start of the meeting
Enrolled at or employed by an academic institution when the meeting starts
Must attend in person and present a poster abstract
Only one scholarship per applicant per meeting year (1 July to 30 June)
Only one award per lab for the meeting
documents: Poster abstract submitted and paid for (USD 50 refundable abstract fee for in-person meetings) by the scholarship deadline
Scholarship application form on the financial aid portal
Letter from your mentor, submitted on your behalf
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the abstract: the quality of the science and its relevance to the meeting, the significance of the research question and results, clarity and style, and whether the conclusions follow logically.
important_dates: Scholarship and short-talk abstract deadline: 18 November 2026 (11:59 PM US Mountain Time)
opportunities.about_provider: Keystone Symposia on Molecular and Cellular Biology is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) organisation that runs scientific conferences across the life sciences. Its financial aid programme helps students and postdocs attend its meetings and present their work.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First submit your abstract for the meeting and pay the abstract fee. Then complete the scholarship application on the Keystone Symposia financial aid portal (keystonesymposia.smapply.us) and ask your mentor to submit a supporting letter, all before 18 November 2026.
opportunities.notes: Only one application per abstract. Questions go to scholarships@keystonesymposia.org. Keystone also runs Global Health Awards for selected meetings and Early-Career Travel Awards.

opportunities.title: US-MEPI Tomorrow's Leaders Program 2027/2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full four-year undergraduate scholarship at AUB or LAU in Lebanon for high school seniors or 2026 graduates from MENA countries, so in Africa only Algerian, Egyptian, Libyan, Moroccan and Tunisian nationals qualify.
opportunities.description:
The Tomorrow's Leaders Undergraduate Program, funded by the U.S.-Middle East Partnership Initiative (MEPI) of the U.S. Department of State, gives secondary school graduates from the Middle East and North Africa a full scholarship for a bachelor's degree at the American University of Beirut or the Lebanese American University in Lebanon. Each student can also spend a semester at a university in the United States.

Alongside their degree, scholars receive leadership training, career workshops, internships, faculty mentoring and academic advising. The next cohort starts in August 2027 and recruitment is managed by FHI 360 for MEPI.

North African students from Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia are eligible, making this one of the few fully funded undergraduate packages open to them in the region.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition for up to four academic years, enrolment fees, university housing (double room), health insurance, visa and residency fees, a monthly living allowance, a yearly book allowance, a laptop, two return flights a year where applicable, a study-abroad semester in the US, plus internships, mentoring and leadership training.
requirements: Citizen of Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Tunisia, Syria, Yemen or Iraq, or a West Bank/Palestinian applicant legally resident in a third country
High school senior or 2026 graduate (2025 graduates also eligible from Iraq, Libya, Syria, Yemen and West Bank/Palestine)
Strong grades and a pass in the high school leaving exam
TOEFL iBT of at least 80, taken less than two years before the start
Leadership potential, maturity and flexibility
US citizens and permanent residents are not eligible
opportunities.about_provider: MEPI is a U.S. Department of State programme that supports education, civil society and economic opportunity in the Middle East and North Africa. FHI 360, a non-profit development organisation, runs recruitment for the Tomorrow's Leaders programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the full eligibility rules and apply through the Tomorrow's Leaders website (tomorrowsleadersprogram.org), which is linked from the MEPI page.
opportunities.notes: Up to one year of intensive English can be provided if needed before degree study.

opportunities.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Edinburgh 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young African postgraduate applicants who attended the September 2026 information sessions and were invited to apply.
opportunities.description:
The University of Edinburgh's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program funds young Africans to take postgraduate degrees, on campus in Edinburgh or online, starting in September 2027. It is part of the Mastercard Foundation's effort to develop leaders who will drive change in their communities across Africa.

For the 2027-28 cycle Edinburgh changed its process: attending one of the compulsory virtual information sessions held from 15 to 24 September 2026 was the only route to an invitation to apply, and invitations went out on 13 October 2026. Only invited candidates can now submit the main application, which closes on 19 November 2026.
opportunities.benefits: A Mastercard Foundation scholarship for a postgraduate programme at Edinburgh, on campus or online; see the programme's eligibility page for the full package.
requirements: African applicant to a 2027-28 postgraduate programme at Edinburgh
Attended a mandatory virtual information session (15-24 September 2026)
Received an invitation to apply (sent 13 October 2026)
documents: Postgraduate Assessment and Scholarship Main Application form
opportunities.selection_process: Invited applicants complete the combined assessment and scholarship form, and outcomes are announced in early to mid February 2027.
important_dates: Main application closes: 19 November 2026, 5pm UK time
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Edinburgh is one of the UK's oldest and largest research universities. The Mastercard Foundation is a Canadian foundation that works with African young people and partner universities on education and employment.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Only candidates who attended an information session and were invited can apply. They must submit the Postgraduate Assessment and Scholarship Main Application by 5pm UK time on 19 November 2026. Contact mcfsp@ed.ac.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: New applicants who missed the September information sessions cannot apply this cycle. Edinburgh also runs the Wits-Edinburgh Sustainable Africa Futures Doctoral Programme under the same partnership.

opportunities.title: Planet Health Film Fund 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Documentary directors aged 18+ from any country with a festival or broadcast credit and a registered production company can apply by 19 November 2026 for one of five GBP 20,000 film awards.
opportunities.description:
The Planet Health Film Fund will commission five short documentaries that explore how human health and the health of the environment are linked. It is run by Earthrise, a climate storytelling studio, together with the healthcare company Bupa, with BAFTA albert as sustainability partner, and the finished films will premiere at SXSW London.

Each selected filmmaker receives GBP 20,000 to make one short documentary plus two two-minute cut-downs for social media. Selected filmmakers join an online development programme in early 2027, develop and produce their films between January and May 2027, and see them premiered on 26 May 2027 at SXSW London, with an audience award announced in June.

The call is open to international applicants, so African documentary directors with a festival or broadcast track record and a registered production company can compete for funding and an international premiere.
opportunities.benefits: Five awards of GBP 20,000 each, meant to cover the full cost of producing and delivering the film and its supporting materials. Winners also join an online development programme and have their films premiered at SXSW London 2027. No other production finance may be added, and the award is paid to a production company, not an individual.
requirements: Aged 18 or over; international applicants accepted
Lead applicant must be the director (co-directors allowed)
Has directed at least one completed film selected for a recognised festival or commissioned/distributed by an established broadcaster or documentary platform
Legally registered production company at the time of applying
Documentary/non-fiction project that has not yet entered production or post-production
Application in English; the film may be in any language with subtitles
No AI-generated content in audience-facing materials
Available for online development sessions in early 2027
One entry per person
documents: Online application in English with your project idea and creative materials
Evidence of your previous directing credit
Proof of access to the story and contributors, where relevant
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are notified in December 2026 and the five selected filmmakers are announced in early January 2027. The site does not set out detailed scoring criteria.
important_dates: World premiere at SXSW London: 26 May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Earthrise is a studio and media platform making multimedia stories about the climate, and has won Webby and Cannes Lions awards. Bupa is an international healthcare company that looks after the health of more than 60 million people.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the application page on planethealthfilmfund.com before 6pm GMT on 19 November 2026. Read the fund's terms and conditions first, since they set out the rules on finance, rights and delivery.
opportunities.notes: The deadline has already been extended once, so do not expect another. The award cannot be combined with other production money.

opportunities.title: Sir Cyril Taylor Young African Leaders Program 2027
opportunities.provider: AFS Youth Assembly (Sir Cyril Taylor Foundation)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young leaders aged 18-35 from Sub-Saharan Africa running SDG-related projects can apply by 19 November 2026 for a fully funded 12-month programme including the AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva in August 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Sir Cyril Taylor Young African Leaders Program is a fully funded, 12-month leadership programme for ten young people from Sub-Saharan Africa, now in its third edition. It is run by the AFS Youth Assembly and paid for by a grant from the Sir Cyril Taylor Charitable Foundation.

Participants first complete the virtual AFS Global Competence Certificate and pre-Assembly workshops, then travel to Geneva, Switzerland, in August 2027 for the AFS Youth Assembly and an "Effect+ in the Community" workshop. After returning home they spend six months running an impact project with seed funding from the programme.

The programme is aimed at young African changemakers already leading social impact work linked to the Sustainable Development Goals who want international exposure, training and a network of peers.
opportunities.benefits: Fully funded: travel and accommodation for the Youth Assembly in Geneva, enrolment in the Global Competence Certificate, workshops and the Effect+ programme, and seed funding for your impact project (amount not stated).
requirements: Citizen of a Sub-Saharan African country
Aged 18 to 35
Proven leadership record and potential for growth
Preferably leading a social impact project related to the SDGs
Able to travel to Geneva in person in August 2027
Unexpired passport
At least intermediate English
Interest in global affairs, sustainable development and youth issues
documents: Online application form with narrative answers
opportunities.selection_process: The page says applications are reviewed on a first come, first served basis, so applying early helps. Ten leaders are chosen; earlier editions drew almost 6,000 applications. Using AI to write the narrative answers is strongly discouraged.
important_dates: AFS Youth Assembly and Effect+ workshop: August 2027, Geneva
Impact project: about six months after the Assembly
opportunities.about_provider: The Youth Assembly, founded in 2004, gathers 700 to 900 young people from over 100 countries each year, about 40% of them from Sub-Saharan Africa. It is now part of AFS Intercultural Programs, an international non-profit volunteer organisation based in New York.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the application form linked from the official Youth Assembly announcement before 23:59 UTC on 19 November 2026. Check that your passport is valid, since Swiss visa processing can take months.
opportunities.notes: Only 10 places. Write your answers yourself and apply early because review is first come, first served.

opportunities.title: Ajou University International Undergraduate Entrance Scholarships (Spring 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students with TOPIK level 3 or equivalent can apply by 20 November 2026 for Spring 2027 entry to Ajou University, Korea, with scholarships of up to 100% tuition.
opportunities.description:
Ajou University in Suwon, South Korea, offers a range of tuition scholarships to international students entering its undergraduate programmes. The current admission round is for the Spring 2027 semester, with online applications and documents due by 5 pm Korean time on 20 November 2026.

New students can receive Ajou Frontier Scholarships of up to 100% tuition for as long as four years, chosen internally for outstanding grades, including a Frontier U award for students from OECD aid-recipient countries with no current Ajou students or those facing war or disaster. Ajou Global Scholarships of 30% to 100% for the first semester are tied to Korean (TOPIK) or English test scores.

Since applicants need TOPIK level 3 or an Ajou Korean language pass, this suits African students who have already studied Korean or completed a Korean language course.
opportunities.benefits: Ajou Frontier Scholarships: 100% tuition for 4 years (S), 2 years (A), 1 year (J) or 1 semester (O); Frontier U: 100% for 1 semester to 4 years. Ajou Global Scholarships for the first semester: 100% (TOPIK 6, IELTS 8.0 or TOEFL iBT 100), 70% (TOPIK 5, IELTS 7.0, iBT 90), 50% (TOPIK 4, IELTS 6.5, iBT 80) or 30% (TOPIK 3, IELTS 5.5, iBT 75). Challenger Scholarships of 20-30% for Ajou Korean language levels 5-6.
requirements: Applicant and both parents are non-Korean citizens
High school graduate (or expected) with a qualification recognised by the home country
TOPIK level 3 or higher, or a level 3+ pass at an affiliated Korean language centre, or a pass in Ajou's Korean exam
For Global Scholarships: the TOPIK, IELTS or TOEFL score for the chosen tier
documents: Admission documents as listed in Ajou's admission guide (school certificates, transcripts, language scores, passport copies)
opportunities.selection_process: Frontier Scholarships are chosen internally based on outstanding grades; Global Scholarships depend on language test scores at entry.
important_dates: Application and documents: 28 September to 20 November 2026, 17:00 KST
opportunities.about_provider: Ajou University is a private research university in Suwon, near Seoul, with strengths in engineering, IT and business. Its international admissions office handles applications from foreign students and also runs a Korean language programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through Ajou's international undergraduate admissions site and submit the documents in the admission guide by 5 pm KST on 20 November 2026. Scholarships are considered as part of admission. Contact admission@ajou.ac.kr with questions.
opportunities.notes: Global Scholarships only apply to the first semester; later semesters depend on grades. Ajou also handles GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) undergraduate applications.

opportunities.title: BiO Global South Conference Travel Grants (20 November 2026 round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers based in most African countries can apply by 20 November 2026 for up to GBP 3,000 to attend an international conference abroad.
opportunities.description:
The Company of Biologists offers Global South Conference Travel Grants through its journal Biology Open to help early-career researchers based in the Global South attend an international scientific meeting held in a country other than their own. The current round closes on 20 November 2026 and covers travel after 21 December 2026.

Each grant is worth up to GBP 3,000 and can pay for registration, travel, accommodation, subsistence and visa fees. Because demand is high, eligible applications are chosen by random lottery, and further rounds close on 18 June 2027 and 19 November 2027.

Most African countries are on the eligible Global South list (including Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Ethiopia and Tanzania), making this one of the most accessible conference travel grants for African PhD students and postdocs.
opportunities.benefits: Up to GBP 3,000 per applicant towards conference registration, travel, accommodation, subsistence and visa fees. Awards may be partial. Travel insurance is not covered and costs already incurred are not funded retrospectively.
requirements: Based in a country on the Global South list in the applicant handbook (most African countries; Sudan, South Sudan and Zimbabwe are not listed)
Usually a PhD student or postdoc early in their career; independent group leaders without travel funding may also apply
Attending an international scientific meeting in a different country from where you are based (not a Company of Biologists Journal Meeting or Workshop)
No other Company of Biologists funding in the past 12 months
Unsuccessful applicants must wait 12 months to reapply
documents: Signed supervisor letter on headed paper (or head-of-department letter for PIs confirming no independent travel funds)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are checked for eligibility and scope, then grantees are chosen by random lottery among the eligible applications.
opportunities.about_provider: The Company of Biologists is a not-for-profit publisher and UK registered charity (no. 277992) that runs five journals: Development, Journal of Cell Science, Journal of Experimental Biology, Disease Models & Mechanisms and Biology Open. Its surplus funds grants and events for the research community.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Click Apply on the grant page to reach the Company of Biologists grants portal, complete the form in English and upload the supervisor letter, abstract and CV before 20 November 2026.
opportunities.notes: After the meeting you must send receipts, return unspent money within a month, submit a 250-word report with two photos within three months, and acknowledge Biology Open in your talk or poster. Travel must take place within six months of the award.

opportunities.title: Gerda Henkel Foundation Research Scholarships (historical humanities)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Postdoctoral historians, archaeologists and other historical humanities researchers of any nationality with a published PhD from the last ten years can apply by 20 November 2026 for 1-24 month research scholarships.
opportunities.description:
The Gerda Henkel Foundation awards research scholarships to postdoctoral researchers in the historical humanities, including archaeology, history, historical Islamic studies, art history, history of law, prehistory and history of science. Neighbouring disciplines qualify if the central research question is historical.

Scholarships run for one to 24 months and pay a monthly stipend plus travel and material costs as needed. The current deadline of 20 November 2026 feeds into the Foundation committee's spring 2027 meeting, with decisions in April 2027 and funding starting from May 2027 at the earliest.

The Foundation funds researchers regardless of nationality or place of work and does not require an institutional affiliation, which makes it a valuable option for African historians and archaeologists who have published their doctoral thesis.
opportunities.benefits: Postdocs receive EUR 2,760 per month; researchers with a habilitation or equivalent receive EUR 3,720 per month. A family allowance of EUR 480 for the first child and EUR 120 for each further child under 18 is added, plus travel and material costs as required. Short-term scholarships are capped at EUR 30,000. No overheads or tuition fees are paid.
requirements: PhD (or habilitation) in a historical humanities field; PhD awarded within the last ten years (does not apply to habilitation holders)
Doctoral thesis published as a full monograph with an ISBN
Research project different from the thesis topic
No previous Gerda Henkel scholarship in the last five years and no rejected application in the last three years
No salary or pension during the scholarship
Any nationality and place of work; no institutional affiliation needed
Doctoral candidates are not eligible
documents: Project description of up to 8 pages (11 pt, 1.5 spacing) plus bibliography
Copies of master's and PhD certificates
One (maximum two) recommendation letters uploaded by the referee through the Foundation's online form
opportunities.selection_process: The Foundation's committees meet twice a year to decide on applications. Incomplete applications are not considered and reasons for rejection are not given.
important_dates: Deadline: 20 November 2026 (for the spring 2027 committee meeting)
opportunities.about_provider: The Gerda Henkel Foundation, established in 1976 in Düsseldorf, Germany, supports research in the historical humanities and cultural heritage. It has funded more than 9,000 projects.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the online application form on the Gerda Henkel Foundation website in German or English, with PDFs of up to 6 MB each, and ask your referee to upload their letter through the online recommendation form. Applications by email are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: Any use of generative AI must be declared. You may only apply to one Gerda Henkel programme per year, and conference-only funding is not available.

opportunities.title: Harvard Mahindra Humanities Center Postdoctoral Fellowships in Environmental Humanities 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent humanities PhDs of any nationality (degree from May 2024 onward) with an environmental humanities project.
opportunities.description:
The Mahindra Humanities Center at Harvard University is offering four one-year postdoctoral fellowships for 2027-28 on the theme of environmental humanities. Scholars from any humanistic discipline can apply, as long as their research speaks to the environment, and fellows spend the year in residence in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Fellows take part in a seminar that meets every two weeks across both semesters, alongside the Center's wider programme of lectures and events. International fellows hold the post from 1 September 2027 to 31 August 2028 on a J-1 research scholar visa or F-1 OPT. There is no nationality restriction, so recent African PhDs working on climate, land, water, extraction or ecological history are well placed to apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of $70,000 for the year, medical insurance, $2,500 in research funds, and up to $1,500 for moving costs (only for fellows not already living in Greater Boston).
requirements: PhD awarded on or after May 2024, or all degree requirements including the defence completed by 1 August 2027
Research in a humanities discipline connected to environmental humanities
Able to be in residence at Harvard from September 2027 to August 2028
No nationality restriction
documents: One writing sample of up to 40 pages
Three referees, who are asked for letters automatically after you submit
opportunities.about_provider: The Mahindra Humanities Center is Harvard's main hub for interdisciplinary work in the humanities. It runs seminars, lectures and fellowships that bring scholars from around the world to Harvard.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Harvard's ARIES academic positions portal (posting 16602), uploading the CV, research statement and writing sample and entering three referees. Referees are emailed automatically and must upload their letters by 4 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Four fellowships are offered. Questions go to the Center's fellowship coordinator, Lisa Brown. The Center also runs Interdisciplinary Dissertation Completion Fellowships.
