opportunities.description:
MIPRO 2027 is the 50th jubilee edition of the MIPRO ICT and Electronics Convention, held in Opatija, Croatia, from 31 May to 4 June 2027. It is made up of 18 conferences and programmes covering information and communication technology, electronics, computing and related fields, including a MIPRO Junior track for student papers.

The convention invites scientific, technical and review papers. English-language papers that are accepted are submitted to IEEE Xplore.

Anyone can submit, so African researchers, engineers and students in ICT and electronics can use MIPRO to publish in IEEE Xplore and present at a long-established European convention.
opportunities.benefits: Presentation at the convention and publication of accepted English papers in IEEE Xplore. IEEE and MIPRO members get 10% off registration. No funding is offered.
requirements: Scientific, technical or review paper in a MIPRO conference topic
Peer review of the full paper
Open to researchers, engineers and students from any country
opportunities.selection_process: Papers are peer reviewed.
opportunities.about_provider: MIPRO is a Croatian professional society (Hrvatska udruga MIPRO) that has organised the MIPRO convention in Opatija for five decades, with IEEE technical co-sponsorship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your paper through the submission system on the MIPRO call for papers page by 30 November 2026. Questions go to mipro@mipro.hr.

opportunities.title: MPIfG Student Internship 2027
opportunities.provider: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Societies (MPIfG)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Economics and social science students (bachelor's 5th semester or later, or master's) can apply by 30 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Max Planck Institute for the Study of Societies (MPIfG) in Cologne offers student internships in 2027 inside its ongoing research projects. Interns support research in economic sociology and political economy and can attend the institute's lectures and seminars.

Voluntary internships last up to 12 weeks, while compulsory internships follow the rules of the student's study programme. Interns receive a monthly allowance in line with federal guidelines.

The call is open to economics and social science students at any university, so African students on bachelor's (5th semester or later) or master's programmes can apply for research experience at a leading German social science institute.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly allowance of EUR 450 under the federal internship guidelines.
requirements: Studying economics or social sciences
At least in the 5th semester of a bachelor's, or in any semester of a master's
Enrolled at a university during the internship
Strong interest in social science research
Very good grades
documents: Motivation letter stating preferred length and projects of interest
Excerpt of a seminar paper (up to 10 pages)
All combined in a single PDF
opportunities.selection_process: Placement depends on availability in individual research projects; projects of directors, emeriti and visiting researchers do not take interns.
opportunities.about_provider: The MPIfG in Cologne is part of the Max Planck Society and carries out basic research on the governance of modern societies, particularly the links between economy, society and politics.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the institute's career portal using the link on the internship posting, uploading one PDF with all documents by 30 November 2026. Email and postal applications are not accepted. Contact: Almut Landgraf.

opportunities.title: Make Your Mark Scholarship (Fall 2026 round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students studying in the US can submit a short reflection by 30 November 2026 for one of seven USD 3,000 awards.
opportunities.description:
The Make Your Mark Scholarship is a small award from LewerMark for international students studying in the United States. In the current round, applicants submit a short written reflection on the theme "Message to the 'Me' I'm Becoming".

Seven winners each receive USD 3,000. Applications are accepted from 1 August to 30 November 2026 through an online form.

African students already studying in the US can use this to get extra support for their costs; the page sets no rules on nationality, level or grades.
opportunities.benefits: USD 3,000 for each of seven winners.
requirements: International student studying in the United States
Written reflection on the theme "Message to the 'Me' I'm Becoming"
Application submitted within the 1 August to 30 November 2026 window
documents: Written reflection on the set theme
opportunities.about_provider: LewerMark is part of the Lewer family of companies and provides student health insurance and related services for international students in the United States.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Write your reflection and submit it with the online form linked from the LewerMark scholarship page by 30 November 2026.

opportunities.title: NorthWest Biosciences (NorthWestBio) BBSRC Doctoral Training Partnership PhD Studentships 2027
opportunities.provider: NorthWest Biosciences DTP (University of Glasgow, Lancaster University, Queen's University Belfast, University of Strathclyde)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with a first or upper-second class honours degree (or international equivalent) in a relevant science can apply for a fully funded four-university bioscience PhD; international candidates, including Africans, compete for about 30% of places and must apply by 30 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
NorthWest Biosciences is a doctoral training partnership funded by the UK's Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC). It recruits a new cohort of PhD students each year to work on projects supervised across its partner universities, and the 2027 cohort starts on Monday 4 October 2027.

Projects sit under four research themes: animal biology in health and disease, underpinning bioscience discovery, understanding pathogens from molecules to phenotypes, and plant health, resilience, yield and growth. Applicants browse the project list and may pick up to three projects, each based at a different institution. Only one student is recruited for each project.

For African graduates the key point is that the partnership sets aside roughly 30% of every cohort for international candidates, and international studentships pay full tuition fees as well as the stipend. International applicants also have an earlier window than home applicants: theirs runs from 1 October to 30 November 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees (including international fees for international students), a stipend of £21,805 a year at the UKRI 2026/27 rate (£30,488 for holders of a veterinary degree), laboratory expenses and a small annual research training support grant. Visa and Immigration Health Surcharge costs are not covered.
requirements: First or upper-second class UK honours degree, or the international equivalent, in an appropriate science
International candidates compete for around 30% of the cohort
IELTS 6.5 (or an approved SELT) for candidates whose first language is not English; evidence can follow later but is needed before an offer is confirmed
Choose up to three projects, each at a different partner institution
documents: Personal statement of no more than one A4 page
Completed Recruitment Information Form (international version) quoting your 8-digit application number
English language evidence (before an offer is confirmed)
opportunities.selection_process: Supervisory teams shortlist applications blind. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed in late February and March 2027; anyone shortlisted for more than one project is interviewed for their preferred project. Offers follow in late March or early April 2027.
important_dates: International application window: 1 October to 30 November 2026
Shortlisting and interviews: late February to March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: NorthWestBio is a BBSRC-funded doctoral training partnership led from the University of Glasgow together with Lancaster University, Queen's University Belfast and the University of Strathclyde. It trains bioscience PhD researchers in a shared programme across the four institutions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the University of Glasgow postgraduate research admissions portal and start an application for the NorthWestBio programme. Then fill in the international Recruitment Information Form in full, quoting your 8-digit application number; applications without the form are not shortlisted. Name up to three projects at different institutions and give two academic referees.
opportunities.notes: A research proposal is not required. Questions go to northwestbio@glasgow.ac.uk. Budget separately for the UK visa and the Immigration Health Surcharge, which the studentship does not pay.

opportunities.title: Routledge Handbook of Hip Hop and Sport, Culture, and Activism (call for chapters)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars anywhere can propose chapters on hip hop, sport, culture and activism for a Routledge handbook.

opportunities.title: Strathclyde Faculty of Engineering International Scholarship for Master's Study (January 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded international (non-EU) offer-holders starting a full-time, on-campus engineering master's at Strathclyde in January 2027 receive £6,000 off tuition automatically, with a 30 November 2026 deadline.
opportunities.description:
The University of Strathclyde's Faculty of Engineering gives a £6,000 tuition fee reduction to self-funded international students who start a full-time, on-campus postgraduate taught engineering master's in Glasgow in January 2027. There is no application form: the award is made automatically to every eligible offer-holder.

The scholarship covers a wide range of engineering subjects, from aeronautical, chemical, civil and electrical engineering to naval architecture, renewable energy, product design and prosthetics and orthotics. It applies to the January 2027 intake only and cannot be deferred or moved to another start date.

For African engineers this is a simple, guaranteed saving on a master's at one of the UK's strongest technological universities, provided they secure an offer and meet the fee-status and funding conditions before the deadline.
opportunities.benefits: £6,000 deducted from the tuition fee.
requirements: International (non-EU) fee status
Self-funded (not fully sponsored by a government office or embassy)
Offer for a full-time, on-campus postgraduate taught course in Glasgow starting January 2027

Course in an eligible engineering subject (e.g. aeronautical, architecture, biomedical, chemical, civil and environmental, electronic and electrical, mechanical and aerospace, naval architecture, ocean, renewable energy, product design, prosthetics and orthotics)
Only one Strathclyde scholarship per academic year
documents: No separate scholarship application; the master's admission application and offer are enough
opportunities.selection_process: Awarded automatically to all eligible offer-holders; the scholarship is added to the student record once the tuition deposit has been paid. The Faculty's decision is final.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Strathclyde is a leading technological university in the centre of Glasgow, Scotland, founded in 1796. It is known for engineering, business, science and law, and for its close links with industry.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible full-time engineering master's starting in January 2027 and obtain an offer. Pay the deposit by the deadline; the scholarship is then recorded automatically. Questions go to eng-scholarships@strath.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: The award cannot be deferred or transferred to another intake. The Faculty also offers more competitive Dean's International Excellence Awards worth £9,000 to £12,000.

opportunities.title: Strathclyde Faculty of Science International Master's Scholarship (January 2027 intake)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New self-funded international (non-EU) students starting a full-time, on-campus Faculty of Science taught master's at Strathclyde in January 2027 receive £6,000 off tuition automatically on paying the deposit by 30 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
Strathclyde's Faculty of Science gives £6,000 off tuition to new international students who start a full-time, on-campus taught master's in January 2027. The award is automatic and is applied once the student pays the tuition deposit, up to the 30 November 2026 deadline.

The page describes the scholarship as being for Faculty of Science master's courses, but its subject eligibility line lists only computer science. Applicants on other science courses should confirm with the faculty before relying on it.

For African students starting computing or other science master's in Glasgow in January, this is a straightforward reduction in fees that needs no extra paperwork.
opportunities.benefits: £6,000 deducted from tuition fees for one year.
requirements: International (non-EU) fee status
New, self-funded student (not fully sponsored by a government or embassy)
Full-time, on-campus taught master's in the Faculty of Science starting January 2027
Subject eligibility listed on the page: computer science
Online degrees, PG Certificates and PG Diplomas are excluded
Only one Strathclyde scholarship per academic year
opportunities.selection_process: Awarded automatically to eligible students when the deposit is received, until 30 November 2026. Appeals are not considered.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Strathclyde is a leading technological university in the centre of Glasgow, Scotland, founded in 1796. It is known for engineering, business, science and law, and for its close links with industry.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Secure an offer for an eligible January 2027 science master's and pay the deposit before 30 November 2026; the £6,000 is then applied automatically. Contact science-scholarships@strath.ac.uk to confirm subject eligibility.
opportunities.notes: The award cannot pay the deposit itself and cannot be deferred or moved to another intake.

opportunities.title: Strathclyde Humanities & Social Sciences Dean's International Excellence Scholarship (January 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded international (non-EU) offer-holders starting a full-time taught master's in one of ten humanities and social science subjects at Strathclyde in January 2027 are considered automatically for £10,000 off tuition (deadline 30 November 2026).
opportunities.description:
Strathclyde's Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences offers a limited number of Dean's International Excellence Scholarships worth £10,000 towards one year of tuition for self-funded international students starting a full-time taught master's in January 2027.

The award is based on merit rather than financial need. Candidates are judged on their past or current academic results and on relevant extra-curricular or professional experience. Only ten subject areas qualify: education, English, history, international relations, journalism, languages, law, politics, psychology and social policy.

For African graduates in these fields, the scholarship can cut the cost of a Glasgow master's substantially, and no separate application is needed. Winners are expected to act as student ambassadors, including at recruitment events.
opportunities.benefits: £10,000 towards tuition fees for one year.
requirements: International (non-EU) fee status
Self-funded
Offer for a full-time postgraduate taught master's starting January 2027
Subject must be one of: education, English, history, international relations, journalism, languages, law, politics, psychology, social policy
Excluded: online or blended programmes, PG Diplomas, PG Certificates, PGDE and the MSW Social Work
Only one Strathclyde scholarship per academic year
documents: No separate scholarship application; consideration is based on the programme application
opportunities.selection_process: A limited number of awards are made on merit, looking at current or previous academic performance and relevant extra-curricular or professional experience. Financial need is not considered.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Strathclyde is a leading technological university in the centre of Glasgow, Scotland, founded in 1796. It is known for engineering, business, science and law, and for its close links with industry.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible full-time master's starting in January 2027; you are considered automatically once you hold an offer. Questions go to hass-pgt-admissions@strath.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: Winners must enrol in January 2027; the award is forfeited if you defer or transfer to another programme or faculty. Recipients take part in student ambassador activities.

opportunities.title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships 2027-2028 (research fellowships and PhD)
opportunities.provider: Swiss State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI) / Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers born after 31 December 1991 who hold (or will hold by 31 July 2027) a master's degree and have a host professor in Switzerland can apply through GO ESKAS by their country's deadline (27 or 30 November 2026 for the African countries still open).
opportunities.description:
The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are the Swiss Confederation's flagship awards for foreign researchers. For the 2027-2028 academic year the scheme funds two kinds of stays for applicants from African countries: research fellowships of 6 to 12 months, and PhD scholarships of 12 months that can be renewed up to a total of 36 months. All awards start on 1 September 2027 at a Swiss university, federal institute of technology or other recognised Swiss higher education institution.

The programme is run by the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI), and candidates are selected by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS). Deadlines are set separately for each country. For the African countries whose calls are still open, applications close on 27 November 2026 (for example Nigeria, Ghana, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Benin, Togo and Madagascar) or on 30 November 2026 (for example Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, DR Congo, Namibia and Botswana). Countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Morocco, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Tunisia, Algeria and Mozambique have already closed for this cycle.

The scholarship is a strong option for African master's graduates and doctoral candidates who already have a research idea and a Swiss professor willing to supervise it, because it pays a monthly living allowance and health insurance for a full research stay in Switzerland. It does not pay tuition, so applicants should check the fees of their host institution.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly allowance of CHF 2,450 for living costs; compulsory Swiss health insurance paid by the FCS for holders from outside the EU/EFTA; a one-time grant of CHF 600 towards a housing deposit; a half-fare travelcard for Swiss public transport; and a return-flight allowance whose amount depends on the country. Tuition and semester fees, conference costs and fieldwork are not covered.
requirements: Citizen of an eligible country whose call is open (for Africa: deadline 27 or 30 November 2026)
Master's degree (or equivalent) completed by 31 July 2027 (30 June 2027 for ETH Zurich)
Born after 31 December 1991
A professor at a Swiss institution who agrees to supervise the research and writes a letter of support
A research project of your own linked to the host's work
No more than three earlier unsuccessful applications
documents: Research plan on the FCS/ESKAS form (maximum 5 pages)
Letter of support from the Swiss supervisor, plus the supervisor's CV
Email addresses of two professors who will send recommendation letters
Swiss residence permit, if already living in Switzerland
opportunities.selection_process: The FCS assesses complete applications on three main criteria: the candidate's academic profile and motivation, the originality and methodology of the research project, and the quality of the supervision and the prospect of future research collaboration. Incomplete applications and applications without a Swiss supervisor are rejected. Results are announced by the end of May 2027 at the latest.
opportunities.about_provider: SERI is the Swiss federal government's specialised agency for national and international matters of education, research and innovation policy. The Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS) assesses applications and awards the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships every year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a professor in Switzerland who agrees to host your project and obtain a signed letter of support. Check your country's deadline in the SERI country list, then submit the full application online through the GO ESKAS portal linked from the SERI scholarships page; paper and email applications are not accepted. Your two referees receive a request by email to upload their letters.
opportunities.notes: Only research fellowships and PhD scholarships are offered to African countries (the art scholarships are limited to other countries). Research fellowships cannot be extended. Check the latest version of the SERI country list, which was updated in October 2026, before applying.

opportunities.title: UN Young Professionals Programme (YPP) 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals of this year's participating countries, 32 or younger in the exam year, with at least a relevant bachelor's degree and fluent English or French; entry exam for professional UN Secretariat careers.

opportunities.title: UN-OHRLLS Doha Programme of Action Midterm Review Journalism Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists aged 18+ from the 44 Least Developed Countries, with at least two years of published work, can apply for a fully funded trip to report on the UN Midterm Review in Doha (25-27 March 2027).
opportunities.description:
The UN Office of the High Representative for the Least Developed Countries, Landlocked Developing Countries and Small Island Developing States (UN-OHRLLS) is selecting ten journalists to cover the Midterm Review of the Doha Programme of Action, to be held in Doha, Qatar, from 25 to 27 March 2027.

The Doha Programme of Action is the UN's ten-year plan for the world's Least Developed Countries. Fellows attend the review, receive briefings and produce reporting that brings the discussions to audiences in their own countries. Each fellow must publish at least three pieces of journalism and send the links by 30 April 2027.

Most of the eligible countries are in Africa, including Ethiopia, Senegal, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Mozambique, DR Congo and many others, so this is a valuable chance for African reporters covering development to gain international exposure with costs paid.
opportunities.benefits: Round-trip economy-class flights to Doha, a daily subsistence allowance for accommodation and meals under UN rules, pre-conference orientation where applicable and access to briefings. The exact support is set out in the award letter; there is no cash alternative. Fellows pay for passports, visas and accreditation unless the award letter says otherwise.
requirements: Aged 18 or over
National of one of the 44 Least Developed Countries listed on the page
Work regularly published or broadcast by a recognised media outlet (staff or freelance)
At least two years of professional journalism experience
Willing and able to travel to Doha
Interest in sustainable development and the DPoA priority areas
documents: Two published work samples, at least one on development issues
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are screened for eligibility and scored between 22 November and 17 December 2026. Only successful candidates are notified, a reserve list may be used, and decisions are final.
important_dates: Deadline: 30 November 2026 (milestone table shows the call open 27 September - 19 November 2026)
opportunities.about_provider: UN-OHRLLS is the United Nations office that advocates for and coordinates support to the Least Developed Countries, Landlocked Developing Countries and Small Island Developing States. It leads follow-up of the Doha Programme of Action for LDCs.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the online application form linked from the UN-OHRLLS page with your biography, two work samples and reporting proposal. There is no application fee; late or incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Ten fellowships are available. Contact: Ms Sithembile Siziba (sithembile.siziba@un.org). Fellows also file a short report within six weeks after the Review.

opportunities.title: United Diplomats Global Assembly Bangkok 2027 (UDGA)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young people aged 15 to 35 from any country can apply for funded seats by 30 November 2026 (USD 30 fee).
opportunities.description:
The United Diplomats Global Assembly (UDGA) 2027 is a five-day simulation of the UN General Assembly held at the United Nations Conference Centre in Bangkok, Thailand, from 25 to 29 January 2027. Its theme is "AI for Peace and Sustainable Development", and delegates debate and negotiate as country representatives.

The event has 280 seats, of which 150 are scholarship places: 30 fully funded, 50 partially funded and 70 semi-funded. Fully funded delegates have their programme fee and hotel covered and receive help with airfare. United Diplomats is an independent organiser; the event is not run or endorsed by the United Nations.

The assembly is open to students, young professionals and community leaders aged 15 to 35, so young Africans interested in diplomacy and international affairs can apply for a funded place.
opportunities.benefits: Fully funded (30 seats): 100% of the programme fee, 4 nights in a shared twin hotel room, airfare assistance, airport pickup and a city tour. Partially funded (50 seats): 70% of the fee and hotel. Semi-funded (70 seats): 50% of the fee and hotel. Self-funded fees: Standard Delegate USD 1,000 (USD 800 early bird) and Full Experience USD 1,500 (USD 1,200 early bird).
requirements: Aged 15 to 35
Student, young professional or social leader
Workable English (no IELTS or TOEFL needed)
Parental consent for ages 15 to 18
Non-refundable application fee of USD 30
documents: Passport (a national ID is accepted if you do not yet have a passport)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on achievements, leadership and community work, motivation, and interest in the theme. Decisions are final.
opportunities.about_provider: United Diplomats is an independent organiser of international youth diplomacy simulations, with an address in Gillingham, Kent, UK. It states that its events are not organised or endorsed by the UN.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online application on the United Diplomats website and pay the USD 30 fee before 30 November 2026. Selected delegates then register for the event through the UN Indico page given to them.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship covers fees and hotel; check which costs (visa, part of airfare) you must still pay yourself.

opportunities.title: University of Vienna Law Fellowship Programme Summer 2027
opportunities.provider: University of Vienna Faculty of Law
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Legal researchers at universities outside Austria, with a Vienna faculty endorser, can apply by 30 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Faculty of Law of the University of Vienna offers four fellowships for international legal researchers to spend part of the summer semester 2027 in Vienna. Two Senior Fellowships are for professors and two Junior Fellowships are for doctoral candidates and postdocs.

Fellows carry out a research project linked to one of the Faculty's research priorities, with the endorsement of a member of its academic staff. Senior fellows and postdocs can stay from two weeks to three months, and doctoral candidates from one to three months. The fellowships are not employment contracts.

Researchers at any university outside Austria may apply, so African law academics and doctoral students can use this to spend a funded research stay at one of Europe's oldest law faculties.
opportunities.benefits: Senior Fellowship: EUR 1,050 per month (2 places). Junior Fellowship: EUR 800 per month (2 places).
requirements: Affiliated with a university outside Austria
No employment at the University of Vienna in the past 6 months
Research project matching a Faculty of Law research priority
Endorsement from a professor, habilitated staff member, or associate or assistant professor of the Faculty
Doctoral candidates: 1 to 3 months; senior fellows and postdocs: 2 weeks to 3 months
documents: CV (maximum 3 pages; five key publications for senior and postdoc applicants)
For PhD candidates: a letter from the home supervisor
opportunities.about_provider: The Faculty of Law (Juridicum) of the University of Vienna is one of the largest law faculties in the German-speaking world, part of a university founded in 1365.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Send the completed application by email to the Faculty's fellowship address shown on the call page between 1 and 30 November 2026.

opportunities.title: Université de Toulon Excellence Master Scholarship 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Foreign nationals with a foreign bachelor's degree, at least 15/20 in the final year and C1 French can apply by 30 November 2026 for €950 a month during a master's at the Université de Toulon.
opportunities.description:
The Université de Toulon, on France's Mediterranean coast, offers Excellence Master scholarships to bring strong international students into its master's programmes in 2027-28. The award pays €950 a month for 12 or 24 months and is open to any of the university's master's programmes except work-study (alternance) ones.

The scholarship targets students who are not already in France: candidates must hold a foreign nationality and a bachelor's degree from a foreign university, and anyone currently studying in France is excluded. The research topic for the thesis or internship must fit one of the university's strategic areas, and winners commit to acting as a link with their home university.

For students from francophone Africa in particular this is an accessible route to a funded French master's, since the language requirement is French at C1 level. The same call page also covers the national Eiffel Excellence scholarships, which Toulon nominates for.
opportunities.benefits: €950 per month for 12 or 24 months during the master's.
requirements: Foreign nationality only (dual French nationals ineligible)
Not currently studying in France
No other French government, Erasmus+ or AUF grant at the time of application
Bachelor's degree from a foreign university (or foreign bac+5 grande école)
Average of at least 15/20 in the third year of the bachelor's
French at C1; English at B2 for fully English-taught programmes (an advantage for others)
Research/internship topic linked to a UTLN strategic area
Commitment to act as an ambassador with your home university
documents: Transcripts for the last two years of study
Proof of C1 French for non-francophone applicants (certificate, proof of study in French, or check by the programme lead)
Description of the research topic and home-university link (via the online form)
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates have a compulsory interview with the head of the master's programme. Academic excellence is the main criterion, along with the coherence of the academic and professional project. The number of awards is not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: The Université de Toulon is a French public university based in Toulon and La Garde in the Var region. It teaches across sciences, engineering, law, economics, humanities and sport, with strong research links to marine and coastal sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online excellence scholarship request form on the university's e-services site (formulaires.idemarches.univ-tln.fr), linked from the call page, before 30 November 2026. Contact the international office at international@univ-tln.fr with questions.
opportunities.notes: The same page explains Toulon's Eiffel nominations: €1,200 a month for master's candidates born after 31 March 1997 and €2,100 a month for doctoral candidates born after 31 March 1991.

opportunities.title: WHO TDR Research Fellowship for African Scientists
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Research fellowship for African scientists working on infectious diseases of poverty.

opportunities.title: YSI Poster Session at the Centro Sraffa Winter School on the Surplus Approach 2027
opportunities.provider: INET Young Scholars Initiative and Centro Sraffa (Roma Tre)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students and young economists anywhere can apply by 30 November 2026 to present a poster, with possible travel support.
opportunities.description:
The Young Scholars Initiative (YSI) of the Institute for New Economic Thinking is organising a poster session at the Centro Sraffa Winter School on the surplus approach, an advanced school on classical and Sraffian economics. The school takes place at the Department of Economics of Roma Tre University in Rome from 22 to 27 February 2027.

PhD students and young scholars can present a poster on their research, and those selected to present may receive a partial travel and accommodation stipend from YSI/INET. The session is organised with YSI's Keynesian Working Group and the Centro Sraffa research centre.

No nationality limits are stated, so African doctoral students and early-career economists working on heterodox or classical economics can use this to present their work and get support to attend.
opportunities.benefits: Selected poster presenters may receive a partial travel and accommodation stipend from YSI/INET (amount not stated).
requirements: PhD student or young scholar
Research suitable for a poster on the surplus approach or related economics
Both the Centro Sraffa and the YSI application forms must be submitted
documents: Centro Sraffa application form (indicating interest in the poster session)
opportunities.about_provider: The Young Scholars Initiative is the student and early-career network of the Institute for New Economic Thinking (INET). The Centro di Ricerche e Documentazione "Piero Sraffa" at Roma Tre University promotes research on Sraffa and the surplus approach.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the Centro Sraffa winter school form and say you want to present a poster, then complete the separate YSI form explaining why you need funding. Both must be in by 30 November 2026. Questions go to cswinterschool2027@gmail.com.

opportunities.title: Yale Center for British Art Short-Term Research Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Curators, academics, independent scholars and doctoral students of any nationality working on British visual and material culture can apply by 30 November 2026 (5 pm ET) for a funded 2-4 week research stay at Yale.
opportunities.description:
The Yale Center for British Art (YCBA) in New Haven, Connecticut, awards short-term research fellowships for scholars who need to work on site with its collections, which form the largest holding of British art outside the United Kingdom. Fellowships last two, three or four full weeks and fall between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028.

The fellowships are open to all nationalities and to a broad range of people: university academics, museum curators, independent scholars and doctoral students. North American doctoral candidates must have completed everything except the dissertation. Fellows get a dedicated desk in the Reference Library, give a short presentation on their research and acknowledge the fellowship in later publications.

African researchers studying British empire, colonial visual culture, art history or material culture can use the award to consult YCBA's paintings, prints, drawings, rare books and archives in person.

Every admitted scholar receives the Yenching Fellowship, which pays tuition, on-campus housing, a monthly stipend, one round trip to Beijing, medical insurance and research-trip expenses. Studies begin in early September 2027 in Beijing.

The programme is open to non-Chinese citizens with a bachelor's degree by August 2027, so outstanding African graduates in any discipline who want to understand China and its links with Africa and the world can apply.

opportunities.title: A*STAR Research Attachment Programme (ARAP)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students at A*STAR partner universities, nominated jointly by their university and an A*STAR supervisor, for a one to two year research attachment in Singapore.
opportunities.description:
The A*STAR Research Attachment Programme (ARAP) lets PhD students from A*STAR's partner universities abroad spend one to two years doing their doctoral research in Singapore. Students are jointly supervised by their home university and a researcher at one of A*STAR's research institutes, and must be based in Singapore for the whole attachment.

ARAP is not an open application scheme. The student's home university and an A*STAR supervisor nominate the student together, and A*STAR researchers submit nominations twice a year, by 1 June and 1 December. The attachment should start at least six months after the nomination deadline.

Partner universities include Manchester, UCL, Surrey and Warwick, among others on A*STAR's list. African PhD students enrolled at one of these partners can use ARAP to gain research experience in a leading Asian science hub with a monthly stipend and allowances.
opportunities.benefits: Monthly stipend of S$3,600; housing allowance of S$300 a month; one-time airfare grant of S$1,500; one-time settling-in allowance of S$1,000 (may be recovered if the stay is under a year); one-time IT allowance of S$800; visa costs; medical insurance; and a conference allowance. Tuition fees are not covered.

Applications are welcome from predoctoral and postdoctoral researchers and from professionals with relevant experience, so African researchers working on ocean governance or climate science with a policy angle can apply.

Fellows within five years of their PhD are eligible for benefits; others receive full or partial reimbursement of health insurance premiums. Access to most Harvard libraries and facilities.

opportunities.title: Damon Runyon Quantitative Biology Fellowship Award 2027

No more than 24 months in the mentor's lab before the deadline
Must not hold, or have been awarded, an NIH K award
Physician-scientists: residency completed, board eligible in the US, at least 80% research time and no more than five years of postdoctoral experience
Non-US citizens must do the research at a US institution
Two mentors: one computational and one experimental
documents: Diploma copy or letter from the graduate school confirming the defence
Letters and commitments from both mentors
Other forms listed on the Foundation's application forms page
opportunities.selection_process: The Quantitative Biology Fellowship Award Committee reviews the applications and the Foundation's Board of Directors approves the awards. Applications are judged on the quality and commitment of the applicant, the quality and track record of the mentorship team, the quality of the research proposal and its computational innovation.
important_dates: Deadline: 1 December 2026, 4:00 pm US Eastern Time
opportunities.about_provider: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation is a US non-profit that funds promising early-career cancer scientists through fellowships and awards. Its Quantitative Biology Fellowship is reviewed by a dedicated committee and approved by the Foundation's Board of Directors.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application through Altum ProposalCentral (proposalcentral.com) by searching for the Quantitative Biology Fellowship Award. Follow the detailed instructions on the Foundation's forms page, and arrange both mentor letters well before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Contact: awards@damonrunyon.org or +1 212 455 0520. The Foundation also runs other fellowships and awards listed on its application guidelines pages.

opportunities.title: EAI GOODTECHS 2027 Call for Papers (Smart Technologies for Social Good)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers can submit full or short papers by 1 December 2026 for GOODTECHS 2027 in Heraklion, Greece, 22-23 April 2027.
opportunities.description:
EAI GOODTECHS 2027 is the 13th International Conference on Smart Objects and Technologies for Social Good, organised by the European Alliance for Innovation (EAI). It takes place in person on 22-23 April 2027 at the Aquila Atlantis Hotel in Heraklion, Crete, Greece.

The call invites research from academia, industry and government on how technologies such as AI, big data, the Internet of Things, blockchain, cloud and cybersecurity can serve society, including smart healthcare, education, energy, agriculture, disaster management, transport, cultural heritage and support for people with disabilities.

Accepted papers appear in Springer's LNICST series, indexed in Scopus and Web of Science, giving African researchers working on technology for development a recognised international outlet.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of registered and presented papers in Springer LNICST proceedings; extended versions can go to EAI Endorsed Transactions journals at a discounted fee (30% new content required). A 50% discount on the second paper applies only if the same author registers both and is the sole attendee. No travel grants are stated.
requirements: Original, unpublished work in English
Full papers of 12 to 20 pages or short papers of 6 to 11 pages (excluding references and appendices), in Springer format
Anonymised PDF submission
At least one author registers and presents in person
documents: Anonymised paper PDF in Springer LNICST format
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are peer reviewed by the programme committee, with notifications on 1 February 2027.
important_dates: Abstract registration and paper submission: 1 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: The European Alliance for Innovation (EAI) is a non-profit that organises research conferences worldwide and publishes the EAI Endorsed Transactions journals. GOODTECHS 2027 is chaired by researchers from Imperial College London, the University of Rijeka, FORTH-ICS and the University of Pisa.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register your abstract and upload the anonymised full or short paper through EasyChair by 1 December 2026, following the Springer template. If accepted, register for the conference and submit the camera-ready version by 1 March 2027.
opportunities.notes: Ignore older 2024/2025 track deadlines still shown in the website sidebar. Pages beyond the limit cost extra. Contact: conferences@eai.eu.

opportunities.title: ECTRIMS Postdoctoral Research Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD or MD holders of any nationality can apply by 1 December 2026 for a funded MS research fellowship in Europe.
opportunities.description:
The ECTRIMS Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Exchange Programme funds early-career researchers to spend one or two years doing research on multiple sclerosis in a European laboratory or clinic. The host must be in a different country from the candidate's current position, so the fellowship is designed as an exchange.

ECTRIMS pays EUR 55,000 a year to the host institution to cover the fellow's salary or stipend and benefits, plus economy travel. Applications for the 2027 programme are open until 1 December 2026, and fellows usually start in September or October 2027.

Citizens of any country can apply, so African doctors and scientists with a PhD or MD interested in MS and neuroimmunology research can use the fellowship to train at a European centre.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 55,000 per year paid to the host institution for the fellow's salary or stipend and benefits, plus economy travel for the fellow. Congress travel is funded separately.
requirements: MD, PhD, ScD or equivalent at the time of application
Citizens of any country
Host lab or clinic in Europe, in a different country from the current placement
Confirmation that there is no language barrier at the host
Recommended: no more than five years of postdoctoral experience and generally under 40
One application per cycle
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed on the candidate's qualifications, the quality of the mentor and host, the research plan and the letters.
opportunities.about_provider: ECTRIMS (European Committee for Treatment and Research in Multiple Sclerosis) describes itself as the world's largest professional organisation dedicated to understanding and treating multiple sclerosis. Its secretariat is in Basel, Switzerland.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree a project with a host mentor in another European country, prepare the documents as PDFs and submit them through the ECTRIMS online fellowship portal by 1 December 2026.

opportunities.title: Echidna Global Scholars Program 2027 (Brookings Institution)
opportunities.provider: Brookings Institution, Center for Universal Education
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mid-career researchers and practitioners from the Global South with a master's degree, at least 10 years of experience and a commitment to return home can apply by 1 December 2026 for a six-month visiting fellowship on gender-transformative education.
opportunities.description:
The Echidna Global Scholars Program is a six-month visiting fellowship at the Brookings Institution's Center for Universal Education (CUE) in Washington, DC. Each cohort brings together mid-career leaders from the Global South who carry out research on gender-transformative education, meaning education policy and practice that tackles the gender norms holding girls and women back.

The programme has run since 2012 and is funded by Echidna Giving. It has completed 14 cohorts and has 48 alumni from 25 countries. Applications for the 2027 visiting fellowship are open now and close on 1 December 2026.

Fellows spend their time producing policy research with the support of Brookings experts, then take it back to their own country. That makes the programme especially relevant to African education researchers, NGO leaders, academics and civil servants who already work on girls' education and want a global platform for their work.
opportunities.benefits: A six-month visiting fellowship at Brookings with research support and mentoring from the Center for Universal Education. The pages read do not state the stipend or other amounts.
requirements: Master's degree or higher
At least 10 years of professional experience in research or academia, NGOs, community or civil-society organisations, or government
Background in education, development, public policy, economics or a related social science or humanities field
Substantial experience in and ties to a Global South country, with a clear plan to return there
Good command of English
documents: Research proposal of 3 to 5 pages on gender-transformative education
opportunities.selection_process: Brookings reviews the cover letter, CV, questionnaire and research proposal against the programme's eligibility criteria and its focus on gender-transformative education. The pages read do not describe interview stages.
opportunities.about_provider: The Brookings Institution is a non-profit public policy organisation in Washington, DC. Its Center for Universal Education works to make quality education available to every child and young person, and hosts the Echidna Global Scholars Program.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare a cover letter, CV and a 3 to 5 page research proposal, then start the application from the Brookings programme page, which links to the Brookings careers portal (iCIMS) where you answer the questionnaire and upload your documents. Brookings also offers a virtual information session for applicants.
opportunities.notes: The research must focus on gender-transformative education in the Global South.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Clinical Linguistics (EMCL) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with three years of study in speech pathology, linguistics, psychology, biomedical sciences or special education and strong English.
opportunities.description:
The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Clinical Linguistics (EMCL) is a two-year research master taught in English by a consortium of the University of Groningen, Ghent University and the University of Eastern Finland. It trains students in the linguistic, cognitive and neurological study of speech and language disorders, for the 2027-2029 intake.

Students move between the partner universities and attend an edition of the Science of Aphasia conference. A limited number of EU-funded Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover full tuition and a monthly allowance, and some scholarships are reserved for particular countries.

Graduates in speech and language therapy, linguistics, psychology, biomedical sciences or special education from African countries can apply for a fully funded European research master by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship (limited number, up to two years): full tuition waiver and €1,400 per month for travel, visa, insurance and living costs. Self-funded students pay a consortium fee of €18,000 (non-EU) or €9,000 (EU/EEA) for the whole programme, which covers registration, administration, insurance, excursions, lab costs and one Science of Aphasia conference, but not books, housing or travel.
requirements: At least three years of higher education (BA, BSc or equivalent) in speech and language pathology, linguistics (at least 60 ECTS of general linguistics), biomedical sciences, psychology or special education

English: IELTS Academic 7.0 (6.0 per part), TOEFL iBT 100 (21 per part) or the new TOEFL scale 5/6 (4 per part), PTE Academic 71, LanguageCert 75, Cambridge C1/C2 or Linguaskill 185; tests no older than two years
Medium-of-instruction letters are not accepted as proof of English
Previous Erasmus+ or Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders cannot get the scholarship
documents: Official transcripts and degree certificate (with translations if needed)
For linguistics backgrounds: transcript showing at least 60 ECTS in linguistics
opportunities.selection_process: A selection board ranks all eligible applicants, and offers with or without a scholarship are made from mid-February 2027.
important_dates: Application portal open: 1 October to 1 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: EMCL is run by three European universities with strong linguistics and clinical research groups: Groningen (Netherlands), Ghent (Belgium) and Eastern Finland. It is co-funded by the EU's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the application form from the EMCL website and submit it with all documents through the EMCL portal on Formdesk between 1 October and 1 December 2026. Upload everything at once, because missing documents cannot be added later and English proof cannot follow after the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Finnish residence permits may require biometrics in a third country for some nationalities, so plan visa steps early.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master in Public Policy (Mundus MAPP) 2027-2029
opportunities.provider: Mundus MAPP consortium (CEU, IBEI, ISS Rotterdam, University of York)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of three-year social science bachelor's degrees with a GPA of at least 3.17/4.0 can apply; scholarship applicants must apply by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
Mundus MAPP is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's in Public Policy, co-funded by the European Union and run by a consortium of Central European University (CEU), the Institut Barcelona d'Estudis Internacionals (IBEI), the International Institute of Social Studies (ISS) in The Hague and the University of York. The 2027-2029 cohort is now recruiting.

Students study in two different countries, with at least 30 ECTS in each, following tracks such as CEU-IBEI, ISS-IBEI or ISS-York. The programme focuses on policy analysis and global and regional governance.

Top-ranked applicants receive full EU scholarships covering tuition and a monthly allowance. Applicants from many English-speaking African countries with an English-taught degree do not need an English test, which lowers the cost of applying.
opportunities.benefits: EMJM scholarship (limited number, for 24 months): €1,400 per month (up to €33,600) for travel, visa, installation and living costs, plus a full tuition waiver. Institutional scholarship: one per track, a 50% tuition waiver in both years, with no stipend. Health insurance is arranged by the consortium. Not covered: the study visit and winter school (about €600 to €1,000 each) and travel between home and the consortium countries.
requirements: Bachelor's degree of at least three years from a recognised university, preferably in the social sciences (natural science and engineering degrees are not eligible)
Upper second class (2.1) where applicable and a GPA of at least 3.17 out of 4.0, given on a 4.0 scale
Residence in a country other than those of your chosen track
Not already an EMJM scholarship holder

English: TOEFL iBT 95, IELTS Academic 7.0, Duolingo 130, PTE Academic 76 or Cambridge C1/C2, unless you are a citizen of a listed English-speaking country (including Botswana, Gambia, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Namibia, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia) with an English-taught degree
Work experience is preferred but not required
documents: Transcripts with GPA converted to a 4.0 scale
opportunities.selection_process: Each application is assessed by at least two evaluators. EMJM scholarships go to the top-ranked candidates on academic merit. Appeals are allowed only on procedural grounds, by 20 April 2027.
important_dates: Deadline for scholarship applicants and early self-funded applicants: 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET
opportunities.about_provider: Mundus MAPP is delivered by four European institutions with strong public policy and international studies programmes: CEU, IBEI, ISS (Erasmus University Rotterdam) and the University of York. The programme is co-funded by the Erasmus+ programme of the European Union.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Mundus MAPP online portal by 1 December 2026 if you want a scholarship, choosing your study track and including your GPA, English scores and motivation statement. Check the admissions checklist on the programme site before submitting.
opportunities.notes: Your country of residence must differ from the countries on your chosen track. Budget for the study visit, winter school and your own travel, which the scholarship does not cover.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master in Transfers-Fluids-Materials for Aeronautics Sustainable Applications (TFMASA) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-European (including African) applicants can apply by 1 December 2026 for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship in aeronautics engineering.
opportunities.description:
TFMASA (Transfers-Fluids-Materials for Aeronautics Sustainable Applications) is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's degree in which students study at partner universities in Bordeaux (France), Louvain-la-Neuve (Belgium) and Cottbus (Germany). It trains engineers in fluid dynamics, heat transfer and materials for more sustainable aviation.

The application campaign for the 2027-2029 cohort opened on 1 September 2026 and closes on 1 December 2026 at 10:00 CET. The best candidates receive Erasmus Mundus scholarships worth EUR 1,400 a month plus a yearly contribution to participation costs.

Partner-country applicants, which includes all African nationalities, can compete for the scholarships, although no more than 10% of awards may go to one nationality.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship of EUR 1,400 per month plus EUR 4,500 per year towards participation costs (tuition and insurance), for partner- and programme-country students alike.
requirements: Partner-country applicants: nationals of countries outside the Erasmus+ programme countries (EU-27, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye)
Not a previous Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship holder
No more than 10% of awards per nationality
Degree, grade and language requirements as set on the programme's admission pages
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are ranked competitively, with interviews in mid-February, subject to the nationality rules.
opportunities.about_provider: The TFMASA consortium is a group of European universities, coordinated from Bordeaux, that runs this EU-funded Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online only through the TFMASA application platform linked from the programme's key dates page before 10:00 CET on 1 December 2026. Paper and email applications are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: The programme also mentions other funding not managed by the consortium, such as the Erasmus+ study grant and the Eiffel Excellence scholarship.

opportunities.title: Ernst Mach Grant Worldwide 2027
opportunities.provider: OeAD (Austrian Agency for Education and Internationalisation)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students, postgraduates, postdocs and researchers from universities outside Austria can apply for a 1 to 9 month research stay in Austria.
opportunities.description:
The Ernst Mach Grant Worldwide is a scholarship from Austria's Agency for Education and Internationalisation (OeAD), funded by the Austrian science ministry, that brings international doctoral students, postgraduates, postdocs and researchers to Austria for a research stay at an Austrian university or research institution.

Grants last between one and nine months and cannot be extended. All fields of study are eligible, and the aim is to strengthen exchange between Austrian institutions and researchers from abroad. For stays in 2027/28 the application deadline has been moved to 1 December 2026.

African doctoral candidates and early-career researchers who have a host contact in Austria can use this grant to fund a focused research visit.
requirements: Doctoral student, postgraduate, postdoc or researcher at a university outside Austria
Research stay at an Austrian university or research institution
Any field of study
Stay of 1 to 9 months (no extensions)
opportunities.about_provider: OeAD is Austria's national agency for international cooperation in education and research. It manages Austrian government scholarships, including the Ernst Mach programmes, and publishes them in its grants.at database.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the full conditions for the Ernst Mach Grant Worldwide in the OeAD grants.at database, then submit your application online there by 1 December 2026. Contact OeAD through its online contact form with questions.
opportunities.notes: OeAD also offers an Ernst Mach grant for study at an Austrian university of applied sciences (non-European bachelor's and master's students, deadline 1 February 2027) and a follow-up grant for former OeAD scholars from developing countries (deadline 1 February 2027).

opportunities.title: FINEC 2027 Financial Econometrics Conference (SoFiE sponsored)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers can submit financial econometrics papers by 1 December 2026 (GBP 30 fee) for the 21-23 April 2027 conference at Lancaster.
opportunities.description:
FINEC 2027 is a joint financial econometrics conference sponsored by the Society for Financial Econometrics (SoFiE) and hosted by Lancaster University Management School in the UK. It runs fully in person at Lancaster University on 21-23 April 2027, with no online sessions.

The organisers invite papers on high-frequency econometrics, market microstructure, forecasting, asset pricing, volatility, fintech and blockchain, climate econometrics, machine learning and factor models. Keynote speakers include Torben Andersen, Oliver Linton, Roberto Renò and Viktor Todorov.

For African doctoral students and researchers in finance and econometrics, it is a chance to present to leading figures in the field and compete for a best-paper prize.
opportunities.benefits: The Lancaster Financial Econometrics Prize of £1,000 for the best paper. No travel grants are stated.
requirements: Research paper in financial econometrics or a related listed topic
Paper submitted as a PDF
Payment of the £30 submission fee
In-person presentation at Lancaster if accepted
documents: Flywire payment reference for the £30 submission fee
opportunities.about_provider: The conference is organised by Lancaster University Management School's Centre for Financial Econometrics, Asset Markets and Macroeconomic Policy (EMP) with its departments of Accounting and Finance and of Economics. It is sponsored by SoFiE, the international society for financial econometrics.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Pay the £30 submission fee through the Flywire link on the call page, then upload your paper and enter the payment reference in the conference's Qualtrics submission form by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The payment link's address refers to a different 2026 conference, so you may want to confirm it with the organisers before paying.

opportunities.title: Graduate Ellison Scholars Programme at Oxford 2027 (DPhil)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Candidates from any country who meet University of Oxford DPhil entry requirements and fit an EIT research project can apply by 1 December 2026 for fully funded doctoral study starting October 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Graduate Ellison Scholars Programme funds full-time doctoral (DPhil) study at the University of Oxford for students who will work on research projects linked to the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT) in Oxford. EIT, founded and funded by Larry Ellison, works on science and technology for global challenges such as health, food security, climate and AI.

Applications for October 2027 entry opened in mid-September and close on 1 December 2026. Depending on the project, candidates either apply through the EIT portal (pathogen, MDLS, plant biology and economics projects) or through Oxford's own route (the AI and robotics centre for doctoral training, the generative biology doctoral training programme and correlates of immunity). Conditional offers and Oxford applications follow from January to March 2027, with announcements in April 2027.

The programme recruits from around the world and pays tuition and living costs, which makes it a strong option for African graduates with excellent records in the life sciences, AI, economics and related fields. The separate undergraduate Ellison round for 2027 entry has already closed.
opportunities.benefits: University of Oxford tuition fees, a living stipend (amount not stated), travel and conference costs, a technology set-up allowance and arrival costs such as flights, visa and healthcare. Packages differ for the doctoral training routes.
requirements: Meet University of Oxford DPhil entry requirements
Full-time doctoral study starting October 2027
Research interests aligned with an EIT project
Excellent academic record (EIT gives a GPA of 3.7/4 as an example of the standard expected)
Final-year students may apply
documents: EIT online application or Oxford application, depending on the project route
opportunities.selection_process: EIT looks for alignment with one of its projects, academic excellence, innovation, collaboration, tenacity and integrity. Shortlisted candidates receive conditional offers and complete an Oxford application between January and March 2027; final announcements come in April 2027.
important_dates: Conditional offers and Oxford applications: January to March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Ellison Institute of Technology is a research institute in Oxford founded by Larry Ellison to develop solutions to global problems in health, food, climate and AI. Its scholars programme funds students at the University of Oxford.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the EIT graduate research areas and pick a project. For pathogen, MDLS, plant biology and economics projects apply on the EIT Ellison Scholars portal; for the AI and robotics, generative biology and correlates of immunity routes apply through the University of Oxford. Submit before 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The undergraduate Ellison Scholars round for October 2027 entry closed on 31 July 2026.

opportunities.title: HKU Presidential PhD Scholar Programme 2027-28
opportunities.provider: The University of Hong Kong Graduate School
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All applicants to full-time PhD study at HKU who apply in the main round (1 September to 1 December 2026) are considered for the HKU Presidential PhD Scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The HKU Presidential PhD Scholar Programme (HKU-PS) is the University of Hong Kong's most prestigious funding package for new doctoral students. It is offered to selected full-time PhD students admitted for 2027-28 and combines a tuition fee waiver, a monthly scholarship, a cash award, a travel allowance and a guaranteed hall place in the first year.

Applicants are considered automatically if they apply for a full-time PhD during the main round, which runs from 1 September to 1 December 2026. Shortlisted candidates may be interviewed. HKU also encourages applicants to apply for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme at the same time.

The package is worth up to about US$57,000 in the first year, which makes it one of the most valuable PhD awards in Asia for African researchers in any field.
opportunities.benefits: For 2027-28 admission the package is worth up to about HK$445,800 (US$57,150) in year one and up to about HK$428,300 (US$54,920) in later years. It includes a cash award of HK$40,000 in year one and HK$20,000 in later years, a tuition fee waiver of HK$49,500 a year, a postgraduate scholarship of HK$28,700 a month, a travel allowance of HK$14,400 a year and a guaranteed hall place in year one.
requirements: Applicant for full-time PhD study at HKU for 2027-28
Application submitted in the main round (1 September to 1 December 2026)
Meet HKU and programme admission and English requirements
Outstanding academic and research potential
documents: HKU research postgraduate online application with the documents required by the chosen programme (transcripts, degree certificates, research proposal, references, English test results if needed)
opportunities.selection_process: All full-time PhD applicants in the main round are considered. Shortlisted candidates may be invited to an interview.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Hong Kong is Hong Kong's oldest university and a leading research institution in Asia. Its Graduate School oversees research postgraduate admissions and scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a supervisor and programme, then submit the HKU research postgraduate online application (linked from the HKU-PS page) by 1 December 2026. No separate scholarship form is needed; also consider applying for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme.
opportunities.notes: The number of awards is not stated.

opportunities.title: HKU School of Computing and Data Science Master Programmes Entrance Scholarship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: The University of Hong Kong, School of Computing and Data Science
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants to HKU's taught master's programmes in computing and data science for 2027-28 who apply by the main-round deadline (1 December 2026, noon HKT) are considered for entrance awards of HK$10,000 to HK$50,000.
opportunities.description:
The University of Hong Kong's School of Computing and Data Science (CDS) awards entrance scholarships to strong applicants for its taught master's programmes, such as the MSc in Computer Science, for the 2027-28 intake. Awards range from HK$10,000 to HK$50,000 and are given on academic performance, with an interview where applicable.

The main application round closes at noon Hong Kong time on 1 December 2026 and a clearing round on 30 April 2027. Applying in the main round gives the widest choice of places and awards. The school also lists other awards, including an International Postgraduate Scholarship for Computer Science for non-local students with an overseas bachelor's degree, and several HK$100,000 prizes for top students.

For African computer science and engineering graduates these awards reduce the cost of a one-year master's at a top-ranked Asian university, though applicants should plan funding for most of the tuition and living costs.
opportunities.benefits: CDS Master Programmes Entrance Scholarship: HK$10,000 to HK$50,000. Other school awards include the International Postgraduate Scholarship for Computer Science (full or partial, for non-local students with an overseas bachelor's), the Tongcheng Travel Scholarship (HK$100,000, up to three, CGPA 3.8 or above) and the QRT-HKU Excellence Prize (HK$100,000, up to four, CGPA 3.5 or above, full-time students).
requirements: Applicant to a CDS taught master's programme for the 2027-28 intake
Strong academic performance
Interview if requested
Meet HKU's admission and English language requirements
documents: English language test score if required
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are decided on academic performance, with an interview where applicable, as part of the admission review.
important_dates: Main round deadline: 1 December 2026, 12:00 noon HKT
Clearing round deadline: 30 April 2027, 12:00 noon HKT
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Hong Kong, founded in 1911, is Hong Kong's oldest university. Its School of Computing and Data Science runs taught master's programmes in computer science, data science and related fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a CDS taught master's programme on the HKU taught postgraduate admissions portal, pay the HK$780 application fee and upload your documents in the online admission system before the main-round deadline. Applicants are considered for the entrance scholarship as part of admission.
opportunities.notes: The application fee is HK$780 per programme for 2027-28.
