opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD applicants to Harvard GSAS.

opportunities.title: Harvard University Africa Fellowship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: African graduate applicants.

opportunities.title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Outstanding graduates of any nationality seeking full-time PhD admission at one of eight Hong Kong universities.
opportunities.description:
The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) was set up by the Research Grants Council (RGC) in 2009 to attract the best students from around the world to do a PhD in Hong Kong. For the 2027/28 intake, 400 fellowships will be awarded.

Fellows study full time at one of eight Hong Kong universities: City University, Hong Kong Baptist University, Lingnan, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the Education University, Polytechnic University, HKUST and the University of Hong Kong. Each applicant may choose up to two programmes or departments.

The scheme is open regardless of country of origin, work experience or ethnic background, and it pays one of the most generous PhD stipends in Asia, which makes it a strong option for high-achieving African graduates.
opportunities.benefits: For 2026/27 the stipend was HK$344,400 a year (about US$44,150) plus a conference and research travel allowance of HK$14,400 a year (about US$1,840), for up to three years. The 2027/28 rates are not yet stated.
requirements: Open to applicants of any nationality, work background or ethnicity
Must seek admission as a new full-time PhD student at one of the eight universities
Outstanding academic record and research potential
Must meet the chosen university's own admission requirements
documents: HKPFS initial application (online) to obtain an HKPFS reference number
Full PhD application to the chosen university with the documents it requires
opportunities.selection_process: Two RGC selection panels (one for sciences, medicine, engineering and technology; one for humanities, social sciences and business) assess shortlisted candidates. The main criterion is academic excellence, followed by research ability and potential, communication and interpersonal skills, and leadership.
important_dates: Initial application deadline: 1 December 2026, 12:00 noon Hong Kong time
University full application deadline: 1 December 2026, 11:59 pm Hong Kong time
opportunities.about_provider: The Research Grants Council operates under Hong Kong's University Grants Committee and funds research at Hong Kong's universities. It runs the HKPFS together with the eight participating universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First submit an initial application in the HKPFS electronic system to get your reference number, then submit a full PhD application to your chosen university (up to two programmes) quoting that number, both by 1 December 2026. Submit the initial application early because it closes at noon.
opportunities.notes: Note the two different closing times on 1 December: noon for the RGC initial application and 11:59 pm for most university applications.

opportunities.title: IAS School of Mathematics Memberships and Postdoctoral Positions 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists at any career stage (postdoc categories within 5 years of PhD) apply through MathJobs for stipendiary memberships of one or two years.
opportunities.description:
The School of Mathematics at the Institute for Advanced Study (IAS) offers research memberships in mathematics and theoretical computer science for periods of 2 to 11 months, hosting about 85 members a year with support from the US National Science Foundation.

Categories include postdoctoral memberships for those up to five years from the PhD (one or two years), joint postdoctoral positions with DIMACS at Rutgers, Princeton (Veblen Instructorship) and the Bourgain Fellowship, Von Neumann Fellowships for those 5 to 15 years from the PhD, other mid-career and senior memberships, and a special-year programme open to all career stages.

The School encourages applications from women, minorities and mid-career scientists, and there is no stated nationality restriction, so African mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists can apply.
opportunities.benefits: The School offers competitive salaries, on-campus housing and other resources; Von Neumann Fellows receive a grant equivalent to a competitive salary, while some senior members receive limited support. Amounts are not stated.
requirements: Mathematician or theoretical computer scientist at any career stage
Postdoctoral membership: no more than five years from the PhD
Von Neumann Fellowship: 5 to 15 years from the PhD
Joint positions require applying to both institutions
documents: Application and supporting materials submitted through MathJobs
Reference letters (due by the same deadline)
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute for Advanced Study is an independent research institute in Princeton, New Jersey. Its School of Mathematics hosts mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists at all career stages.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to the IAS School of Mathematics through MathJobs; all materials, including reference letters, are due by 1 December.

opportunities.title: IIAS - National Library of Israel Individual Fellowship 2028-2029
opportunities.provider: National Library of Israel and Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (IIAS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Tenured humanities scholars from outside Israel can apply for a joint NLI and IIAS fellowship in Jerusalem for 2028-2029.
opportunities.description:
The National Library of Israel (NLI) and the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (IIAS) jointly offer an individual fellowship for the 2028-2029 academic year. The fellow divides their time between the Library and the Institute in Jerusalem.

The fellowship is for projects in Jewish studies, Israel studies, Islamic and Middle Eastern studies, music or the wider humanities, with preference for projects that draw on the Library's special collections. Residencies last 10 months from 1 September, or 5 months from 1 September or 1 February.

It is open to established scholars with tenured posts at institutions outside Israel, so African humanities scholars working on the Middle East, Islam or music can use it for an extended archival research stay.
opportunities.benefits: A fellowship that the organisers describe as generous, plus subsidised accommodation. Amounts are not stated.
requirements: Established scholar with a tenured post at an academic or research institution outside Israel
Not open to postdoctoral researchers
Project in Jewish studies, Israel studies, Islamic and Middle Eastern studies, music or general humanities
Preference for projects using NLI special collections
opportunities.selection_process: A joint NLI and IIAS Academic Committee chooses the fellows and announces decisions within seven months of the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered.
important_dates: Decisions: within seven months of the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The National Library of Israel holds major collections in Judaica, Islam and the Middle East, and music. The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, founded in 1975, hosts fellows and research groups from all disciplines.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the online form linked from the IIAS homepage ("Open Call for IIAS - NLI Individual Fellowship") before 1 December 2026, making sure every part of the application is complete.

opportunities.title: IIAS Open Call for Individual Fellowships 2028-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Tenured academics in any discipline, from Israel or abroad, can apply for a 5 or 10 month residency in Jerusalem in 2028-2029.
opportunities.description:
The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (IIAS) at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem invites tenured scholars from Israel and abroad to apply for individual fellowships for the 2028-2029 academic year. Fellows spend time in residence at the Institute on the Givat Ram campus in Jerusalem working on an innovative research project in any discipline.

Residencies last either 10 months from 1 September or 5 months starting on 1 September or 1 February, within an academic year that runs from 1 September to 30 June. Two or three scholars working on the same project must each apply individually.

The call is aimed at established, tenured academics, so it suits senior African researchers who want an extended research stay at an international institute for advanced study.
opportunities.benefits: Fellows from abroad receive what the Institute describes as a generous fellowship, plus subsidised accommodation. Amounts are not stated.
requirements: Tenured position at an academic research institution (in Israel or abroad)
Not open to postdoctoral researchers
Former IIAS fellows may apply only 10 years after their previous term ended
An innovative research project in any field
documents: Online application form with personal details
Names and contact details of four international experts
Letter of intent of up to 1,000 words describing and justifying the project
Professional CV and full list of publications
opportunities.selection_process: The IIAS Academic Committee reviews applications and announces decisions within seven months of the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered.
important_dates: Decisions: within seven months of the deadline
Residency: from 1 September 2028 (10 or 5 months) or from 1 February 2029 (5 months)
opportunities.about_provider: The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies was founded in 1975 and is based at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. It hosts individual fellows and research groups from all disciplines each year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use the "Apply Here" link on the IIAS homepage to fill in the online form, upload your letter of intent, CV and publication list, and name four international experts, all before midnight on 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The Institute also runs an open call for research groups (5 to 8 core fellows) with the same 1 December 2026 deadline. Contact: iiassecret@savion.huji.ac.il.

opportunities.title: IIAS Open Call for Research Groups 2028-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars from any institution worldwide may propose a 5-8 person research group in residence in Jerusalem in 2028-2029 by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (IIAS) at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem invites scholars to propose Research Groups for the 2028-2029 academic year. A Research Group brings together five to eight core fellows, plus one postdoctoral fellow, to work on a shared question while in residence at the Institute.

Residencies last 10, 5 or 3 months, and the group works on the Edmond J. Safra Campus at Givat Ram in Jerusalem. Fellows coming from abroad receive what the Institute calls a generous fellowship, together with family accommodation.

Scholars from any institution in Israel or abroad may lead or join a proposal, so African researchers can take part as group leaders or members in a collaborative, internationally reviewed research project in any discipline.
opportunities.benefits: A residential fellowship in Jerusalem for each group member; fellows from abroad receive a fellowship stipend and family accommodation. Amounts are not stated on the call page.
requirements: Scholars affiliated with any institution in Israel or abroad may apply
Groups have 5 to 8 core fellows plus one postdoctoral fellow
Residency of 10, 5 or 3 months during the 2028-2029 academic year
Former IIAS fellows may apply only after 10 years since their last fellowship
documents: Pre-proposal with an extended abstract, a list of potential members and key scholars
Full proposal written to the IIAS guidelines and template (short-listed groups)
opportunities.selection_process: The Institute's Academic Committees draw up a short list. Each short-listed proposal is reviewed by at least three external referees. In recent years 40 to 50% of short-listed proposals were accepted.
opportunities.about_provider: The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies is an institute for advanced research hosted by the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. It runs Research Groups alongside individual fellowships and joint programmes such as the NLI-IIAS fellowship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use the online application link on the IIAS Research Groups call page to submit the Initial Form and pre-proposal by midnight on 1 December 2026. Short-listed groups then prepare a full proposal using the Institute's guidelines and template. Questions can go to iiassecret@savion.huji.ac.il.
opportunities.notes: The call and application pages give slightly different decision times (six or seven months), but both point to decisions by the end of July.

opportunities.title: International Excellence Entrance Scholarship 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International high school graduates entering a direct-entry programme with a 90% average and demonstrated leadership can apply for a $25,000 entrance award.
opportunities.description:
The International Excellence Entrance Scholarship is the University of Manitoba's flagship entrance award for international high school students who combine outstanding grades with leadership. It is given to students starting their first year of an undergraduate programme in 2027/28.

Each year the university gives three awards: one worth $25,000 and two worth $10,000. The top award goes to a student entering a direct-entry programme (including University 1) with a very high admission average, while the two smaller awards are open to international applicants who meet the normal admission requirements and show strong leadership.

The University of Manitoba is in Winnipeg, Canada. African secondary school students applying for undergraduate study in Canada can compete for these awards by sending a complete admission and award application before the 1 December deadline.
opportunities.benefits: One award of $25,000 and two awards of $10,000 each, paid towards first-year study.
requirements: International student currently in high school
Applying to a direct-entry programme or University 1 and studying full time (at least 80% course load) in first year

$25,000 award: admission average of at least 90% over five of the listed senior courses (for example Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, English, History, Geography, Music or Visual Arts)
$10,000 awards: meet the minimum admission requirements for University 1 or a direct-entry faculty
Strong leadership and community involvement
documents: University of Manitoba admission application and application fee
One reference letter from a current teacher or principal (translated into English if needed)
Predicted or interim grades and transcripts (grades due by 1 March)
opportunities.selection_process: Shortlisted applicants are ranked first, second and third using both the award application and the admission application.
important_dates: Complete application and documents: by 1 December 2026
Predicted or interim grades: by 1 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Manitoba is a research university in Winnipeg, Canada. Its Financial Aid and Awards office runs entrance scholarships for new domestic and international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission through the University of Manitoba's admissions portal and pay the fee, then complete the award application and arrange the teacher or principal reference letter. All parts must arrive by 1 December.
opportunities.notes: Contact: awards@umanitoba.ca, +1 204 474 9531. The university also lists other entrance awards and international student awards on its financial aid pages.

opportunities.title: International Nieman Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-US journalists with five or more years of full-time experience can apply by 1 December 2026 for a paid year at Harvard.
opportunities.description:
The International Nieman Fellowship gives experienced journalists from outside the United States an academic year at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Fellows audit Harvard classes, take part in Nieman seminars and pursue a study plan of their choice, starting in mid-August 2027.

Fellows receive a stipend of USD 90,000 over nine months, with extra allowances for health insurance and child care. About two dozen journalists are chosen each year across all Nieman fellowships.

The international category is for non-US citizens, so African journalists with at least five years of full-time experience are strongly encouraged to consider it; no degree is required.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 90,000 over nine months, a health insurance supplement of up to USD 6,250 each for the fellow and a spouse and USD 3,750 per child under 18, and a child-care allowance of USD 10,500 (one child aged 12 or under) up to USD 16,750 (four or more).
requirements: Non-US citizen (including those working in the US)
Working journalist with at least five years of full-time media experience (public relations excluded)
Fluent English
No residential fellowship of four months or more in the past five years
No age limit and no degree required
documents: Profile (up to 100 words) and study summary (up to 50 words)
Four samples of published work (print or digital)
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates are judged on their essays, work samples and recommendation letters, and finalists have Zoom interviews.
opportunities.about_provider: The Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard, founded in 1938, runs the oldest mid-career fellowship programme for journalists.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Nieman Foundation's SlideRoom portal by 1 December 2026 and ask your three recommenders to submit by 15 December.
opportunities.notes: Nationals of countries for which the US has suspended J visas are advised to wait unless they hold another passport.

opportunities.title: Jim Leech Mastercard Foundation Fellowship on Entrepreneurship 2027
opportunities.provider: Dunin-Deshpande Queen's Innovation Centre, Queen's University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students and recent graduates of any post-secondary institution in Africa, in any discipline, who can give at least 10 hours a week can apply by 1 December 2026 for the free, fully online eight-month programme.
opportunities.description:
The Jim Leech Mastercard Foundation Fellowship on Entrepreneurship is a free, fully virtual eight-month programme run by the Dunin-Deshpande Queen's Innovation Centre (DDQIC) at Queen's University in Kingston, Canada, with support from the Mastercard Foundation. It helps African students and recent graduates turn business ideas into ventures through online courses, coaching and a pitch competition.

The 2027 cohort runs from January to August 2027 in phases: Explore (January to February), Ignite (March to April) and Launch and Fellowship (May to August), ending with graduation in August. More than 1,000 candidates start the first phase, about 180 finalists progress, and up to 60 are named Fellows. Applications close on 1 December 2026 and results are announced in late December.

Because it is online and open to any discipline at any African post-secondary institution, the programme is an accessible way for young African founders to gain business training, mentors and a chance at seed funding without leaving home.
opportunities.benefits: Free courses, coaching and micro-credentials; a stipend for up to 60 Fellows (stated as CAD 500 on the page and FAQ, and as USD 350 in the timeline); pitch competition prizes of up to CAD 15,000; and seed funding for Fellows who reach the Launch phase.
requirements: Student or recent graduate of a post-secondary institution in Africa
Any field of study
Able to commit at least 10 hours a week for eight months
Able to work in English (mentoring may also be in French)
documents: Online application form (Qualtrics); the page does not list other documents
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates progress through phases based on completing milestones and the quality of their venture pitches: over 1,000 take part in phase one, around 180 finalists go on, and up to 60 are selected as Fellows.
important_dates: Launch and Fellowship: May to August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Dunin-Deshpande Queen's Innovation Centre is the entrepreneurship hub of Queen's University in Kingston, Ontario. It runs venture programmes for students and, with the Mastercard Foundation, this fellowship for African students and graduates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form linked from the programme page before 1 December 2026. Successful applicants join the Explore phase in January 2027 and advance by completing assignments and pitching their ventures.
opportunities.notes: All content is online and self-paced within each phase. Check the page for the confirmed stipend amount, since it states two figures.

opportunities.title: Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships 2027-2029 (TU Delft MSc)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Excellent non-EU applicants aged 35 or under who have applied to a two-year regular TU Delft MSc programme by 1 December 2026 can be considered for one of 16 full scholarships.
opportunities.description:
The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships are TU Delft's main full scholarships for international master's students. For the 2027 intake the university offers 16 awards, two per faculty, to outstanding applicants admitted (or conditionally admitted) to one of its two-year regular MSc programmes in Delft, the Netherlands. Each award runs for the full 24 months of the programme.

The scholarships are paid from a fund left by Justus van Effen, a TU Delft graduate from the 1940s, and his wife Louise. They are intended for applicants who rank roughly in the top 10% of their bachelor's class, although applicants do not need to prove a ranking. The deadline for both the MSc application and the scholarship form is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET, and applicants hear the outcome by email by the end of March 2027.

For African engineers, scientists and designers this is one of the few awards in the Netherlands that covers both full non-EU tuition and a living allowance, so it is worth applying early: the English test result and all admission documents must already be in the MSc application when the scholarship deadline passes.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees for the two years of the MSc (at the statutory or institutional rate that applies to the student's nationality) plus a monthly contribution towards living costs for 24 months; the exact monthly amount is set in the scholarship contract. The second year continues only if the student earns at least 48 of the 60 ECTS credits of year one.
requirements: International applicant without EU citizenship (dual EU/non-EU nationals are not eligible)
Aged 35 or under on 1 September 2027
Admitted or conditionally admitted to a two-year regular TU Delft MSc programme (not a joint programme)
Excellent academic record, as an indication in the top 10% of the bachelor's cohort
Not a TU Delft bachelor's student and no Dutch bachelor's degree
English language certificate uploaded before the deadline unless exempt
Not available for Metropolitan Analysis Design and Engineering, Applied Geophysics, Berlage Post-master, Industrial Ecology or GIMA
documents: Complete MSc application (bachelor's diploma or proof of enrolment, transcript, English test certificate, motivation letter, CV, passport/ID)
Form and reference letter combined into a single PDF
opportunities.selection_process: The Admissions Office first assesses the MSc application. Applicants with a positive assessment are then reviewed by the selection committee of the faculty that runs their programme, which chooses its two scholarship holders on academic excellence and motivation. Results are sent by email by the end of March 2027.
important_dates: Deadline for MSc application and scholarship form: 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET
opportunities.about_provider: TU Delft is the oldest and largest technical university in the Netherlands, with eight faculties covering engineering, applied sciences, architecture and design. Its scholarship programmes are run with the faculties, which select their own candidates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your chosen two-year MSc through TU Delft's online application system and upload every required document, including the English test result, before 1 December 2026. Download the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029 from the scholarships page, combine it with one reference letter in a single PDF and upload it in the same application before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Holders may not combine the award with any other scholarship, and part-time work is discouraged. Programmes that are joint degrees with other universities are excluded.

opportunities.title: Kansas State University International Scholarships (Wildcat Nonresident) for Spring 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International freshmen with a GPA of 3.25 or more starting at K-State in spring 2027 can receive 50 to 100% non-resident tuition discounts.
opportunities.description:
Kansas State University offers international and other non-resident undergraduates a merit-based discount on the non-resident part of their tuition, often called the Wildcat Nonresident award. The level of the award depends on the student's grade point average, and the university lists 1 December as the international application priority date for a spring start.

The discount ranges from 50% to 100% of the non-resident tuition portion, which the university estimates at up to about USD 19,101 a year based on 30 credit hours.

African students with strong secondary school grades who want to start a degree at K-State's Manhattan campus in spring 2027 should apply for admission by the priority date to be considered.
opportunities.benefits: Estimated discounts on the non-resident tuition portion (30 credit hours a year): GPA 3.90+ 100% (about USD 19,101 a year, USD 76,404 over four years); 3.75 to 3.89 80% (about USD 15,281); 3.50 to 3.74 60% (about USD 11,461); 3.25 to 3.49 50% (about USD 9,551).
requirements: Admitted to K-State as a non-Kansas resident (including international students)
Minimum GPA of 3.25 (weighted or unweighted) for the lowest award level
Apply by the international priority date for spring entry
important_dates: International priority date, spring start: 1 December
International priority date, fall start: 1 May
opportunities.about_provider: Kansas State University is a public land-grant research university in Manhattan, Kansas, USA. Its Office of Student Financial Assistance manages the international merit awards.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission to K-State Manhattan by the 1 December priority date for spring entry; awards are based on your GPA. Also complete the K-State Scholarship Network application for other awards.
opportunities.notes: Priority dates are not hard deadlines, but applying by them gives the best chance of an award. Olathe and online campuses use different dates.

opportunities.title: Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellowship 2027/2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fully funded fellowship for accomplished mid-career journalists.

opportunities.title: LIDo Doctoral Training Partnership PhD Studentships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with a strong bioscience, physical science, computing, engineering or maths degree can apply for four-year BBSRC PhDs in London; up to seven places cover overseas fees.
opportunities.description:
The London Interdisciplinary Doctoral Programme (LIDo) is a BBSRC-funded doctoral training partnership that trains bioscience PhD students across a group of London research institutions. It recruits a new cohort each year for four-year PhDs starting in 2027.

There are two routes. In the standard DTP route, students spend their first year doing two four-month research rotations at two partner institutions before choosing a PhD project. In the iCASE route, students apply directly to a named project with an industry partner and spend between 3 and 18 months working with that company.

Projects must fall within the BBSRC's remit, so clinical work, human cancer and non-infectious human disease research are excluded. The programme welcomes students from biological, biomedical, veterinary, physical, computational, engineering and mathematical backgrounds, and some studentships cover full overseas fees, which makes it open to strong African applicants.
opportunities.benefits: Each studentship pays home tuition fees and a stipend at the UKRI London rate of £23,805 per year for four years. Up to seven studentships a year also cover full overseas fees. Visa and relocation costs are not covered.
requirements: First-class or high upper second-class honours degree (or equivalent), or a relevant master's
Degree in a biological, biomedical, veterinary, physical, computational, engineering or mathematical subject
Comfortable with computers and some numeracy (at least GCSE maths or statistics, or equivalent)
If English is not your first language: proof of English, preferably IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in each part
documents: Online LIDo application (sections set out in the application overview PDF)
Evidence of English proficiency where needed
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are shortlisted using LIDo's published guidelines and shortlisted candidates are interviewed on Zoom. iCASE applicants have two interviews, one with a LIDo panel and one with the project supervisors. In the 2025/26 round about 900 people applied and over 300 were interviewed.
opportunities.about_provider: LIDo is a doctoral training partnership of UK universities and research institutes in London, funded by the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC). It offers about 26 studentships a year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the LIDo website and complete the online application before the deadline. You can choose the rotation-based DTP route or apply directly to named iCASE projects. Read the FAQ and shortlisting guidelines first.
opportunities.notes: Only up to seven of the 26 studentships cover overseas fees, so competition for international places is strong. Visa and relocation costs are your own.

opportunities.title: Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LEXS) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Top-10% non-EEA graduates applying to a September-start Leiden master's can apply for a partial tuition scholarship by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS) is a partial tuition-fee scholarship for outstanding non-EEA students admitted to a full-time master's programme at Leiden University in the Netherlands, starting in September. It is awarded for the length of the programme.

About 25 scholarships are given each year and more than a thousand students apply. The award level is set by the university at one of five amounts and cannot be negotiated. The LLM (non-advanced) and the MSc programmes of Leiden Law School are excluded, and February-start programmes do not qualify.

African graduates in the top 10% of their class can apply simply by adding a short motivation letter to their Leiden master's application before the 1 December deadline.
opportunities.benefits: A tuition-fee contribution of €10,000, €15,000, €17,500, €18,500 or €19,000 a year, for the duration of the programme. It is not a full scholarship: recipients from outside the EEA must still prove sufficient funds for their visa.
requirements: Non-EEA/EFTA passport and not eligible for Dutch government student finance (LLM Advanced Studies and MSc International Relations and Diplomacy are open to all nationalities)
Among roughly the top 10% of graduates in your previous relevant degree
Applying for a full-time September-start master's (not the LLM non-advanced or Law School MSc programmes)
Not already holding a Leiden master's, except where a previous master's is required
documents: Leiden master's application with application fee paid
Signed agreement to the LExS terms and conditions (if awarded)
opportunities.selection_process: Faculty selection committees nominate recipients within 10 weeks of the deadline, and all applicants are told the outcome before the end of March.
important_dates: Nominations: within 10 weeks of the deadline
All applicants informed: before end of March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands. Its Student and Educational Affairs scholarships team manages the LExS.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your online application for a Leiden master's programme and pay any fee, then open the Scholarships section of the application screen, select LExS and upload your motivation letter before 1 December 2026. Allow up to three working days to create your application, and apply separately for each programme.
opportunities.notes: Late or incomplete applications are not considered. The LExS cannot be combined with another full external scholarship. Contact: scholarships@sea.leidenuniv.nl.

opportunities.title: Managing the Atom Fellowship 2027-2028 (Harvard Belfer Center)
opportunities.provider: Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs, Harvard Kennedy School
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral students at dissertation stage, recent PhDs, faculty and mid-career professionals from any country with a nuclear policy research project can apply by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Project on Managing the Atom at Harvard Kennedy School's Belfer Center offers ten-month research fellowships in Cambridge, Massachusetts, from 1 September 2027 to 30 June 2028. Fellows work on nuclear policy, with priority given to research on rethinking nuclear deterrence and reducing its dangers, and on resolving regional nuclear proliferation crises.

The fellowship is open to pre-doctoral researchers in the dissertation stage, postdoctoral researchers, university faculty and mid-career professionals from academia, national laboratories, government and industry. Applications opened on 1 October 2026 and close on Tuesday 1 December 2026, with recommendation letters due by 15 December 2026.

The Belfer Center welcomes applicants from all over the world and runs an application mentorship programme for applicants from developing countries and other under-represented groups, which makes this a realistic opportunity for African scholars of nuclear energy, security and diplomacy.
opportunities.benefits: A 10-month stipend of USD 50,000 for pre-doctoral fellows or USD 60,000 for postdoctoral fellows, health insurance, discounted public transport passes, shared office space and modest administrative support. Self-funded scholars can be offered non-stipendiary appointments; applicants must say whether they need full or partial funding.
requirements: Doctoral student in the dissertation stage who has passed general exams, or a recent PhD (or equivalent), or a university faculty member or mid-career professional
A research project with a clear nuclear policy focus
Open to applicants of any nationality
documents: Research statement of 3 to 5 double-spaced pages, including a statement of policy relevance
Writing sample of under 50 double-spaced pages
opportunities.selection_process: The project reviews the research statement, writing sample, CV and references, looking for strong research with policy relevance to its priority areas. Applicants are notified by 15 February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs is Harvard Kennedy School's hub for research and teaching on international security, science, technology and diplomacy. Its Project on Managing the Atom studies nuclear weapons, nuclear energy and non-proliferation policy.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the Belfer Center fellowship portal linked from the fellowship page and submit the research statement, CV, writing sample and (for pre-docs) transcript by 1 December 2026. Enter three recommenders, who must upload their letters by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Applicants from developing countries can ask for help through the Belfer Center's application mentorship programme (contact details on the fellowship page).

opportunities.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholarship at Arizona State University for academically talented young Africans with financial need and a commitment to giving back to their communities.

opportunities.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at UC Berkeley (master's)
opportunities.provider: UC Berkeley Center for African Studies with the Mastercard Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Citizens of African countries who apply to an eligible UC Berkeley master's programme of two years or less in its first application round can be considered for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.
opportunities.description:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of California, Berkeley supports talented young Africans who are admitted to Berkeley master's degrees of two years or less. It is run by Berkeley's Center for African Studies in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation, and the university is recruiting scholars through autumn 2028. The programme is not open to undergraduates or doctoral students.

There is no single scholarship deadline. Applicants apply to one of the eligible Berkeley master's programmes (including the MBA, Master of Journalism, MPH, MPP and several Master of Engineering degrees) by that programme's first-round deadline, which falls between September and early January, mostly in December. Programmes then nominate candidates, who are invited to a supplemental application in February, interviewed online in March and told the final decision in late March or early April.

The programme looks for academic excellence, leadership potential, a commitment to community and an intention to return to Africa, and gives priority to applicants with an African first degree, no earlier postgraduate degree and no previous Mastercard Foundation support.
opportunities.benefits: The scholarship supports the full cost of a Berkeley master's degree for selected scholars; the pages read do not list amounts. African applicants can also request a waiver of the Berkeley graduate application fee.
requirements: Citizen of an African country (Africans displaced or with refugee status within Africa included)
Not a dual citizen, asylee, refugee or permanent resident of the US, Canada, the UK or the EU
Applying to an eligible UC Berkeley master's programme of two years or less, in its first application round (before January)
Academic excellence and leadership potential
Commitment to community and intention to return to Africa
Priority for applicants with an African undergraduate degree and no previous postgraduate degree
documents: UC Berkeley graduate application with the documents required by the chosen programme
Supplemental Mastercard Foundation Scholars application (by invitation, in February)
opportunities.selection_process: Graduate programmes nominate admitted candidates; nominees complete a supplemental application in February and an online interview in March, and final decisions are made in late March or early April. There are always more qualified candidates than places.
important_dates: Programme deadlines: September to early January, most in December (first round only)
Fee-waiver application: by 15 November (passed for this cycle)
Final decisions: late March or early April
opportunities.about_provider: The University of California, Berkeley is a leading public research university in California. Its Center for African Studies runs the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, part of the Mastercard Foundation's network of partner universities that fund African students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose an eligible master's programme and submit the UC Berkeley graduate application by that programme's first-round deadline. If nominated, you will be invited to complete the Scholars Program supplemental application and an online interview. Questions go to mcfs.programinfo@berkeley.edu.
opportunities.notes: Only master's programmes of two years or less qualify; bachelor's, doctoral, concurrent and dual degrees do not. You must apply in your programme's first round. The pages say there are always more strong candidates than places, and the programme recruits through fall 2028. Eligibility questions: mcfs.programinfo@berkeley.edu.

opportunities.title: Miami University Presidential Fellows Program (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: High-achieving first-year applicants for fall 2027 with SAT or ACT scores can apply by 1 December for one of 15 full rides.
opportunities.description:
The Presidential Fellows Program is Miami University's top scholarship for first-year students entering in fall 2027. Each year 15 Fellows are chosen and receive a full-ride award for four years at the university in Oxford, Ohio, together with an academic enrichment fund.

Applicants show their interest on the admission application and submit everything by the firm 1 December deadline. Semi-finalists then submit extra materials, and finalists are invited to interviews on campus in February.

The page does not limit nationality, so high-achieving African secondary school students applying to Miami can be considered, but they must self-report ACT or SAT scores, which are required for fall 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition and fees for eight semesters (while keeping a 3.50 GPA), housing up to the cost of a standard double room, the Diplomat Standard meal plan with USD 500 Dining Dollars, and an academic enrichment fund of up to USD 5,000. Books, computers, health insurance, study-abroad fees and deposits are not covered.
requirements: Indicate interest in the programme on the admission application
Self-reported ACT or SAT scores (required for fall 2027)
Keep a cumulative GPA of 3.50 to renew the award
All materials submitted by 1 December
documents: Admission application and materials through the application status page
opportunities.selection_process: Selection is based on the full admission application, test scores, semi-finalist supplemental materials and an on-campus finalist interview in February. Choices are finalised within two weeks after the interviews.
opportunities.about_provider: Miami University is a public research university founded in 1809 in Oxford, Ohio, known for its strong undergraduate teaching.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Miami for fall 2027, mark your interest in the Presidential Fellows Program and complete all materials through the application status page by 1 December. Contact PresidentialFellows@MiamiOH.edu with questions.

opportunities.title: Montana State University Presidential Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Incoming first-year students with an unweighted high-school GPA of at least 3.7 who are fully admitted to Montana State University can apply by 1 December 2026 for a four-year tuition waiver and stipend.
opportunities.description:
The Presidential Scholarship is Montana State University's most prestigious academic award for new undergraduates. Run through the Honors College in Bozeman, Montana, it supports first-year students who start in 2027 for up to eight semesters of study, and both Montana residents and non-residents can apply.

The 2027 Presidential Scholarship is open now and closes at midnight Mountain Standard Time on 1 December 2026. Applicants must already be accepted to MSU with full (not conditional) admission and must submit the general scholarships application and a separate Presidential application with recommendations.

Recipients usually have an unweighted GPA of 3.9 or higher and rank in the top 3% of their class, and they act as ambassadors for the university through leadership and service. International students who are not selected are still considered automatically for MSU's international merit scholarship of USD 5,000 to USD 12,000 a year.
opportunities.benefits: A yearly tuition waiver, a stipend (amount not stated on the page) and priority course registration for up to eight semesters. Renewal requires a 3.5 MSU GPA and an average of 16 MSU credits per semester. Separately, international undergraduates with a GPA of 2.5 or higher and full admission are considered automatically for an international merit scholarship of USD 5,000 to USD 12,000 a year.
requirements: Incoming first-time first-year student (fewer than 12 university credits)
Unweighted high-school GPA of 3.7 or higher on a 4.0 scale
Full (not conditional) admission to Montana State University
Evidence of leadership and service
documents: General Scholarships Application in the Cat$cholarships portal
Recommendations from one high-school counselor and two other recommenders, uploaded through the portal
opportunities.selection_process: The Honors College reviews applications for academic excellence, leadership and service, and fit with the Honors College. Recommendations are submitted through the portal only; mail and email are not accepted.
opportunities.about_provider: Montana State University is a public land-grant research university in Bozeman, Montana. Its Honors College offers smaller classes and enrichment for high-achieving undergraduates and manages the Presidential Scholarship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply and be accepted to MSU, then claim your NetID. Sign in to the Cat$cholarships portal, submit the General Scholarships Application, then complete the Presidential Scholarship application and invite your counselor and two recommenders before midnight MST on 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Applicants with 12 or more university credits are not eligible. The international merit scholarship is not given to conditionally admitted students.

opportunities.title: National Geographic Society Grants: The Human Thread (Storytelling) RFP
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Storytellers aged 18 or over anywhere may apply online for funding for a human-experience storytelling project by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The National Geographic Society is accepting proposals under a request for proposals called "The Human Thread", which funds storytelling projects that shed light on the wide range of human experience. The opportunity is supported by Lilly Endowment Inc. and is listed among the Society's current funding calls with a closing date of 1 December 2026.

National Geographic grants back explorers, storytellers, educators and scientists, and each request for proposals sets its own focus and budget. Projects funded under this call must start at least six months after the deadline, so successful work would begin from mid-2027 onwards.

For African photographers, filmmakers, writers and other storytellers, this is a chance to obtain funding and recognition from one of the world's best-known organisations for exploration and storytelling. Applications are made online only, through the Society's funding portal.
opportunities.benefits: Grant funding for a storytelling project. The budget is set per request for proposals; the amount for this call is given on the RFP page in the funding portal, not on the main grants page.
requirements: Applicants must be at least 18 years old
The project must start at least six months after the 1 December 2026 deadline
An applicant may lead only one National Geographic project at a time
Final reports on any earlier National Geographic Society grants must have been submitted
The project must match the focus of The Human Thread request for proposals
documents: Online application in the National Geographic Society Funding Portal
Project budget following the Society's budget guidelines
opportunities.selection_process: Proposals are reviewed by the Society against the focus of the request for proposals; the grants page does not describe the stages in more detail.
important_dates: Earliest project start: six months after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The National Geographic Society is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) organisation founded in 1888. According to its grants page it has awarded more than 16,000 grants to explorers, scientists, educators and storytellers worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the National Geographic Society Funding Portal (funding.nationalgeographic.org), open The Human Thread request for proposals and submit your application there before 1 December 2026. Applications sent by email or post are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: The detailed RFP page sits behind the portal login, so read it there for the exact focus, budget limit and any geographic rules before you apply.

opportunities.title: Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Two-year funded postdoctoral fellowship at Dartmouth for recent PhDs doing computational research in any discipline.

opportunities.title: Next Asia Policy Lab Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhDs working on contemporary Asia in one of SNAPL's four tracks can apply for a two-year Stanford postdoc.
opportunities.description:
The Stanford Next Asia Policy Lab (SNAPL), directed by Professor Gi-Wook Shin and housed at APARC, is recruiting two postdoctoral fellows for 2027-2029. Each fellow spends two years in residence at Stanford from fall quarter 2027, leads a thematic research group and helps with student programmes.

The fellowships are organised around four tracks: talent flows and development; nationalism and racism; US-Asia relations; and democratic crisis and reform, all with a focus on contemporary Asia.

No nationality rule is stated, so African scholars whose work on migration, race, democracy or great-power relations connects with Asia can apply for two years of salaried research at Stanford.
opportunities.benefits: Annual salary of $83,000 plus benefits for two years, with a possible extension.
requirements: PhD received within three years of the fellowship start date
Dissertation approved for conferral by 30 June 2027 and certified by 31 August 2027
Research fitting one of the four SNAPL tracks on contemporary Asia
Residence at APARC for the fellowship
documents: Formal letter of request setting out research plans and solo and co-authored publications
Academic CV of up to two pages with a publication list
Three recommendation letters emailed to SNAPLcontact@stanford.edu
opportunities.about_provider: SNAPL is a research lab at Stanford's Walter H. Shorenstein Asia-Pacific Research Center (APARC), part of the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies. It studies policy challenges facing Asia and the United States.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the online Qualtrics application linked from the SNAPL fellowships page with your letter of request and CV, and have three referees email letters to SNAPLcontact@stanford.edu by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: SNAPL also offers a one-year STINT-SNAPL postdoc (same deadline) and visiting fellowships with a 1 March 2027 deadline. Contact: Natalia Slavney, SNAPLcontact@stanford.edu.

opportunities.title: Notre Dame College of Arts and Letters Provost's Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars who earned a doctorate within three years of the cohort start date can apply by 1 December 2026 for a two-year salaried postdoctoral fellowship, with visa support for international fellows.
opportunities.description:
The University of Notre Dame's Provost's Postdoctoral Fellowship Program in the College of Arts and Letters is designed to bring new postdoctoral researchers to the university in Notre Dame, Indiana. The current call is for the cohort starting in 2027.

Applicants propose their research and may name a primary mentor or co-mentors at Notre Dame, but the university asks applicants not to contact potential host faculty before applying. Doctorates must be recent, with some flexibility for parental or family leave.

Notre Dame says it plans to support visas for fellows, so researchers from African countries with a recent doctorate in the humanities, arts or social sciences can apply.
requirements: Doctorate from an accredited institution received within three years of the cohort's start date (extensions for recent parental or FMLA leave)
ABD applicants may apply if they will defend by June before the start
Master's-only applicants are not eligible
Current Notre Dame students, graduates and fellows are not eligible
documents: Cover letter of up to 4 pages (double-spaced, 12 pt) on your research path and motivation
Research statement of up to 5 pages on achievements and proposed projects, optionally naming mentors
Writing sample of up to 10,000 words
At least three recommendation letters submitted through Interfolio
opportunities.selection_process: Applications without all letters are not reviewed. Finalists are interviewed as time allows, and decisions are made by 1 March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Notre Dame is a private research university in Indiana, USA. Its College of Arts and Letters runs the Provost's Postdoctoral Fellowship Program to attract early-career scholars.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the programme's Interfolio posting (apply.interfolio.com/190347), uploading your cover letter, research statement and writing sample and requesting at least three letters through Interfolio Dossier. Do not ask referees to email letters, and do not contact host faculty beforehand.
opportunities.notes: Applicants are responsible for making sure every letter arrives by the deadline. Contact: alprovostpostdocs@nd.edu, +1 574 631 7085.

opportunities.title: Public Humanities special issue: African American Roots and Routes (call for articles)
opportunities.provider: Public Humanities journal (Cambridge University Press), guest editor Neal A. Lester
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars can propose chapters for an edited Cambridge volume on African American roots and routes.
opportunities.description:
The open-access journal Public Humanities, published by Cambridge University Press, plans a special issue on "African American Roots and Routes", guest edited by Neal A. Lester of Arizona State University. The issue invites articles on African American beginnings and their routes, written in accessible language for a wide readership.

Authors first send a 300-word abstract with a proposed title to the guest editor. Full articles of no more than 6,500 words (excluding abstract, notes and bibliography) then go through the journal's peer-review system and appear digitally in open access.

Scholars of the African diaspora, including African researchers working on transatlantic histories and cultures, can contribute.
requirements: Article on African American beginnings, roots or routes
Accessible writing for a broad public readership
Maximum 6,500 words excluding abstract, footnotes and bibliography
documents: 300-word abstract with proposed title (to the guest editor)
Full article submitted through the Public Humanities ScholarOne site (mc.manuscriptcentral.com/pubhum)
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email a 300-word abstract and proposed title to guest editor Neal A. Lester (neal.lester@asu.edu) by 1 December 2026, then submit the full article through the Public Humanities online peer-review system.

opportunities.title: RAND Graduate Student Summer Associate Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time doctoral or professional-degree students with at least two years of graduate study (and some engineering, computing and operations research master's students) who will live in the US during summer 2027 can apply by 1 December 2026 for a paid 12-week research placement at RAND.
opportunities.description:
RAND's Graduate Student Summer Associate Program places advanced graduate students on real, funded RAND research projects for 12 weeks (60 working days) in summer 2027. Each summer associate is matched with a project and a mentor and produces research that feeds into RAND's policy work.

Associates can work in person at RAND's offices in Santa Monica, Washington DC, Pittsburgh or Boston, or remotely from home, but they must live in the United States for the whole assignment. Tentative start dates are 24 May and 14 June 2027, and the placement must be completed between May and October.

US citizenship is not required except for particular projects, so international students, including Africans studying at US universities or able to be in the US for the summer, can apply. The programme is highly selective: RAND receives more than 600 applications a year and expects about 15 to 20 placements for 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Approximately USD 15,000 (before taxes) for the 12-week placement, paid every two weeks. Relocation costs are not provided. RAND supplies documentation to a student's international office where work authorisation is needed.
requirements: Full-time graduate student with at least two years of doctoral or professional-degree study (PhD, EdD, DrPH, JD, MD, etc.)
Enrolled full-time in spring and fall 2027 and not graduating before December 2027
Master's students considered only in engineering, computer or information science and operations research
Undergraduates and postdocs are not eligible
Must live in the United States for the entire assignment; international students planning to be in the US in summer 2027 may apply
Work authorisation for the position (RAND provides supporting documents)
Only one application per person
documents: Online application with university, department and degree details
Answers to three short questions (up to 250 words each)
Contact details for two recommenders (letters requested only after interview)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications receive a holistic review. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed between early February and March 2027, and offers are usually made in mid-to-late March. Fewer than 10% of applicants receive offers.
important_dates: Tentative start dates: 24 May and 14 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: RAND is a nonprofit, nonpartisan research organisation that works on public policy challenges. It has offices across the United States as well as in Europe and Australia.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'Apply Now' link on RAND's Summer Associate page, which leads to RAND's Workday careers site. Submit your CV, cover letter and short answers and name two recommenders. Students in disciplines not listed among RAND's priorities can email Summer_Director@rand.org first.
opportunities.notes: Extra applications from the same person are withdrawn at random, so submit only one. Check the priority disciplines listed for 2027 before applying.

opportunities.title: Salzburg Global Seminar Internship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Internship at Schloss Leopoldskron in Salzburg for senior undergraduates, graduate students and young professionals aged 18+, with room, board, travel and insurance covered in kind.
opportunities.description:
Salzburg Global Seminar has opened its call for 2027 internships. Interns join its teams either at Schloss Leopoldskron in Salzburg, Austria, or in its Washington, D.C. office, and support its international programmes and operations.

In Salzburg the roles include Communications, Development, Library and Program internships; in Washington there are Donor Communications, Advancement and Program internships. Salzburg internships can last at most 90 days because of Austrian labour and visa rules, while D.C. internships usually last three to four months. The working language is English, and German is not required.

Salzburg internships are unpaid but include free room and board at the Schloss, travel and insurance, so they are a realistic way for African students and graduates to gain experience in an international non-profit in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Salzburg: unpaid, but interns receive room and board at Schloss Leopoldskron, travel to and from Salzburg, accident and health insurance (excluding pre-existing conditions, dental and glasses) and help with visa processing; a €100 security deposit is refunded if there is no damage, and visa fees are paid by the intern. Washington, D.C.: a stipend (amount not stated).
requirements: At least 18 years old
Program and Development internships in Salzburg are open to bachelor's students; Communications and Library need a completed relevant degree
Non-EU citizens need a visa for Salzburg (support is given)
D.C. roles require US work authorisation
English is the working language; German not needed
documents: Assignments where a role requires them
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed only during an open call, and the organisation describes the process as highly competitive. Spontaneous applications are not reviewed and individual questions about applications are not answered.
opportunities.about_provider: Salzburg Global Seminar is an independent non-profit founded in 1947, with offices in Salzburg and Washington, D.C. It has run programmes involving participants from more than 170 countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on Salzburg Global's online application platform through the current openings linked from the internships page, and apply to the role(s) you want with your CV, cover letter and any required assignment. You may apply for more than one role, but the organisation advises focusing.
opportunities.notes: Academic credit can be arranged. Rejected applicants may reapply in a later call. Contact: info@SalzburgGlobal.org.

opportunities.title: Shorenstein Postdoctoral Fellowship on Contemporary Asia 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhDs (within three years) researching contemporary Asia can apply for a 10-month Stanford postdoc.
opportunities.description:
Stanford's Walter H. Shorenstein Asia-Pacific Research Center (APARC) offers postdoctoral fellowships for junior scholars researching contemporary Asia. Fellows spend a 10-month appointment in residence at Stanford, starting in the fall quarter of 2027, turning their research into a publishable product such as a book or articles.

Projects may focus on political, economic or social change in Northeast, Southeast or South Asia, or on international relations and political economy in the Asia-Pacific. APARC normally appoints two such fellows each year.

There is no stated nationality restriction, so African scholars with a recent PhD on Asia, or on Africa-Asia relations within the region's political economy, can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Pay based on an annual rate of $83,000, prorated for the 10-month appointment, plus up to $3,000 for research expenses.
requirements: PhD awarded no more than three years before the fellowship starts
Degree conferred and certified by 30 June 2027 (proof due by 31 August 2027)
Research on contemporary Asia-Pacific politics, economy, society or international relations
Residence at Stanford for the full appointment
documents: Research statement of up to five double-spaced pages describing the project and its publishable output
Three recommendation letters emailed as PDFs to shorensteinfellowships@stanford.edu
important_dates: Deadline for all materials including letters: 1 December 2026 (Pacific Time)
opportunities.about_provider: APARC is part of Stanford's Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies and is based in Encina Hall. It runs research programmes and fellowships on the politics, economics and societies of the Asia-Pacific.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in APARC's online Qualtrics form, upload your CV and research statement as PDFs and submit, then have three referees email their letters to shorensteinfellowships@stanford.edu before the deadline. You receive a confirmation email once every part, including all three letters, has arrived.
opportunities.notes: Stanford is closed from 21 December 2026 to 1 January 2027, so replies may be slow then. Contact: Kristen Lee, shorensteinfellowships@stanford.edu.

opportunities.title: TU Delft Faculty Scholarship: MSc Electrical Engineering (Microelectronics) 2027
opportunities.provider: Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), Faculty of EEMCS
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants with a bachelor's grade average of at least 80% of the maximum who apply to the MSc Electrical Engineering (Microelectronics track) by 1 December 2026 can win one of up to two partial tuition scholarships.
opportunities.description:
TU Delft's Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) offers up to two partial scholarships to excellent international students who start the two-year MSc in Electrical Engineering, track Microelectronics, in September 2027. The award is given through the faculty's Microelectronics department, where the scholarship holder also carries out the master's thesis.

The scholarship reduces the tuition fee (at the statutory or institutional rate that applies to the student) and can be renewed for the second year if the student keeps an average grade of 8.0 out of 10 in year one. An outstanding thesis project (grade 9 or higher) can lead to the offer of a PhD position in the department.

The award suits African electrical and electronic engineering graduates with very strong grades who want to specialise in chip design, circuits and microsystems. Because it is partial, applicants should plan other funding for living costs or apply for the Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship at the same time.
opportunities.benefits: A partial waiver of the tuition fee for year one (at the statutory or institutional rate), renewable for year two if the student keeps an average grade of 8.0 (80%). No monthly allowance is stated.
requirements: International applicant
Admitted or conditionally admitted to the two-year MSc Electrical Engineering, track Microelectronics
Bachelor's degree from a well-regarded university outside the Netherlands
Grade average of at least 80% of the maximum of the grading scale
English language certificate uploaded before the deadline unless exempt
documents: Complete MSc application (diploma or proof of enrolment, transcript, English test certificate, motivation letter, CV, ID)
opportunities.selection_process: After the Admissions Office gives a positive assessment of the MSc application, the Microelectronics department selects up to two scholarship holders on academic excellence. Results are sent by email by the end of March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: TU Delft is the largest technical university in the Netherlands. Its Faculty of EEMCS hosts the Microelectronics department, which works on integrated circuits, sensors and microsystems.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for the MSc Electrical Engineering (Microelectronics track) through TU Delft's online application system with all documents, including your English test result, before 1 December 2026. Add the scholarship application form and one reference letter to the same application before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: The master's thesis must be done in the Microelectronics department; a thesis grade of 9 or higher can lead to a PhD offer.

opportunities.title: The Black Scholar Special Issue: Adjacency: Black Alternatives
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars and writers anywhere may submit articles or shorter pieces on alternative cultural expressions of Blackness by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Black Scholar, a long-running journal of Black studies and research, has opened a call for contributions to a themed special issue titled "Adjacency: Black Alternatives". The issue looks at less familiar, alternative ways in which Blackness is expressed in culture, with suggested themes that include neurodivergence, speculative fiction, artificial intelligence and sustainability.

The special issue is guided by three guest editors, Joshua K Reason, Alexandria C. Cunningham and Suzanne Nimoh, and is planned to appear as issue 57.4 in Winter 2027. It accepts both full peer-reviewed research articles and shorter pieces such as essays, roundtables and interviews.

For African scholars, writers and researchers working on Black culture, the diaspora, technology or futures thinking, this is a chance to publish in an established international journal of Black studies. Submission is online and open to authors anywhere; there is no fee or travel involved.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in a themed special issue (issue 57.4, Winter 2027) of The Black Scholar after peer review. The call does not mention any payment or fee.
requirements: Peer-reviewed research articles of 5,000 to 7,500 words
Essays, roundtables and interviews of 4,000 to 5,000 words, endnotes included
Work must fit the special issue theme of alternative cultural expressions of Blackness
Authors must follow the journal's submission guidelines
Authors must obtain permission for any third-party material they reproduce
documents: Manuscript prepared under The Black Scholar's submission guidelines
Permissions for any third-party material used
opportunities.selection_process: Full articles go through the journal's peer review; the guest editors shape the issue around the stated theme.
opportunities.about_provider: The Black Scholar describes itself as a journal of Black studies and research. It is published by Taylor & Francis and run by an editorial team that includes a managing editor named on its website.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your manuscript according to the journal's guidelines on theblackscholar.org, then submit it through the journal's Taylor & Francis submission page (tandfonline.com/journals/rtbs20) by 1 December 2026, indicating that it is for the "Adjacency: Black Alternatives" special issue.
opportunities.notes: Word limits include endnotes for the shorter formats. The call was posted on 17 July 2026.

opportunities.title: UBC Beyond Tomorrow Scholars Award 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Black Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons with financial need entering a UBC degree can apply by 1 December.
opportunities.description:
The Beyond Tomorrow Scholars Award is a University of British Columbia entrance award for students who self-identify as Black, including African, African-American, African-Canadian and Afro-Caribbean students, and who show strong academics and financial need. It applies to direct-entry undergraduate programmes at UBC Vancouver and UBC Okanagan.

Applicants must apply to UBC and submit the separate entrance award application by 1 December. UBC contacts recipients by 15 May, and awards apply only to the student's first-choice campus and degree.

The award is restricted to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons, so it fits Black and African-heritage students already living in Canada, not international applicants. International students should look instead at UBC's International Scholars Program and international entrance scholarships.
opportunities.benefits: An entrance award for undergraduate study at UBC; the page does not state the amount or duration.
requirements: Self-identify as Black (African, African-American, African-Canadian or Afro-Caribbean)
Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person
Strong academic record meeting UBC admission requirements
Demonstrated financial need
Entering from high school or transferring from post-secondary, with no previous degree
documents: Parent/Guardian Form (if in high school within the past 48 months)
important_dates: UBC application and award application: by 1 December
opportunities.about_provider: The University of British Columbia is one of Canada's leading research universities, with campuses in Vancouver and Kelowna (Okanagan). It reports spending more than CAD 35 million a year on awards for international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to UBC through its online application, then complete the 2027 entrance awards application on UBC's scholarship portal by 1 December.

opportunities.title: UZH International Excellence Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International Master's applicants.

opportunities.title: University of Missouri International Honors and Merit Scholarships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year students admitted to on-campus study at Mizzou for fall 2027 who complete their application by 1 December 2026 are considered for USD 10,000 or USD 20,000 a year towards non-resident tuition.
opportunities.description:
The University of Missouri in Columbia, Missouri, gives international first-year students two main merit awards for the 2027-28 academic year: the International Honors Scholarship of USD 20,000 a year and the International Merit Scholarship of USD 10,000 a year. Both are applied to the non-resident part of tuition.

To be considered for these and the university's other freshman scholarships, fall 2027 applicants must apply and send all required application materials by 1 December 2026. Offers are sent by late January. Students then use the Mizzou Scholarship Application Portal to be matched with general and departmental scholarships, and admitted students can also apply to the Honors College.

The awards make a large public research university more affordable for African students, but they are not combinable with most other Mizzou scholarships and do not cover the whole cost of attendance, so applicants should plan the rest of their budget.
opportunities.benefits: International Honors Scholarship: USD 20,000 per year. International Merit Scholarship: USD 10,000 per year. Both reduce the non-resident portion of tuition and generally cannot be combined with other Mizzou awards. Transfer students can receive USD 20,000 (3.90 GPA) or USD 10,000 (3.00 GPA) with 24 or more transferable credit hours.
requirements: International degree-seeking student admitted for on-campus study (not online)
Fall 2027 first-year applicant with all application materials submitted by 1 December 2026
Proof of English proficiency
SAT or ACT scores preferred for the honors and merit awards
Stamps Scholarship not open to international applicants living outside the US (in-person interview required)
documents: Completed Mizzou admission application with all required materials
Award letter from any government or outside sponsor, sent to the MU Sponsored Student Program
opportunities.selection_process: Admitted international applicants are reviewed holistically for the honors and merit awards. General and departmental scholarships are matched through questions in the Mizzou Scholarship Application Portal. Offers are sent by late January 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Missouri is the flagship public research university of the state of Missouri, founded in 1839 and based in Columbia. It offers more than 300 degree programmes and has an Honors College for high-achieving students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission through the Mizzou application site and send all required materials by 1 December 2026. After applying, open the Mizzou Scholarship Application Portal from your Application Status Page and answer its questions to be considered for further scholarships; the Honors College application also appears on the Status Page once you are admitted.
opportunities.notes: Scholarships apply only to the non-resident portion of tuition. Global Black & Gold awards require a parent who graduated from Mizzou.

opportunities.title: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Global Excellence Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to UNL can be considered for USD 15,000 a year by applying by 1 December 2026 for Spring 2027 or by 1 May 2027 for Fall 2027.

opportunities.title: Vanderbilt Ingram Scholars Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: First-year applicants to Vanderbilt for fall 2027, including international applicants, can apply for the Ingram Scholarship through MyAppVU by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Ingram Scholars Program at Vanderbilt University in Nashville, Tennessee, is a full-tuition merit scholarship for students who combine academic strength with a deep commitment to civic service. It was created in 1993 by E. Bronson Ingram and is run by Vanderbilt's Office of Student Financial Aid and Scholarships.

Ingram Scholars do about 20 hours of community service a month and design a summer service project after their second year, for which they receive extra funding. The scholarship is renewed each year to graduation as long as scholars keep a 3.0 GPA and meet the service requirements. First-year applicants for fall 2027 must submit the Ingram application electronically through their MyAppVU account by 1 December 2026.

Vanderbilt's scholarship FAQ confirms that international applicants can receive any of its merit scholarships, so this is a realistic route for African students with strong service records to study at a leading US university with tuition, fees and housing paid.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition, all required fees and the value of on-campus housing each year, renewable to graduation; a stipend for a summer service project; and additional need-based aid if a student's need exceeds full tuition.
requirements: Applicant for first-year admission to Vanderbilt for fall 2027 (transfer students not eligible)
International applicants eligible for Vanderbilt merit scholarships
Strong record of civic-minded service, entrepreneurial spirit, character and leadership
Ingram application submitted via MyAppVU by 1 December 2026
To renew: 3.0 GPA and about 20 hours of service a month
opportunities.selection_process: The selection committee reviews the Ingram application together with the full admission file and invites finalists to interview. Selection looks for civic-minded service, entrepreneurial spirit, strength of character and leadership potential.
important_dates: Current first-year students: application mid-January 2027, due 28 February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Vanderbilt University is a private research university in Nashville, Tennessee, founded in 1873. Its signature merit scholarships, including the Ingram and Cornelius Vanderbilt scholarships, go to about 1% of first-year applicants.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Vanderbilt for first-year admission, then complete the Ingram Scholarship application in your MyAppVU account before 1 December 2026. Finalists are invited to interview with the selection committee.
opportunities.notes: Vanderbilt is test-optional for fall 2027 applicants. The Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship has the same 1 December 2026 deadline.
