opportunities.description:
Besides its flagship Cornelius Vanderbilt and Ingram scholarships, Vanderbilt University in Nashville, Tennessee, gives a set of additional merit awards to first-year students. They include the Carell Family Scholarship, the Clark Scholars Program for engineering students and the Curb Leadership Scholarship, plus other merit awards worth from USD 8,000 a year.

There is no separate form for these awards: students are considered when they submit the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship application, which is due on 1 December 2026 for fall 2027 entry. Vanderbilt confirms that international applicants can receive any of its merit scholarships, and most winners hear in late March.

For African students aiming at a top US university, these awards add to Vanderbilt's other aid and can make the cost of study much lower.
opportunities.benefits: Carell Family Scholarship: full tuition and fees. Clark Scholars Program: USD 20,000 per year plus support for a summer immersive experience. Curb Leadership Scholarship: USD 8,000. Other additional merit awards start from USD 8,000 per year (limited number).

International applicants are eligible

Curb: creative leadership that has changed a community
Submit the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship application by 1 December 2026

opportunities.about_provider: Vanderbilt University is a private research university in Nashville, Tennessee, USA. It offers several merit scholarship programmes to first-year undergraduates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Vanderbilt for fall 2027 and complete the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship application by 1 December 2026; no other form is needed for the Carell, Clark or Curb awards.
opportunities.notes: The scholarships pages differ on financial need: the Carell and Clark descriptions mention need, while the FAQ says need is not a factor in merit selection. Vanderbilt's Chancellor's Scholarship ends for fall 2027 applicants.

opportunities.title: Wageningen Africa Scholarship Programme (ASP) MSc 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: African citizens with a first-class bachelor's (GPA 80%+) who submit a complete WUR MSc application by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Africa Scholarship Programme (ASP) at Wageningen University & Research supports talented African students to complete a two-year MSc at Wageningen in the Netherlands, starting in September 2027, as part of the university's commitment to capacity building in Africa.

There is no separate scholarship form: applicants are assessed if they submit a complete MSc application before 1 December 2026, already hold their bachelor's degree and have their English test results by that date. The WU Scholarship Selection Committee then selects finalists, and the final awards are decided by lottery.

The scholarship covers tuition, living costs and travel for the full 24 months, making it one of the most complete master's awards in the Netherlands for African citizens in life sciences, agriculture, food and environment.
opportunities.benefits: Travel to and from the Netherlands, a living allowance for 24 months, tuition fees for 24 months, visa costs and health insurance. The living allowance amount is not stated.
requirements: Citizen of an African country
Complete application to a WUR MSc programme submitted before 1 December 2026, with unconditional admission
Bachelor's degree completed before 1 December 2026 with first-class honours and a GPA of 80% or higher
English test results meeting WUR's requirements available before 1 December 2026
Preference for applicants without a master's degree
opportunities.selection_process: The WU Scholarship Selection Committee assesses eligible applicants and shortlists candidates, who are informed around March-April 2027. A lottery among the final candidates decides who receives the award on 7 April 2027; the rest are placed on a waiting list.
opportunities.about_provider: Wageningen University & Research (WUR) in the Netherlands is a leading university for agriculture, food, life sciences and the environment. It offers several scholarships to attract talented international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit a complete application for your chosen WUR MSc programme before 1 December 2026, including your bachelor's diploma and English test results; starting an application without submitting it does not count. No separate scholarship form is mentioned for the ASP.
opportunities.notes: Book your English test early, since results must be available before the deadline. WUR's Anne van den Ban Fund also supports students from developing countries with the same 1 December deadline.

opportunities.title: Wageningen Anne van den Ban Fund MSc Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals of ABF-listed lower-income countries, including many in Africa, who complete a Wageningen MSc application by 1 December 2026 can be selected.
opportunities.description:
The Anne van den Ban Fund (ABF) is a scholarship managed by the University Fund Wageningen that helps talented students from low- and lower-middle-income countries take a master's degree at Wageningen University & Research in the Netherlands. It is awarded together with the WU Fellowship Programme for MSc programmes starting in September 2027.

There is no separate scholarship form. Students who apply for a Wageningen MSc programme before 1 December 2026, with a complete application, are considered and the best candidates are invited. The award can be full or partial and is designed to cover the whole two-year programme.

Wageningen is among the world's leading universities in agriculture, food, nutrition and environmental sciences, so the scholarship is especially relevant for African students who want to build careers in food security, rural development, climate and natural resources. Many African countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Uganda, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe, are on the eligible list.
opportunities.benefits: A full or partial scholarship that can cover travel, a living allowance for 24 months, tuition fees for 24 months, and visa and health insurance costs.
requirements: Nationality of a country on the ABF list of low- and lower-middle-income countries (many African countries included)
Not a citizen of an EU country
Unconditional admission to a Wageningen MSc programme starting September 2027
Complete MSc application submitted before 1 December 2026, including English test results and the bachelor's diploma
opportunities.selection_process: Selection is competitive and by invitation: eligible applicants who completed their MSc application in time are assessed and the strongest are invited. Admission to the MSc does not guarantee an award.
important_dates: MSc application deadline for consideration: 1 December 2026
Results to selected candidates: May 2027 (exact date to be announced)
opportunities.about_provider: Wageningen University & Research is a Dutch university and research institute specialising in life sciences, agriculture, food and the environment. The University Fund Wageningen raises and manages funds such as the Anne van den Ban Fund to support students from lower-income countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online for a Wageningen MSc programme before 1 December 2026 and make sure the file is complete, with your English test results and bachelor's diploma. You do not fill in a separate ABF form; candidates are selected from the admitted applicants and invited.
opportunities.notes: Wageningen also lists the Africa Scholarship Programme (African citizens, First Class Honours and 80% GPA, deadline 1 December 2026, awarded by lottery with offers on 7 April 2027) and the NL Scholarship (EUR 5,000) on the same scholarships page.

opportunities.title: CISAC Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.provider: Stanford University, Center for International Security and Cooperation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Pre-doctoral, postdoctoral and early-career scholars of any nationality working on international security topics, with degree rules that vary by track.
opportunities.description:
Stanford's Center for International Security and Cooperation (CISAC) offers fellowships for scholars who want to spend an academic year, or in some cases two, researching an international security issue at Stanford. The 2027-2028 application is now open.

Tracks include AI and the laws of armed conflict, AI in strategic stability, the geopolitics of AI, the Indo-Pacific, an India-US security studies fellowship, and broader international security, natural science and engineering, and nuclear security fellowships. Fellows are based in Encina Hall within the Freeman Spogli Institute.

CISAC considers applicants from the US and abroad regardless of citizenship, so African scholars and scientists working on security, technology or nuclear issues can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Fellows receive support for a year of research at Stanford; the fellowship page does not state stipend amounts.
requirements: Open to applicants from the US and abroad, regardless of citizenship
AI and Laws of Armed Conflict: JD or LLM and/or PhD in a relevant field
AI in Strategic Stability: PhD
Geopolitics of AI: PhD or JD
Indo-Pacific Security: two-year postdoc
India-US Security Studies: early-career scholars (pre-doctoral, postdoctoral or junior faculty)
documents: Online application through the CISAC SlideRoom portal (contents set out in the portal)
opportunities.about_provider: CISAC is part of Stanford University's Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies. It brings together scientists, engineers and social scientists to study international security problems such as nuclear weapons, emerging technologies and conflict.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the track descriptions on the CISAC fellowship page, then submit an application through the center's SlideRoom portal (cisacstanford.slideroom.com) before 2 December 2026. Questions go to CISACfellowship@stanford.edu.
opportunities.notes: Questions: CISACfellowship@stanford.edu. Check each track's degree requirements on the fellowship page before applying.

opportunities.title: DTU PhD scholarship: Predictive Human Digital Twins
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Salaried three-year DTU PhD position open to international applicants with a relevant two-year master's (120 ECTS) and good English.

opportunities.title: Gangseo University International Entrance Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Foreign school leavers whose parents are both foreign nationals, applying to Gangseo undergraduate programmes with TOPIK, IELTS or TOEFL scores.
opportunities.description:
Gangseo University in Seoul gives new international undergraduates a first-semester entrance scholarship based on their Korean or English test results. It is part of the university's 2027 undergraduate admissions for international students, which run in four application rounds.

Applicants with TOPIK level 4 or higher, or IELTS 6.0 or higher, receive KRW 500,000. Those with IELTS 5.5, TOPIK level 3, native English speakers from English-speaking countries, and students coming from Korean language institutes receive KRW 400,000.

The third round runs from 23 November to 2 December 2026 and a fourth round from 21 to 30 December 2026, so African school leavers can still apply for the 2027 intake.
opportunities.benefits: First-semester scholarship of KRW 500,000 (TOPIK 4+ or IELTS 6.0+) or KRW 400,000 (IELTS 5.5, TOPIK 3, native English speaker, or Korean language institute students). Enrolled foreign students are automatically enrolled in National Health Insurance.
requirements: Applicant and both parents must be foreign nationals
Completed the full school curriculum (equivalent of elementary, middle and high school); online schooling and GED not accepted
Korean track: TOPIK 3 or higher
English track: TOEFL iBT 70 or IELTS 5.5, or English-medium high school, or citizen of an English-official country, or pass the interview
opportunities.selection_process: Most majors are decided 100% on the paper application; Contemporary Music uses a practical exam.
opportunities.about_provider: Gangseo University is a private university in western Seoul, South Korea. Its Institute for International Education and Exchange handles international admissions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the 2027 international undergraduate guidelines from Gangseo's admissions page and send the application and documents by email, post or in person within an application window. Pay the KRW 60,000 (US$60) fee, or KRW 70,000 for Contemporary Music. Contact kcu-international@gangseo.ac.kr.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship covers the first semester only.

opportunities.title: International Scholars Program (UBC)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary-school graduates with top grades, leadership and significant financial need can apply by 2 December 2026 for UBC's need-based International Scholars awards for September 2027 entry.
opportunities.description:
UBC's International Scholars Program (ISP) is the University of British Columbia's flagship package of need- and merit-based awards for outstanding international students entering a first undergraduate degree in September 2027, at UBC Vancouver or UBC Okanagan. Since 2001 it has supported more than 680 scholars from over 111 countries.

The programme includes four awards: the Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award, the Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award (for students from areas affected by poverty or war), the International Impact Award, and the Vantage One Excellence Award, which can cover up to the full cost of study and living. Scholars also receive workshops, advising and access to exchange and co-op.

The deadline was extended to 2 December 2026, giving African school leavers with top grades, leadership records and real financial need a little more time to apply to UBC and submit the ISP application.
opportunities.benefits: Awards based on financial need, potentially covering up to the full cost of the academic programme and living expenses (stated for the Vantage One Excellence Award); exact amounts depend on assessed need. Scholars also receive workshops, advising and exchange/co-op opportunities.
requirements: International student entering UBC directly from secondary school (graduated no earlier than June 2026) for a first undergraduate degree
Superior academic achievement (all As or equivalent)
Significant demonstrated financial need
Leadership and community contribution
Meet UBC admission and English requirements (e.g. IELTS Academic 6.5 with no part below 6.0, TOEFL iBT 90, Duolingo 125, PTE 65)
Nominated by your school or a non-profit (up to two per school for Vancouver, one for Okanagan)
Not for Nursing, Dental Hygiene, Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management or dual degrees

opportunities.selection_process: UBC assesses financial need and merit, then may invite candidates to a video interview between January and March 2027. Results are released on a rolling basis from February to April 2027.

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to UBC for September 2027, arrange your nominator and teacher reference, then submit the ISP application on UBC's undergraduate scholarships portal using your UBC student number, all by noon Pacific Time on 2 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Applying to the ISP means you are not considered for UBC's merit-only entrance awards. Nominators and referees must submit their forms a few days before the deadline.

opportunities.title: John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships 2027/2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists and journalism professionals of any nationality with at least five years of experience at editorially independent organisations.
opportunities.description:
The John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships give working journalists, and people whose jobs support journalism, nine months at Stanford University to step back from daily work, learn and think about the problems facing news. The fellowship runs full time and in residence from September to May. Fellows are not asked to deliver a set project, and no university degree is needed to be selected.

Applications for the 2027-28 cohort are open now, and there are separate tracks for US-based and international applicants. The programme is a good fit for African reporters, editors and newsroom managers with solid experience, because it pays a large stipend and covers Stanford tuition and health insurance, so a fellow can take a full academic year away from work.

The fellowship is aimed at people already established in the field. Students, interns, PR staff, government employees and full-time academics are not the intended audience, and applicants must work for media that is editorially independent.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of US$135,000 for the nine months; Stanford tuition and health insurance; a health supplement for dependants who enrol in Stanford coverage; help with finding housing; coaching and workshops during the year.
requirements: At least five years of professional experience (student work and internships do not count)
Work directly on journalistic content, or in operations or strategy at a news organisation, or at an organisation that supports journalists
Freelancers must earn more than half their work from journalism
Must work for editorially independent organisations
Not open to people seeking a degree, PR or corporate communications staff, government employees or full-time academics
Citizens of countries under a US suspension of J visas cannot be offered a place unless they hold another unrestricted citizenship
documents: Online application form completed in the SurveyMonkey Apply portal
Profile answers that place you in the US or international track
opportunities.selection_process: Applications go through several rounds of review over a few months. A small group of finalists is invited to a Zoom interview. The selection team includes the JSK directors and alumni, and for the US fellowships the JSK Selection Committee.

opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the JSK portal (jsk.smapply.org), answer the profile questions to see whether you belong in the US or international track, then complete and submit the online form before 1:00 p.m. Pacific time on 2 December 2026. Late applications and extensions are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: JSK states that it never grants extensions. Questions go to jskfellowships@stanford.edu (+1 650-723-4937).

opportunities.title: Maurice R. Greenberg World Fellows Program 2027
opportunities.provider: Yale Jackson School of Global Affairs

opportunities.description:
The Maurice R. Greenberg World Fellows Program is Yale's flagship four-month, full-time residential programme for exceptional mid-career leaders from around the world. Run by the International Leadership Center of the Yale Jackson School of Global Affairs since 2002, it has more than 450 alumni in over 100 countries.

Fellows live in New Haven, Connecticut, from mid-August to mid-December, taking part in seminars, auditing Yale classes, mentoring students and building a global network. It is a non-degree programme and there are no tuition fees.

The programme is for citizens of countries other than the United States, and many fellows come from Africa, including leaders in government, business, civil society, the arts and media.
opportunities.benefits: No tuition or fees; a taxable living stipend; a furnished one- or two-bedroom apartment; medical insurance; and round-trip travel from the fellow's home country. Amounts are not stated.

Citizen of a country other than the United States (US dual citizens may apply, with preference for work focused outside the US)
Fluent English (assessed at interview; no test needed)
Not a full-time student or full-time academic
Able to live in New Haven full time for the whole programme
documents: Short video statement recorded in the portal
opportunities.selection_process: Fellows are chosen for a record of extraordinary achievement and integrity, commitment to the public good, promise of future leadership and global impact, critical and strategic thinking, and commitment to full residence and mentoring students. Finalists are interviewed and decisions are made by the end of April. Places are extremely limited.
important_dates: Deadline: 2 December 2026, 2:00 pm US Eastern Time
Recommendation letters: up to one week after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The Yale Jackson School of Global Affairs is Yale University's school for international affairs. Its International Leadership Center runs the World Fellows Program.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the World Fellows application portal, uploading your CV, statement and video and asking three referees to submit letters. No nomination is needed.
opportunities.notes: There is no age limit (the average fellow is 39). Reapplicants must submit a full new application, and no individual feedback is given. Contact: world.fellows@yale.edu.

opportunities.title: UBC Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award (International Scholars Program, September 2027 entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary-school students with top grades and documented financial need, applying to their first UBC undergraduate degree for September 2027, can apply by 2 December 2026 (12:00 PT).
opportunities.description:
The Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award is one of four awards within the University of British Columbia's International Scholars Program. It supports outstanding international students entering UBC directly from secondary school who could not afford a UBC degree without significant help. The award is based on both financial need and merit, so the amount is set after a financial assessment rather than being a fixed sum.

A school can nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver (including Vantage College) or one for UBC Okanagan.

For African school leavers, this is one of the most generous need-based awards in Canada. The 2027 cycle is open now, with the deadline extended to 2 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: A need-and-merit award whose value is set by UBC's financial assessment of each student's need; the official page does not give a fixed amount.

opportunities.title: AAAI 2027 Bridge: AI for Scholarly Communication (AI4SC)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit papers by the deadline for this conference (Montreal, 16 February 2027).
opportunities.description:
AI4SC 2027 is the third AAAI Bridge on Artificial Intelligence for Scholarly Communication, a two-day programme on 16-17 February 2027 in Montréal, Canada, co-located with the 41st AAAI Conference. It is chaired by Anna Jacyszyn of FIZ Karlsruhe.

The bridge brings together AI researchers and the scholarly publishing community to discuss how AI can support research discovery, peer review and publishing. It accepts long, short and poster or demo papers for proceedings, as well as non-archival talk proposals, lightning-talk abstracts and tutorial proposals.

It is open to researchers anywhere and is a good venue for African researchers in AI, digital libraries or research information systems, though attendees must register for AAAI-27.
opportunities.benefits: Accepted papers are published in the bridge proceedings and presented at AAAI-27. No travel support is stated; attendance requires paid AAAI-27 registration.
requirements: Paper in English in CEUR-ART style
Long papers 10-15 pages, short papers 5-9 pages, posters or demos under 5 pages
Declaration on any use of generative AI tools
Non-compliant submissions are rejected without review
opportunities.selection_process: Single-blind review by at least three programme committee members per submission.
important_dates: Submission deadline: 3 December 2026 (end of day AoE)
opportunities.about_provider: AAAI, the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence, runs the annual AAAI Conference, which includes bridge programmes linking AI with other fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your paper through EasyChair (conference ai4sc2027) by 3 December 2026. Lightning-talk abstracts can be sent until 14 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Contact: ai4sc2027@easychair.org.

opportunities.title: Cambridge Trust Scholarships
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants to University of Cambridge courses starting in 2027/28, subject to each award's criteria.

The Cambridge Trust is the largest provider of scholarships for international students at the University of Cambridge, offering full-cost and part-cost awards for PhD, master's and some undergraduate study. Its scholarship search covers courses starting in the 2027/28 academic year.

For postgraduate study, most awards require significant academic achievement and potential and are based partly on financial need. Some awards are limited to particular nationalities, and courses such as the MBA, MFin, MEd and postgraduate certificates and diplomas are not funded.

African applicants are considered automatically for many awards by completing the funding section of the University's graduate application before their course's funding deadline.
