Some partner awards need a separate application.

opportunities.title: Concordia Carlini-DeLuca RISE Award 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time Concordia science or engineering undergraduates in second year or above with a GPA of at least 3.30, including international students.
opportunities.description:
The Carlini-DeLuca Undergraduate RISE Award (Resilience In Science and Engineering Pathways to Success) is one of Concordia University's application-based awards for 2026-27. It recognises science and engineering undergraduates who have kept up strong studies while dealing with serious personal strain or exceptional challenges.

The award is worth CA$1,500 and is open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and international students. That means African students already studying science or engineering at Concordia in Montreal can apply on the same terms as Canadians.

It is a one-off award for current students rather than an entrance scholarship, so it suits African students in their second year or later who want to have their resilience and results recognised.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time award of CA$1,500.
requirements: Undergraduate in science or engineering at Concordia
Second year of study or higher
Minimum GPA 3.30
Full-time in fall 2026 and winter 2027
Canadian citizen, permanent resident or international student
Has faced significant personal strain or exceptional challenges
documents: Online application form (Microsoft Form linked from the awards page)
opportunities.about_provider: Concordia University is a large public university in Montreal, Canada. Each autumn it opens a round of application-based awards for its undergraduates across all faculties.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Open Concordia's application-based awards page, find the Carlini-DeLuca RISE Award in the Faculty of Arts and Science section, and complete its online form before midnight on 3 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The same page lists other Concordia awards open to international students with the same 3 December deadline, such as the Colors of Concordia Award and the Back on Track Award.

opportunities.title: Concordia Morgan Stanley Race and Ethnic Diversity Scholarship 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Concordia undergraduates in eligible tech, engineering or finance programmes with a GPA of 3.30+ who identify as Black or Asian, including international students.
opportunities.description:
The Morgan Stanley Race and Ethnic Diversity Scholarship is a Concordia University award funded by Morgan Stanley. It supports undergraduates from under-represented racial and ethnic groups in business technology, computing, engineering and quantitative finance programmes at Concordia's John Molson School of Business and Gina Cody School of Engineering and Computer Science.

The scholarship is worth CA$2,500 and is open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and international students who self-identify as Black, Southeast Asian, South Asian or East Asian. African students enrolled in the eligible programmes can therefore apply.

It is part of Concordia's 2026-27 round of application-based awards, which all close on 3 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time award of CA$2,500.
requirements: Undergraduate, full-time or part-time, in an eligible programme (Business Technology Management, Computer Engineering, Computer Science including Computational Arts, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Mathematical and Computational Finance)
GPA of 3.30 or higher
Self-identifies as Black, Southeast Asian, South Asian or East Asian
Canadian citizen, permanent resident or international student
documents: Online application form (Microsoft Form linked from the awards page)
opportunities.about_provider: Concordia University is a large public university in Montreal, Canada. Morgan Stanley, the global financial services firm, funds this award to widen diversity in technology and finance.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Go to Concordia's application-based awards page, find the Morgan Stanley Race and Ethnic Diversity Scholarship under the business or engineering section, and submit the online form before midnight on 3 December 2026.

opportunities.title: Joint ICTP-MSA-COMSTECH-SESAME School on AI-Driven Biomaterials Design (Mar 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: School at SESAME in Allan, Jordan, 14 to 25 March 2027, for early-career researchers who submit a poster abstract, with no fee and limited grants prioritising developing-country participants.
opportunities.description:
The Joint ICTP-MSA-COMSTECH-SESAME School on AI-Driven Biomaterials Design runs from 14 to 25 March 2027 in Jordan (the event page lists "Allan - Jordan", home of the SESAME synchrotron). It takes early-career researchers from characterisation to additive manufacturing and from lab to market.

Topics include synchrotron micro-CT and FTIR, atomic force microscopy, AI-driven design and 3D printing of biomaterials. Participants present a short research poster.

There is no registration fee and a limited number of grants give priority to participants from developing countries, so African researchers in materials science, biomedical engineering or physics are a key target group.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants are available, with priority for participants from developing countries; amounts are not stated.
requirements: Early-career researcher in a relevant field
Online application through the ICTP e-portal
Short research abstract for a poster using the ICTP template
opportunities.about_provider: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste is a UNESCO Category 1 institute that runs schools and workshops for scientists from developing countries. This school is co-organised with MSA University, COMSTECH and SESAME.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the "Apply here" link on the ICTP event page (smr 4343), which leads to the ICTP e-portal, and upload your poster abstract by 3 December 2026. Request a grant in the application if you need travel support.
opportunities.notes: Contact: smr4343@ictp.it.

opportunities.title: Kyoto University International Undergraduate Program (Kyoto iUP) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary school graduates with strong grades and English can apply; no Japanese is needed.
opportunities.description:
The Kyoto University International Undergraduate Program (Kyoto iUP) is a four-and-a-half-year bachelor's route for international students. It starts with a six-month preparatory course in Japanese and foundation subjects, followed by a four-year degree in the student's chosen faculty at Kyoto University in Japan, for the October 2027 intake.

No Japanese is needed at the time of application. The programme looks for applicants with strong academic records, good English, motivation and a broad world view, and all students receive scholarships.

Kyoto iUP gives African secondary school leavers a funded path into one of Asia's top universities, with a monthly allowance in the preparatory phase and dormitory housing at the start.
opportunities.benefits: All Kyoto iUP students receive scholarships that waive the admission fee in full and tuition in full or in part for four and a half years. During the preparatory course, students can receive an allowance of up to JPY 120,000 per month, and further merit-based allowances from supporters may follow. Dormitory housing is provided for the first one and a half years.
requirements: Strong academic record
English proficiency (Form C English Proficiency Evaluation)
Motivation and a global outlook
Japanese not required at application
Must pass the eligibility screening set out in the application guidelines
documents: Form B: Evaluation (some forms uploaded by the school)
Form C: English Proficiency Evaluation Form
All documents in English or with English translations
important_dates: Online application system open: 2 November to 3 December 2026 (5 pm Japan time)
opportunities.about_provider: Kyoto University is one of Japan's leading national research universities. Kyoto iUP is its programme for recruiting international undergraduates into its regular faculties.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the Application Guidelines for October 2027 Enrolment, then apply through the Kyoto iUP online application system while it is open, pay the application fee and click "Complete" before 5 pm Japan time on 3 December 2026. Late or incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Check the eligibility screening and FAQ on the Kyoto iUP site before applying, and make sure your school uploads its forms on time.

opportunities.title: MCW Global Young Leaders Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young people aged 18-26 from any country with fluent English who commit to a year-long community leadership programme.
opportunities.description:
The MCW Global Young Leaders Fellowship is a year-long leadership programme for people aged 18 to 26 who want to tackle problems in their own communities. It runs in three phases: a one-month community needs assessment in June 2027, a 10-day in-person training in New York City and Burlington, Vermont from 20 to 29 July 2027, and then ten months of carrying out a community project with an alumni mentor, ending in July 2028.

Projects focus on education, health or economic security. The programme has no geographic restrictions, so young Africans can apply and then run their projects at home with support from MCW's alumni network.

The first-round deadline is 3 December 2026; a second round closes on 8 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Economy return international flights; housing from 19 to 29 July 2027; three meals a day from 20 to 29 July; round-trip travel between New York City and Burlington; mentoring by alumni during the project year. Passport, visa and in-country costs are not covered, and no stipend is mentioned.
requirements: Aged 18 to 26 on 1 June 2027 (no exceptions)
Open to all countries
Fluent written and spoken English
Able to obtain a visa and travel documents
Commitment to all three phases
Reliable email and internet access
documents: Online application in English with two essays (a community issue and a leadership challenge)
Resume of no more than one page
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed in two rounds, followed by interviews with alumni. MCW warns that answers written with AI tools will hurt an applicant's chances.
important_dates: First-round deadline: 3 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. New York time
opportunities.about_provider: MCW Global is a non-profit based in New York that trains young leaders and supports community projects around the world, with a strong presence in Africa.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through MCW's applicant portal (applicant.mcwglobal.org) with your essays, one-page resume and two recommendation letters. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed by alumni in February 2027, and successful fellows confirm by paying a refundable US$100 deposit.
opportunities.notes: The US$100 deposit is returned when the fellowship is completed. Write your own essays; MCW says AI-generated answers count against you.

opportunities.title: Simons Postdoctoral Fellowships in Plant Biology 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhD holders of any nationality with a sponsor at a US non-profit institution, doing basic plant biology research.
opportunities.description:
The Simons Postdoctoral Fellowships in Plant Biology fund three years of basic research on fundamental questions in plant biology at a US non-profit university or research institute. The 2027 call supports two kinds of fellow: plant biologists who want to learn new skills from a mentor outside their field, and researchers from other fields who want to bring their expertise to plant biology. Up to two mentors are allowed.

The awards are generous: an US$85,000 annual stipend plus up to US$35,000 a year for research and related costs. Both US citizens and foreign applicants may apply, so African PhD holders who find a US host can compete.

Fellows start between July and October 2027 after decisions in May 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Up to US$360,000 in total over three years: a stipend of US$85,000 per year, an annual allowance of up to US$35,000 (for health insurance, supplies, travel and similar costs) and up to US$2,000 for relocation. No indirect costs are paid.
requirements: PhD (or equivalent) awarded no earlier than three years before the deadline, or expected by the start date
US citizens and foreign nationals may apply
Must be hosted by a US non-profit research university or institution
The sponsor cannot be the applicant's thesis adviser
Only one application per sponsor per year
Cannot hold another postdoctoral fellowship at the same time
documents: Proposal narrative on the Simons template
Sponsor biosketch (max 5 pages) and other-support document
Four confidential letters: thesis adviser, two research scientists and the sponsor
Institutional assurances (IRB, IACUC or biosafety) where relevant
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by Simons Foundation scientific staff and an external expert committee.
important_dates: Start: the first of a month between 1 July and 1 October 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Simons Foundation is a private foundation in New York that funds research in mathematics and the basic sciences. Its Life Sciences division runs this plant biology fellowship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: The applicant creates the application in their own Simons Award Manager (SAM) account at sam.simonsfoundation.org, uploads the documents and arranges the four letters. The host institution's signing official must approve it before final submission by noon Eastern time on 3 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Simons offices are closed 25-27 November 2026, so ask questions early.

opportunities.title: AAAI-27 Student Scholar and Volunteer Program (Montreal, Feb 2027)
opportunities.provider: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time student AAAI members who submitted a paper to AAAI-27 and have a faculty recommendation can apply between 30 November and 4 December 2026 for partial travel support or complimentary volunteer registration.
opportunities.description:
The AAAI-27 Student Scholar and Volunteer Program helps students attend the 41st AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, held in Montréal, Canada, from 16 to 23 February 2027. It offers partial travel support to student scholars and free technical programme registration to a limited number of volunteers.

Applications open on 30 November 2026 and close on 4 December 2026. Applicants must be full-time students, AAAI members, and have submitted a paper to the conference with a recommendation from their faculty adviser.

African students with papers at AAAI-27 can use the programme to reduce the cost of attending one of the world's largest AI conferences.
opportunities.benefits: Partial travel support for selected student scholars (amount not stated) and complimentary technical programme registration for a limited number of volunteers. Volunteers are not paid.
requirements: Full-time undergraduate or graduate student
AAAI member
Submitted paper(s) to AAAI-27
Recommendation letter(s) from a faculty adviser
Repeat applicants must have met earlier volunteer and reporting duties
opportunities.selection_process: If requests exceed funds, preference goes first to students with an accepted technical paper and then to students actively taking part in the conference. Volunteer places also favour participating students.
opportunities.about_provider: The Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) is a scientific society that promotes AI research and runs the annual AAAI Conference.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply during the 30 November to 4 December 2026 window using the form announced on the AAAI-27 Student Scholar Volunteer Program page. Do not register for the conference until you hear back, or you lose the free registration.
opportunities.notes: Early registrants are not refunded. Contact: scholars@aaai.org.

opportunities.title: ACM MobiSys 2027 Call for Papers (Ho Chi Minh City, Jun 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Papers for ACM MobiSys 2027 in Ho Chi Minh City (21-25 June 2027) are due 4 December 2026 with abstracts by 27 November; travel support has not been announced yet.
opportunities.description:
ACM MobiSys 2027, the 25th International Conference on Mobile Systems, Applications, and Services, takes place in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, from 21 to 25 June 2027. It is sponsored by ACM SIGMOBILE and is one of the top venues for research on mobile and wireless systems.

The call seeks original papers on mobile systems, applications and services. Since 2026 review is single-blind, so author names appear on submissions, and there is an Emerging Ideas track for early-stage work. Reviews include an early rejection round and a rebuttal.

For African researchers in mobile computing, IoT and networking, MobiSys offers a high-impact publication and a conference in Asia.
opportunities.benefits: Accepted papers are published by ACM. Authors whose institutions are not in ACM Open pay a 2027 article processing charge of $500 (ACM/SIG members) or $750 (non-members). No travel grants are stated.
requirements: Original work not under review elsewhere
At most 12 pages of main content (double column, 10 pt, US Letter, ACM sigconf template); references and appendix unlimited
Author names and affiliations included (single-blind review)
Human-subjects work needs ethics (IRB or similar) approval
At least one author registers at a non-student rate and presents in person
opportunities.selection_process: Papers go through an early rejection round, a rebuttal of up to 500 words, then conditional acceptance with shepherding. Accepted papers receive a one-page public review.
opportunities.about_provider: ACM SIGMOBILE is the Association for Computing Machinery's special interest group on mobility of systems, users, data and computing. It runs MobiSys, MobiCom and other leading conferences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register your abstract by 27 November and upload the full paper by 4 December 2026 on HotCRP (mobisys27.hotcrp.com). For the Emerging Ideas track, start the title with "[Emerging Ideas]" and tick the box.
opportunities.notes: Deadlines will not be extended, placeholder abstracts are desk-rejected, and authors cannot be changed after submission.

opportunities.title: ASLE 2027 roundtable: Transboundary Waters and Critical Border Zones
opportunities.provider: Association for the Study of Literature and Environment (ASLE)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars can send abstracts for an in-person roundtable at the ASLE 2027 conference at the University of Maryland, 22-24 June 2027.
opportunities.description:
This call invites contributors to a proposed roundtable, "Riparian Terrors, Borderline Terroirs: Transboundary Waters and Critical Border Zones", for the 2027 biennial conference of the Association for the Study of Literature and Environment (ASLE). The conference runs on 22-24 June 2027 at the University of Maryland, College Park, under the theme "Territory: Terra, Terroir, Terror".

The organisers, Priyanka Sharma (George Washington University) and Minket Lepcha (University of Manitoba), will include selected abstracts in a roundtable proposal to ASLE, which makes the final decision. ASLE roundtables have a chair and five to seven panellists who each speak for 8 to 10 minutes, and most sessions are in person only.

Scholars writing on rivers, borders and environmental conflict, including on African transboundary waters such as the Nile, Niger or Zambezi basins, can respond.
opportunities.benefits: ASLE offers a small number of $500 travel awards for members in precarious circumstances without institutional funding; applications open in late February 2027.
requirements: Abstract of up to 300 words on transboundary waters or border zones
Short bio of under 100 words
Able to attend in person in College Park, Maryland
Only one individual abstract per person may be submitted to ASLE
opportunities.selection_process: The organisers select abstracts for their roundtable proposal, which ASLE then reviews; ASLE decisions are due by 26 February 2027.
important_dates: Abstracts to the roundtable organisers: 4 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: ASLE, the Association for the Study of Literature and Environment, is an international scholarly association for environmental humanities. It holds a biennial conference in the United States.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email your abstract and bio to the roundtable organisers at the address given in the call by 4 December 2026. If selected, you will be included in the roundtable proposal they submit to ASLE through its Pheedloop portal.
opportunities.notes: Questions about the conference: 2027asleconf@gmail.com.

opportunities.title: Andlinger Center Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellows 2027
opportunities.provider: Princeton University Andlinger Center for Energy and the Environment
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhDs (within three years) in energy or environment fields with two Princeton mentors.
opportunities.description:
Princeton University's Andlinger Center for Energy and the Environment is recruiting Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellows for 2027. Fellows design an interdisciplinary research plan on energy and the environment with at least two Princeton faculty members or senior researchers as mentors.

Appointments are expected to last two years, renewed after the first year on good performance, starting as early as June 2027 in Princeton, New Jersey. Teaching is not required, but fellows may give guest lectures.

No nationality restriction is stated, so African scientists and engineers with a recent PhD in energy, climate or environmental fields can apply for a well-paid, prestigious postdoc.
opportunities.benefits: Salary of $75,000 per year plus $3,500 per year for conference travel and career development, and Princeton's benefits package for eligible employees.
requirements: Doctorate in a related field awarded no more than three years before the start date
Research plan co-developed with two or more Princeton faculty or senior researchers
Preference for candidates not currently at Princeton
The primary mentor cannot be hosting a current Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellow
Background check required
documents: Contact details of the Princeton primary mentor(s), plus a mentor letter committing part of the funding
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the strength of the research, its interdisciplinary framing, its fit with the Center's mission and whether it builds new collaborations.
opportunities.about_provider: The Andlinger Center for Energy and the Environment at Princeton University supports research and education on sustainable energy and environmental technologies.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree a project with your proposed Princeton mentors, then submit your application on Interfolio (apply.interfolio.com/189606) by 4 December 2026. Your mentors must send a supporting letter and commit part of the financial support.
opportunities.notes: Contact: Charles Sharpless, csharpless@princeton.edu.

opportunities.title: Cannes Lions 2027 Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fully funded trip to Cannes Lions for under-30 creative professionals from under-represented groups.
opportunities.description:
The LIONS Scholarship gives ten under-represented young creative and marketing professionals a fully funded place at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity in 2027. Five places are on the Creative Academy, for creatives such as art directors, copywriters, designers and journalists, and five on the Brand Marketing Academy, for client-side marketers.

Scholars attend their academy and receive a Young Lions festival pass, joining the world's biggest gathering of the advertising and creative industry in Cannes, France. The programmes are in English.

The scholarship is meant for talent under-represented in the industry, so young African creatives and marketers with at least two years of work experience are a natural fit.
opportunities.benefits: A fully funded trip to Cannes Lions 2027, including travel, accommodation and a food allowance during festival week, plus a Young Lions festival pass. There is no application fee. Guests and family are not funded.
requirements: Born on or after 25 June 1996 and at least 18 years old (proof of age required)
At least two years of work experience in a relevant role
Creative Academy: working creative; Brand Marketing Academy: brand or client-side marketer
Able to take part in English
documents: Online application (see the official Entry Kit for details)
opportunities.selection_process: A two-stage process: a jury of more than 40 creatives builds a shortlist from the first applications, then a final stage selects the ten scholars.
opportunities.about_provider: Cannes Lions is the annual international festival of creativity for the advertising, marketing and communications industry, operated by Informa Events (Europe) Limited.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the LIONS Scholarship Entry Kit and apply through the Cannes Lions competitions portal (competitions.canneslions.com) before 00:01 GMT on 4 December 2026. You may apply to both academies but can be accepted onto only one.
opportunities.notes: The deadline is one minute past midnight GMT, so submit on 3 December. You can reapply in later years. Contact: talentprogrammes@canneslions.com.

opportunities.title: DTU PhD scholarship: Data-driven Design of Architected Materials
opportunities.provider: Technical University of Denmark (DTU Engineering Technology)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Salaried three-year DTU PhD position open to international applicants with a relevant two-year master's (120 ECTS) and good English.

opportunities.title: IEEE I2MTC 2027 Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide may submit full papers on instrumentation and measurement for I2MTC in Chongqing, 17-20 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
IEEE I2MTC 2027, the International Instrumentation and Measurement Technology Conference, is the flagship conference of the IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Society. It takes place in Chongqing, China, on 17-20 May 2027 under the theme "Smart Instrumentation for a Connected World".

The call covers sensors, industrial digital transformation, medical and biomedical instrumentation, AI and machine learning in measurement, robotics, energy, environmental and agricultural monitoring, and communications and IoT. Accepted and presented papers appear in IEEE Xplore.

The conference has student travel grants and an IMS Conference Equity Travel Grant, which can help African students and researchers in measurement science attend.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in IEEE Xplore for accepted and presented papers. Student travel grants and IMS Conference Equity Travel Grants are offered (details on the conference site; amounts not read).
requirements: Full paper in the conference's required IEEE format
Original work on instrumentation and measurement topics
Registration and presentation for inclusion in IEEE Xplore
important_dates: Early registration and final manuscript: 19 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Society (IMS) is the IEEE society for measurement science and instrumentation. I2MTC is its flagship annual conference.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Follow the author instructions on the I2MTC 2027 website and submit your full paper by 4 December 2026. Check the student travel grant and equity grant pages if you need funding.

opportunities.title: Italian Academy Fellowship Program 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: Italian Academy for Advanced Studies, Columbia University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars of any nationality holding a PhD (or completing one by June 2027) can apply for a salaried residential research fellowship in New York.
opportunities.description:
The Italian Academy for Advanced Studies at Columbia University in New York offers residential research fellowships to advanced scholars, from postdoctoral researchers to full professors. Its homepage announces a call for 2027-28 fellowships.

Fellows spend one or two semesters in residence (fall: September to December; spring: January to April). Projects are proposed in English, and scientists must arrange a collaboration with a Columbia lab director before applying.

There is no stated nationality restriction, so African scholars across the humanities, social sciences and sciences can consider it once the official call details are published.
opportunities.benefits: According to the fellowship page, a taxable salary of $5,000 to $8,000 per month, a travel allowance for airfare to and from New York, and part of health insurance costs. Housing is not provided, though the Academy helps with Columbia housing applications.
requirements: Advanced scholar, from postdoctoral to full professor level
Doctorate in hand by the summer after applying
Residence for one or two semesters
Scientists must secure a pledged collaboration with a Columbia lab
No concurrent fellowships; former fellows wait four years
opportunities.about_provider: The Italian Academy for Advanced Studies is a research institute at Columbia University, 1161 Amsterdam Avenue, New York.

opportunities.title: Newberry Library Short-Term Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders and ABD candidates of any nationality receive $3,000 a month, usually for one month, to research the Newberry's collections in Chicago.
opportunities.description:
The Newberry Library in Chicago offers Short-Term Fellowships for 2027-28 to scholars who need to consult specific items in its collections. Fellows spend one or two months in residence at any point between June 2027 and August 2028.

The fellowships are open to PhD holders at any career stage, including curators, librarians and independent scholars, and to doctoral candidates who are ABD. No institutional affiliation is needed, but the project must show why particular Newberry materials are essential.

African historians and humanities scholars working on topics such as the Atlantic world, maps, travel and exploration, or early modern history can use the fellowship to fund archival research in Chicago.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of $3,000 per month for one or two months. Housing is not provided, so the stipend must cover accommodation, travel and living costs.
requirements: PhD holder at any career stage, or ABD doctoral candidate
Project that needs specific items in the Newberry's collections
Residence in Chicago for one or two months between June 2027 and August 2028
Some fellowships carry extra residency or membership rules (see FAQ)
documents: List of Newberry materials to consult (maximum 300 words)
One recommendation letter in English, sent by the referee (up to 14 December 2026)
opportunities.about_provider: The Newberry Library is an independent research library in Chicago with major collections in the humanities. It runs short- and long-term fellowship programmes for researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your application through the Newberry's SlideRoom portal by 4 December 2026, then have your referee upload their letter within ten days. The library matches applicants to its named fellowships automatically, except those with special requirements.
opportunities.notes: Long-term Newberry fellowships close on 20 November 2026. Contact: research@newberry.org.

opportunities.title: Obama Foundation Leaders Africa 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Changemakers aged 24-45 living in Africa with 3+ years of Africa-focused leadership experience can apply by 4 December 2026 (priority 23 November) for the free 2027-2028 Obama Foundation Leaders Africa programme.
opportunities.description:
Obama Foundation Leaders Africa is an eight-month leadership development programme for 35 emerging leaders who are driving change across the African continent. Applications for the 2027-2028 cohort opened on 9 November 2026.

The programme runs from the week of 1 September 2027 to no later than 1 May 2028 and takes about 8 to 12 hours a month, with weekly sessions, coaching and small community groups. The main page describes it as hybrid and the FAQ as virtual, so applicants should expect mostly online participation. Participants join a global network of more than 1,800 Obama Leaders alumni.

It is designed for people already leading changemaking work focused on Africa, whatever their job title or formal education, and there is no cost to take part.
opportunities.benefits: Free leadership training, coaching, peer community groups and lifelong membership of the Obama Leaders network. There is no stipend and no grant for participants' own projects.
requirements: Live in an eligible African country for the whole programme and be a citizen, permanent resident, refugee or asylum seeker there, or have lived there for 5+ years
Work focused on Africa, with at least 3 years of relevant experience
Hold a leadership role in changemaking work (no title needed)
Aged 24 to 45 on 1 September 2027
Professional-level English
Not a previous Obama Leaders participant
Not standing for elected office from acceptance until 1 May 2028
documents: Two references, who complete the Foundation's reference form (other letters not accepted)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on a clear issue focus with measurable impact, values-based leadership and willingness to learn in a group. Decisions are shared in July 2027.
important_dates: Final deadline: 4 December 2026, 12:00 PM US Central Time
opportunities.about_provider: The Obama Foundation is a nonpartisan 501(c)(3) non-profit based in Chicago, founded by Barack and Michelle Obama. Its Leaders programmes train changemakers in Africa, Asia-Pacific, Europe and the United States.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Submittable portal linked from the Leaders Africa page and nominate two referees. Submitting by the 23 November priority date is best; later applications up to 4 December are considered as space allows.
opportunities.notes: No formal education requirement. Accessibility questions can go to globalleaders@obama.org.

opportunities.title: RSS 2027 Call for Papers (Robotics: Science and Systems)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit a 6-page extended abstract via OpenReview by 4 December 2026 (final paper due 16 April 2027) for RSS 2027, held 6-11 July 2027 in Athens.
opportunities.description:
Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2027 will be held in Athens, Greece, on 6-11 July 2027. RSS is one of the leading robotics research conferences, run by the RSS Foundation, and in 2027 it uses a new two-stage submission process.

In Stage 1 authors submit a short, anonymous extended abstract setting out their hypothesis and method. Promising papers receive an "Extension Charter" from the area chairs and reviewers, and in Stage 2 authors submit the full paper, which is judged on whether it delivered what the charter set out. Negative results are welcome if rigorously tested.

There are no restrictions on who may submit, so African robotics researchers can take part, but authors should create OpenReview profiles early.
opportunities.benefits: Accepted papers are presented at RSS 2027 and published in its proceedings. No travel grants are stated on the pages read.
requirements: Stage 1: 6-page PDF (5 pages of content plus 1 page of references) in the RSS template
Fully anonymous: no names, affiliations, acknowledgements or external links
Not under review at another venue at the RSS deadline (preprints allowed)
Type-1 fonts only; papers with hallucinated references are desk-rejected
Stage 2 full paper of up to 8 pages excluding references
documents: Stage 1 extended abstract PDF (LaTeX or Word template)
opportunities.selection_process: Stage 1 filters on hypotheses and methodology; selected papers get a rebuttal and then an Extension Charter. Stage 2 checks the full paper against the charter. Reviewer and chair names are published for accepted papers.
important_dates: Stage 1 extended abstract: 4 December 2026, 11:59 pm AoE
opportunities.about_provider: The RSS Foundation organises the annual Robotics: Science and Systems conference, which brings together researchers across robotics.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the Stage 1 extended abstract on OpenReview (RSS 2027 conference group) by 4 December 2026. Every author needs a complete OpenReview profile; profiles without an institutional email can take up to two weeks to approve.
opportunities.notes: LLM use is allowed and disclosure is encouraged. The abstract can be edited until the deadline.

opportunities.title: SOAS Online Scholarships (January 2027 intake)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a 2:1 degree and an offer for a January 2027 SOAS Online master's.
opportunities.description:
SOAS University of London offers five scholarships of £2,000 each for students starting one of its online master's programmes in January 2027. The awards reduce the cost of studying a SOAS degree fully online from anywhere in the world.

Eligible programmes include online MSc degrees in Public Policy and Management, Banking and Finance, International Business, Global Development, Humanitarian Action, Global Sustainability, and Climate Change and Development, and online MA degrees in Global Diplomacy, Gender and Global Politics, Global Histories, Global Media and Digital Cultures, and Social Anthropology.

Because study is online, African professionals can earn a London master's while staying in their jobs, and this scholarship helps with fees.
opportunities.benefits: A one-off £2,000 scholarship towards fees; five awards in total.
requirements: Offer for the January 2027 intake of an eligible SOAS Online programme
Upper second-class (2:1) undergraduate degree or international equivalent
Not studying through a partnership with discounted fees (dual, joint or progression)
documents: Scholarship application through the SOAS admissions portal
opportunities.selection_process: A scholarship panel reviews all applications after the deadline, and successful applicants are told by 11 December 2026.
opportunities.about_provider: SOAS University of London specialises in the study of Africa, Asia and the Middle East. It runs a range of online master's programmes for working students worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First apply for an eligible SOAS Online programme, then log in to the SOAS admissions portal and complete the scholarship application, which appears only to applicants who meet the basic criteria, by noon on 4 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Contact: scholarships@soas.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: ICANN89 Policy Forum Fellowship 2027 (Vancouver)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: ICANN Fellowship alumni aged 21+ from any country; first-time applicants must wait for the ICANN90 round.
opportunities.description:
ICANN's Fellowship Program helps people take part in ICANN meetings and its policy work on the internet's domain name system. This round is for ICANN89, the Policy Forum meeting in Vancouver, Canada, from 14 to 17 June 2027 (online if the meeting moves to a virtual format).

Important: the Policy Forum round is open only to people who have already completed an ICANN Fellowship. First-time applicants cannot apply now; they should watch for the ICANN90 round (Adelaide, 30 October - 4 November 2027), which opens on 22 March 2027 and closes on 22 April 2027.

Fellows get travel support, a mentor and training, which makes the programme a valuable path for African internet policy professionals, engineers and researchers.
opportunities.benefits: Travel assistance to attend the meeting, a mentor and training.
requirements: Must be an ICANN Fellowship Program alumnus (first-time applicants not eligible for the Policy Forum)
At least 21 years old at application
Must have completed the mandatory ICANN Learn course(s)
Not taking part in another ICANN-supported travel programme at selection
No more than two previous fellowships
An ICANN account is required
documents: Online application in the ICANN fellowship portal
opportunities.selection_process: A Fellowship Selection Committee reviews applications against ICANN's published selection criteria.
important_dates: ICANN90 round (first-timers): opens 22 March 2027, closes 22 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: ICANN (Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers) is the global non-profit that coordinates the internet's domain names and IP address system through a multi-stakeholder community.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Log in with an ICANN account and complete the application in the fellowship portal linked from icann.org/fellowships before 23:59 UTC on 5 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: ICANN also runs the Paul Muchene Fellow Award for African-region fellows with a technical background.

opportunities.title: IMF Economist Program (EP) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New or near-completion macroeconomics PhDs under 34 from IMF member countries.
opportunities.description:
The IMF Economist Program (EP) is the Fund's entry route for new PhD economists. Recruits join IMF headquarters in Washington, D.C. as economists, starting in September 2027, and spend three years in two different departmental assignments. The IMF stresses that the EP is a regular job, not a training scheme.

Citizens of any IMF member country can apply, which includes every African country that is a Fund member. The programme is a strong career path for African macroeconomists finishing their doctorates.

Applications usually open in late September, with interviews from October to January and offers in early February.
opportunities.benefits: A three-year economist appointment at IMF headquarters; the IMF provides G-4 visa documentation for non-US citizens. Salary is not stated on the posting.
requirements: Recent PhD, or within one year of completing a PhD, in macroeconomics or a related field
Solid grounding in macroeconomic analysis
Under 34 when the programme starts in September 2027 (allowance for mandatory military service)
Citizen of an IMF member country
Excellent written and spoken English and strong analytical, quantitative and computer skills
documents: Online application on the IMF careers site
If asked after the first interview: PhD transcript, three academic references (not from current IMF staff), and a publishable research paper or one or two dissertation chapters
opportunities.selection_process: A 30-40 minute preliminary interview, then submission of supporting materials, then an in-person panel with senior economists and HR plus a 90-minute written test, and finally an internal committee review. The panel and the research paper weigh most.
opportunities.about_provider: The International Monetary Fund is an organisation of 190 member countries that works on global monetary cooperation, financial stability and economic policy advice.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'Economist Program 2027' posting on the IMF Workday careers site. Shortlisted candidates are invited to a preliminary interview and then asked for transcripts, references and a research paper.
opportunities.notes: Apply as early as possible; the posting does not show a fixed closing date.

opportunities.title: IMF Fund Internship Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Paid 10-12 week summer internship at IMF headquarters in Washington, D.C. for PhD students in economics.
opportunities.description:
The IMF Fund Internship Program (FIP) brings about 50 graduate students from around the world to IMF headquarters in Washington, D.C. each summer. Interns work for 10 to 12 weeks between June and October on research and policy projects in the Fund's departments.

The internships are paid and give students an inside view of how the IMF works with its member countries on economic policy and financial stability.

According to the IMF, applications usually open in early December through vacancy postings on the IMF Career Site, so African graduate students in economics and related fields should watch for the 2027 posting.
opportunities.benefits: A paid summer internship at IMF headquarters; amounts are not shown on the official page.
important_dates: Internships: between June and October 2027, lasting 10 to 12 weeks
opportunities.about_provider: The International Monetary Fund is an organisation of 190 member countries that works on global monetary cooperation, financial stability and sustainable economic growth.

opportunities.title: University of Florida Funded PhD in Engineering and Computing
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Funded PhD positions in engineering and computing for international applicants.

opportunities.title: ICIAM 2027 Congress Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD and graduate students of any nationality who submit a poster or mini-symposium contribution to ICIAM 2027 can apply for a 500-1,000 euro attendance grant.
opportunities.description:
ICIAM 2027, the International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics, takes place in The Hague, Netherlands, from 12 to 16 July 2027. The organisers describe it as the largest industrial and applied mathematics conference in the world, and it runs a grant scheme that helps graduate students and PhD candidates pay part of the cost of attending.

The grants are worth between 500 and 1,000 euros and are paid after the congress ends, so recipients must first cover their own travel and registration. Preference goes to applicants who present a poster or speak in a mini-symposium, and the grant application can only be made after a poster abstract or mini-symposium proposal has been submitted; both close on 7 December 2026.

The scheme is open to students of any nationality and professional situation, which makes it a practical route for African doctoral and master's students in applied mathematics to present at a major world congress.
opportunities.benefits: A grant of 500 to 1,000 euros towards the cost of attending (exact amount confirmed in mid-January 2027), paid after the congress. It covers only part of the costs.
requirements: Enrolled in a PhD or graduate programme at the time of the congress (July 2027)
Any nationality and any professional situation
Must first submit a poster abstract or mini-symposium proposal (deadline 7 December 2026)
Poster presenters and invited mini-symposium speakers are preferred
documents: Personal and professional details (name, nationality, email, affiliation)
Statement of up to 300 words on your scientific interests and goals, noting any other grants you were refused or could not get
Recommendation letter from your supervisor or an industrial and applied mathematics specialist, with full contact details
Proof of enrolment in a PhD or graduate programme valid for July 2027
opportunities.selection_process: A Grant Committee chooses recipients, giving preference to applicants presenting a poster or speaking in a mini-symposium. Decisions are sent in mid-January 2027.
important_dates: Abstracts, mini-symposium proposals and grant applications: 7 December 2026 (midnight CET)
Grant recipients must register and pay by 9 February 2027 (early-bird deadline)
opportunities.about_provider: ICIAM is the International Council for Industrial and Applied Mathematics, which holds a world congress every four years. The 2027 congress is hosted in The Hague and managed by the congress organiser Congress by Design.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit a poster abstract or mini-symposium proposal through the ICIAM 2027 call for submissions, then complete the grant application with the documents listed, as PDFs, by 7 December 2026. If awarded, register and pay the fee by 9 February 2027; the grant is reimbursed after the congress.
opportunities.notes: Because the grant is paid after the event, plan how to pre-finance your travel and visa. Questions go to ICIAM@congressbydesign.com.

opportunities.title: MIAS Marcel Bataillon Programme
opportunities.provider: Madrid Institute for Advanced Study (MIAS) and Casa de Velázquez
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders in the humanities and social sciences whose research concerns the Iberian Peninsula, the Maghreb or the Atlantic world can apply for a ten-month paid contract in Madrid.
opportunities.description:
The Marcel Bataillon Programme offers up to two ten-month research contracts at the Madrid Institute for Advanced Study, formalised by the Casa de Velázquez. Fellows start on 1 October 2027 and the contract ends on 31 July 2028; it is a full-time Spanish researcher contract with social security cover.

Projects must fit the Casa de Velázquez research areas, which cover the Iberian Peninsula, the Maghreb and the Atlantic world in relation to the Peninsula, in the arts, humanities, social and legal sciences. Projects outside this scope are not admitted.

With the Maghreb named as a core region and no nationality restriction, this is a strong option for North African and other African scholars whose research connects to Spain, Portugal or the western Mediterranean.
opportunities.benefits: A gross salary of about 33,000 euros for the ten months, with Spanish social security. Optional housing at the Casa de Velázquez for 500 euros a month (researcher and spouse). It cannot be combined with other jobs or MIAS fellowships.
requirements: Hold a PhD
Legally able to sign a Spanish employment contract (Article 7 of the Workers' Statute)
Good command of at least two of English, French and Spanish
Not have lived or worked in Spain for more than 12 months in the 36 months before the call opened
Project within the Casa de Velázquez research areas (Iberian Peninsula, Maghreb, Atlantic region)
documents: Up to two optional reference letters (Annex II)
Research project summary (Annex III) in English plus Spanish or French, max 8 pages per language
Copy of ID card or passport
PhD certificate showing the award date
opportunities.selection_process: In phase one, two external experts score the project's interest, originality and feasibility (0-50), academic and scientific merit (0-25) and national and international activity (0-25), with attention to balance across fields. Shortlisted candidates then have an interview, in person or by video, in Spanish or English, with the International Scientific Advisory Board.
opportunities.about_provider: The Madrid Institute for Advanced Study (MIAS) is a joint research centre of the Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (UAM) and the Casa de Velázquez, the French school in Madrid. It joined the NetIAS network of European institutes for advanced study in 2019 and UBIAS in 2020.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the MIAS Bataillon and Tomás y Valiente portal (bataillon-tomasyvaliente.madrid-ias.eu) with the annexes and documents before the deadline. Reserve candidates may be contacted until 15 July 2027.
opportunities.notes: Check that your project clearly fits one of the Casa de Velázquez scientific areas, since projects outside them are declared inadmissible.

opportunities.title: MIAS Short-Term Research Stays: François Chevalier and Lucienne Domergue Programmes
opportunities.provider: Madrid Institute for Advanced Study (MIAS) and Casa de Velázquez
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders in the humanities, social sciences or arts can apply for a funded three-month residency in Madrid, with extra travel aid for applicants from Africa.
opportunities.description:
The François Chevalier and Lucienne Domergue programmes offer three-month research residencies at the Madrid Institute for Advanced Study for researchers who already hold a PhD. The 2026 call funds stays between 1 September 2027 and 31 July 2028, with housing at the Casa de Velázquez, and accepts projects in the humanities, social sciences and arts.

Chevalier stays focus on the Iberian Peninsula, Latin America and the Maghreb in relation to the Peninsula. The Lucienne Domergue strand, run with the Institut français d'Espagne, prefers researchers linked to French research centres and requires French.

The call is especially relevant to African scholars: it names applicants from Africa and Latin America as eligible for an extra mobility payment, and the Maghreb is one of its research regions.
opportunities.benefits: 1,000 euros per month for three months; a travel contribution of up to 250 euros between Madrid and your country of residence; an extra mobility aid of up to 300 euros that applicants from Africa or Latin America may request; housing at the Casa de Velázquez (subject to availability, not for families or minors); and 5 euros per weekday towards lunch. Visa and insurance are the researcher's own responsibility.
requirements: Hold a PhD
Good command of at least two of Spanish, English and French (French is essential for the Domergue strand)
Not have lived in Spain for more than 12 months in the 3 years before the deadline
A research project in humanities, social sciences or arts that can be done in a three-month stay in Madrid
No MIAS residency in the last 5 years
documents: Short CV using Annex I (max 4 pages) in Spanish, French or English
Up to two optional reference letters (Annex II)
Research project summary (Annex III) in English plus Spanish or French, max 6 pages per language, bibliography max 2 pages
Copy of ID card or passport
PhD certificate showing the award date (certified translation if not in Latin script)
opportunities.selection_process: The MIAS International Scientific Advisory Council and Governing Board score applications: CV and scientific merit (0-25), interest, originality and feasibility of the project (0-50), and participation in national and international activities (0-25). A provisional result is published from 1 April 2027, followed by 10 working days for claims.
opportunities.about_provider: The Madrid Institute for Advanced Study (MIAS) is a joint research centre of the Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (UAM) and the Casa de Velázquez, the French school in Madrid. It joined the NetIAS network of European institutes for advanced study in 2019 and UBIAS in 2020.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the MIAS short-stay platform (short-term.madrid-ias.eu), verify your email, upload the annexes and documents, and submit before 17:00 Madrid time on 7 December 2026. Applications are online only, and your CV and project cannot be changed after the deadline. Questions go by email to contact@madrid-ias.eu.
opportunities.notes: African applicants should request the additional mobility aid in the application. Up to 27 months of residency are shared across all three-month stays in this call.

opportunities.title: MIAS Tomás y Valiente (MOTyVES) Fellowship
opportunities.provider: Madrid Institute for Advanced Study (MIAS) and Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences, 3 to 10 years after their PhD, can apply for one of three 3-to-5-year contracts at UAM in Madrid.
opportunities.description:
The Tomás y Valiente UAM MOTyVES 2026 call offers three research contracts at the Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, hosted with the Madrid Institute for Advanced Study. Contracts last three years and can be extended for two more, up to 60 months, and may lead to a permanent UAM post if the fellow meets the Spanish ANECA requirements.

The call is co-funded by the European Union's MSCA COFUND 'Choose Europe for Science' scheme and targets early and mid-career researchers in the social and legal sciences and the humanities. Fellows join a UAM department and also work at MIAS, starting on 1 September 2027.

No nationality restriction is stated, so African researchers with a PhD obtained 3 to 10 years ago and recent research experience outside UAM can compete for one of the best-paid humanities postdoctoral positions in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Annual gross salary of about 60,909 euros (monthly employer cost 6,085 euros) plus a mobility allowance of 615 euros a month, and 7,500 euros a year for research and training costs. Optional Casa de Velázquez housing for the first year at 500 euros a month.
requirements: PhD defended between 3 and 10 years before the end of the year the call was published (extensions for parental leave, illness, caring duties or service)
Legally able to sign a Spanish employment contract
Not have lived or worked in Spain for more than 12 months in the 36 months before the call opened
At least one year of contracted research at an institution other than UAM in the last three years
Not previously held a Tomás y Valiente, Ramón y Cajal, ATRAE, César Nombela or similar contract
Project in the social and legal sciences or humanities, linked to a UAM department listed in Annex I
documents: CV in English using Annex II (max 4 pages, with publications)
Up to two reference letters in English (Annex III)
Research project in English (Annex IV), max 8 pages plus a 2-page bibliography
Copy of ID card or passport
PhD certificate with the award date
Sworn statement on qualifications (Annex V) and proof of the residence and research-experience conditions
opportunities.selection_process: Two external reviewers score merit (0-40), internationalisation (0-15), project quality and feasibility (0-35) and fit with MOTyVES aims (0-10); only candidates above 80 points go on. They then have an interview, scored 0-10 by the MIAS International Scientific Advisory Committee, in Spanish or English.
opportunities.about_provider: The Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (UAM) is a leading Spanish public university. MIAS, its joint institute with the Casa de Velázquez, supports the call and hosts the fellows.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the MOTyVES guide for applicants, then apply online through the MIAS Bataillon and Tomás y Valiente portal with all annexes before the deadline. Questions can go to mias@madrid-ias.eu or programa.propio.inv@uam.es.
opportunities.notes: Only three contracts are offered, so the project's alignment with a named UAM department matters. Keep proof of every period you claim as a career-break extension.

opportunities.title: Soka University Scholarship for International Graduate Students (September 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Japanese applicants admitted to Soka graduate programmes through exams that include scholarship selection.
opportunities.description:
Soka University's Scholarship for International Graduate Students gives partial support towards tuition and living costs for non-Japanese students in its graduate schools in Tokyo. Master's students receive JPY 500,000 a year for two years; doctoral students receive JPY 400,000 a year for three years.

For the September 2027 master's intake, the scholarship is linked to the February Examination for International Students in the Graduate School of Economics (International Business Studies Program). Awards go to the applicants with the highest results among those who pass.

African applicants with foreign citizenship qualify if they meet the admission requirements and apply through an examination that includes scholarship selection.
opportunities.benefits: Master's: JPY 500,000 per year for two years. Doctoral (April intake only): JPY 400,000 per year for three years. Paid in two instalments per year after enrolment; cannot be used for the admission fee or first-semester tuition. Master's tuition is JPY 650,000 per year and the admission fee JPY 200,000.
requirements: Non-Japanese nationality
Qualifies for admission to the graduate programme
Applies through an entrance exam that includes scholarship selection (September master's: February Examination for International Students, Economics IBSP)
documents: Online application in the TAO system, indicating the wish to be considered for the scholarship
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarships go to the highest-scoring applicants among those who pass the relevant entrance exam; results come with the admission results.
opportunities.about_provider: Soka University is a private university in Hachioji, Tokyo, founded in 1971, with undergraduate and graduate schools and many international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the TAO system for the relevant entrance exam and tick the scholarship option. Check Soka's graduate admissions guidelines for the exam dates.

opportunities.title: YSI and IM-TCD Pre-Conference Workshop on Digital Money 2027
opportunities.provider: INET Young Scholars Initiative and Trinity College Dublin
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students and postdocs of any nationality working on digital money and payments can apply to present at this free Dublin workshop with travel stipends for presenters.
opportunities.description:
The Young Scholars Initiative (YSI) Financial Stability Working Group and the Department of Economics at Trinity College Dublin are holding a one-day pre-conference workshop for young researchers on digital money and the future of payments. It takes place at Trinity College Dublin on 11 January 2027, the day before the main conference that Trinity and the Central Bank of Ireland host on 12-13 January 2027.

The workshop covers stablecoins, crypto-assets, central bank digital currencies and payment systems, and particularly welcomes advanced research projects. There is no registration fee, meals are provided, and presenters receive a travel stipend.

The call has no nationality restriction, so African PhD students and postdocs working on monetary economics and fintech can present their work to central bankers and researchers.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee, meals for all participants and a travel stipend for presenters (amount not stated).
requirements: PhD student or postdoctoral researcher
Research on digital money, stablecoins, crypto, CBDCs or payment systems
Advanced research projects are particularly encouraged
opportunities.about_provider: The Young Scholars Initiative is the early-career network of the Institute for New Economic Thinking (INET), with thematic working groups that run workshops and conferences. Trinity College Dublin is Ireland's oldest university.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your paper or extended abstract through the Google form linked on the YSI event page by 7 December 2026. Problems with the form go to Giuseppe Gurrado (gurradog@tcd.ie).
opportunities.notes: Check Irish visa timelines early, since the workshop is only five weeks after the deadline. Contacts: Giuseppe Gurrado and Maylis Avaro at Trinity College Dublin.

opportunities.title: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students from 19 African Commonwealth countries who hold at least a 2:1 and cannot afford UK study can apply for a fully funded one-year UK master's.
opportunities.description:
Commonwealth Shared Scholarships fund one-year master's degrees at participating UK universities for talented students from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford to study in the UK. The awards are for 2027/28 entry, starting in September or October 2027, and are jointly paid for by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) and the host university.

Applicants choose from a list of approved master's courses, must secure admission to the course, and apply both to the university and through the CSC's online system. Each university selects and nominates its candidates to the CSC in March 2027.

The scheme is open to citizens of 19 African countries, making it one of the main fully funded UK master's routes for African students focused on development impact.
opportunities.benefits: Return airfare to the UK; full tuition fees; a stipend of £1,712 a month (£2,000 a month in London); a thesis grant; a study travel grant; a contribution to a TB test where needed for the visa; and, for widowed, divorced or single-parent scholars, a child allowance of £622 a month for the first child and £154 for the second and third under 16. No application fee.
requirements: Citizen of, or refugee in, an eligible Commonwealth country (African list: Botswana, Eswatini, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia)
Permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country
First degree of at least upper second class (2:1), or a lower second plus a relevant postgraduate qualification, by September 2027
Not studied or worked for more than one academic year in a high-income country
Unable to afford UK study without the scholarship
Available to start in the UK by September 2027; no age limit
documents: Full transcripts of all higher education, with certified translations if not in English
At least two signed references in PDF, uploaded to CSC Central
opportunities.selection_process: Each participating university runs its own selection and nominates candidates to the CSC in March 2027. Candidates are judged on merit, the quality of their study plan and its likely impact on their home country's development.
opportunities.about_provider: The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK is funded by the UK government and runs scholarships and fellowships with international development aims. Shared Scholarships are co-funded with UK universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Pick an approved course at a participating university and apply for admission there, then complete the Commonwealth Shared Scholarship application on CSC Central (portal.csccentralonline.org.uk) by 16:00 GMT on 8 December 2026. Everything, including references, must be submitted inside the system; incomplete applications are ineligible.
opportunities.notes: The CSC does not set an IELTS requirement, but your university may. Check each university's own internal deadline, which can be earlier than the CSC's.

opportunities.title: David E. Bell Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: Harvard Center for Population and Development Studies
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhDs (completed August 2024 to August 2027) of any nationality working on population and development can apply for a Harvard postdoctoral fellowship.
opportunities.description:
The Harvard Bell Postdoctoral Fellowship (David E. Bell Fellowship) supports early-career researchers working on population and development at the Harvard Center for Population and Development Studies. The current call recruits the 2027-2029 cohort of Bell Fellows.

Applicants must have completed their doctorate between 13 August 2024 and 13 August 2027, and the programme welcomes international as well as US scholars. Applications are made through an online form with a research proposal, writing sample and three recommendation letters.

Because the fellowship is not federally funded and is open to international applicants, African demographers, economists and public-health researchers are eligible to apply.
opportunities.benefits: A Harvard postdoctoral appointment with salary and benefits (amounts not stated on the pages read).
requirements: Doctorate completed between 13 August 2024 and 13 August 2027, with proof by 13 August 2027
Open to US and international scholars
Research in population and development
documents: Three recommendation letters on letterhead, sent through a separate portal by the deadline
important_dates: Doctorate completion window: 13 August 2024 to 13 August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Harvard Center for Population and Development Studies is an interdisciplinary research centre at Harvard that studies population health and development.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the Harvard Qualtrics application form with your CV, proposal and writing sample, and give your three referees the separate letter portal link so their letters arrive by noon ET on 8 December 2026. Referees should state how long they have known you, rank you and comment on your writing, analysis and creativity.
opportunities.notes: International applicants should read the Harvard International Office visa guidance. Contact: popcenter@hsph.harvard.edu.

opportunities.title: Exeter EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award Studentships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with a first or 2:1 (or equivalent) in science, engineering or technology, from the UK or abroad, applying to a listed Exeter PhD project.
opportunities.description:
The University of Exeter is offering up to 16 fully funded PhD studentships for September 2027 under its EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award. Each studentship is tied to a listed research project in science, engineering or technology, and lasts up to three and a half years of full-time study.

Up to 30 per cent of places can go to international candidates, including Africans. International award holders have their full tuition covered through the home fee rate plus an Exeter fee waiver, and they receive the same stipend and research budget as UK students.

Applicants choose a project from Exeter's list and apply through the link in that project's description.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees; an index-linked stipend for up to 3.5 years (currently £21,805 per year for 2026/27); a research training support grant of £5,000 over 3.5 years. International students pay their own visa, health surcharge and relocation costs.
requirements: First or upper second-class UK honours degree (or equivalent) in a relevant science, engineering or technology subject
Lower second considered with a master's degree or significant relevant experience
Home or international fee status (international places capped at about 30%)
Proof of English for nationals of non-majority-English-speaking countries
Some projects set extra requirements
documents: Personal statement naming the project at the top
Two references emailed by referees from institutional addresses to PGRApplicants@exeter.ac.uk
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are shortlisted, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed in February 2027. Offers are made in early March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Exeter is a research-intensive UK university in south-west England and a member of the Russell Group. The Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), part of UK Research and Innovation, funds the Doctoral Landscape Award.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a project on Exeter's EPSRC DLA project list, then apply only through the application link at the bottom of that project's PDF before midday on 8 December 2026. Applications sent by other routes are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Put the project title at the top of your personal statement and name each PDF with your surname. The official page mixes 2026 and 2027 in a few dates; the 2027 cycle is intended.

opportunities.title: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Citizens of any country outside the UK applying for a full-time PhD, MLitt or one-year master's at Cambridge can be considered for a full Gates Cambridge Scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The Gates Cambridge Scholarship funds outstanding applicants from any country outside the UK to take a full-time postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge. For entry in 2027/28 it covers PhD and MLitt study and one-year postgraduate courses (with some exceptions), plus a part-time PhD pilot.

There is no separate application: candidates apply for their Cambridge course through the University's graduate portal and complete the Gates Cambridge section by their course's funding deadline. For applicants outside the US, that deadline is either 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 depending on the course, as shown in the Cambridge course directory.

The scholarship looks for intellectual ability, leadership and a commitment to improving the lives of others, and it is open to African applicants on equal terms with all non-UK citizens.
opportunities.benefits: A full-cost scholarship for postgraduate study at Cambridge (the pages read do not list amounts).
requirements: Citizen of any country outside the UK
Applying for a full-time PhD, MLitt or one-year postgraduate course at Cambridge (or the part-time PhD pilot)
Not eligible: undergraduate degrees, MASt, MBA/EMBA and other part-time courses
Current Cambridge students may apply only for a new course
documents: Answers to the four Gates Cambridge questions (about 200-300 words each)
opportunities.selection_process: Departments first rank and nominate candidates; the Trust then shortlists and interviews them. Criteria are intellectual ability, reasons for the course choice, commitment to improving the lives of others, and leadership potential.
important_dates: Course funding deadline: 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, by course (11:59 pm UK time)
opportunities.about_provider: The Gates Cambridge Trust was established with a gift from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation to fund postgraduate scholars from outside the UK at the University of Cambridge.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find your course in the Cambridge course directory to see whether its funding deadline is 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, apply through the University's graduate application portal and tick the Gates Cambridge option, and complete the funding section and Gates reference by that date.
opportunities.notes: The US round closed on 14 October 2026. Contact: info@gatescambridge.org.

opportunities.title: INSEAD Master in Management Women's Merit Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Women of any nationality admitted to INSEAD's Master in Management for August 2027 can receive a 20,000-25,000 euro merit scholarship.
opportunities.description:
INSEAD's MIM Women's Merit Scholarship rewards exceptional women joining its Master in Management, a 14-month full-time programme taught across its France and Singapore campuses. Several awards are made each year for the August 2027 intake.

There is no separate scholarship form: candidates are considered automatically from their admission application, and awards are announced after admission. Scholarships are available in every application round; Round 2 closes on 8 December 2026, followed by Round 3 (23 February 2027) and Round 4 (27 April 2027).

The award is open to women of any nationality, so African women with a bachelor's degree and a GMAT or GRE score can compete for a significant reduction of the programme fee.
