opportunities.title: Bangor University Vice-Chancellor Scholarship (January 2027 intake)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded international undergraduate and taught master's students with an offer from Bangor and outstanding grades.
opportunities.description:
Bangor University's Vice-Chancellor Scholarships are its flagship awards for excellent international students. They take £10,000 off tuition in the first year of an undergraduate or taught postgraduate degree, with up to £6,000 a year in later years for longer courses.

This entry covers the January 2027 intake, for which one undergraduate and one taught postgraduate award are available, closing on 11 December 2026. Later rounds close on 9 April 2027 (May intake, postgraduate) and 28 May 2027 (September intake, ten awards each level).

There is no nationality restriction, so self-funding African students who already hold a Bangor offer can apply.
opportunities.benefits: A £10,000 tuition fee discount in year 1; up to £6,000 per year in subsequent years.
requirements: Undergraduate: A grades (or equivalent) in at least half of subjects plus notable extra-curricular achievements; full 3- or 4-year on-campus degree, no advanced standing
Postgraduate taught: equivalent of a UK first-class bachelor's and a commitment to sustainable development
Must pay international fees and be self-funded (not fully sponsored)
Full-time, on campus; not BUIC or study-abroad students
Must already hold an offer from Bangor
documents: An offer of study from Bangor University
opportunities.selection_process: Bangor reviews scholarship applications from offer holders against the academic and extra-curricular criteria; winners are told by early January 2027 for the January intake.
important_dates: Offer conditions met by: 1 December 2026 (January intake)
opportunities.about_provider: Bangor University is a public university in north Wales, UK, known for environmental sciences, psychology and ocean sciences among other fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First obtain an offer from Bangor, then complete the online scholarship application form linked from the Vice-Chancellor Scholarships page before the deadline for your intake. Winners must return an acceptance form and tuition deposit within two weeks.
opportunities.notes: Only one award is available per level for January 2027, so competition is tight; the September 2027 round has ten awards per level. Undergraduate winners must make Bangor their firm choice.

opportunities.title: ESRC South East Doctoral Training Arc (SEDarc) Studentships
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality with a social-science project that fits a SEDarc theme can apply for an October 2027 PhD at Reading, but international candidates must fund the gap between UK and international fees.
opportunities.description:
The South East Doctoral Training Arc (SEDarc) is a doctoral training partnership funded by the UK Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC). It brings together six universities, Royal Holloway, Kent, Kingston, Reading, Surrey and Sussex, and funds social-science PhDs that start in October 2027. This entry follows the University of Reading route, where candidates first apply to Reading and are then nominated to the partnership.

Projects must fit one of five SEDarc themes, such as Inclusive Economic Growth or Living Sustainably, and subjects include Economics, Education, Human Geography, Linguistics, and Politics and International Relations. A studentship lasts 3.5 years with a three-month placement, or 3.25 years without one, and some awards add a master's year for applicants who do not already hold a social-science master's.

For African applicants the award is a route into a fully structured UK PhD with a stipend, but it is important to plan finances carefully: the ESRC covers only the UK-rate fee, so international students must find the difference themselves.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition at the UK (home) rate; the UKRI stipend of £21,805 a year (2026/27 rate); a £1,000 travel fund for the placement. International students must pay the difference between home and international fees themselves (about £16,512 to £19,212 a year at 2026/27 rates). Visa costs and the NHS surcharge are not covered.
requirements: Open to UK and international applicants
Research project that fits one of the five SEDarc themes
Social-science subject area (e.g. economics, education, human geography, linguistics, politics and IR)
International candidates must fund the gap between UK and international fees
No more than 30% of SEDarc awards go to international students
documents: University of Reading PhD application via the RISIS portal
SEDarc application template (supplied to nominated candidates)
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates first talk to the relevant academic at Reading and apply for a Reading PhD with a draft proposal. Reading then nominates its strongest candidates, who submit a full application to SEDarc for a partnership-wide competition. Outcomes are expected in April 2027.
important_dates: Expressions of interest: end of November 2026
Final SEDarc applications from nominees: 29 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: SEDarc is one of the ESRC's doctoral training partnerships in England, linking six universities in the south east to train social scientists. The University of Reading is a research-intensive UK university and one of the partners.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact the subject academic listed on the Reading page about your project, then apply for a PhD at Reading through the RISIS portal with a draft SEDarc proposal by 11 December 2026. If Reading nominates you, complete the SEDarc application template by 29 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Reading's site also lists AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards and Centenary PhD Bursaries, which may suit humanities applicants.

opportunities.title: FANE Research Support Fund for Master's Students (Université Sainte-Anne) 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time Canadian or international students starting their master's thesis in francophone cultures at Université Sainte-Anne can apply by 11 December 2026 for a one-off $3,500 research award.
opportunities.description:
The Fédération acadienne de la Nouvelle-Écosse (FANE) funds a research award at Université Sainte-Anne for a master's student who is beginning to write a thesis on a contemporary issue facing Acadian society. The award is a single, non-renewable grant of $3,500.

It is linked to the university's Master of Arts in francophone cultures and spaces (Maîtrise en cultures et espaces francophones). Projects focused on Acadian Nova Scotia get priority, but comparative approaches are welcome, which can suit international students who compare Acadian issues with francophone communities elsewhere, including in Africa.

The award is open to both Canadian and international students, so it is mainly relevant to African francophone students who are already enrolled, or about to enrol, in this master's programme.
opportunities.benefits: A one-off research award of $3,500 (not renewable).
requirements: Full-time student at Université Sainte-Anne
At the start of writing the master's thesis (MA cultures et espaces francophones)
Research on a contemporary issue in Acadian society; Nova Scotia Acadian projects prioritised
Canadian and international students eligible
Mandatory master's coursework completed
documents: Letter of intent of up to two pages (project, methodology, progress, how the award helps)
Letter of support from the thesis director
Transcript showing completion of the mandatory master's courses
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reviews the applications and selects one recipient.
opportunities.about_provider: Université Sainte-Anne is Nova Scotia's only French-language university, with its main campus at Church Point. It serves Acadian and francophone communities in Atlantic Canada and welcomes many students from francophone Africa.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email the letter of intent, the thesis director's support letter and the transcript to the coordinator of the Maîtrise en cultures et espaces francophones before the deadline. The university's recruitment office (1-888-338-8337) can supply the coordinator's contact.
opportunities.notes: This is a small internal award for enrolled students rather than an entrance scholarship.

opportunities.title: Postgraduate Research Scholarship in Transnational Musical Exchange
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Domestic and international applicants for a full-time PhD or DMA in transnational musical exchange at the Sydney Conservatorium can apply for a stipend and fee scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The University of Sydney offers a postgraduate research scholarship for a PhD or Doctor of Musical Arts on transnational musical exchange at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music. Applications opened on 24 September 2026 and close on 11 December 2026.

The scholarship pays a living stipend at the Australian Research Training Program rate for up to 12 research periods and, for international applicants, covers course fees. Applicants must choose a lead supervisor from Associate Professors Coady, Harris or Case.

International students, including African musicologists and performers, can apply if they hold or obtain an unconditional offer for full-time doctoral study.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend at the Research Training Program rate for up to 12 research periods, plus course fees for international students (dollar amounts not stated).
requirements: Unconditional offer for, or enrolment in, full-time PhD or DMA study at the Sydney Conservatorium
A master's by research, a coursework master's with a research component, or a bachelor's with First Class Honours
Nominate a lead supervisor from Coady, Harris or Case
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic merit, the research proposal, CV and referee reports, and may be interviewed.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Sydney is Australia's oldest university, and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music is its music school.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact your chosen supervisor, apply for doctoral admission, and complete the scholarship Formstack application linked on the scholarship page by 11 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Enquiries: 1800 793 864 within Australia or +61 2 8627 1444.

opportunities.title: Sophia University New Student and Benefactors' Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants to Sophia University's English-taught degree programmes who will hold a Student visa, have strong grades and need financial help can apply; the Adachi award is reserved for students from listed countries including several African ones.
opportunities.description:
Sophia University in Tokyo runs two first-year tuition scholarships for new international students in its English-taught programmes: the New Student Scholarship and the Benefactors' (Adachi) Scholarship. Both aim to help academically strong students who have chosen Sophia as their first choice but face financial difficulty.

The New Student Scholarship reduces first-year tuition by one third, one half or the full amount and is open to any nationality. The Adachi Scholarship pays full first-year tuition plus the education enhancement fee and is reserved for students from a list of Southeast Asian and African countries, among them Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Mozambique and South Africa.

The undergraduate window covers the Autumn 2027 intake and the second Spring 2027 round, while graduate applicants have separate windows. For African students admitted to an English-taught programme, the Adachi award can remove the full cost of the first year's tuition.
opportunities.benefits: New Student Scholarship: one third, half or all of first-year tuition. Adachi Scholarship: full first-year tuition plus the education enhancement fee. Entrance and enrolment fees are not covered, and both awards apply to the first year only.
requirements: Applicant to one of Sophia's English-taught undergraduate or graduate programmes listed on the page
Must hold a Student visa at admission
Excellent academic record
Demonstrated financial hardship
Adachi award: citizen of one of the listed Southeast Asian or African countries
documents: Typed scholarship application form with signed pledge
Income certificate of the financial supporter for 2025, in English or Japanese
Applicants whose families live in Japan: original residence, tax and enrolment certificates
opportunities.selection_process: Sophia screens the documents and decides on the basis of the applicant's financial situation and academic grades.
important_dates: Undergraduate (Autumn 2027 and second-round Spring 2027): 11 November to 11 December 2026
Autumn 2027 graduate and transfer applicants: 10 March to 7 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Sophia University is a private Jesuit university in central Tokyo, known for its international programmes taught in English. Its Center for Student Affairs administers the scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the scholarship form and gather the financial documents, then post them to the Center for Student Affairs by registered mail or EMS, separately from your admission documents. Email submission is accepted only if postal service is unavailable; questions go to scholarship-co@sophia.ac.jp.
opportunities.notes: Late applications are not accepted. The awards cover only the first year, so plan funding for later years.

opportunities.title: UCC Futures Scholars PhD Programme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality with a 1.1/2.1 honours degree or a master's, supported by a UCC lead supervisor, can apply for a fully funded PhD at University College Cork starting 1 October 2027.
opportunities.description:
The UCC Futures Scholars Programme is a new PhD scholarship scheme at University College Cork in Ireland, funded through Research Ireland's Empower initiative. Award holders are also recognised as Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholars. The 2027 call is a pilot intake open to all disciplines, with applications reviewed by panels leaning towards either STEM or the arts, humanities and social sciences.

Each scholarship provides an annual stipend of EUR 25,000, a tuition contribution of up to EUR 5,750 a year (UCC waives any remaining non-EU fee), and at least EUR 5,000 a year for research costs. New entrants can be funded for up to four years; students who registered for their first PhD year between 1 September 2026 and 31 August 2027 can be funded for up to three years. The PhD starts on 1 October 2027.

The call is explicitly open to applicants of all nationalities with no age limit, which makes it a strong option for African graduates. The key step is finding a UCC lead supervisor early, because the supervisor submits the application through UCC's research system before 5pm Irish time on 11 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of EUR 25,000 per year; tuition contribution up to EUR 5,750 per year (any remaining non-EU fee waived by UCC); at least EUR 5,000 per year in research costs; up to 4 years for new entrants (3 years for current first-year PhD students). Awardees pay the annual postgraduate capitation fee.
requirements: Open to all nationalities, no age limit
First or Upper Second Class Honours degree (1.1/2.1) or a master's, or international equivalent (to be completed by 30 September 2027)
English meeting UCC's postgraduate English language policy
A UCC lead supervisor with a Pure research profile
No previous doctoral degree or doctoral scholarship; not permanent university staff
Full-time study with no full-time employment during the award
documents: Research proposal of up to 2,700 words
opportunities.selection_process: Eligibility check, written review and shortlisting, then an online interview (a 3-minute presentation plus structured questions) and a final decision by the UCC Futures Scholarship Board. Weighting: applicant profile and training plan 45%, research project 45%, research environment 10%.
important_dates: Admission documents in UCC Apply: by 1 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: University College Cork is a public research university in Cork, Ireland. It runs the UCC Futures programmes to recruit doctoral and postdoctoral researchers in priority research areas.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact a potential UCC supervisor with your CV and project idea, then prepare the application form and proposal together. The lead supervisor submits the application in UCC Pure (applicants cannot submit directly) before the deadline. Questions go to uccempowerapplications@ucc.ie.
opportunities.notes: Only one application per applicant, and the whole grant must be accepted. Some departments set earlier internal dates for expressions of interest (the French department asked for them by 15 November), so contact supervisors immediately.

opportunities.title: WGSSS ESRC Doctoral Studentships 2027
opportunities.provider: Welsh Graduate School for the Social Sciences (ESRC)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a first or upper-second UK-equivalent degree or a master's can apply for a WGSSS ESRC social-science PhD at the University of South Wales starting October 2027; up to 30% of the cohort may be international.
opportunities.description:
The Wales Graduate School for the Social Sciences (WGSSS) is the ESRC-funded doctoral training partnership for Wales. Through the University of South Wales it offers studentships starting in October 2027 in two pathways: Social Care, Social Work and Social Policy, and Law and Criminology.

The award runs for 3.5 years as a PhD, or as a 1+3.5 model with a master's first, and includes a compulsory three-month Research in Practice placement. Unlike some UK doctoral awards, international students are not charged the difference between UK and international fees.

This makes it one of the few UK social-science doctoral awards that can be fully funded for African applicants, although competition is strong because no more than 30% of the cohort can be international.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees (international students are not charged the UK/international fee difference); a stipend at the UKRI minimum rate (£21,805 a year full-time in 2026/27); a Research Training Support Grant.
requirements: First or upper-second class UK honours degree or equivalent, or a master's degree
Meet UKRI eligibility rules (up to 30% of the cohort may be international)
Social-science project fitting the Social Care/Social Work/Social Policy or Law and Criminology pathway
English language proof where relevant
Applicants from non-traditional backgrounds are welcome
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are shortlisted, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed, giving a short presentation and answering panel questions.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of South Wales is a public university with campuses in Cardiff, Newport and Pontypridd. WGSSS is the ESRC's doctoral training partnership for Welsh universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the WGSSS application form from the University of South Wales funded-studentships page, complete it with your CV, transcripts and other documents, and arrange two references. Submit everything by 11 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Incomplete applications are not considered. The same page lists AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards (closing 31 January 2027) and a Welsh-medium psychology PhD.

opportunities.title: Comunicazioni Sociali Special Issue: Playing the Anthropocene (Ecogames)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers can submit a 300-400 word abstract by 13 December 2026 for an open-access special issue on ecogames published in September 2027.

opportunities.title: Du Bois Fellows Program 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: Hutchins Center for African & African American Research, Harvard University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Predoctoral and postdoctoral scholars in African and African American studies can apply for a one- or two-semester residency at Harvard's Hutchins Center.
opportunities.description:
The Du Bois Fellows Program at Harvard's Hutchins Center for African & African American Research invites up to twenty predoctoral and postdoctoral scholars a year to spend one or two semesters in residence in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The application for 2027-28 is open, with a deadline of 14 December 2026.

The programme, which began in 1975, has supported more than 700 fellows working in African and African American studies. Fellows pursue their own research projects within the Hutchins Center's community.

It is one of the best-known residential fellowships for scholars of Africa and the African diaspora, and there is no application fee.
important_dates: Residency: one or two semesters in 2027-28
opportunities.about_provider: The Hutchins Center for African & African American Research at Harvard University is home to the W. E. B. Du Bois Research Institute and many research and arts programmes on Africa and the diaspora.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create a SlideRoom account and submit the Du Bois Fellows application there by 14 December 2026; letters of recommendation are due by 21 December 2026. There is no fee.
opportunities.notes: The Black Film Project fellowship has a separate application on Submittable. Contact: Dr Lori De Lucia, loridelucia@fas.harvard.edu.

opportunities.title: Humboldt Residency Programme 2027: Oceanic Horizons
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers and Humboldt alumni based outside Germany, plus journalists, artists and civil-society practitioners, can apply for a funded six-week ocean-themed residency in Germany.
opportunities.description:
The Humboldt Residency Programme brings together twelve people from research, the arts and civil society for a six-week residency in Germany around one annual theme. The 2027 theme is 'Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet'.

The programme runs from a virtual kick-off on 29 June 2027 to a virtual wrap-up on 26 October 2027. The in-person part, which is mandatory, is two weeks at Schloss Wiepersdorf in Brandenburg (2-13 August) and four weeks in Berlin (13 August to 10 September), with excursions to Germany's northern coasts. Participants create outputs for non-academic audiences.

Places are split between Humboldt alumni (5), early-career researchers (3) and civil-society practitioners such as journalists, artists and NGO staff (4). Researchers must be based outside Germany, which suits African scientists and practitioners working on oceans and coasts.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly allowance during the residency, travel to and from Germany, accommodation (two weeks at Schloss Wiepersdorf, four weeks in a Berlin aparthotel), a budget for public events or outputs, and support with family accommodation and childcare for accompanying dependants (amounts not stated).
requirements: Early-career researchers: PhD ongoing or completed less than four years before August 2027, academic position, based outside Germany, science-communication experience
Humboldt alumni: relevant expertise, academic position, based outside Germany, no other Humboldt funding from August 2027
Civil-society practitioners: no current academic post; creatives or practitioners with a clear link to the ocean theme
Full in-person participation from 2 August to 10 September 2027
documents: Introduction video (max 60 seconds, landscape 16:9) uploaded via Smash and linked in the form
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee meets in mid-February 2027, with decisions expected at the end of February 2027. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
opportunities.about_provider: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation is a German foundation funded mainly by the Federal Foreign Office that sponsors international research cooperation through fellowships and awards.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Humboldt Foundation's application portal for the residency programme, uploading your CV and linking your video, before 14 December 2026. Questions go to residency@avh.de.
opportunities.notes: An FAQ document linked from the call explains the criteria in detail. Because evaluation is rolling, applying early is wise.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Foreign passport holders with a bachelor's and a GMAT, GRE or CAT score can receive a tuition fee waiver for the MBA.

opportunities.title: Ontario Graduate Scholarship for International Students (Brock University) 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International graduate students applying through Brock University can receive CAD 10,000 for two terms or CAD 15,000 for three terms.

opportunities.title: Sciences Po Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: African citizens under 35 without a master's degree, holding a bachelor's from a partner institution (or from a bridge programme, or with refugee status), can apply for full support for a two-year master's at Sciences Po.
opportunities.description:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Sciences Po funds students from the African continent through a two-year master's degree at Sciences Po in Paris. It is a partnership between Sciences Po and the Mastercard Foundation, which supports young Africans committed to transforming their communities.

The programme covers the scholar's full financial needs during the master's and adds leadership development and mentoring. Applicants must first check their eligibility on the programme platform and then apply for a Sciences Po master's, choosing one of two deadlines depending on when they want their admission decision.

Selection looks beyond grades to the barriers the applicant has overcome, their commitment to Africa's development and their leadership potential.
opportunities.benefits: Full financial support for the two-year master's according to the scholar's needs (the official page does not give amounts), plus a waiver of the Sciences Po application fee.
requirements: Citizen of an African country (dual citizenship with a non-African country is not eligible)
Bachelor's degree from a listed partner institution, or completion of a bridge or mentoring programme, or UNHCR refugee status
Under 35 on 1 September of the year of application
No existing master's degree and first application to this programme
Not a current Sciences Po student or graduate of French higher education
Meet the minimum academic requirements and be admitted to a two-year Sciences Po master's (dual degrees, one-year master's and journalism excluded)
documents: Passport, national ID, UNHCR card or travel document
Bachelor's certificate or proof of current studies
Proof of refugee status if applicable
Written assignments set by the programme
opportunities.selection_process: Eligible applicants complete written assignments and a Zoom interview of about 25 minutes. Reviewers consider the barriers to education the applicant has faced, their commitment to African development and their transformative leadership. Results are communicated in April 2027.
important_dates: Deadline for a master's decision by 11 February 2027: 23 November 2026
Deadline for a master's decision by 1 April 2027: 14 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: Sciences Po is a leading French university in the social sciences, based in Paris. The Mastercard Foundation is a private foundation that funds education and employment opportunities for young people in Africa.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First verify your eligibility on the programme's platform linked from the official page, then create a Sciences Po master's application on admission.sciencespo.fr, which unlocks the fee waiver. Submit everything before your chosen deadline; questions go to info.mcfsp@sciencespo.fr.
opportunities.notes: Scholarship offers are valid only for the academic year in which they are made.

opportunities.title: Surrey Business School PhD Fee-Waiver Studentships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international applicants with two Surrey supervisors can compete for a full PhD fee waiver at Surrey Business School for April 2027 entry.
opportunities.description:
Surrey Business School at the University of Surrey offers competitive PhD fee-waiver studentships for April 2027 entry. They are open to UK and international candidates applying to either the Management and Business PhD or the Hospitality, Tourism, Transport and Events PhD.

The award waives full tuition fees for 36 months of full-time study (72 months part-time) and adds a research training grant, but it does not include a living stipend. Study starts on 1 April 2027 and cannot be deferred.

African applicants can apply as international candidates, but they must plan their own living costs and visa expenses.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee waiver (home or international rate) for 36 months, plus a Research Training Support Grant of £750 a year, up to £2,250 in total. No stipend, visa or accommodation costs are covered.
requirements: Open to UK and international candidates
Meet the entry requirements of the chosen PhD, including English language
Two Surrey supervisors who agree to support the application, with the primary supervisor in Surrey Business School
Start on 1 April 2027 (no deferral)
documents: Fee Waiver Application Form (April 2027), completed with your supervisors
Online PhD application naming the fee waiver and both supervisors
opportunities.selection_process: A panel of academic reviewers scores proposal quality (60%) and applicant quality (40%) on a 1-5 scale; the Executive Dean gives final approval. Results come by the end of February 2027, and no feedback is given.
important_dates: Outcome: by the end of February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Surrey is a research university in Guildford, England, ranked in the QS 2027 top 250. Surrey Business School is part of its Faculty of Arts, Business and Social Sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree a project with two Surrey supervisors, fill in the fee-waiver form with them, apply online for April 2027 entry to the relevant PhD and upload the form, then email it to Dr Sebastiano Massaro (Management and Business) or Dr Jason Chen (Hospitality, Tourism, Transport and Events) by the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Late or incomplete applications are not considered. Budget for living costs, since there is no stipend.

opportunities.title: Toshizo Watanabe International Scholarship FY2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students with a refugee background who live in Japan (or arrive through complementary pathways) and are, or will be, admitted to a Japanese university can apply for this need-based scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The Toshizo Watanabe International Scholarship (TWIS) is a donor-funded award administered by Pathways Japan, an NGO that supports refugee education. The FY2027 round helps students with a refugee background to study at Japanese universities and graduate schools.

It is a grant, not a loan: it pays tuition up to a set limit and a monthly living subsidy that varies with the year of study. Eligibility depends on refugee background and residence status in Japan rather than on nationality, so African refugees living in Japan can apply.

Applicants who live outside Japan cannot apply, unless they are admitted through one of the complementary pathways the programme recognises.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition up to ¥1,700,000 a year (decided case by case) and a monthly living subsidy of up to ¥70,000 (undergraduate years 1-2), ¥60,000 (year 3) or ¥50,000 (year 4 and graduate study). No repayment is required.
requirements: Refugee background, living in Japan with a qualifying status (for example Student or Designated Activities), or admitted through a complementary pathway, or unable to return home because of conflict
12 years of schooling
Demonstrated financial need
Japanese-medium undergraduate study: EJU/JLPT results; other programmes: an English test plus JLPT N4
Accepted, or expecting acceptance, at a Japanese university or graduate school
opportunities.selection_process: Pathways Japan screens the documents, then interviews shortlisted applicants in Tokyo or online.
opportunities.about_provider: Pathways Japan is a non-profit organisation that creates education pathways in Japan for refugees and displaced students. It manages the Toshizo Watanabe scholarship on behalf of its donor.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the FY2027 guidelines and FAQ on the Pathways Japan site, then submit the online application linked from the official page with the supporting documents before 14 December 2026. Shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview.
opportunities.notes: Applicants living outside Japan generally cannot apply. Check the official page for the exact steps, since one step mentions 12 January.

opportunities.title: ACM Web Science Conference 2027 (WebSci'27) Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers from any country can submit full or short papers to WebSci'27 in Singapore by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
WebSci'27, the 19th ACM Web Science Conference, will take place in Singapore from 25 to 28 May 2027, at the National University of Singapore. Its theme is 'Towards a Healthy, Safe, Flourishing and Equitable Web', and it welcomes research on the Web as a sociotechnical system from computing, social science and the humanities.

Full papers (6-10 pages) and short papers (up to 5 pages) in the ACM two-column format are due on 15 December 2026, a firm deadline. Review is double-blind with at least three reviewers, and the best papers are invited to a special issue of ACM Transactions on Social Computing.

African researchers can submit, and limited student travel funding is offered through SIGWEB and WebIST.
opportunities.benefits: Limited student travel funding through SIGWEB and WebIST (amounts not stated). Accepted papers pay a subsidised ACM open-access charge of 500 USD for ACM/SIG members or 750 USD for non-members; waivers are rare.
requirements: Original research on the Web as a sociotechnical system
Full papers 6-10 pages or short papers up to 5 pages, including references
ACM acmart two-column template, anonymised for double-blind review
ORCID requested
opportunities.selection_process: Each paper gets at least three peer reviews plus a senior programme committee member.
opportunities.about_provider: The ACM Web Science Conference is an annual interdisciplinary conference sponsored by ACM and its SIGWEB group.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your paper in the ACM template and submit it as a PDF on EasyChair (conf=websci27) by 15 December 2026. Contact: info@websci27.webscience.org.
opportunities.notes: There is also a PhD symposium call on the conference site.

opportunities.title: African Journalism Studies special issue: African and Global Media Representations of Africa
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars of any nationality can submit research on media representations of Africa to this African Journalism Studies special issue by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
African Journalism Studies, published by Routledge (Taylor & Francis), is calling for papers for a special issue on 'African and Global Media Representations of Africa'. It welcomes empirical, theoretical and methodological work on how Africa is portrayed in African and international media.

Suggested themes include digital and algorithmic media, diaspora media, visual cultures and reparative approaches to representation. Full manuscripts of 6,000 to 8,500 words are due on 15 December 2026.

The guest editors are Sisanda Nkoala (University of the Western Cape), Dani Madrid-Morales (University of Sheffield) and David Cheruiyot (University of Queensland), and the call is a strong outlet for African media and journalism scholars.
requirements: Manuscript of 6,000-8,500 words including abstract, tables, notes and references
Abstract of 150-250 words and 5-6 keywords
Word file, double-spaced, 12-point, 1-inch margins
Fully anonymised, with author details on a separate title page
documents: Separate title page with author details
opportunities.about_provider: African Journalism Studies is a peer-reviewed Routledge journal on journalism and media in and about Africa, published by Taylor & Francis.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Follow the journal's instructions for authors and submit through the Taylor & Francis submission portal for African Journalism Studies (journal code RECQ), selecting the special issue, by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Questions can go to the guest editors listed on the call page.

opportunities.title: EADA International Master's Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Admitted applicants to EADA's international master's programmes in Barcelona can apply for scholarships covering 10-35% of tuition, including an Africa Scholarship.
opportunities.description:
EADA Business School in Barcelona offers scholarships to applicants to its international master's programmes, such as the Master in Management and the Master in AI for Business. The awards reduce tuition and are decided alongside the admission decision.

Most scholarships cover 10 to 25% of tuition, the Scholarship for Excellence can reach 35%, and the diversity scholarships, which include an Africa Scholarship, cover up to 25%. The Master in Management costs €28,000, so the awards can make a real difference for self-funded African students.

Scholarships are awarded in rounds through the year, with earlier rounds for the January 2027 intake and later rounds for October 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition reductions of 10-25%, up to 35% for the Scholarship for Excellence and up to 25% for diversity scholarships (including the Africa Scholarship). Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Complete EADA's admission process first
Programme aimed at talented candidates aged roughly 21-25
Excellence award: outstanding academic record or GMAT 700+
Enrol within 10 working days of the award and take part in an EADA project
Apply for at most two scholarships and receive at most one
opportunities.selection_process: A Scholarship Committee reviews applications and announces the result with the admission decision.
important_dates: January 2027 intake: rounds closing 15 November and 15 December 2026
October 2027 intake: 20 December 2026 (MBA diversity only), then 20 January, 20 February, 20 March, 20 April, 20 May and 20 June 2027 (while funds last)
opportunities.about_provider: EADA Business School is a private business school in Barcelona, Spain, known for its management and MBA programmes with a strong international student body.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the scholarship form with your master's application and email the documents to EADA admissions before the round's deadline. You receive the scholarship decision together with your admission result.

opportunities.title: ENS-PSL International Selection in Sciences 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students under 26 who have completed at least one year of undergraduate study abroad can apply to enter ENS-PSL at L3 or M1 level with a monthly grant.
opportunities.description:
The École normale supérieure (ENS-PSL) in Paris runs an International Selection that admits a small number of foreign students each year into its diploma programme in the sciences. Successful candidates join at third-year bachelor's (L3) or first-year master's (M1) level.

Winners receive a grant of €1,000 a month for 36 months and can ask for a room in an ENS residence. Selection is highly competitive, with only 5 to 10% of candidates admitted, and includes a scientific oral exam and an interview.

For African students with outstanding science records, the selection offers a funded route into one of France's most prestigious research schools.
opportunities.benefits: A grant of €1,000 per month for 36 months, plus the option to request a room in an ENS campus residence.
requirements: Under 26 years old on the day applications open
At least one year of undergraduate study at a foreign university, and two years completed by enrolment
No registration in French higher education for more than six months in the competition year or the year before
Must not have applied before
Entry at L3 or M1 level
documents: Argued cover letter of 1-3 pages (Times New Roman 12, 1.5 spacing)
Two to four recommendation letters requested through the platform
opportunities.selection_process: A jury shortlists candidates from their files, then holds a scientific oral exam (weight 6) and an interview (weight 3). About 5-10% of applicants are selected.
important_dates: Applications: 16 October to 15 December 2026, 14:00 Paris time
opportunities.about_provider: ENS-PSL is a French grande école focused on research and teaching, part of Université PSL in Paris. It trains researchers and teachers across sciences and humanities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply on the OnePSL30 platform (concoursens.candidature.onepsl30.fr), upload your documents and request your recommendation letters through the platform before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Do not use an icloud.com email address. Incomplete applications are rejected. The same page covers an Arts and Humanities track, which requires French at B1.

opportunities.title: EPFL Master Excellence Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students of any nationality applying to an EPFL master's by 15 December 2026 can be considered for a CHF 10,000-per-semester excellence fellowship.
opportunities.description:
EPFL, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, awards Master Excellence Fellowships to a limited number of outstanding students admitted to its master's programmes. The fellowship is donor-funded and pays a stipend each semester, with guaranteed student housing for external candidates.

Anyone applying to an EPFL master's programme can be considered, as long as the application is paid and validated by 15 December. EPFL offers 29 master's programmes across five schools and two colleges, all in Lausanne.

No nationality restriction applies, so African students with excellent academic records can apply for both admission and the fellowship in one step.
opportunities.benefits: CHF 10,000 per semester for up to four semesters (two to three semesters of courses plus the master's project), a guaranteed student room for external candidates, and a certificate of excellence. It cannot be combined with other large scholarships.
requirements: Applying to an EPFL master's programme (one programme per year)
Application paid and validated by 15 December
Not already holding a master's degree or enrolled in an EPFL master's
Renewal for year two needs at least 50 ECTS and a 5.0 average
documents: Reference letters uploaded within one week after the deadline (external candidates)
opportunities.selection_process: Departments screen candidates first, then the Excellence Fellowships Committee chooses, based on academic record and on research, entrepreneurship and social engagement. A waiting list is kept.
important_dates: Reference letters: one week after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: EPFL is one of Switzerland's two federal institutes of technology, based in Lausanne. The fellowship belongs to its Student Support Program's 'Attract Talent' pillar.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to your chosen master's through EPFL's online application, tick the box for the Excellence Fellowship, and pay the fee so the file is validated by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The fellowship is paid into a Swiss bank or postal account. Awards are limited, so a strong academic record is essential.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in International Humanitarian Action (NOHA) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality with a relevant bachelor's and C1 English can apply for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship for the NOHA humanitarian action master's by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The NOHA Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's in International Humanitarian Action is a two-year, 120 ECTS programme taught across a network of European universities: Aix-Marseille, Malta, Groningen, Bochum, Deusto, University College Dublin, Warsaw and Uppsala. The 2027-2029 application round opened on 1 October 2026.

Students spend their first two semesters at NOHA universities, then choose a regional training semester with partner universities worldwide (including Makeni University in Sierra Leone) or a work placement, and finish with a research semester. The programme was the first humanitarian master's in Europe, set up in 1993 with European Commission support, and has more than 3,500 graduates.

For 2027-2029 it offers 16 Erasmus Mundus scholarships, eight of them for partner-country candidates, which includes African applicants; the deadline for scholarship applicants is 15 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: 1,400 euros a month for 24 months, covering travel, visa, installation and living costs. Self-funded students pay 4,000 euros per semester.
requirements: Bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) in a relevant field such as medicine, law, economics, engineering, social sciences, education or humanities, completed before the deadline for scholarship applicants
English at C1: IELTS 6.5 (no part below 6.0), TOEFL iBT, CAE or CPE, unless a native speaker or English-taught degree holder
French C1 for Aix-Marseille or Spanish B2 for Deusto where relevant
No more than 10% of scholarships to one nationality
documents: Diploma and Diploma Supplement (translated if not in English)
Two signed reference letters in English (not older than two years)
Proof of residence issued within 12 months of the deadline (ID cards and bills not accepted)
opportunities.selection_process: A Joint Admissions Board assesses academic record, research, professional and humanitarian experience, motivation, intercultural sensitivity, languages, references and an interview, with attention to nationality and gender balance. Results come in March 2027, with seven days to appeal.
important_dates: Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadline: 15 December 2026, 23:59 GMT
opportunities.about_provider: NOHA is an international association of universities that runs joint education and research in humanitarian action, drawing on more than 150 in-house experts.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online at apply.nohanet.org before 23:59 GMT on 15 December 2026 to be considered for a scholarship. Paper and email applications are not accepted. Questions go to nohamasters@deusto.es.
opportunities.notes: The proof-of-residence rule is strict, so get a certificate of residence from your local authority early.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Neurasmus Scholarship 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Science graduates from any country with IELTS 6.5 or equivalent can apply for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship for the Neurasmus neuroscience master's by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
Neurasmus is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in neuroscience, coordinated by the University of Bordeaux and taught in English by a European university consortium. The 2027-2029 Erasmus Mundus scholarship call opened on 1 September 2026 and closes at noon CET on 15 December 2026.

The programme is for graduates in biology, chemistry, medicine, psychology or other natural sciences with a solid base in biology, chemistry and maths. A separate self-funded call opens on 19 November 2026 and runs to 20 February 2027.

Scholarships are open to students from anywhere in the world, so African graduates compete for partner-country awards, with no more than three students selected per nationality.
opportunities.benefits: For the 2026-2028 edition: a monthly allowance of 1,400 euros and a contribution of 4,500 euros per semester towards participation costs (tuition and insurance). The 2027-2029 amounts were not yet stated.
requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent in natural sciences or a related field (e.g. biology, chemistry, medicine, psychology)
Solid knowledge of biology, chemistry and mathematics
English: IELTS Academic 6.5 (no band below 6), TOEFL iBT 93, CAE/CPE, or proof of English-medium study; tests taken within two years of the start
No more than three students per nationality
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are ranked by the consortium, following EU nationality rules; shortlisted candidates are interviewed in mid-February and results come in March 2027.
important_dates: Scholarship call: 1 September to 15 December 2026, 12:00 noon CET
opportunities.about_provider: The Neurasmus consortium is coordinated from the University of Bordeaux, France, and offers a two-year joint master's degree in neuroscience funded by the EU's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Neurasmus eMundus platform before noon CET on 15 December 2026; paper or email applications are not accepted. Help: neurasmus-application@u-bordeaux.fr.
opportunities.notes: Note the noon deadline rather than midnight. Incomplete files are not considered.

opportunities.title: FEMS MICRO Ljubljana 2027 Attendance Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career microbiologists worldwide who are first author and presenter of an accepted abstract can get free registration for FEMS MICRO Ljubljana 2027.
opportunities.description:
The FEMS MICRO Attendance Grant waives the registration fee for early-career researchers presenting at FEMS MICRO Ljubljana 2027, the congress of the Federation of European Microbiological Societies in Slovenia. Applications are made during abstract submission, which runs from 2 September to 15 December 2026.

The grant is for active microbiologists who are first author and presenter of an accepted abstract, and who are PhD students or hold their highest degree for less than five years.

FEMS states that the grant is for both European and non-European early-career researchers, so African microbiologists can apply.
opportunities.benefits: A full waiver of the congress registration fee (value not stated). The free registration cannot be transferred.
requirements: PhD student, or highest degree (bachelor's, master's or PhD) obtained less than five years before the deadline (leave periods excluded)
Active microbiologist
First author and presenter of an accepted abstract
European and non-European applicants eligible
documents: Abstract, with the grant request made during abstract submission
important_dates: Abstract and grant submission: 2 September to 15 December 2026, 23:59 CET
opportunities.about_provider: The Federation of European Microbiological Societies (FEMS) brings together microbiology societies across Europe, runs the FEMS MICRO congress and funds grants for microbiologists.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract on the FEMS MICRO abstracts site and apply for the attendance grant in the same submission before 15 December 2026. Wait for the grant result before registering.
opportunities.notes: FEMS also offers meeting attendance and research and training grants. Contact: info@fems-microbiology.org.

opportunities.title: Folger Long-Term Public Humanities Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars, artists, writers, educators, community leaders and doctoral candidates of any nationality with a public humanities project on the early modern world can apply for a nine-month residential fellowship in Washington DC.
opportunities.description:
The Folger Shakespeare Library offers Long-term Public Humanities Fellowships for 2027-28 through its Folger Institute. They support projects that combine research on the early modern world, roughly 1400 to 1800, with public engagement.

Fellows receive $70,000 for a standard nine-month period in residence in Washington DC, of which up to three months may be spent working virtually. Each fellow must plan at least one public humanities activity developed with Folger staff, such as a programme, performance or exhibition.

No terminal degree is required and there is no nationality restriction, so African writers, artists and scholars whose work engages early modern history or literature can apply.
opportunities.benefits: $70,000 for a nine-month fellowship, intended to cover travel, housing and living costs; up to three months may be virtual.
requirements: Faculty, independent scholar, artist, writer, PhD candidate, postdoc, community leader, educator or similar
A terminal degree is not required, but equivalent training must be described
Project on the early modern world that uses Folger collections
At least one public humanities engagement developed with Folger staff
documents: Project description of up to 1,500 words, including the public humanities plan and any virtual time
List of Folger primary sources to be used (1-2 pages)
One recommendation letter submitted through the portal
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by the Folger Institute; details of the criteria are in the fellowships FAQ.
opportunities.about_provider: The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington DC holds one of the world's largest collections of early modern books and manuscripts. Its Folger Institute runs fellowships and scholarly programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Folger fellowships portal (onlineapplicationportal.com/folgerfellowships) with your abstract, project description, CV and source list, and ask your referee to upload a letter. Questions go to Ashley Buchanan (abuchanan@folger.edu).
opportunities.notes: The Folger does not provide studio space or archive the resulting materials; check the current COVID vaccination policy.

opportunities.title: Folger Long-Term Scholarly Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars of any nationality with a terminal degree can apply for a year (70,000 USD) or semester (35,000 USD) research fellowship at the Folger in Washington, DC.
opportunities.description:
The Folger Institute at the Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington, DC, offers long-term residential research fellowships for 2027-28. Fellows can stay for a full year (nine months, up to three of them virtual) or a semester (five months, up to one virtual), working with the Folger's collections of early modern books and manuscripts.

Applications opened on 15 September 2026 and close at 11:59 pm Eastern time on 15 December 2026. An external committee, chosen each year for disciplinary and geographic diversity, selects the fellows.

No nationality condition is stated, so African scholars of the early modern world, Shakespeare and the Atlantic can apply.
opportunities.benefits: 70,000 USD for a year-long fellowship or 35,000 USD for a semester, intended to cover travel, housing and living costs. Folger housing or private housing can be used.
requirements: Hold a terminal degree in your field
Apply for either the year-long or the semester fellowship, not both
Project that makes use of the Folger collections
documents: Project description (1,500 words) including on-site and virtual plans
One- to two-page list of the primary sources and rare materials you will use
One recommendation letter through the portal
opportunities.selection_process: An external committee judges impact, relevance, originality and sophistication of approach, feasibility and use of the Folger collections, with most weight on impact, relevance and approach.
opportunities.about_provider: The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington, DC holds the world's largest Shakespeare collection, and its Folger Institute supports research in early modern studies.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your application and request your recommendation letter through the Folger fellowships portal before the deadline. A missing letter does not disqualify you but may weaken the application. Questions go to Institute@Folger.edu.
opportunities.notes: Show clearly which Folger materials your project needs, since use of the collection is a key criterion.

opportunities.title: Harvard Scholars at Risk Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars, writers, artists and independent intellectuals who face persecution because of their beliefs, scholarship or identity, and who are not US citizens or permanent residents, can apply or be nominated.
opportunities.description:
Harvard's Scholars at Risk Program offers fellowships that let threatened academics and intellectuals spend up to ten months or a year at Harvard. Fellows continue their work in safety while the university hosts them.

The fellowship provides a stipend, insurance and travel, with the amounts set according to where the scholar is coming from and how many dependants they bring. It is not a degree programme, and fellows are expected either to return home or to find a longer-term placement afterwards.

African scholars who are at risk because of their research, beliefs or identity can apply directly or be nominated by someone else.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend, health insurance and travel costs, with amounts that depend on the scholar's location and number of dependants; no fixed amounts are published.
requirements: Facing a risk of persecution because of belief, scholarship or identity
Meets Harvard's academic standards (writers, artists and independent intellectuals may qualify)
Not a US citizen or US permanent resident
Some people with permanent residence outside their home country may not be eligible
documents: Application or Nomination Form (Word document) from the programme website
opportunities.selection_process: A Scholars at Risk Committee reviews applications and nominations and may verify the scholar's credentials and the risk they face.
opportunities.about_provider: The Harvard Scholars at Risk Program, part of Harvard University, hosts persecuted scholars and works with the international Scholars at Risk Network.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the single Application or Nomination Form from the programme website; scholars can apply themselves or be nominated. Send it by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The fellowship lasts at most ten months or one year; visa questions go to the Harvard International Office.

opportunities.title: ICTP Surfaces in Trieste: Workshop on Two-Dimensional Dynamics (Apr-May 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students and early-career researchers in two-dimensional dynamics can apply to this free ICTP school and conference, with limited grants that prioritise developing-country participants.
opportunities.description:
Surfaces in Trieste is a two-week ICTP activity (smr 4349) on two-dimensional dynamics, held at the Adriatico Guest House in Grignano, Trieste, Italy, from 26 April to 7 May 2027. The first week (26-30 April) is a school of five mini-courses of about five hours each; the second week (3-7 May) is a research conference built around invited lectures.

The event is aimed at students and early-career researchers working on dynamical systems on surfaces and related geometry and topology, and it gathers a large international team of directors and speakers. It is co-sponsored by CNRS, the European Union and the National Natural Science Foundation of China.

There is no registration fee, and ICTP sets aside a limited number of grants for selected participants, giving priority to people from developing countries. Since African countries are not on ICTP's developed-country list, African applicants fall in the priority group for this support.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants (amounts not stated) support attendance of selected participants, with priority for developing-country participants. Applicants from developed countries may ask for travel support, but their accommodation and meals may not be covered.
requirements: Researcher, student or early-career scientist working in two-dimensional dynamics or related fields
Apply through the ICTP e-applications portal by 15 December 2026
Priority for grants goes to participants from developing countries (African countries included)
documents: Online application on the ICTP portal
Abstract using the template provided on the event page (if presenting)
opportunities.about_provider: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste is a UNESCO Category 1 institute governed jointly by UNESCO, the IAEA and the Government of Italy. It runs schools, workshops and conferences to build scientific capacity, especially in developing countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply here' link on the event page, which opens the ICTP e-applications portal for activity 4349, create an account and complete the form before 15 December 2026. Indicate in the form if you need financial support, and upload an abstract using the template on the event page if you want to present.
opportunities.notes: Grants are limited, so apply well before the deadline and explain clearly why the event matters for your research.

opportunities.title: IEEE ISIE 2027 Call for Papers (Paris, Jun 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Regular papers for the IEEE International Symposium on Industrial Electronics in Paris (15-17 June 2027) are due 15 December 2026; no travel funding is stated on the call.
opportunities.description:
The IEEE International Symposium on Industrial Electronics (ISIE 2027) takes place in Paris, France, from 15 to 17 June 2027. It is a three-day IEEE conference on industrial electronics, and researchers can submit regular papers, work-in-progress papers, special session and tutorial proposals and panel proposals.

Regular papers are due on 15 December 2026, with acceptance decisions on 15 March 2027. Authors who need a visa to travel to France can ask for early acceptance, which is announced on 1 March 2027; this is useful for African authors who usually need a Schengen visa and should plan for long processing times.

The important-dates page does not mention travel grants, so attendance is normally at the author's own cost.
opportunities.benefits: No travel funding is stated on the official important-dates page.
important_dates: Early acceptance for visa requesters: 1 March 2027
opportunities.notes: Ask for early acceptance if you need a visa. Final manuscript and registration dates were still to be confirmed on the official page.

opportunities.title: IHS AI Workforce Faculty Research Grant Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academic scholars researching how artificial intelligence affects jobs, productivity and economic opportunity can apply for up to $20,000.
opportunities.description:
The Institute for Humane Studies (IHS) has issued a request for proposals on AI and the Workforce. It funds academic research on how artificial intelligence shapes employment, productivity, changes in occupations, economic opportunity and innovation over time.

Awards of up to $20,000 support projects that produce peer-reviewed publications, policy white papers or research databases. The money can pay for research costs such as travel, research assistants and data, but not living expenses or overhead.

The page does not limit eligibility by nationality, so African faculty researching the labour-market effects of AI may apply; check the funding FAQ for detailed rules.
opportunities.benefits: Up to $20,000. Eligible costs include travel to conferences and archives, research assistants, datasets, LLM subscriptions and journal or book costs. Living expenses, hardware, retroactive costs and overhead are not covered.
requirements: Academic scholar (the call is aimed at faculty)
Research on AI's effects on employment, productivity, occupations, opportunity or innovation
Planned output: peer-reviewed publication, policy white paper or research database
documents: Online proposal form linked from the official page
opportunities.selection_process: IHS reviews proposals and announces decisions on 15 January 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute for Humane Studies is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) that supports scholars working on ideas of freedom and human flourishing through grants, fellowships and programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit a proposal through the 'Apply Now' form on the IHS AI and the Workforce page before 15 December 2026, describing the research question, planned outputs and budget.
opportunities.notes: IHS also runs Expense Support Grants for Faculty (up to $5,000), the Humane Studies Fellowship and residency funding.

opportunities.title: ITEC Training Scholarships (January-March 2027 courses)
opportunities.provider: Government of India, Ministry of External Affairs
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Public servants from ITEC partner countries can be nominated for fully funded short courses in India; the Tanzania route closes 15 December 2026, other countries vary.

opportunities.title: Joint ICTP-IAEA Workshop on Dose Management Systems (Apr 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Medical physicists, with priority for those from developing countries, can apply to this free ICTP-IAEA workshop in Trieste with limited travel grants.
opportunities.description:
The Joint ICTP-IAEA Workshop on Dose Management Systems (smr 4347) trains medical physicists to set up and quality-assure dose management systems in medical imaging. It runs at ICTP in Trieste, Italy, from 12 to 16 April 2027, and covers DICOM and PACS, dose tracking and imaging quality assurance.

The workshop is co-sponsored by the IAEA, IOMP, EFOMP and AAPM. There is no registration fee, and a limited number of grants support selected participants, with priority for people from developing countries.

African medical physicists working in hospitals and regulators are a core audience for this kind of ICTP-IAEA training.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants (amounts not stated) for selected participants, with priority for developing countries.
requirements: Medical physicist or related professional working with imaging dose management
Apply through the ICTP portal by 15 December 2026
Priority for grants goes to developing-country participants
documents: Online application on the ICTP portal
Optional short abstract on the ICTP template for an oral presentation
opportunities.about_provider: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) is a UNESCO Category 1 institute in Trieste governed by UNESCO, the IAEA and Italy, which runs training activities for scientists from developing countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply here' link on the event page to reach the ICTP e-portal, create an account and submit the form for activity 4347 by 15 December 2026, indicating if you need a grant.
opportunities.notes: Contact: smr4347@ictp.it.

opportunities.title: Keystone Symposia Ending HIV (N4) Global Health Award and Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and postdocs (within 8 years of their doctorate) who present a poster in person can apply for a scholarship of up to 1,500 USD; scientists from and based in LMICs can apply for a Global Health travel award.
opportunities.description:
Ending HIV: At the Crossroads of Innovation and Delivery (N4) is a Keystone Symposia scientific meeting held at the Fairmont Hotel Vancouver in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada on 16-19 May 2027, run jointly with the Vaccinology (N3) meeting. It can be attended in person, by livestream or on demand, and is organised by Julie Ake, Esper Georges Kallas, Darrell J. Irvine and Jeff Murry.

Keystone offers scholarships so that graduate students and postdocs can attend in person and present a poster. The first deadline is for Keystone Global Health Awards (15 December 2026); scholarship applications and short-talk abstracts follow on 19 January 2027, and poster abstracts on 26 April 2027.

Scientists who come from and work in low- and middle-income countries, which includes most African countries, can also apply for a Keystone Global Health Award, which pays registration, lodging and airfare. This makes the meeting a realistic option for African researchers working in this field.
opportunities.benefits: Scholarship: up to 1,500 USD per award, paid as a reimbursement against receipts, towards airfare, ground transport, lodging and part of the registration fee. Global Health Award (for scientists from and based in low- and middle-income countries): a travel award covering meeting registration, lodging and airfare (and ground transport at some venues), with no other costs covered; livestream and on-demand registration options are also offered. Registering early gives a 250 USD discount on in-person registration.
requirements: Be a graduate student, or a postdoc within 8 years of a PhD, MD or DVM (counted to the meeting start date)
Attend the meeting in person
Submit and present a poster abstract
Only one Keystone scholarship per meeting year (1 July to 30 June) and one per lab
Global Health Award: be from, and live or work in, a low- or middle-income country (LMIC)
Global Health Award: open to students, fellows, career scientists and clinicians
Global Health Award: only one travel award per applicant per meeting year
Hold, or be able to obtain, a passport and any visa needed to travel
documents: Abstract (up to 1,000 words; one per person per meeting), with a refundable 50 USD abstract fee for in-person meetings
opportunities.selection_process: Abstracts are reviewed by the meeting organisers. Scholarship applications are judged on the quality and relevance of the abstract, looking at relevance, significance, style and clarity.
opportunities.about_provider: Keystone Symposia on Molecular and Cellular Biology is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) that organises scientific conferences across the life sciences. Alongside its meetings it runs financial-aid schemes, including student and postdoc scholarships and Global Health Awards, the latter supported in part by the Gates Foundation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract through the meeting page and pay the refundable abstract fee, then complete the scholarship (or Global Health Award) application on Keystone's SurveyMonkey Apply portal (keystonesymposia.smapply.us) and arrange for your mentor's letter. All deadlines close at 11:59 pm US Mountain Standard Time. Questions on scholarships go to scholarships@keystonesymposia.org.
opportunities.notes: One scholarship per meeting year and one per lab. Scholarships are reimbursed after the meeting, so keep all receipts. Keystone also lists Early-Career Travel Awards and student discounts on its financial-aid pages.

opportunities.title: Keystone Symposia Neural-Immune Interactions: Immune Modulation of CNS Biology (M2) Scholarships 2027

opportunities.title: MBZUAI MSc and PhD Funded Admission, Fall 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: STEM graduates of any nationality with a CGPA of 3.0-3.5 can apply for fully funded AI MSc and PhD places at MBZUAI for Fall 2027.
opportunities.description:
Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) in Abu Dhabi admits students to fully funded MSc and PhD programmes in artificial intelligence. For Fall 2027 the portal opened on 1 September 2026 and the final deadline is 15 December 2026 at 5 pm Gulf time.

PhD students receive central funding in their first year while they match with a faculty adviser, who funds them from year two. MSc places are funded through faculty-sponsored assistantships, approved government scholarships or merit funding; the fee-paying Master in Applied AI is not funded.

International students, including Africans with strong STEM degrees, apply on the same terms and receive free tuition, a stipend, flights, health insurance and a UAE visa when funded.
opportunities.benefits: Funded students get free tuition, a monthly stipend (listed in AED, for international students 15,500 for MSc and 17,500 for PhD), one return flight a year, health insurance, and a UAE residence visa and Emirates ID. Application fee AED 200, waived if your screening exam score is above 75% or you are admitted.
requirements: STEM bachelor's (e.g. computer science, electrical or computer engineering, maths, physics) from an institution recognised by the UAE Ministry of Education
Minimum CGPA of 3.0 or 3.5 out of 4.0 depending on the programme
English proficiency meeting MBZUAI's criteria
Final-year students can apply with current transcripts
Only one application per cycle
documents: Bachelor's transcript and certificate (or expected-graduation letter)
Master's transcript (PhD applicants with a master's)
Referees: three for PhD, two for MSc
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants sit a screening exam in advanced maths and programming (PhD candidates also machine learning and core computer science); some are invited to a technical interview. Merit funding is considered during review.
opportunities.about_provider: MBZUAI is a graduate research university in Abu Dhabi, UAE, dedicated to artificial intelligence, offering master's and doctoral degrees.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the MBZUAI admissions portal with all documents in English (or legally translated) before 5 pm Gulf time on 15 December 2026, then take the screening exam when invited.
opportunities.notes: Fall 2027 cost figures were still being finalised on the page.

opportunities.title: MOPGA 2027 Visiting Fellowship for Early-Career Researchers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-French researchers with a PhD from the last five years can apply for a 12-month funded climate research stay in a French lab.
opportunities.description:
The Make Our Planet Great Again (MOPGA) 2027 Visiting Fellowship brings early-career foreign researchers to France for a 12-month research stay in a French laboratory. It is funded by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs with the Ministry of Higher Education and Research, and run by Campus France.

Projects must address climate and environmental topics, such as Earth system science, climate and sustainability, the energy transition, environmental social challenges or One Health; purely medical projects are not eligible. Stays start between September and December 2027.

Any nationality except French is eligible, so African researchers who earned their PhD in the last five years can apply with a French host laboratory.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly allowance of 2,500 euros for 12 months plus a 500 euro settling-in payment, with health, civil liability and repatriation insurance. International travel is not covered. It cannot be combined with a French employment contract or other French government funding.
requirements: Doctorate awarded less than five years before the deadline (defended December 2021 to December 2026)
Any nationality except French
Not living and working in France when applying
No previous MOPGA fellowship
A host laboratory in France and a climate or environment project
documents: Support letter from the host supervisor co-signed by the lab director
Project description in the online form
opportunities.selection_process: Experts appointed by the ministry review applications, then a scientific committee makes the final choice; results are expected in May-June 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Campus France is the French national agency for promoting higher education and managing government scholarships. MOPGA was launched by the French government to attract climate researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a host laboratory in France and build the project with them, then apply online on Campus France's SMApply portal (MOPGA 2027) in English or French before 15 December 2026. Emailed applications are not accepted. Contact: mopga@campusfrance.org.
opportunities.notes: Contact host labs early, since the supervisor letter must be co-signed by the lab director.

opportunities.title: P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Women from outside the US and Canada studying for a graduate degree there can apply for up to 12,500 USD in need-based support.
opportunities.description:
The P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship (IPS) gives need-based grants to women from outside the United States and Canada who are studying for a graduate degree at an accredited university in either country. Applications are accepted each year from 15 September to 15 December.

The fund was set up in 1949 to promote world peace through education, and recipients are expected to return home to use their education. Awards are announced in May.

African women admitted to US or Canadian graduate programmes, with at least a full year of coursework left, are eligible.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 12,500 USD per student, with smaller awards based on individual need. It is not meant to cover all costs; applicants must show their other resources.
requirements: Woman from a country other than the US or Canada
Pursuing a graduate degree at an accredited US or Canadian university
At least one full academic year of formal coursework remaining, enrolled and in residence all year
Intend to return home to use your education
Not a US/Canadian citizen or permanent resident; not dissertation-only doctoral students (first-time applicants); no online-only study
documents: Online IPS application form with financial details of other resources
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are based mainly on demonstrated financial need; recipients are announced in May.
opportunities.about_provider: P.E.O. International is a philanthropic women's organisation based in Des Moines, Iowa, that funds education for women through several scholarship and loan programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the IPS application on the P.E.O. online portal between 15 September and 15 December 2026, listing your other funding such as family support, assistantships and scholarships.
opportunities.notes: Read the IPS policies document before applying. Phone: P.E.O. Executive Office, +1 515-255-3153.
