opportunities.title: Politecnico di Milano Merit-Based Scholarships for International MSc Students 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted to the first year of an English-taught MSc at Politecnico di Milano for 2027-28, who paid the application fee by 1 December 2026, can apply for one of 64 merit awards by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
Politecnico di Milano, Italy's largest technical university, offers 64 merit-based scholarships to international students entering the first year of its English-taught Laurea Magistrale (MSc) programmes in the 2027-2028 academic year. The awards cover programmes on the Milan campus and on the regional campuses of Piacenza, Cremona, Lecco and Mantova.

Every award includes a waiver of the tuition fee, and most also pay a cash grant of EUR 2,500 to EUR 10,000 for the year. The application window ran from 1 October 2026 and closes at 12:00 noon Italian time on 15 December 2026; to qualify, students must have applied for admission and paid the application fee between 1 October and 1 December 2026.

The scholarships are a good fit for African engineering, architecture and design graduates who want a well-ranked European technical degree at moderate cost. Priority is given to students from countries affected by war or civil conflict, and the commission also considers geographic balance and gender balance.
opportunities.benefits: All awards waive the tuition fee for the year (students still pay an administrative fee of about EUR 170-190 and insurance). Platinum (10 awards, Milan): EUR 10,000 gross paid in two instalments of EUR 5,000. Gold (18, Milan): EUR 8,000 gross in two instalments. Gold Piacenza (16; SAL, LLH and RES programmes): EUR 5,000 gross in two instalments. Bronze (10, Piacenza; Mechanical Engineering and Mechatronics for Manufacturing): EUR 2,500 in one payment. Silver (10; Cremona, Lecco, Mantova and Piacenza): tuition waiver only. Awards can be renewed for year two if the student earns 1,000 points (Platinum) or 700 points (other awards) by 10 August 2028.
requirements: International student
Admitted to the first year of an English-taught MSc (Laurea Magistrale) for 2027-2028
MSc application fee paid between 1 October and 1 December 2026
Strong grade average and academic record
Valid English language certificate, verified by the International Students Office (by 4 March 2027 according to the page)
documents: Scholarship application form in Politecnico Online Services
Academic transcripts and degree documents from the MSc application
opportunities.selection_process: A university commission ranks candidates on academic merit (grade average and achievements), how well their previous studies match the chosen MSc, their documents and the form. Priority goes to students from countries affected by military aggression or civil war, and geographic origin, gender balance and age are also considered. Results come three to four months after the deadline.
important_dates: MSc application fee paid by: 1 December 2026
Scholarship form deadline: 15 December 2026, 12:00 noon Italian time
Results: about three to four months after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: Politecnico di Milano is a public science and technology university founded in 1863, with campuses in Milan and several Lombardy and Emilia-Romagna cities. It teaches engineering, architecture and design and runs many MSc programmes entirely in English.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to an English-taught MSc on the Politecnico Online Services portal and pay the application fee by 1 December 2026. Then fill in the merit-based scholarship form in the same portal before 12:00 noon Italian time on 15 December 2026. Questions go to international-scholarships@polimi.it.
opportunities.notes: The page and the official call give slightly different administrative fees (about EUR 170 versus about EUR 190). Egyptian, Ethiopian, Ghanaian and Tunisian students can also look at the Italian government's Invest Your Talent in Italy scheme.

opportunities.title: Pre-PhD Student Internship at ÚFAL (Spring 2027)
opportunities.provider: Institute of Formal and Applied Linguistics (ÚFAL), Charles University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students who have completed or nearly completed a master's with a strong computer-science background and an interest in NLP, machine learning or AI can apply for a 1-3 month partly paid research stay at ÚFAL in Prague.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Formal and Applied Linguistics (ÚFAL) at Charles University in Prague offers pre-PhD research internships to students who are thinking about doctoral study in computational linguistics. The spring session runs roughly from March to May 2027.

Interns spend one to three months at ÚFAL as visitors, working with a supervisor on a research topic, and are expected to aim for a joint publication. Two sessions run each year, with one intern selected per session, and a successful internship counts in the candidate's favour in later PhD admission.

For African students interested in language technology, this is a supported way to test a research career in a leading European NLP group.
opportunities.benefits: Travel costs up to 15,000 CZK and accommodation up to 8,000 CZK per month (or actual costs if lower); a bonus may be paid at ÚFAL's discretion.
requirements: Master's degree completed or nearly completed
Excellent computer-science background and programming experience
Interest in NLP, machine learning, AI, data mining or music information retrieval
documents: CV naming your programme and university
Transcript with grades and the grading scale
Proposed topics or project proposal and preferred supervisors
opportunities.selection_process: ÚFAL reviews the applications and selects one intern per session.
important_dates: Internship period: roughly March to May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: ÚFAL is part of the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics at Charles University in Prague and is one of Europe's major centres for computational linguistics and natural language processing.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form linked from the ÚFAL internships page, in English, with your CV, transcript and research interests. It helps to agree a possible supervisor first.
opportunities.notes: Emails asking whether your profile is good enough are not answered. Contact: zabokrtsky@ufal.mff.cuni.cz.

opportunities.title: Provost's Postdoctoral Fellowship in Engineering 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality who completed, or will complete, a doctorate between June 2025 and September 2027 can apply for a two-year engineering postdoc at Notre Dame.
opportunities.description:
The University of Notre Dame's Provost's Postdoctoral Fellowships in Engineering fund early-career researchers for two years in the College of Engineering. Fellows design their own research with a primary mentor from the college and a co-mentor.

The fellowship pays a $75,000 annual stipend and a $15,000 allowance for research, training and professional development. Scholars of all nationalities can apply, which makes it open to African engineers who have recently finished, or are about to finish, a PhD.

The programme aims to develop future leaders in engineering research, so applicants need a clear research plan at the forefront of their field.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of $75,000 a year for 24 months plus a $15,000 allowance for research, training and professional development.
requirements: Doctorate completed or expected between June 2025 and September 2027 (earlier dates allowed after parental or medical leave in the past two years)
Open to scholars of all nationalities
Primary mentor from the College of Engineering
Current Notre Dame postdocs are not eligible
documents: Research statement of up to five pages (excluding citations) covering goals, accomplishments, mentoring, proposed research and mentors
PDF of up to five slides
Three recommendation letters submitted through Interfolio
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on scientific excellence and on a clear research plan at the forefront of engineering. Decisions are made by 31 March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Notre Dame is a private research university in Indiana, USA. Its College of Engineering runs research across aerospace, chemical, civil, computer, electrical and mechanical engineering.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree a primary mentor in the College of Engineering and a co-mentor, then apply through the programme's Interfolio posting with your CV, research statement, slides and three letters, which referees upload directly.
opportunities.notes: Applicants whose mentor is in the College of Science should apply to the Society of Science Fellows instead. Contact: eng-postdocs@nd.edu.

opportunities.title: SFU Undergraduate Scholars Entrance Scholarships (international) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: High school students worldwide with at least a 90% average (or 31 IB points) who apply for fall entry to SFU can apply for an entrance scholarship worth up to $140,000.
opportunities.description:
The Undergraduate Scholars Entrance Scholarships are Simon Fraser University's main merit awards for students coming straight from high school. Both Canadian and international students can apply, and international winners can receive up to $140,000 across their degree.

The awards look for students who combine strong grades with achievement outside the classroom. Applicants need an average of at least 90% (or 31 IB points without bonus points) in the courses required for their intended programme.

There is no nationality rule, so African secondary-school students applying to SFU for fall entry can compete. A living allowance may be added for winners who show financial need. The application window opened on 1 October 2026 and closes on 15 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Entrance scholarships worth up to $140,000 for international students (from $20,000 up to $60,000 for domestic students). A living allowance may also be offered to students with demonstrated financial need.
requirements: Current high school student applying for fall undergraduate entry
Minimum 90% average, or 31 IB points excluding bonus points, in the courses required for your programme
Academic and extracurricular excellence
Must submit a separate scholarship application
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic excellence and extracurricular achievement. Financial need is considered only for the optional living allowance.
opportunities.about_provider: Simon Fraser University is a public research university in British Columbia, Canada, with campuses in Burnaby, Vancouver and Surrey. It is regularly ranked among Canada's leading comprehensive universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to SFU and submit the separate Undergraduate Scholars Entrance Scholarship application before 15 December 2026. Students are only considered if they apply.
opportunities.notes: Check SFU's admission dates page because the admission application must also be submitted in time.

opportunities.title: Stirling Vice-Chancellor's Postgraduate International Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded international students with an offer for a full-time taught master's at Stirling can apply for a £7,000 fee waiver.
opportunities.description:
The University of Stirling's Vice-Chancellor's Postgraduate International Scholarship gives 100 new international master's students a £7,000 tuition fee waiver for September 2027 or January 2028 entry. It is for self-funded students on full-time taught master's courses on the Stirling campus in Scotland.

Applications are assessed in windows, the first running from 1 September to 15 December 2026, with later windows until June 2027 (and October 2027 for January 2028 entry). Applicants need an offer of a place before applying, and must pay a £1,000 deposit to secure the award.

Any international fee-paying student can apply, and Stirling also lists separate scholarships for students from Kenya, Nigeria and Ghana.
opportunities.benefits: A £7,000 reduction in tuition fees for the master's year.
requirements: Conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible full-time taught master's on the Stirling campus
New student starting September 2027 or January 2028
International fee status
Self-funded (not sponsored or holding another scholarship)
Not online, MRes or MPhil courses, and not INTO pre-master's progression students
documents: £1,000 deposit by the deadline in the offer letter
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed by window and placed on a waiting list as funding becomes available; outcomes are sent by 15 July.
important_dates: Window 1: 1 September to 15 December 2026 (deposit by 1 February 2027)
Window 2: 15 December 2026 to 28 February 2027 (deposit by 1 April 2027)
Window 3: 1 March to 30 April 2027 (deposit by 1 June 2027)
Window 4: 1 May to 15 June 2027 (deposit by 15 July 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Stirling is a public university in central Scotland that recruits students internationally and holds an Athena Swan Silver award.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's course and get an offer, then complete the Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship 2027-28 online form, and pay the £1,000 deposit by the date in your offer to secure the award.
opportunities.notes: Apply in an early window, as only 100 awards are available. Contact: international@stir.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: Cumbria International Undergraduate Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded international students with an offer for a full-time on-campus bachelor's at the University of Cumbria starting in January 2027 receive £1,500 a year off tuition automatically.
opportunities.description:
The University of Cumbria gives an international undergraduate scholarship worth £4,500 in total to self-funded students with overseas fee status. It is paid as a £1,500 tuition reduction in each of three years.

There is no separate application: eligible students who meet their offer conditions and pay their deposit by the deadline get the award automatically. For the January 2027 start, the deadline for meeting conditions and paying the deposit is 16 December 2026.

It applies to full-time, in-person bachelor's degrees at the Ambleside, Carlisle and Lancaster campuses, so African students on those courses benefit without extra paperwork.
opportunities.benefits: £4,500 in total: £1,500 a year for three years, deducted from tuition at registration. No cash alternative, and it cannot be combined with other university awards or discounts.
requirements: Offer for a full-time in-person bachelor's (at least 360 credits) at Ambleside, Carlisle or Lancaster
Self-funded with overseas fee status
Meet the minimum academic entry requirements
Excludes pre-registration health, distance or blended, partner and International College programmes
opportunities.selection_process: No competition: every eligible student who meets the conditions and pays the deposit on time receives the award.
important_dates: Conditions and deposit for January 2027 start: 16 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Cumbria is a public university in north-west England with campuses in Carlisle, Lancaster and Ambleside. It is known for education, health, outdoor studies and arts programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible bachelor's programme, meet your offer conditions and pay the deposit by 16 December 2026 for a January 2027 start; the scholarship is then applied automatically.
opportunities.notes: The award applies to the 2026/27 entry year and cannot be deferred.

Healthy Aging and Therapeutic Opportunities (D3) is a Keystone Symposia scientific meeting held at the NTUH International Convention Center in Taipei, Taiwan on 12-15 April 2027. It can be attended in person, by livestream or on demand, and is organised by Derek Huffman, Kristen Fortney, Brian K. Kennedy and Shu-Chun Teng.

Keystone offers scholarships so that graduate students and postdocs can attend in person and present a poster. Scholarship applications and short-talk abstracts are due on 16 December 2026; poster abstracts can be sent until 22 March 2027.

The scholarship is open to students and postdocs without a stated nationality restriction, so African researchers can apply. Keystone's separate Global Health Awards for scientists from low- and middle-income countries are listed on its financial-aid pages; this meeting's page did not show a Global Health Award date.
opportunities.benefits: Scholarship: up to 1,500 USD per award, paid as a reimbursement against receipts, towards airfare, ground transport, lodging and part of the registration fee. Global Health Award (for scientists from and based in low- and middle-income countries): a travel award covering meeting registration, lodging and airfare (and ground transport at some venues), with no other costs covered; livestream and on-demand registration options are also offered. Registering early gives a 250 USD discount on in-person registration.
requirements: Be a graduate student, or a postdoc within 8 years of a PhD, MD or DVM (counted to the meeting start date)
Attend the meeting in person
Submit and present a poster abstract
Only one Keystone scholarship per meeting year (1 July to 30 June) and one per lab
documents: Abstract (up to 1,000 words; one per person per meeting), with a refundable 50 USD abstract fee for in-person meetings
opportunities.selection_process: Abstracts are reviewed by the meeting organisers. Scholarship applications are judged on the quality and relevance of the abstract, looking at relevance, significance, style and clarity.
opportunities.about_provider: Keystone Symposia on Molecular and Cellular Biology is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) that organises scientific conferences across the life sciences. Alongside its meetings it runs financial-aid schemes, including student and postdoc scholarships and Global Health Awards, the latter supported in part by the Gates Foundation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract through the meeting page and pay the refundable abstract fee, then complete the scholarship (or Global Health Award) application on Keystone's SurveyMonkey Apply portal (keystonesymposia.smapply.us) and arrange for your mentor's letter. All deadlines close at 11:59 pm US Mountain Standard Time. Questions on scholarships go to scholarships@keystonesymposia.org.
opportunities.notes: One scholarship per meeting year and one per lab. Scholarships are reimbursed after the meeting, so keep all receipts. Keystone also lists Early-Career Travel Awards and student discounts on its financial-aid pages.

opportunities.provider: Graduate Association for African American History, University of Memphis
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate and undergraduate students working on any topic in Black Studies can submit a paper or panel proposal by 18 December 2026 for the GAAAH conference in Memphis, 24-26 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Graduate Association for African American History (GAAAH) at the University of Memphis is inviting proposals for its 2027 annual conference, themed "Under Siege but Undefeated: Countering the Erasure of Black History". The conference takes place from 24 to 26 February 2027 at the Maxine A. Smith University Center on the Memphis campus in Tennessee, with historian and writer Dr Clint Smith as keynote speaker.

The organisers welcome papers on any subject within Black Studies, from any discipline and using any method, which makes the call relevant to students researching Africa, the African diaspora and transatlantic Black history. Both individual papers and complete panels can be proposed.

The meeting is run by graduate students for graduate and undergraduate presenters, so it is a supportive first conference for early researchers. Limited travel funding is available from the university's African and African American Studies programme on a first-come, first-served basis.
opportunities.benefits: Limited travel funding from the University of Memphis African and African American Studies (AAAS) Program, given first-come, first-served; no amounts are published. No registration fee is mentioned in the call.
requirements: Graduate or undergraduate student
Paper on any topic within Black Studies
Individual paper or full panel proposal
Able to present in person in Memphis, 24-26 February 2027
documents: Individual paper: abstract of up to 300 words, paper title, CV or resume and email address
Panel: one email with a 200-word panel description plus each panellist's CV and email
Full paper by 31 January 2027 if accepted
opportunities.selection_process: The GAAAH organising committee reviews proposals and notifies applicants by 8 January 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: GAAAH is a graduate student association in the Department of History at the University of Memphis that organises an annual conference on African American and Black history.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email your abstract, title and CV (or the panel package) to the GAAAH president, Neil Sharma, at the address in the call PDF by 18 December 2026. For travel funding, contact Dr Brian Kwoba of the AAAS Program early, since support is first-come, first-served.
opportunities.notes: The call says students 'from around the country' are welcome; it does not exclude international presenters, but international participants need their own US visa and should ask about travel funding as early as possible.

opportunities.title: World Physiotherapy Congress 2027 Bursary (Guadalajara)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Qualified physiotherapists who are nationals and residents of a low or lower-middle income country whose national association pays World Physiotherapy's reduced membership fee can apply by 21 December 2026 for a bursary to attend the 2027 congress in Mexico.
opportunities.description:
World Physiotherapy offers a limited number of bursaries so that physiotherapists from low and lower-middle income countries can attend the World Physiotherapy Congress 2027, held in Guadalajara, Mexico, from 14 to 16 May 2027. The congress, hosted with the Mexican physiotherapy association AMEFI, is the main global meeting of the profession, with three days of scientific sessions, networking and professional development.

A bursary can be full or partial and pays the main costs of attending, from travel and hotel to registration and visa. Applicants do not need an accepted abstract. The application form closes at 23:59 UTC on 21 December 2026, and applicants are told the outcome in February 2027.

The award is designed for physiotherapists who will bring what they learn back to their workplace and country, so it suits African clinicians, educators and postgraduate physiotherapy students whose national association is a World Physiotherapy member paying the reduced fee.
opportunities.benefits: Full or partial support covering an economy return flight or ground transport, four nights' hotel with breakfast, full three-day congress registration, an allowance of USD 60 for local transport and meals, travel insurance, the visa fee and a social event ticket where applicable. Extra events, personal expenses and travel to embassies are not covered.
requirements: Qualified physiotherapist who is employed or enrolled in a relevant postgraduate programme (entry-level students are not eligible)
Member in good standing of a World Physiotherapy member organisation
National and resident of a low or lower-middle income country whose member organisation pays the reduced membership fee
Commitment to return to your home country after the congress
Not a previous bursary recipient
Evidence of efforts to find other funding
opportunities.selection_process: A World Physiotherapy panel reviews applications against five outcome-based criteria: the benefit to the applicant's professional development, how learning will be shared with the employer, the local impact, the contribution to developing the profession, and the applicant's efforts to secure other funding.
opportunities.about_provider: World Physiotherapy (formerly the World Confederation for Physical Therapy, WCPT) is the global body representing physiotherapists through its national member organisations. It organises the World Physiotherapy Congress every two years.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online bursary application on the congress's Oxford Abstracts portal, linked from the bursary page, before 21 December 2026. Explain how attending will benefit you, your employer and physiotherapy in your country, and what other funding you have sought.
opportunities.notes: Recipients must send a report within one month of the congress. The abstract call for the congress closed on 29 September 2026.

opportunities.title: Peking University Scholarships for New International Graduate Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Chinese citizens applying to full-time master's or PhD programmes at Peking University for September 2027 can be considered for its scholarships.
opportunities.description:
Peking University (PKU) is accepting applications from international students for full-time master's and doctoral programmes starting in September 2027, and applicants can be considered for several scholarships at the same time. These include the PKU Scholarship for New International Students, the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B, university programme) and the Beijing Government Scholarship.

Admission follows an 'application plus examination' model: the International Student Division checks the file, then each school's expert panel reviews it and runs a second-round assessment between January and March 2027. Programmes are offered in Chinese and in English across PKU's campuses in Beijing and its Shenzhen Graduate School.

For African graduates, this is a route to one of China's top two universities with funding that can cover tuition, housing, living costs and insurance. The first-round window runs until 25 December 2026, so documents such as authenticated degree certificates should be prepared early.
opportunities.benefits: Depending on the scheme: the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B) offers full or partial cover of tuition, accommodation, living allowance and medical insurance; the PKU Scholarship for New International Students covers full or partial tuition, living expenses and medical insurance; the Beijing Government Scholarship (Types A, B, C) ranges from tuition and insurance up to tuition, housing, a living stipend and insurance. The page does not give amounts.
requirements: Non-Chinese citizen with a valid passport, in good health and with no criminal record
Master's: bachelor's degree recognised by China's Ministry of Education
PhD: master's degree (bachelor's holders may apply to some science and engineering PhDs)
Chinese-taught programmes: HSK level 6 with at least 200 (sciences) or 210 (humanities) and writing 65 or more
English-taught programmes: TOEFL, GRE (above 315) or other proof as each programme sets
Beijing Government Scholarship age limits: master's 35 or under, PhD 40 or under
documents: Personal statement and research plan (about 1,500 words for master's, 3,000 for PhD)
Any extra materials required by the school
opportunities.selection_process: The International Student Division first checks eligibility, then school expert panels review the files and hold a second-round assessment (January to March 2027) of research ability, language and potential. A preliminary admission list is released by the end of May 2027.
important_dates: Preliminary admission list: by end of May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Peking University, founded in 1898, is one of China's leading comprehensive research universities. Its International Student Division handles admission and scholarships for degree-seeking international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through PKU's International Student Service System (studyatpku.com), choosing up to two programmes and paying the non-refundable RMB 800 fee per programme. Indicate the scholarships you wish to be considered for, upload all documents and submit before 25 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Master's programmes last 2 to 3 years and PhDs 4 to 5 years. Beijing Government Scholarship holders cannot hold another Chinese government or PKU scholarship. Check each school's catalogue for language scores, as the general guide's TOEFL figure is unclear.

opportunities.title: CityUHK (Dongguan) International Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International (non-Chinese) school leavers aged 18+ with strong A-Level/IB or equivalent results and English scores such as IELTS 6.5.
opportunities.description:
City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan) is admitting international students to its four-year bachelor's programmes for 2027 entry, and every admitted applicant is considered for its International Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship. This is the mainland China campus in Dongguan, Guangdong, not the Hong Kong campus.

There are two awards. The Full Scholarship pays full tuition for four years, on-campus accommodation, a monthly living allowance and medical insurance; the International Talent Scholarship pays RMB 50,000 a year towards the four-year programme plus medical insurance. Awards go to applicants with outstanding academic results and achievements, and competition is strong.

Applications are taken in three rounds, and the first round closes on 31 December 2026 (Beijing time). For African school leavers with good A-Level, IB or national results and strong English, it is a way to study in China with most or all costs covered.
opportunities.benefits: Full Scholarship: full tuition for the four-year programme, on-campus accommodation each year, a living allowance of RMB 2,500 per month for 12 months a year, and general medical insurance. International Talent Scholarship: RMB 50,000 per year for the four-year programme plus general medical insurance. (For reference, 2026-entry tuition was RMB 115,000 per year.)
requirements: Foreign citizen without Chinese nationality (Chinese-heritage applicants are screened out by the eligibility survey)
Applicants under the Ministry of Education rule need 4 years of foreign nationality and 2 years living abroad in the last 4 years, as of 30 April of the admission year
At least 18 years old (applicants under 18 need a guardian living in mainland China)
Completed high school with a strong record, e.g. GCE A Level grade E or better in three subjects or IB Diploma 30+; other qualifications assessed case by case
English: IELTS Academic 6.5, PTE 62, TOEFL iBT 79 (older format), SAT EBRW 590, ACT 24 English and 24 Reading, or Cambridge CAE/CPE grade C, taken within 2 years; home-edition tests not accepted
documents: Passport copy and proof of nationality
Qualification or high-school certificate (or enrolment letter)
English test result (waived for native speakers)
Optional: reference letter, talent or competition evidence
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic performance, achievements and overall excellence. Shortlisted applicants are invited to an online interview, then receive a conditional or unconditional offer; scholarships are decided at the same time.
opportunities.about_provider: City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan) is a campus of City University of Hong Kong in Dongguan, in mainland China's Greater Bay Area. It admits international students to English-taught undergraduate programmes through its own international admissions office.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the international admissions system (intladmissions.cityu-dg.edu.cn), complete the eligibility survey and upload the documents. Admitted applicants are considered for the entrance scholarship automatically; apply in round 1 for the best chance. Questions go to intladmissions@cityu-dg.edu.cn.
opportunities.notes: The guide prints the new TOEFL score as '4.5 out of 6'; check the exact TOEFL requirement with the university. Fees and residence permit costs (RMB 400-1,000) are extra if not covered.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Plant Health in Sustainable Cropping Systems (PlantHealth), first call
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Holders of a 180-ECTS bachelor's in agronomy, agriculture or a related field with some plant-health coursework and B2 English, from any country.
opportunities.description:
PlantHealth is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (120 ECTS) on protecting crops in sustainable farming systems. It is run by a European consortium coordinated by the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), and students move between partner campuses: UPV in Valencia, AgroParisTech, the University of Göttingen, Institut Agro and the University of Padova. Teaching is in English and French and the programme is delivered in person.

The first application call is open from 1 October to 31 December 2026; online applications must be in before midnight (CET) at the start of 1 January 2027, and results are expected at the end of February 2027. The dates point to a cohort starting in autumn 2027. Only applicants in this first call can be considered for the EU-funded Erasmus Mundus (EMJM) scholarships or consortium grants. A second call (20 May to 15 June 2027) is only for self-funded or externally funded candidates.

For African graduates in agronomy or agriculture, the programme is a fully funded route to training in plant pathology, pest management and crop protection across several European countries, and the scholarship is open to non-EU students.
opportunities.benefits: The Erasmus Mundus (EMJM) scholarship covers 100% of the participation (tuition) costs, health insurance and mandatory academic costs, and pays €1,400 per month for up to 24 months. Without a scholarship, total participation costs are €10,000 for applicants from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland (€9,000 for EU/EEA/Swiss students), paid in two instalments; self-funded students may receive an Erasmus+ grant of about €300 per month in the second year.
requirements: An official bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS in agronomy, agriculture or a related field
At least 4 ECTS of coursework in plant health or crop protection
Final-year students may apply if they will graduate before the end of August
English at B2 level shown by IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge (FCE/CAE/CPE), Trinity ISE, ESOL, OTE or PTE (Duolingo, TOEIC and university certificates are not accepted)
Native speakers or graduates taught entirely in English are exempt with proof
Applicants who already received an EMJM scholarship, or who hold another EU grant at the same time, cannot get the scholarship
documents: Two signed and stamped recommendation letters with referee contact details
Motivation statement of up to 1,000 characters in the online form
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored on academic record (GPA and merits) for 60%, the recommendation letters for 20% and the applicant's motivation for 20%. Scholarships are awarded only to applicants of the first call.
important_dates: First call closes: 31 December 2026 (before 1 January 2027, 00:00 CET)
Second call (self-funded only): 20 May to 15 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The PlantHealth consortium is a group of European universities offering an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master co-funded by the European Union. It is coordinated by the Universitat Politècnica de València in Spain, with AgroParisTech, Institut Agro, the University of Göttingen and the University of Padova as partners.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an applicant account and submit the single online form on the PlantHealth portal (planthealth.upv.es/user/create_applicant); the same form is used for scholarship and self-funded applications. Upload your diplomas, transcripts, CV, English certificate and two recommendation letters, and write the short motivation statement in the form before the first-call deadline.
opportunities.notes: Apply in the first call if you need funding: second-call applicants cannot receive scholarships. Check the consortium's financial support page and the University of Padova's scholarships for second-year students at Padova.

opportunities.title: Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship at NTU 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality with a non-computer-science PhD from the last 3 years who propose an AI-in-science project with an NTU mentor.
opportunities.description:
The Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) in Singapore supports early-career researchers who want to apply artificial intelligence to problems in engineering, the natural sciences or the mathematical sciences. It is part of a global programme funded by Schmidt Sciences to speed up the use of AI across STEM research.

Fellows work at NTU for up to two years with a faculty mentor, receive a competitive salary package and travel allowances, and take at least one AI course module each year to build their skills. The current call closes on 31 December 2026 at 23:59 Singapore time.

The fellowship targets scientists whose PhD is not in computer science, which makes it a good fit for African researchers in fields such as chemistry, physics, biology, materials or civil engineering who want to add AI methods to their work. The page sets no nationality limit.
opportunities.benefits: Up to two years of postdoctoral employment at NTU with an attractive remuneration package (amount not published), travel allowances, and AI training through at least one AI module per year.
requirements: PhD (or equivalent) obtained within the last 3 years, in a field other than computer science
Excellent academic record and research potential
Research project applying AI to engineering, natural sciences or mathematical sciences
An NTU faculty member who agrees to mentor the project and writes a support letter
documents: CV with Scopus Author ID and full publication list
Official transcript or degree certificate in English
Research proposal of up to 2 pages (using the template on the page)
Support letter from the NTU mentor, attached to the proposal
Names of two referees, one of them the PhD supervisor (NTU contacts them)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on academic record, research potential and the quality of the AI-in-science proposal with its NTU mentor. The page does not describe interview stages.
opportunities.about_provider: Nanyang Technological University is a leading research university in Singapore. Schmidt Sciences, founded by Eric and Wendy Schmidt, funds this AI in Science postdoctoral programme at a group of universities worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First find an NTU faculty mentor and agree a project, then submit the application on NTU's TRACS portal (apps.ntu.edu.sg/TRACS_ui/welcomepage?pgm=EWSA) with the proposal, CV, transcripts and publications. Your two referees will be contacted by NTU after you submit. Questions go to FA-RSO@ntu.edu.sg.
opportunities.notes: Computer science PhDs are not eligible. NTU also lists other postdoctoral schemes on its research careers pages, such as the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship and the Presidential Postdoctoral Fellowship.

opportunities.title: ITLOS Internship Programme July-September 2027
opportunities.provider: International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students with at least three years of university study or recent graduates, usually aged 32 or under, with good English or French and an interest in international law.
opportunities.description:
The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) in Hamburg runs a three-month, full-time internship programme for students and recent graduates interested in international law. The call now open is for the July to September 2027 period, with applications due by 31 December 2026; applications for later periods can also be submitted.

Interns support the Registry in areas such as law, international relations, political science, public relations, library science and translation. About 20 internships are offered each year, and since 1997 the Tribunal has hosted 420 interns from 106 States.

The internship itself is unpaid, but a trust fund gives a limited number of allowances for travel and living costs to nationals of developing countries in financial need, which includes many African countries. This makes it a realistic way for African law and international relations students to gain experience at an international court.
opportunities.benefits: Internships are unpaid. The Trust Fund for the Law of the Sea gives a limited amount of funding to cover travel and living costs, paid as a monthly allowance, for selected interns who are nationals of and normally live in an OECD DAC developing country and are in financial need. Funding must be requested in the online application form; late requests are not considered.
requirements: At least three years of university study completed
Enrolled in a degree or postgraduate course during the internship, or graduated within 12 months before applying
Normally aged 32 or under
Good English and/or French
Interest in international law; background in law, international relations, political science, public relations, library science or translation
Not currently in employment
documents: Cover letter of up to one page
Optional: research or writing sample up to 10 pages
Optional: proof of enrolment, degrees and transcripts
Translations of documents not in English or French
opportunities.selection_process: An Internship Selection Committee reviews complete applications, and the Registrar decides with the approval of the President. Geographic diversity and gender balance are taken into account, and applicants hear the result about one month after the deadline.
important_dates: Results: about one month after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: ITLOS is an independent international court set up under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. It sits in Hamburg, Germany, and settles disputes about the interpretation and application of the Convention.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online internship application form on the ITLOS website and upload your cover letter and CV, plus any optional documents. If you need financial support, request it in the same form when you apply. Incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: No time of day is given for the deadline, so apply early. Questions go to press@itlos.org.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD-holding researchers at accredited institutions worldwide can apply for USD 75,000 AI-and-jobs research gifts by 31 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Microsoft AI Economy Institute has opened its fourth research call, focused on AI and jobs. Selected principal investigators join a 12-month Senior Fellows programme with bi-weekly virtual workshops and an in-person workshop, and contribute a book chapter and a journal manuscript.

Each selected proposal receives a research gift of USD 75,000 and a travel allowance. Research starts in May 2027. The institute states that the research is independent and does not represent Microsoft's views.

opportunities.title: Nusa Putra International Undergraduate Scholarships 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International high-school graduates aged up to 22 (26 for the Berlian scheme) with English proof.
opportunities.description:
Nusa Putra University in Sukabumi, West Java, Indonesia, offers international undergraduate scholarships for its English-taught bachelor's degrees starting in the 2027/2028 academic year. The awards last for the full eight semesters of a degree.

There are three schemes. The Genusian Scholarship is the most complete, covering tuition, a monthly living allowance, housing help, visa sponsorship and health insurance. The International Islamic Boarding Scholarship offers the same support with full residence in the university's pesantren (Islamic boarding school). The Berlian Scholarship covers tuition and language and academic support only.

Registration runs from 1 November to 31 December 2026, and every stage of selection, including a computer-based test and interviews, takes place online, so African school leavers can apply without travelling. Results are announced on 1 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Genusian Scholarship: 100% tuition for 8 semesters, a monthly living allowance, housing assistance, KITAS C316 student visa sponsorship, Indonesian language classes (BIPA), health insurance in Indonesia and airport pick-up. International Islamic Boarding Scholarship: the same, plus a full pesantren dormitory place. Berlian Scholarship: 100% tuition for 8 semesters, BIPA classes, airport pick-up and academic mentoring (no living allowance, visa fees, housing or insurance). None of the schemes pays for the passport, international flights or medical checks.
requirements: High-school graduate with a strong academic and disciplinary record
Maximum age 22 for the Genusian and Islamic Boarding schemes; 26 for the Berlian scheme
Islamic Boarding scheme: practising Muslim willing to live full time in the pesantren
English proof: valid TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo result, or an official certificate of English-medium schooling
Passport valid for at least 18 months from the planned entry date
documents: Confidential recommendation letter from a principal, senior teacher, counsellor or community leader
High-school diploma and transcripts for grades 10-12

opportunities.selection_process: Selection is fully online: document screening, a computer-based test (CBT) and an interview; Islamic Boarding applicants also take a Quran recitation test.

opportunities.title: Takemi Program in International Health Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mid-career health professionals and researchers with a graduate degree, publications and already-collected data, from any country.
opportunities.description:
The Takemi Program in International Health at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health in Boston is a one-year, in-person research fellowship for mid-career health professionals and researchers, mainly from low- and middle-income countries. It describes itself as the oldest continuing mid-career research and training programme in global health, and since 1983 it has hosted 330 fellows from 62 countries, about 70 of them from Africa.

Fellows spend an academic year (1 August to 30 June) analysing data they have already collected, writing papers, attending seminars and building networks. Applications for the 2027-2028 year are open until 31 December 2026 at midnight US Eastern time, with decisions in February and applicants informed by March.

Applicants should note that the programme itself does not fund fellows: most must bring their own funding, and only very limited internal support exists for two fellows from low-income countries. It suits African health researchers who already have funding or an employer's support and want a year at Harvard to turn their data into publications and policy.
opportunities.benefits: The programme gives a year of in-person research time at Harvard, seminars, mentoring and a certificate, but it does not provide funding. Limited internal support (from a Japan Pharmaceutical Medical Association donation) may cover two fellows from low-income countries, decided at acceptance. Fellows must show at least US$36,410 a year for the J-1 visa; the page estimates real costs at US$60,000-77,000 a year (2024-25 figures).
requirements: A completed graduate (advanced) degree in any discipline
Significant work and research experience, including publications in internationally recognised journals
Leadership potential in your home country
Good English (TOEFL, IELTS, or a transcript from an English-medium university)
Commitment to a career in health
Data already collected before the fellowship (active data collection is not supported)
Able to attend in person for the full year
documents: Research proposal of up to 5 pages (single-spaced, 12-pt Times New Roman, with aims, background, data sources and methods)
Statement of interest answering five set questions
Publications list and one sample English-language publication
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reviews applications and meets in mid-February to choose fellows; applicants are told by March. Reapplying in later years is allowed.
important_dates: Deadline: 31 December 2026, midnight US Eastern time
Fellowship year: 1 August 2027 - 30 June 2028 (orientation late August)
opportunities.about_provider: The Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is Harvard University's school of public health in Boston. The Takemi Program, named after Dr Taro Takemi of the Japan Medical Association, has trained mid-career global health leaders there since 1983.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form (Harvard Qualtrics link on the apply page), uploading your CV, proposal, statement and publications, and ask three referees to email their letters. Start looking for funding early, using the programme's list of possible funding sources. Questions go to takemi@hsph.harvard.edu.
opportunities.notes: There is no programming in January and no remote option. Plan funding in advance: most fellows are supported by their employer, government or an external funder.

opportunities.title: Wallenberg-NTU Presidential Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.provider: Nanyang Technological University and Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality within 5 years of their PhD proposing AI, data, software, security or autonomy research.
opportunities.description:
The Wallenberg-NTU Presidential Postdoctoral Fellowship is a two-year independent research fellowship split between Singapore and Sweden. Fellows spend the first year at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and the second year with a research group in the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP) in Sweden. The scheme is supported by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.

Five fellowships are offered in this call, and research must fall in one of five areas: artificial intelligence, machine learning, big data and analytics, software and security, or mobility and autonomy. Applications close on 31 December 2026 at 23:59 Singapore time, referee reports are due by 7 January 2027, and fellows must be able to start by 31 December 2027.

The fellowship is open to researchers from Singapore and around the world, with no nationality list, so African computing and data scientists within five years of their PhD can compete for a well-funded start to an independent research career on two continents.
opportunities.benefits: In the Singapore year: an annual salary of up to SGD 80,000, a research grant of up to SGD 100,000, and a relocation allowance and housing grant for the fellowship. In the Sweden year: an annual support package covering salary, supervision and travel at WASP's standard postdoctoral level.
requirements: PhD or equivalent obtained within the last 5 years
Intellectual excellence and the maturity to lead independent research
A research proposal in AI, machine learning, big data and analytics, software and security, or mobility and autonomy
Available to start no later than 31 December 2027
Open to applicants of any nationality
documents: Official transcript or PhD certificate in English
Research proposal of up to 2 pages (template on the page)
Top 3 publications in PDF and other supporting documents
Two referees, one of them the PhD supervisor
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed on academic excellence, independence and the research proposal, together with referee reports due one week after the deadline. Five fellows are chosen.
opportunities.about_provider: Nanyang Technological University is a leading research-intensive university in Singapore. The Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation is Sweden's largest private research funder and finances WASP, Sweden's major national programme in AI and autonomous systems.

opportunities.notes: Only five awards are made and only the five research areas are eligible. Older SP Group calls shown on the same page are past cycles.

The Institute of Global Value Inquiry (IGVI) runs a travel grant programme for scholars in the humanities and social sciences whose work deals with questions of value, preferably with a philosophical focus. Grants help pay for attending conferences and workshops or for research trips.

There are three application rounds every year, closing on 1 January, 1 May and 1 September, and applications are usually processed within about two weeks. The next round closes on 1 January 2027.

The programme is aimed specifically at scholars based in World Bank low- and lower-middle-income countries, which covers most of Africa, and there is no career-stage limit, membership requirement or abstract requirement.

Working in the humanities or social sciences on value inquiry (philosophical focus preferred)
Proof that you have applied to the event or research activity
Any career stage
documents: Proof of application to the event or activity
Cost evidence (for example a travel agent quote or screenshot)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the relevance of the research project and of the trip, and on available funds in that round.
important_dates: Later rounds: 1 May and 1 September each year

opportunities.about_provider: IGVI is a research institute that supports inquiry into values across the humanities and social sciences, with a focus on including scholars from the Global South. It funds travel, research grants and research positions.

NSU also lists a General International Student Scholarship and merit awards of USD 500 to 5,000 for new international students, so African students can combine support to make study in the US more affordable.

requirements: International student pursuing a first bachelor's or master's degree

Live in on-campus housing (legacy students exempt)
Incoming freshmen: GPA of at least 3.0

opportunities.description:
Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) in the Netherlands offers the TU/e Scholarship for Excellence to top students starting a full-time master's on 1 September 2027. The 2027-2028 edition, titled 'Shaping the Future of Microchip Innovation', is funded by the Dutch national Beethoven Program and supports master's programmes linked to the semiconductor and high-tech industry.

Eligible programmes include Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Data Science and AI, Embedded Systems, Industrial and Applied Mathematics, Systems and Control, Sustainable Energy Technology, Automotive Technology, Nuclear Fusion, and Artificial Intelligence and Engineering Systems. About 35 awards are made, 15 of them for students from outside the EEA, and only about 2% of applicants succeed.

The award is €7,500 a year for two years, so it is a partial scholarship rather than full funding. Non-EEA winners also receive part of the NL Scholarship in their first year. Strong African engineering and science graduates with a GPA of 7.5/10 or better can apply as part of their master's application by 1 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: €7,500 per academic year for two years (€15,000 in total). Non-EEA recipients also receive a share of the NL Scholarship in year one (not applied for separately). It is not a full scholarship; keeping the year-two award needs at least 45 ECTS in year one.

High-school diploma or bachelor's obtained outside the Netherlands
No previous Dutch higher education (exchange periods allowed)
GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 (or equivalent) on the latest transcript
Able to meet Dutch visa and residence-permit rules
Not a JADS joint master's or European double degree, and not admitted on an earlier intake's decision
documents: Confirmation in the application that you want to be considered
opportunities.selection_process: The International Office checks eligibility, then a Scholarship Selection Committee ranks candidates. Results are confirmed by the end of March 2027 and cannot be appealed.

opportunities.description:
CENTA, the Central England NERC Training Alliance, is recruiting for its project-based PhD studentships starting in autumn 2027. CENTA is a doctoral training partnership funded by the UK's Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) and led by the University of Birmingham with partner universities and research centres across central England.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: International master's candidates aged up to 29 and doctoral candidates aged up to 35 can be nominated by a French higher-education institution for the 2027 Eiffel call.
opportunities.description:
The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship is the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs' flagship award for bringing top international students to French universities and grandes écoles. Campus France runs the programme on the ministry's behalf, and the 2027 call opened on 2 October 2026.

The award supports two tracks: master's study and doctoral study (usually a mobility period within a co-supervised or co-directed doctorate). Students do not apply to Campus France themselves. Instead, a French institution that has admitted or is admitting the student puts the candidate forward, and the institution files the application with Campus France.

For African students this is one of the most visible French government awards, and it is open to applicants from any country outside France. Because the institution must nominate you, the practical first step is to apply for admission early to a French programme and ask its international office whether it nominates candidates for Eiffel.
opportunities.benefits: The programme funds a monthly allowance and related support for the master's or doctoral stay in France; the exact amounts and coverage are set out in the 2027 programme regulations published by Campus France.
requirements: Nominated by a French higher-education institution (no direct student applications)
Master's track: aged 29 or under
Doctoral track: aged 35 or under
Admitted to, or being admitted to, a programme at the nominating institution
documents: Application file prepared with the host institution (following the Campus France filing guide)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored by expert evaluators drawn from French university teacher-researchers, using separate published grids for the master's and doctoral tracks. Results are announced by Campus France.
opportunities.about_provider: Campus France is the French national agency for promoting higher education, hosting international students and managing government scholarships. It administers the Eiffel programme for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to a French institution and ask its international office about its internal Eiffel deadline, which falls before 6 January 2027. The institution prepares and submits the file to Campus France; new institutions contact candidatures.eiffel@campusfrance.org to get access.

The programme is mainly for UK students, but a limited number of full studentships are available to international applicants, which makes it a realistic route for strong African graduates in earth, ocean, climate, ecology and related fields.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates near completion, postdocs, professors and non-academic knowledge producers working on slavery and strong dependency can apply by 10 January 2027 for a 2027/2028 fellowship in Bonn.
opportunities.description:
The Heinz Heinen Fellowships are offered by the Bonn Center for Dependency and Slavery Studies (BCDSS), a Cluster of Excellence at the University of Bonn. They bring international researchers to Bonn to work on strong asymmetrical dependencies, including slavery, with proposals expected to address periods before 1900 and to take a comparative view.

No nationality limits are stated, and the programme's focus on slavery and dependency makes it highly relevant to African historians and scholars of the African past and its diasporas.
opportunities.benefits: Monthly stipend of €1,700 (doctoral), €2,600 (junior postdoc), €3,100 (postdoc) or €3,600 (senior); outward and return travel allowance; accommodation lump sum of up to €1,000 per month (€1,250 with children) for fellows from outside Bonn; desk and computer, workshop funding and childcare support.

Postdoc: PhD awarded more than 4 years ago
Senior: full professor
Alternative knowledge producers: journalists, artists, curators and similar

Application in English

What the award covers varies by faculty: Arts and Business and Social Sciences combine a tuition waiver with a monthly grant, while Natural and Technical Sciences give 100% tuition waivers. For African applicants, applying early and presenting excellent grades is key.
opportunities.benefits: Full or partial tuition fee waiver; in some faculties also a monthly living grant, usually for the whole programme.

Applied for an Aarhus master's by 15 January (summer intake) or 15 September (winter intake)
Excellent academic record

documents: No extra documents: the regular master's application is used (do not upload scholarship documents)
opportunities.selection_process: Faculties rank applicants on academic excellence when assessing admission; some faculties focus on particular countries or programmes. Offers have a short acceptance window.

opportunities.about_provider: Aarhus University is Denmark's second-largest university, founded in 1928, with faculties of arts, natural sciences, technical sciences, health and business and social sciences.

opportunities.description:
The American Antiquarian Society (AAS) offers 19 different one- to two-month residential fellowships through a single application, for scholars who need to work in its library in Worcester, Massachusetts. The library holds one of the largest collections of printed material from early America.

Fellowships can be taken at any time between 1 June and 31 May; a second month is rarely granted. Most awards are open to doctoral candidates working on dissertations, and several also accept postdocs, independent researchers and holders of terminal degrees such as MLS or MFA.

International scholars are explicitly welcome, so African researchers working on Atlantic history, slavery, print culture or the African diaspora in early America can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of $2,400 per month. Rooms in the AAS scholars' housing (about $600 to $1,000 a month) can be deducted from the stipend.
requirements: Doctoral candidate, postdoc, independent scholar or terminal-degree holder (depending on the fellowship)
Project that needs the AAS collections
Preference for applicants without an AAS fellowship in the past three years
Arrange your own visa: AAS cannot sponsor J-1 visas
documents: Statement of previous support and current appointment
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on scholarly qualifications, the significance of the project and how well it fits the AAS collections.
opportunities.about_provider: Founded in 1812, the American Antiquarian Society is a national research library and learned society focused on American history and culture up to 1876.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Combine all documents into one PDF and submit it through the AAS online fellowship form (Breezy portal) by 15 January 2027. One application covers all 19 short-term fellowships.
opportunities.notes: Some named fellowships have extra restrictions (for example one reserved for German citizens or residents).

opportunities.description:
The Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (EGLS) is American University's flagship award for international first-year students who will study in Washington DC on a student visa. It targets young people who have shown leadership, a commitment to social change in their communities and resilience in overcoming obstacles.

For Fall 2027 entry, two students receive a full award covering all billable university costs, and other strong applicants receive partial awards. Awards renew for up to four years with satisfactory progress.

African secondary-school students who are ambitious about public service, international affairs or community leadership are a natural fit for this scholarship.
opportunities.benefits: Full award (two students): full tuition, room and board for up to four years. Partial awards: up to US$40,000 a year, with no separate application. Not covered: health insurance, books, airfare, taxes and personal costs (about US$4,000 a year).
requirements: Not a US citizen or permanent resident, and will need an F-1 or J-1 visa
Has not enrolled in or started university study
Finished secondary school no earlier than 2024 (preference for students graduating by June 2027)
Proof of English proficiency
Evidence of leadership and community commitment
Able to show at least US$4,000 a year for uncovered costs

opportunities.about_provider: American University is a private research university in Washington DC, known for international service, public affairs, law and communication.

The 2027-2028 call applies to four LLM programmes: International and European Law, Transnational and European Private Law, Law and Finance, and International Criminal Law.

The scholarship is meant for applicants with outstanding grades who do not qualify for Dutch student finance. The amount for 2027-2028 has not yet been announced by the faculty, so applicants should treat it as a partial award and plan other funding.

African law graduates aiming at an international or European law career are eligible, provided they meet the grade threshold and can obtain a Dutch study visa.
opportunities.benefits: A scholarship towards the LLM year; the amount for 2027-2028 is to be announced by the university. Only one scholarship is awarded each year.

Applying for a first master's at the UvA
Full-time enrolment in one of four LLM programmes (International and European Law; Transnational and European Private Law; Law and Finance; International Criminal Law)
Previous degree grades comparable to a 4.0 US GPA, UK first-class honours or 8.0 on the Dutch scale (for a non-law bachelor, only law courses count)
Able to meet Dutch visa requirements
documents: Motivation letter of up to 500 words
All documents required for the LLM application (incomplete files are not considered)
opportunities.selection_process: The award goes by lottery among applicants who meet all the requirements. Results are announced by the end of March.
important_dates: Deadline: 15 January 2027, 23:59 CET (with the LLM application)
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Amsterdam is a large public research university in the Netherlands. Its Amsterdam Law School runs English-taught LLM programmes through the Amsterdam Graduate School of Law.

opportunities.title: Folger Short-Term Scholarly Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars with a PhD, or PhD candidates at the dissertation stage, of any nationality, can apply by 15 January 2027 for a one- to three-month Folger fellowship paying USD 5,000 a month in residence or USD 4,000 virtually.
opportunities.description:
The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington, DC offers short-term scholarly fellowships for researchers whose projects need its collections of early modern books, manuscripts and other materials. The 2027-2028 round funds stays of one, two or three months, and fellows may choose to work on site in Washington, virtually, or in a hybrid arrangement.

The fellowships are run by the Folger Institute, the library's research and scholarly programmes arm. They exist to support original research that makes real use of the Folger holdings, and the selection committee aims for a mix of disciplines, methods and geographical backgrounds among fellows.

There is no nationality restriction, so African doctoral candidates who have reached the dissertation stage and early-career or established scholars working on the early modern world, Shakespeare, book history, the Atlantic world or related topics can apply on equal terms with everyone else.
opportunities.benefits: USD 5,000 per month for fellows in residence in Washington, DC, or USD 4,000 per month for virtual fellows, for one to three months. The stipend is meant to cover travel, housing and living costs.
requirements: A terminal degree (such as a PhD), or PhD candidacy at the all-but-dissertation stage, or an international equivalent
A research project that needs the Folger collections
Open to applicants of any nationality
Fellowship of one, two or three months, held on site, virtually or in hybrid form
documents: Project abstract of up to 250 words
Project description of up to 1,500 words, stating the months requested and how each month will be used
One-page list of the Folger primary sources you plan to use
One letter of recommendation submitted through the portal
opportunities.selection_process: An external committee reviews applications for their likely impact, relevance to the field, originality and sophistication, feasibility, and how well they will use the Folger collections. The committee also aims for disciplinary, methodological and geographical diversity.
important_dates: Information sessions: 9 October and 1 December 2026 (12 pm ET, online)
opportunities.about_provider: The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington, DC holds one of the world's largest collections of Shakespeare and early modern printed and manuscript material. Its Folger Institute runs fellowships, seminars and other programmes for researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare the abstract, project description, CV and source list, then apply through the Folger fellowship portal (onlineapplicationportal.com/folgerfellowships). Your recommender uploads their letter through the same portal. Check the Online Catalog and finding aids first so that your source list is specific.
opportunities.notes: Use the Folger catalogue and finding aids to name concrete items in your source list; vague lists weaken an application. The online information session on 1 December 2026 is a good chance to ask questions.

opportunities.title: Houghton Library Visiting Fellowships 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality, from doctoral students to independent scholars and archive professionals, can apply by 15 January 2027 for a USD 4,500 Houghton Library visiting fellowship of at least four weeks at Harvard.
opportunities.description:
Houghton Library, Harvard University's main library for rare books and manuscripts, offers visiting fellowships for researchers who need to work with its collections. For the 2027-2028 fellowship year (July to June), the library is awarding fellowships from 15 endowed funds; applicants submit one application and the committee decides which fellowship fits each project.

Fellows must spend at least four weeks in residence at Houghton Library in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The library is keen on projects with a global outlook and contemporary relevance, and some of the named fellowships have a specific focus, for example the Hyde Fellowship for research on early modern Black lives, including Africa and the African diaspora between 1500 and 1800.

The programme is open to all nationalities and to a wide range of researchers, from doctoral students to independent scholars and museum or archive professionals, which makes it a realistic option for African researchers working with historical, literary or archival sources held at Harvard.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 4,500 for the fellowship, paid two to three weeks after arrival. Fellows pay their own travel, housing and taxes; non-US fellows need a J-1 visa, which Harvard sponsors, but the visa fees are paid by the fellow.
requirements: Open to all nationalities
Doctoral students, postdocs, faculty, independent scholars, curators and library, archive or museum professionals
Aged 18 or over
Must not live within commuting distance of Harvard
Research must use Houghton Library holdings
At least four weeks in residence during July 2027 to June 2028
Past fellows must wait five years before applying again
documents: Project proposal of up to 500 words
Preliminary list of Houghton holdings you will consult
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee reviews all applications and assigns each successful applicant to one of 15 endowed fellowships. Proposals that do not name Houghton materials are not considered; the library favours projects with a global lens and present-day relevance. Some fellowships carry extra conditions, such as ASECS membership for the Bate/Bryant ASECS fellowship.
important_dates: Fellowship year: July 2027 to June 2028 (minimum four weeks in residence)
opportunities.about_provider: Houghton Library is Harvard University's principal repository for rare books, manuscripts and archives. It supports outside researchers through a programme of endowed visiting fellowships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Houghton Library Visiting Fellowship Program 2027-2028 form on Submittable (houghtonlibrary.submittable.com), uploading the proposal, holdings list and CV and arranging one reference letter. You do not need to choose a particular named fellowship. Questions go to Peter X. Accardo at Houghton Library.
opportunities.notes: Search HOLLIS and the Houghton finding aids before applying so that your holdings list is precise. Budget for travel, housing and J-1 visa fees, since the USD 4,500 stipend does not cover everything.
