opportunities.title: Kathryn and Peter Yatrakis Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: American School of Classical Studies at Athens, Gennadius Library
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students and scholars who earned a PhD in the last five years, of any nationality, can apply by 15 January 2027 for a 2027-28 Gennadius Library fellowship in Athens.
opportunities.description:
The Kathryn and Peter Yatrakis Fellowship supports a full academic year of research that depends on the Gennadius Library of the American School of Classical Studies at Athens. The library holds more than 150,000 titles on Greece from antiquity to the present, with about 90,000 research titles on open shelves.

The fellowship runs from September 2027 to May 2028 in Athens and includes housing and meals at the School's Loring Hall. Fellows must report on their work and acknowledge the School in resulting publications.

It is open to all nationalities, so African doctoral students and early-career scholars working on Byzantine, Ottoman, modern Greek or wider Mediterranean topics can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of US$11,500 plus room and board at Loring Hall (weekday meals) and waiver of School fees.
requirements: PhD candidate, or PhD awarded within the last five years
Research that requires the Gennadius Library
Open to all nationalities
Concurrent employment only with the Director's permission
documents: Project description (up to 750 words) referring to the Gennadius Library or its holdings
Transcripts of all postsecondary study for current students (translated into English if needed)
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reviews the application materials; awards are announced in mid-March.
opportunities.about_provider: The American School of Classical Studies at Athens, founded in 1881, is a leading research centre on Greece. Its Gennadius Library specialises in post-classical Greek history and culture.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the ASCSA Submittable form for the Yatrakis Fellowship by 15 January 2027, uploading your CV, project description and transcripts, and arrange two online reference letters.
opportunities.notes: Research trips outside Athens need advance approval. The same page lists other Gennadius fellowships open to all nationalities, such as the Macricostas and Schwarz fellowships.

opportunities.title: Lalor Foundation Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career PhD or MD researchers of any nationality in mammalian reproductive biology can apply by 15 January 2027 for a USD 67,000 one-year postdoctoral fellowship at a nonprofit research institution.
opportunities.description:
The Lalor Foundation's Postdoctoral Fellowship Program supports early-career scientists who want to do research in mammalian reproductive biology, especially work connected to the regulation of fertility. The foundation funds one year of postdoctoral training at a nonprofit research institution, with the possibility of a second, renewal year.

Fellowships usually begin in May or June and last 12 months. Applicants of any citizenship may apply, and the host institution can be in any country, provided it is a nonprofit research organisation that can prove its status.

For African PhD and MD graduates in reproductive biology, endocrinology, veterinary science or related fields, the fellowship offers a well-funded first postdoc, either at an institution abroad or at an eligible nonprofit institute at home.
opportunities.benefits: USD 67,000 per year, covering the fellow's stipend, fringe benefits and institutional overhead (overhead may not exceed 5%). Other costs are not allowed. One renewal year may be granted.
requirements: Any citizenship
PhD or MD level training (or in the final year of the doctorate, with the degree expected in the application year)
No faculty appointment at instructor level or above
The foundation prefers applicants who received their doctorate no more than two years before
Host must be a nonprofit research institution (US hosts need 501(c)(3) status and an IRS 'not a private foundation' letter; non-US hosts must prove nonprofit status)
Research in mammalian reproductive biology related to fertility regulation
documents: Appendix A: project narrative of up to 5 pages including figures and references
Appendix B: four letters (two independent expert reviews, one reference letter and one sponsor/mentor letter), with NIH-style biographical sketches
Appendix C: signed institutional representation form
opportunities.selection_process: A confidential scientific review committee scores each application on three equally weighted criteria: the host institution and its resources, the applicant's merit, and the scientific merit of the proposal. The top 8 to 12 are ranked for the trustees, who make the final awards.
opportunities.about_provider: The Lalor Foundation is a US private foundation that advances research and innovation in reproductive health. It has long supported early-career researchers in mammalian reproductive biology.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the Lalor Foundation online application system and use the access code given on the instructions page, then upload the narrative, letters and signed institutional form. Ask referees and the mentor to submit by 1 January so the file is complete well before the 15 January deadline.
opportunities.notes: The FAQ gives the cut-off as midnight EST and the instructions as 11:59 pm EST on 15 January; submit early. Questions go to the foundation's administrator listed on the site.

opportunities.title: Lingnan University Postgraduate Studentships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a good honours bachelor's or a master's can apply by 15 January 2027 for a full-time MPhil or PhD at Lingnan University, Hong Kong, and are normally awarded a monthly studentship of about HK$19,000.
opportunities.description:
Lingnan University in Hong Kong admits full-time MPhil and PhD students through its Direct Admissions route, and full-time admittees are normally awarded a Postgraduate Studentship that pays a monthly stipend. The main round for September 2027 entry runs from 1 September 2026 to 15 January 2027, with two later clearing rounds.

Lingnan is Hong Kong's liberal arts university, and its research degrees span the humanities, social sciences, business and data-related fields. Applicants may apply to a maximum of two programmes in the online admission system.

Non-local students, including Africans, are eligible for the studentship, although they do not receive the Hong Kong government tuition waiver that local students may get. A separate, more generous route is the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme, which closed for this round on 1 December 2026 applications.
opportunities.benefits: Postgraduate Studentship (2026-27 rates): MPhil HK$19,010 per month; PhD HK$19,280 per month, rising to HK$19,660 after confirmation of candidature. Holders give up to 12 hours a week of teaching or research support. Further support is available for conferences and field trips, and for overseas research visits.
requirements: MPhil: relevant bachelor's degree with first or second class honours, or equivalent

PhD: a master's degree, or a bachelor's with first or second class honours plus at least one year of master's study and evidence of research, or a first-class bachelor's with substantial research achievement
If your degree was not taught in English: TOEFL iBT 79 (tests before 21 January 2026) or the new-scale 4 (tests from 21 January 2026), or IELTS 6.5, taken at a test centre within the last two years
Full-time study for the studentship
Programme-specific requirements may apply
documents: Online application in the Lingnan admission system (select 'Direct Admissions (2027-28)')
Research proposal and references as required by the programme
opportunities.selection_process: Programmes review applications on academic record, research potential and proposal; full-time admittees are normally awarded a studentship with the offer.
important_dates: Main round: 1 September 2026 to 15 January 2027, 11:59 pm Hong Kong time (September 2027 intake)
2nd clearing round: 1 May to 31 August 2027 (January 2028 intake)
opportunities.about_provider: Lingnan University is a public liberal arts university in Tuen Mun, Hong Kong. Its School of Graduate Studies runs the research postgraduate (MPhil and PhD) programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Lingnan's online admission system, choosing 'Direct Admissions (2027-28)' and up to two programmes, and pay the non-refundable application fee. Apply in the main round by 15 January 2027 for the best chance of a studentship.
opportunities.notes: You cannot transfer an application between the HKPFS route and direct admission. Lingnan advises its own graduates not to apply for its PhD.

opportunities.title: M. H. Wiener Laboratory Annual Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and holders of a master's or doctorate from any university worldwide can apply by 15 January 2027 for up to nine months of archaeological-science research at the Wiener Laboratory in Athens.
opportunities.description:
The M. H. Wiener Annual Fellowship (formerly the Research Associate Appointment) supports short, focused projects in archaeological science at the Malcolm H. Wiener Laboratory of the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (ASCSA). Projects should relate to the ancient Greek world or neighbouring regions.

The fellowship term is flexible, up to nine months, with the next term beginning in early September 2027. Fellows work with the laboratory's facilities and become associate members of the School.

Applications are welcome from any college or university worldwide and from independent scholars, so African researchers in bioarchaeology, archaeometry, geoarchaeology and related sciences may apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of up to US$7,000 plus waiver of School and Laboratory fees. Room and board are paid by the fellow; the project budget is capped at US$7,000.
requirements: Enrolled in a graduate programme, or holding a master's or doctorate in a relevant field (independent scholars welcome)
Project in archaeological science linked to the Greek world or adjacent regions
Permits or letters from authorities and excavation directors for the material studied
Past recipients of this fellowship or a Wiener Research Fellowship must wait two years
documents: Results of any previous Wiener-funded work
Facilities, equipment and sample numbers needed
One reference letter from a scholar in the field
Statement of expected contributions to the Laboratory and the School
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed for intellectual merit and broader impacts.
opportunities.about_provider: The American School of Classical Studies at Athens, founded in 1881, is a leading centre for research on Greece. Its Wiener Laboratory specialises in archaeological science.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application through the ASCSA Wiener Laboratory fellowships form on Submittable by 15 January 2027 and ask your referee to send the letter by the same date. Applications without the required permits may not be considered.
opportunities.notes: Questions go to the Laboratory Director, Dr Panagiotis Karkanas. Successful applicants receive ASCSA associate membership automatically.

opportunities.title: Mr. Julia Henriëtte Jaarsma-Adolfs Fund Scholarship – Amsterdam Law School
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Dutch applicants with top grades applying to one of four Amsterdam Law School LLM programmes can apply by 15 January 2027 for this single annual scholarship (amount to be announced).
opportunities.description:
The Mr. Julia Henriëtte Jaarsma-Adolfs Fund Scholarship helps one exceptionally talented and motivated non-Dutch student each year to follow a full-time LLM at the University of Amsterdam's Amsterdam Graduate School of Law. Students from both inside and outside the European Economic Area may apply.

The 2027-2028 award is tied to four LLM programmes: International and European Law, Transnational and European Private Law, Law and Finance, and International Criminal Law. The amount for 2027-2028 has not yet been announced.

For African law graduates with very strong grades, this is a second chance at funding alongside the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship, since one application and motivation letter covers both.
opportunities.benefits: A scholarship towards the LLM year; the amount for 2027-2028 is to be announced. One scholarship is awarded per year.
requirements: Non-Dutch nationality and not eligible for Dutch student finance
Applying for a first master's at the UvA
Full-time enrolment in one of four eligible LLM programmes
Grades comparable to a 4.0 US GPA, UK first-class honours or 8.0 on the Dutch scale
Able to meet Dutch visa requirements
documents: Motivation letter of up to 500 words (the same letter covers the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship)
opportunities.selection_process: According to the full scholarship page, the award is decided by lottery among eligible applicants; a shorter UvA summary says selection looks at academic records and motivation. The decision is announced by the end of May.
important_dates: Deadline: 15 January 2027, 23:59 CET (with the LLM application)
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Amsterdam is a public research university in the Netherlands. The Amsterdam Law School administers this fund-based scholarship for its English-taught LLM programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible LLM programme, choose the Jaarsma-Adolfs Fund scholarship on the 'Scholarship' tab, and upload one motivation letter on the 'Additional documents' tab. Incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Apply for both this award and the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship in the same application to double your chances.

opportunities.title: Pomona College need-based financial aid for international students (fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year and transfer applicants to Pomona who apply for aid with their admission application.
opportunities.description:
Pomona College, a liberal arts college in Claremont, California, gives need-based financial aid to international students. There is no separate named scholarship: aid is awarded from the college's own funds based on each family's financial need, and it is set at the time of admission.

Admission for international students is need-aware, which means the admission committee takes financial need into account. Students who do not apply for aid when they apply cannot ask for it later, so applicants who need support must apply for aid at the same time as admission.

The remaining deadlines are 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision (the Early Decision I deadline of 15 November has passed). For African students, Pomona's need-based aid can cover a large part of the cost of a US liberal arts degree.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based grant aid from Pomona College, set at admission according to demonstrated financial need; the amount is not re-assessed each year.
requirements: International first-year applicant (or transfer applicant at the time of admission only)
Apply for aid together with the admission application
Admission is need-aware for international students
documents: CSS Profile (Pomona school code 4607), or the Pomona College International Financial Aid Application if the CSS fee is a burden
Translated copies of prior-prior year tax or income documents
opportunities.selection_process: Aid is calculated on demonstrated need, and financial need is considered by the Admissions Committee when it decides on international applicants.
opportunities.about_provider: Pomona College is a highly selective private liberal arts college in Claremont, California, and a founding member of the Claremont Colleges consortium.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Pomona and, by the same deadline, submit the CSS Profile (or Pomona's international aid form) and translated income documents. Admitted students who did not apply for aid cannot appeal for aid later.
opportunities.notes: The CSS Profile opens on 1 October. The deadlines page does not print a year; the January dates apply to the current admission cycle for fall 2027 entry.

opportunities.title: Reading AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Prospective arts and humanities PhD students, including international applicants, who apply to an eligible Reading PhD by 15 January 2027 can be considered for one of three AHRC studentships paying home fees and a GBP 21,805 stipend.
opportunities.description:
The University of Reading offers three AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award studentships a year for PhD study in the arts and humanities, starting in October 2027. The awards are funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council through its Doctoral Landscape scheme and administered by Reading's Doctoral and Researcher College.

Applicants first apply for a place on an eligible Reading PhD programme by 15 January 2027 and then complete an expression of interest. Departments nominate their strongest candidates to a university panel.

International applicants, including Africans, can win up to 30% of the awards, but the studentship pays fees only at the home rate, so they must find the difference between home and international fees themselves.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition fees at the UK/Republic of Ireland rate, a tax-free stipend (2026/27 rate GBP 21,805 a year) and limited research and training funds. Visa costs and the immigration health surcharge are not covered.
requirements: Apply for a place on an eligible arts and humanities PhD programme at Reading by 15 January 2027
Full-time or part-time study, not by distance learning
Not already a Reading PhD student
International applicants must pay the difference between home and international fees (at least GBP 16,512 a year full-time)
documents: Expression of interest form for the studentship
Revised research proposal if invited (by 1 March 2027)
opportunities.selection_process: Departments review applicants and nominate candidates to a university panel, which judges academic excellence and readiness for research, the quality of the proposal and the supervision arrangements. Nominated applicants are asked to revise their proposal by 1 March 2027.
important_dates: Revised proposals from nominees: by 1 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Reading is a research-intensive UK university. Its Doctoral and Researcher College manages doctoral funding, including UKRI-funded studentships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible Reading PhD programme by 15 January 2027, then complete the studentship expression of interest form linked from the funding page. Discuss your proposal with a potential supervisor first.
opportunities.notes: Only three awards are made each year. International applicants should plan how they will cover the fee difference before applying.

opportunities.title: Rider University First-Year Merit Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: First-year applicants for 2027 entry who apply to Rider University by 15 January 2027 with at least a 2.7 GPA are automatically considered for merit scholarships of USD 15,000 to 28,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
Rider University, a private university in Lawrenceville, New Jersey, awards merit scholarships to first-year students entering in Spring 2027, Fall 2027 or Spring 2028. The awards are given automatically on admission, with no separate application, and can be renewed for up to four years.

Rider is test-optional and considers students for most merit awards without SAT or ACT scores. To be considered for the merit scholarships, students should submit their admission application by 15 January.

The official pages do not describe a separate scholarship just for international students, but they also set no citizenship condition on the merit awards, so international applicants who meet the grade threshold are considered as part of admission. African applicants should confirm with Rider's international admissions office.
opportunities.benefits: Merit scholarships of USD 15,000 to 28,000 per year, renewable for up to four years. Smaller awards include a USD 1,000-a-year Bronc Visit Award for eligible campus visitors and subject awards such as USD 2,000 a year in accounting and up to USD 5,000 a year in teacher education.
requirements: Admissible as a full-time first-year student
Minimum unweighted cumulative GPA of 2.7 on a 4.0 scale
Audition where the programme requires one
Test-optional: SAT/ACT not needed for most merit awards
Keep a 2.0 cumulative GPA to renew
documents: Audition materials for performing arts programmes
opportunities.selection_process: Admitted first-year students are automatically reviewed for merit awards based on their academic record; no separate scholarship application is required.
important_dates: Musical Theatre and Acting applicants: by 15 November
Application for merit consideration: by 15 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Rider University is a private university in Lawrenceville, New Jersey, offering undergraduate and graduate programmes in business, education, arts and sciences, and the performing arts.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for first-year admission through Rider's international admissions process by 15 January 2027; scholarship decisions arrive with the admission offer. Contact Rider One Stop (onestop@rider.edu) with aid questions.
opportunities.notes: The New Jersey Tuition Guarantee applies only to New Jersey residents. Need-based aid at Rider uses the FAFSA, which is generally for US citizens.

opportunities.title: Schwarz Fellowship for Research on Music 2027-28 (Gennadius Library)
opportunities.provider: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to career musicians, PhD candidates and scholars within five years of the PhD, of any nationality, researching music; apply by 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Schwarz Fellowship supports research on music, including Greek and Byzantine musical traditions, carried out with the collections of the Gennadius Library at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (ASCSA).

The award supports research in Athens during the 2027-28 academic year, and fellows are expected to make full use of the library's rare books, archives and open-stack collections.

The ASCSA states that the fellowship is open to all nationalities, so African doctoral students and early-career researchers working on Greek, Byzantine, Ottoman or Mediterranean topics can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of US$11,500 for the academic year, as listed on the ASCSA fellowships page.
requirements: Eligible career stage: career musicians, PhD candidates and scholars within five years of the PhD
Research that requires the Gennadius Library collections
Open to all nationalities
documents: Online application on the ASCSA Submittable portal
Reference letters as requested on the form
opportunities.selection_process: A School committee reviews the applications; awards are announced in the spring.
opportunities.about_provider: The American School of Classical Studies at Athens, founded in 1881, is a leading research centre on Greece. Its Gennadius Library holds more than 150,000 titles on Greece from antiquity to the present.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the fellowship form on the ASCSA Submittable portal before the deadline, uploading your CV and project description and arranging the requested references.
opportunities.notes: Application form: https://ascsa.submittable.com/submit/189405/schwarz-fellowship-at-the-gennadius-library-for-research-on-music

opportunities.title: Smith College Need-Based Financial Aid for International First-Year Students (Fall 2027 entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-US citizens applying as first-year (or transfer) students for September 2027 can receive need-based aid that meets their full documented need, but only if they apply for aid together with their admission application and by the aid deadlines.
opportunities.description:
Smith College, a private liberal arts college for women in Northampton, Massachusetts, offers need-based financial aid to international students who are not US citizens. Aid for the September 2027 entry is awarded alongside the admission decision, and for admitted students who applied for aid on time the college commits to covering their full documented financial need with grants rather than loans.

The main award is the Smith Grant, which is sized from the family's assessed ability to pay against the full cost of attendance (tuition, housing, food, fees, insurance, books, travel and personal costs). The college adjusts the grant over the years so that the family's expected contribution stays broadly stable. International students who receive need-based aid also get a grant covering the college health insurance.

The programme matters for African applicants because Smith is one of a small group of US colleges that meet full need for international students, which can make a degree costing over USD 100,000 a year affordable. The pool is very competitive, and the college states that the level of support varies widely between students. The timing rule is strict: an international student who does not ask for aid before being admitted can never receive institutional aid at Smith later.
opportunities.benefits: A need-based Smith Grant that, together with any outside support, meets 100% of the documented need of admitted students who applied for aid by the deadlines; undergraduate institutional packages contain no loans. Recipients also receive a health grant that covers the college health insurance. For reference, the published 2026-27 cost of attendance is: tuition USD 70,460; food and housing USD 24,520; student activities fee USD 308; health insurance USD 4,030; books USD 800; international transport (average) USD 1,000; personal costs USD 1,910.
requirements: Not a US citizen (international applicant)
Applying for first-year (or transfer) entry in September 2027
Must apply for financial aid at the same time as applying for admission and by the aid deadlines; no institutional aid is ever offered to international students who did not apply before admission

English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, PTE or Duolingo) unless English is the first language, secondary school was taught in English, the student had two years of US English-medium schooling, or holds an IB Diploma or A-levels taught in English
SAT/ACT scores are optional
Women's college: applicants apply under Smith's admission policy for women
documents: Secondary school report with official transcript
Midyear report (by 15 February for Regular Decision)
CSS Profile 2027-28 (Smith code 3762; fee waivers available)
Translated and signed 2025 parent tax return, or the International Parent Non-Filer form plus a translated employer statement of income
Optional standardised test scores and English test results where required
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is holistic, looking at the student's academic record, recommendations, writing and activities. Financial aid staff then review the CSS Profile and income documents using federal and institutional methods to work out the family contribution and the student's need against the cost of attendance. Admission of international applicants is competitive and aid amounts differ widely between students.
important_dates: Early Decision I application and CSS Profile: 15 November 2026
Early Decision II application: 5 January 2027 (aid forms 6 January 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: Smith College is a private women's liberal arts college in Northampton, Massachusetts, USA. It admits first-year and transfer students and awards both need-based aid and merit awards, with merit decided only at the time of admission.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application or Coalition on Scoir (no application fee) and mark that you are applying for aid. Complete the 2027-28 CSS Profile on the College Board site and upload translated tax or income documents through IDOC; Smith then emails instructions for its Net Partner aid portal. Meet the deadline for your chosen round (Early Decision I, Early Decision II or Regular Decision).
opportunities.notes: Early Decision is binding, but a student can be released if the aid offered makes attendance impossible. Outside scholarships first reduce the work-study portion and then the Smith Grant; state or federal grants reduce the Smith Grant dollar for dollar. International students may not take off-campus jobs. Contact Student Financial Services at sfs@smith.edu or +1 413-585-2530.

opportunities.title: Stockholm University Scholarship Scheme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fee-paying non-EU/EEA applicants who apply to a Stockholm University master's by 15 January 2027 and are admitted can receive a full tuition scholarship.
opportunities.description:
Stockholm University's Scholarship Scheme pays the full tuition fee for selected fee-paying students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are admitted to a master's programme starting in autumn 2027. It does not cover living costs.

To be considered, students must apply in the first, international admission round on universityadmissions.se, which closes on 15 January 2027. After the selection results on 1 April, eligible admitted students receive an electronic scholarship application form in their University Admissions account.

Awards are based on academic merit, and priority goes to students who ranked Stockholm University as their first choice, which is a useful tip for African applicants choosing between Swedish universities.
opportunities.benefits: Covers the whole tuition fee for the master's programme. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who must pay tuition fees
Admitted to a master's programme in the first (international) admission round for autumn 2027
Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS or equivalent
English equivalent to Swedish upper-secondary English 6/B
Stockholm University listed as first choice gives priority
documents: Application on universityadmissions.se with degree certificates, transcripts and English proof
Application fee paid and documents uploaded by 1 February 2027
Scholarship form sent after admission results
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarships are awarded on academic merit among admitted fee-paying students, with priority for those who ranked Stockholm University first.
important_dates: Scholarship results: by end of April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Stockholm University is one of Sweden's largest universities, with a broad range of English-taught master's programmes in the sciences, humanities, social sciences and law.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and rank Stockholm University first. Pay the fee and upload documents by 1 February; if admitted and eligible, complete the scholarship form that appears in your account.
opportunities.notes: Business programmes may require GMAT or GRE. Also look at the Swedish Institute scholarships, which are limited to citizens of selected countries.

opportunities.title: Umea University Scholarship for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA citizens who apply by 15 January 2027 to an English-taught Umeå University programme as first priority can register for a full or partial tuition waiver.
opportunities.description:
Umeå University in northern Sweden offers tuition fee waivers to talented students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who start an English-taught bachelor's or master's programme in autumn 2027. Selected students receive a full or partial waiver of their tuition fee.

The process has several steps. Applicants must put an Umeå programme as priority 1 in the first international round on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and pay the application fee by 1 February. Eligible applicants then receive a personal email invitation in early February and must register their interest by 5 March 2027.

African applicants from any country outside the EU/EEA can take part, so this is worth planning for early.
opportunities.benefits: A full or partial waiver of the programme tuition fee. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland

opportunities.title: University of Copenhagen Danish Government Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA applicants admitted to a University of Copenhagen master's who apply by 15 January 2027 are automatically considered for a full tuition waiver plus living allowance.
opportunities.description:
The University of Copenhagen awards a limited number of Danish Government Scholarships each year to non-EU/EEA students admitted to its MA and MSc programmes. The scholarships are funded by the Danish state and are given purely on academic merit; financial need is not considered.

There is no separate application. Every eligible non-EU/EEA applicant to a master's starting in September 2027 is considered automatically, provided they apply in the round that closes on 15 January 2027.

For African students, this is one of the most generous master's awards in the Nordic countries, covering both tuition and basic living costs for the whole two-year degree.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee waiver and basic living costs for 22 months (DKK 11,225 per month at the 2026 level).
requirements: Citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland
Admitted to a University of Copenhagen MA or MSc programme
Granted a time-limited Danish residence permit for study
Not entitled to Danish citizen rights or the Danish SU state grant
Strong academic record (merit-based)
documents: Regular master's application documents (no separate scholarship application)
Payment of the DKK 1,120 application fee
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are made on academic criteria during the admission assessment. Offers must be accepted by the stated deadline or they are withdrawn.
opportunities.about_provider: Founded in 1479, the University of Copenhagen is Denmark's oldest and largest university and one of the leading research universities in Europe.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Pay the application fee, then apply for your chosen master's through the University of Copenhagen application portal by 15 January 2027. Eligible applicants are considered automatically and must accept any scholarship offer by the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Estimated living costs are €1,280-1,800 a month; the allowance covers basic costs only.

opportunities.title: University of Notre Dame Need-Blind Admission and Financial Aid for International Undergraduates (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants are admitted need-blind and considered for need-based University scholarships by submitting the 2027-28 CSS Profile by 15 January 2027 (application due 1 January 2027).

opportunities.title: University of South Florida Green and Gold International Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants for Summer or Fall 2027 who complete their USF application by 15 January 2027 are automatically considered for Green and Gold tuition waivers worth up to USD 11,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
The University of South Florida (USF), a large public research university in Tampa, Florida, gives Green and Gold tuition waivers to international first-year students it admits for Summer or Fall 2027. These are merit awards that reduce tuition each year for up to four years.

There is no separate scholarship form. Every international first-year applicant who submits a complete application by the scholarship consideration date is automatically reviewed, using the same academic record that the admissions team uses. The number of awards is limited, so applying early and completely matters.

For African school leavers who want a US bachelor's degree, the waivers can cut the cost of an international tuition bill substantially, but they do not cover the full cost of study, so applicants should plan for the remaining tuition, housing and living costs.
opportunities.benefits: Green and Gold Presidential Waiver of about USD 44,000 in total (up to USD 11,000 a year); Directors Waiver of about USD 36,000 (up to USD 9,000 a year); Scholars Waiver of about USD 20,000 (up to USD 5,000 a year). These cannot be combined with USF's out-of-state merit tuition waivers.
requirements: International applicant for first-year (freshman) entry in Summer or Fall 2027
Complete application, including test scores, transcripts and fee, by 15 January 2027

For applicants whose first language is not English: SAT Reading and Writing 490+, or ACT English 17+ and Reading 19+, or CLT Verbal Reasoning and Writing 38+ (TOEFL, IELTS and Duolingo are not accepted in place of these for this purpose)
Awards are based on the academic record used for admission
documents: USF online application or Common App
STARS self-reported record or official secondary school transcripts
Official SAT, ACT or CLT scores sent by the testing agency (SAT code 5828, ACT code 0761)
opportunities.selection_process: All admitted international first-year students who completed their file on time are considered automatically. Awards are made on academic merit from the admission file, and numbers are limited.
important_dates: Take SAT/ACT before December so scores arrive in time for Fall decisions
Award notice: by post, also visible in the Student Self-Service portal
opportunities.about_provider: The University of South Florida is a public research university based in Tampa, Florida, with campuses in St. Petersburg and Sarasota-Manatee. Its Office of Admissions handles international first-year applications and merit awards.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for Summer or Fall 2027 through the USF application or the Common App, pay the USD 30 fee, and submit your transcripts and test scores before 15 January 2027. No extra scholarship form is needed; track your file and any award in the USF applicant and Self-Service portals.
opportunities.notes: Questions go to USF International Admissions (international@usf.edu). Because English is assessed through SAT, ACT or CLT section scores, plan your test dates early.

opportunities.title: Wesleyan University Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants who apply for aid with their Regular Decision application are covered by Wesleyan's policy of meeting 100% of every admitted student's demonstrated need.

opportunities.title: XJTLU Postgraduate Research Scholarships for funded PhD projects (2027 intakes)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a bachelor's and master's (or equivalent) and an English test who apply to a listed XJTLU PhD project.
opportunities.description:
Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU) in Suzhou, China, funds full-time PhD students through its Postgraduate Research Scholarships. Students join a listed research project, study for three years, and receive a University of Liverpool PhD degree after a final review by Liverpool.

There are three levels of award: a full scholarship (tuition waiver plus a monthly stipend), a fees-only scholarship, and a partial award that cuts tuition by up to half. Funded projects are advertised across areas such as AI and advanced technology, life and natural sciences, design and semiconductors, and each stays open until filled.

For 2027 entry, applications for existing funded projects close on 15 January 2027 (start 1 June 2027) and 30 April 2027 (start 1 September 2027). The scheme sets no nationality limit, so African master's graduates can compete for a funded PhD with a UK degree while living in China.
opportunities.benefits: Full scholarship: tuition waiver worth RMB 297,000 over three years plus a stipend of RMB 5,000 per month for three years (RMB 180,000 in total); holders must take a teaching or research assistant role. Fees-only scholarship: tuition waiver worth RMB 297,000. Partial scholarship: up to 50% off tuition for three years (worth RMB 148,500). Paid TA/RA roles may also be offered to other award holders.
requirements: Full-time PhD study at XJTLU in Suzhou
Bachelor's and master's degree (or enrolment statement if not yet completed)
English test certificate (IELTS or equivalent)
Application to a specific advertised funded project, ideally after contacting the supervisor
documents: Two references, at least one academic, on letterhead with a handwritten signature
Master's dissertation (Business, Humanities and Social Sciences applicants)
opportunities.selection_process: XJTLU reviews the application first and the University of Liverpool makes the final decision. Merit-based awards are judged on academic excellence, research potential, research experience and achievements.
important_dates: Self-funded / merit scholarship round 2: 15 January 2027 (start 1 September 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University is a joint-venture university in Suzhou, China, founded by Xi'an Jiaotong University and the University of Liverpool. Its PhD degrees are awarded by the University of Liverpool.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose a funded project on the scholarships page and contact the supervisor, then apply through XJTLU's online 'Apply Now' form, uploading the proposal, transcripts, English test and references (each file under 2 MB, in English or with certified translations). Questions go to doctoralstudies@xjtlu.edu.cn.
opportunities.notes: Projects close once filled, so apply early. Minimum English scores are on XJTLU's PhD entry requirements page.

opportunities.title: Joint ICTP-IAEA School on Nuclear Security (Apr 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: School in Trieste, 12 to 22 April 2027, for early-career professionals from developing countries with one to three years of experience who first complete eight IAEA e-learning modules; no fee and limited grants.

opportunities.title: CEGA Visiting Fellowship for African Researchers 2027/2028
opportunities.provider: Center for Effective Global Action (UC Berkeley)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Social science researchers and practitioners from East and West Africa with at least a master's can apply by 17 January 2027 for a 16-week CEGA impact-evaluation fellowship at Berkeley or online.
opportunities.description:
The Center for Effective Global Action (CEGA) at the University of California, Berkeley runs a 16-week Visiting Fellowship that trains East and West African researchers and practitioners in impact evaluation. The 2027-2028 cohort can join in Fall 2027 (August to December) or Spring 2028 (January to May), either as Resident fellows at Berkeley or as Non-Resident fellows working online.

There are two tracks: a Practitioner track (about 7 places) for staff of NGOs, think tanks and ministries, and an Academic track (about 4 places) for doctoral students and university or research staff. Fellows build skills in rigorous evaluation, research design and evidence use, and are expected to return to an institution in East or West Africa.

Alumni can later compete for CEGA's catalyst, pilot and research grants, so the fellowship is also an entry point into a wider research network on development economics.
opportunities.benefits: Resident fellows: round-trip flights, accommodation, meals, visa fees, health insurance and a stipend. Non-Resident fellows: a stipend for internet and data costs. No salary or family support is provided.
requirements: National of an East or West African country (not open to Southern, Central or North Africa)
Completed at least secondary school in Africa
At least a master's degree, or enrolled in a PhD, or PhD completed within the last 8 years, in a social science
Fluent English
Plan to return to an institution in East or West Africa
Resident track only: national of a J-1-eligible country (Djibouti, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Liberia, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Rwanda, Seychelles, Uganda)
Practitioner track: works for an NGO, think tank or ministry; Academic track: doctoral student or university/research staff
Employer leave or support for 40 h/week (Resident) or 15-20 h/week (Non-Resident) for four months
documents: Policy statement (Practitioner) or research proposal (Academic), max 2 pages
Letter from employer approving leave or time commitment
opportunities.selection_process: CEGA reviews applications by track, looking at academic and professional background, quantitative preparation, the policy statement or research proposal, and the applicant's plans to apply evaluation skills in East or West Africa.
opportunities.about_provider: CEGA is a research centre at UC Berkeley that connects researchers and policymakers to generate rigorous evidence on poverty and development. Its African fellowship programme builds evaluation capacity among researchers from the region.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application through CEGA's Submittable portal (2027-28 CEGA Visiting Fellowship). Prepare the statements, CV and employer letter in advance, and register for the 2 December webinar from the call page. Questions go to global-networks-cega@berkeley.edu.
opportunities.notes: Non-Resident priority countries include Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Togo, Zambia and Zimbabwe. The full call is also available as a PDF from the CEGA page.

opportunities.title: CUHK School of Journalism and Communication Internationalization Scholarship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, School of Journalism and Communication
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted to a postgraduate programme of CUHK's School of Journalism and Communication for September 2027 can be nominated for one of five HK$80,000 awards.
opportunities.description:
CUHK's School of Journalism and Communication offers five Internationalization Scholarships each year to international students admitted to its taught postgraduate programmes. The awards recognise students who will add an international perspective to the school's classes in Hong Kong.

There is no separate scholarship form. A selection panel nominates winners on academic merit from the admission materials of applicants to the September 2027 intake. Programme deadlines are 7 December 2026 for the priority round and 18 January 2027 for the final round; the MSc in AI and Communication accepts applications until 31 March 2027. Applying in the priority round gives the best chance of being considered.

For African journalists and communication graduates the award offers a useful contribution towards the cost of a one-year master's at one of Asia's leading communication schools.
opportunities.benefits: HK$80,000 per award; five awards are available each year.
requirements: International student
Admitted to a taught postgraduate programme of the CUHK School of Journalism and Communication for the September 2027 intake
Strong academic merit
Able to add to the international mix of the class
Must start studies in September 2027
documents: Supporting documents sent by courier to the school as requested by the programme
opportunities.selection_process: The school's selection panel nominates awardees on academic merit, judged from the admission application. No separate interview for the scholarship is described.
important_dates: MSc in AI and Communication deadline: 31 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The School of Journalism and Communication at CUHK is one of the oldest journalism schools in Asia and offers MA and MSc programmes in journalism, global communication, new media and related fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online for one of the school's postgraduate programmes through the CUHK Graduate School system, preferably by the 7 December 2026 priority round, and courier any required supporting documents to the school. All admitted international applicants are considered for the scholarship.
opportunities.notes: A separate scholarship for practising Hong Kong journalists is open to local applicants only.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Six fully funded AHRC and BCU PhD studentships for September 2027 open to home and international applicants, with an optional expression of interest by 16 November 2026 and final applications by 20 January 2027.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: People aged 18 to 50 of any nationality with working English can apply (USD 17 fee) for one of 50 fully funded or 100 partially funded places at the 13-16 April 2027 summit in Madrid.

opportunities.title: IJP Southern Africa Federal President Horst Köhler Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists aged 25-40 from SADC countries or Kenya can apply by 20 January 2027 for a two-month placement in a German newsroom with a EUR 3,500 bursary.
opportunities.description:
The International Journalists' Programmes (IJP) run the Federal President Horst Köhler Fellowship, an exchange that places journalists from Southern Africa in German newsrooms for about two months. In 2027 the Southern African fellows are expected to travel in July and August (to be confirmed), starting with an introductory conference in Berlin.

During the placement, fellows work at a German media outlet and produce stories for their home newsroom, building contacts and reporting on Germany and Europe. German journalists take part in the reverse exchange to Southern Africa.

The programme is mainly funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. It is open to journalists from SADC member states and Kenya, and up to five Southern African journalists are chosen each year.
opportunities.benefits: A fixed bursary of EUR 3,500, expected to cover most travel, accommodation and living costs during the fellowship. The full grant depends on a report of at least three pages and copies of published work after the fellowship.
requirements: Journalist from a SADC member state or Kenya
Aged 25 to 40
Working regularly for a media organisation
Strong English; German is an advantage
Employer must agree to the leave of absence
documents: CV with passport photo (and language certificates if available)
Essay of about 800 words: why Germany, three research topics, future role at your home outlet, planned use of the bursary
Reference from your editor-in-chief or head of department that also confirms leave
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee chooses up to five fellows, and its decision is final. Applicants rank preferred host outlets, and IJP agrees the final placement with each fellow.
important_dates: Fellowship: July and August 2027 (to be confirmed), starting in Berlin
opportunities.about_provider: IJP is a German non-profit organisation that runs exchange programmes for journalists from many world regions. Its Southern Africa programme is named after former German Federal President Horst Köhler.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email the CV, essay, work samples and editor's reference to IJP (office@ijp.org) between 1 November 2026 and 20 January 2027. Read the 2027 call PDF on the programme page for the list of eligible countries.
opportunities.notes: Programme coordinator: Marco Vollmar at IJP. Plan research topics that suit German host outlets, as they influence placement.

opportunities.title: Kupcinet-Getz International Summer Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's or master's students past their first year, or recent bachelor's graduates, with a GPA of at least 3.6 can join an eight-week summer research program with a $1,100 stipend and a flight subsidy.

opportunities.title: LISS DTP ESRC Open Competition 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Social science graduates with strong grades, including international applicants, can apply by 20 January 2027 for ESRC-funded doctoral studentships at King's, Queen Mary or Imperial through LISS DTP.
opportunities.description:
The London Interdisciplinary Social Science Doctoral Training Partnership (LISS DTP) is funded by the UK Economic and Social Research Council and led by King's College London with Imperial College London and Queen Mary University of London. Its open competition offers social science doctoral studentships starting in October 2027.

Applicants choose one of two formats: 1+3.5 (a master's year followed by a PhD) or +3.5 (PhD only). They must also apply to a relevant programme at one of the three partner universities and secure supervisor support.

Both home and international students may apply, but UKRI rules cap international awards at 30%, so competition for those places is strong. African social scientists with excellent grades and a well-developed project are eligible.
opportunities.benefits: ESRC studentship covering tuition fees and a stipend for the length of the award; the international fee difference is covered only for a limited number of international students. Visa, immigration health surcharge and travel costs are not covered.
requirements: First degree at first class or upper second (average of 65% or above)
For the +3.5 route, a master's at distinction or high merit
Apply to a relevant programme at King's, Queen Mary or Imperial
Not already holding a PhD, and at least 50% of study time remaining if already enrolled
Live within reasonable travel distance of London once funded
Home and international applicants eligible (international awards capped at 30%)
documents: Online application in the LISS DTP portal (liss-dtp.flexigrant.com)
Official transcripts showing modules, credits and grades (certified translations if needed)
One reference from someone who is not your supervisor, on letterhead
KCL fee-waiver form (by 18 January) or Imperial departmental support form where relevant
opportunities.selection_process: Academic reviewers longlist applications, which are then scored, discussed by research-area panels and finalised by a high-level panel. No individual feedback is given.
important_dates: Final outcomes: end of April 2027 (offers week of 27 April)
opportunities.about_provider: LISS DTP is one of the ESRC's doctoral training partnerships, bringing together King's College London, Imperial College London and Queen Mary University of London to train social science researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree a project with a supervisor at King's, Queen Mary or Imperial, apply for the PhD (or master's plus PhD) there, and submit the LISS DTP application in its portal by 20 January 2027. Contact liss-dtp@kcl.ac.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: Apply for one format only (1+3.5 or +3.5). LISS also offers CASE studentships with partner organisations.

opportunities.title: University of York AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards in the Arts and Humanities 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international applicants with an outstanding record and a York PhD offer in an AHRC subject can apply by 20 January 2027; international winners must cover the gap between home and international fees.
opportunities.description:
The University of York awards six AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards for PhD students in the arts and humanities who start in September 2027. The studentships are funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council, part of UK Research and Innovation, and cover research within the AHRC's remit, whether based in York's Faculty of Arts and Humanities or in its science and social science faculties.

Each award pays a tax-free living stipend and waives tuition at the UK (home) rate. International applicants, including those from Africa, are eligible, but the award does not pay the difference between home and international fees, so they need other funds to cover it.

York runs an online information session on 18 November 2026 and an application-writing workshop on 25 November 2026 for interested applicants.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of GBP 21,805 a year (2026/27 rate; 2027/28 rates published early 2027) plus a tuition fee waiver at the UK home rate. International students must pay the difference between home and international fees themselves.
requirements: An offer of a PhD place in a relevant York department, starting September 2027 (no deferrals)
Outstanding academic record, usually a first-class degree and a master's Distinction or equivalent experience
Research within the AHRC subject remit
Must live in the UK within reasonable distance of York during the PhD; distance learning is not funded
Not already a doctoral student and not in full-time employment at the start
documents: Separate PhD application to York (advised by early December 2026)
opportunities.selection_process: Each department ranks its candidates, and a Faculty of Arts and Humanities panel then ranks the whole group. The process finishes by the end of March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of York is a UK research university and member of the Russell Group. The AHRC is UK Research and Innovation's council for arts and humanities research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a PhD place at York, ideally by early December 2026, and complete the AHRC DLA online studentship form by 20 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Six awards are available. Part-time paid work of up to about six hours a week is allowed with supervisor approval. Contact: pgr-finance@york.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: Wolfson Postgraduate Scholarships in the Humanities, University of York 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Outstanding humanities graduates of any nationality applying for a York PhD in history, literature or languages can apply by 20 January 2027 for a Wolfson scholarship worth GBP 38,000 a year for three years.
opportunities.description:
The University of York, with funding from the Wolfson Foundation, offers three doctoral scholarships in the humanities for PhD study starting in September 2027. The awards cover history, literature and languages, and are among the most generous humanities PhD awards in the UK.

Each scholarship provides GBP 38,000 a year for three years. It pays home-rate tuition fees and the rest goes towards maintenance, research, travel and training. Overseas students receive the home fee rate only, so they need to cover the difference between home and international fees.

The scholarships are open to all nationalities, so outstanding African humanities graduates with a master's can apply, provided they can arrange the extra fee funding.
opportunities.benefits: GBP 38,000 per year for three years (GBP 114,000 in total), covering home-rate tuition fees and, from the balance, maintenance, research, travel and training costs. Overseas students receive home-rate fees only.
requirements: Applied for (ideally holding an offer for) a PhD in a relevant York department in history, literature or languages, starting September 2027 (no deferral)
Outstanding academic record, usually a first-class undergraduate degree and a master's
Live in the UK for the duration of the award
Open to all nationalities; full-time or part-time
International students must fund the gap between home and international fees
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are passed to scholarship panels, which choose three scholars on academic excellence and the strength of the research project.
important_dates: Submit PhD application: ideally by early December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: The University of York is a research-intensive UK university. The Wolfson Foundation is a UK charity that supports excellence in research and education, including its Wolfson Postgraduate Scholarships in the Humanities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your PhD at York (ideally by early December), then complete the online Wolfson scholarship form by 20 January 2027. Questions on funding go to pgr-finance@york.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: York also offers AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards in the arts and humanities in the same window.

opportunities.title: ACM CHI 2027 Posters, Demos and Student Research Competition (Pittsburgh)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Posters, interactive demos and Student Research Competition entries for CHI 2027 in Pittsburgh (10-14 May 2027) are due 21 January 2027; no travel funding is stated on the homepage.

opportunities.title: CERN Summer Student Programme 2027 (Member and Non-Member States)
opportunities.provider: CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's and master's students of any nationality in physics, engineering, computer science or maths, with at least three years of full-time study by the start date, can apply by 21 January 2027 for a paid summer at CERN.
opportunities.description:
Every summer CERN, the particle physics laboratory near Geneva, hosts several hundred university students from around the world for its Summer Student Programme. Students spend between eight and thirteen weeks working on a research or technical project in one of CERN's teams, attend a lecture series given by CERN scientists, visit the facilities and write a short final report. The 2027 programme ideally starts on 14 June 2027 and is fully on site.

The programme is open to students of all nationalities, with separate funding channels for member and non-member states; in 2025 CERN's donor-funded programme alone supported 60 students from non-member states. Projects span experimental and theoretical physics, computing, engineering and mathematics.

For African science and engineering students it is one of the best-known paid research placements in Europe, combining hands-on work at the world's largest physics laboratory with an international network of peers.
opportunities.benefits: A net subsistence allowance of 94 CHF per calendar day, health insurance (the contribution is deducted from the allowance), travel expenses depending on individual circumstances, help finding accommodation on or near site, and the summer lecture programme.
requirements: Bachelor's or master's student (not PhD)
At least 6 semesters (3 academic years) of full-time university study in a relevant field by the start date
Field: physics, engineering, computer science or mathematics
Enrolled full time for the whole stay
Good knowledge of English
Not previously a CERN summer student and not at CERN for more than 3 months under another status
Open to all nationalities
documents: Official transcripts in English or French
opportunities.selection_process: CERN reviews the applications and may invite candidates to an online interview, followed by an offer and onboarding.
opportunities.about_provider: CERN is the European Organization for Nuclear Research, an intergovernmental laboratory on the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva. It operates the Large Hadron Collider and hosts scientists from more than 100 countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'CERN Summer Student Programme 2027' posting on CERN's careers site, which opens an online form (allow about 15 minutes). Upload your CV, transcripts and enrolment certificate, and arrange your academic reference letter.
opportunities.notes: CERN's general page says applications should arrive by the end of January, but the job posting gives 21 January 2027; use the earlier date. A separate CERN openlab summer programme in computing also runs in 2027.

opportunities.title: CERN openlab Summer Student Programme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's or Master's students of any nationality with at least six semesters completed can spend two paid summer months in Geneva working on computing projects.

opportunities.title: Hanken GBSN Scholarship for Students from Developing Countries 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students or alumni of listed GBSN member schools in countries including Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Tunisia can apply by 21 January 2027 for one of two two-year tuition waivers at Hanken.
opportunities.description:
Hanken School of Economics in Finland awards two GBSN scholarships each year to master's applicants who are students or alumni of specific Global Business School Network (GBSN) member schools in listed developing countries. The scholarship waives the full tuition fee for two academic years of an English-taught master's programme.

The award is made only within Hanken's main admission round for English-taught master's degrees, which runs from 7 to 21 January 2027. Applicants are ranked on academic merit, and the best-ranked eligible applicants receive the scholarship.

African countries on the list are Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Tunisia, so graduates of GBSN member business schools there should check whether their school qualifies.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee waiver for two academic years, equivalent to EUR 15,000 a year. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Student or alumnus/alumna of a specified GBSN member school in a listed developing country
Applying in the main admission round for an English-taught Hanken master's
Bachelor's degree with at least 25-30 ECTS in relevant subjects
English language requirement met
GMAT, GRE or GTEBS aptitude test, or the GPA route, as required
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic success and skills from previous studies, scored from 1.00 to 5.00 (minimum 3.00) and ranked; the two scholarships go to top-ranked eligible applicants.
opportunities.about_provider: Hanken School of Economics is a business school in Helsinki and Vaasa, Finland. It is a member of the Global Business School Network, which links business schools working on management education in developing regions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an English-taught master's at Hanken through Studyinfo.fi between 7 and 21 January 2027 and indicate your GBSN member school. Contact Hanken admissions if unsure whether your school is eligible.
opportunities.notes: Only two scholarships are awarded a year, so meet all main-round requirements, including the aptitude test, early.

opportunities.title: University of Eastern Finland Early-Bird Tuition Discount 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students admitted to a UEF international master's for September 2027 get 30% off first-year tuition if they accept and pay within 21 days; applications close 21 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The University of Eastern Finland (UEF) gives a 30% early-bird discount on first-year tuition to non-EU/EEA students admitted to its English-taught master's programmes starting in September 2027. Tuition is EUR 10,000 to 12,000 a year, so the discount is worth EUR 3,000 to 3,600.

The discount applies automatically if the student accepts the study place and pays the fee (or the first instalment) within 21 days of the admission results. A further 30% waiver for the second year is available to students who complete at least 55 ECTS in year one and apply separately.

UEF does not offer full tuition waivers or humanitarian scholarships, so African applicants should budget for the remaining fees and living costs of about EUR 900 to 1,000 a month.

Admitted to a UEF international master's for the September 2027 intake
Accept the offer and pay the fee or first instalment within 21 days of results
Second-year waiver: at least 55 ECTS completed in year one and a separate application

Non-refundable application fee for non-EU applicants
opportunities.selection_process: No separate scholarship selection for the first year: the discount applies to every fee-liable admitted student who accepts and pays on time.

opportunities.about_provider: The University of Eastern Finland is a multidisciplinary university with campuses in Joensuu and Kuopio. It offers international master's programmes in fields such as forestry, health sciences, computing and education.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a UEF international master's on Studyinfo.fi between 7 and 21 January 2027. When admitted, accept the place and pay within 21 days to receive the early-bird discount automatically.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus CLMCE - Children's Literature, Media and Cultural Entrepreneurship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality with a first degree and good English may apply by 22 January 2027 for a fully funded two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in children's literature, media and cultural entrepreneurship.
opportunities.description:
Children's Literature, Media and Cultural Entrepreneurship (CLMCE) is a two-year, full-time Erasmus Mundus International Master that looks at books, media and creative industries made for young audiences, combining literary and cultural study with the business side of producing and selling cultural content. The University of Glasgow coordinates the programme on behalf of a European university consortium, and the course is co-funded by the European Union through the Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scheme.

Students spend their study periods at different partner universities in at least two countries; the third semester is taken at a consortium institution allocated according to the student's ranking. The intake covered here is the fourth edition (2027-2029), starting in September 2027.

Across its four editions the consortium can offer up to 90 Erasmus Mundus scholarships (60 regular and 30 targeted places). These awards pay all tuition plus a monthly allowance, which makes the programme a fully funded route into Europe for African graduates interested in publishing, children's media, storytelling, education or cultural entrepreneurship.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders have all tuition fees and travel insurance covered and receive EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months (up to EUR 33,600 in total). Students can instead choose three advance payments of EUR 1,000 (to help with visa and travel costs) followed by EUR 1,275 per month.
requirements: A first higher-education degree (bachelor's or recognised equivalent); final-year students may apply if they graduate before the course starts
Proof of English for applicants whose first language is not English, uploaded by the scholarship deadline (minimum score set by the University of Glasgow)
Must not have held an Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scholarship before
At most six scholarships per nationality across the four editions; dual nationals must say which nationality they apply under
Study must take place in at least two countries different from the country of residence at enrolment
documents: CLMCE scholarship application form (uploaded as PDF)
Degree certificate(s), if completed, in the original language
Transcripts with grades, plus official English translations
Two reference letters on letterhead (one academic; the second academic or professional)
opportunities.selection_process: Stage 1 checks eligibility and shortlists candidates on academic excellence. Stage 2 ranks shortlisted applicants on their personal statement and motivation, academic record and English, other relevant experience, and references. Results are emailed in April 2027; appeals are possible within 14 days on procedural grounds only.
important_dates: Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadline: 22 January 2027, 13:00 UK time
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow, founded in 1451, is one of the UK's oldest universities and acts as coordinating institution for the CLMCE consortium. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are flagship EU-funded programmes run jointly by several universities in different countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the University of Glasgow postgraduate application portal using the Apply Now link on the CLMCE how-to-apply page, and upload the scholarship form and all documents. Once started, an application must be completed within 42 days. Questions go through the university's online enquiry form, choosing Erasmus as the level of study.
opportunities.notes: Applicants without a master's degree may be preferred when required. Leave time for referees to prepare letters on letterhead before the January deadline.

opportunities.title: Fordham University International Student Merit Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Fordham are automatically considered for merit awards of USD 10,000-25,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
Fordham University in New York City considers every complete first-year application from international students for merit scholarships of USD 10,000 to 25,000 a year. No separate scholarship application is needed: the award, if any, is shown in the online admission letter.

Awards are renewed at the same amount for up to four years as long as the student keeps the required GPA and satisfactory academic progress. Fordham also gives a limited amount of need-based aid to international students, but its admission is need-aware and need-based awards do not cover the full cost.

For the current admission cycle, the Regular Decision deadline has been extended from 3 January to 22 January, and Early Decision II to 15 January. African students applying to a US university in New York can be considered for these merit awards simply by applying on time.
opportunities.benefits: Merit scholarships of USD 10,000 to 25,000 per year for highly qualified first-year international applicants, renewable at the same amount for up to four years. Transfer students can receive up to USD 25,000. Separate need-based aid is limited and does not cover the full cost.
requirements: International applicant on a non-immigrant visa (US citizens and permanent residents use the domestic process)
Complete first-year application through the Common Application
English test (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Pearson) for non-native speakers without four years of recent English-medium schooling
For need-based aid: CSS Profile and an expected family contribution of at least USD 50,000 a year
Keep the required GPA to renew the award
documents: CSS Profile (school code 2259) if applying for need-based aid
opportunities.selection_process: Merit awards are decided automatically from the complete admission file; there is no separate merit application. Need-based aid is awarded to about 5% of aid applicants.

CSS Profile: 15 January for Regular Decision
opportunities.about_provider: Fordham University is a private Jesuit university in New York City, with campuses at Rose Hill in the Bronx and Lincoln Center in Manhattan.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Fordham through the Common Application by the Regular Decision or Early Decision II deadline; you are then considered for merit awards automatically. If you also need need-based aid, submit the CSS Profile by its deadline.
opportunities.notes: Fordham does not give CSS Profile fee waivers or loans in international aid packages. Applying for need-based aid can affect admission, because admission is need-aware for international students.

opportunities.title: Maryam Mirzakhani Scholarships 2027 (master's plus PhD in mathematics)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Women of any nationality who are finishing a bachelor's or first year of master's, preferably in mathematics, and plan to join an eligible Paris-Saclay or IP Paris mathematics master's can apply.
opportunities.description:
The Maryam Mirzakhani Scholarships are part of the Women in Mathematics programme of the Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard (FMJH). They fund talented female students from anywhere in the world through a master's in mathematics and then a three-year PhD at the Hadamard Doctoral School (EDMH) in the Paris region.

Winners join the master's 'Mathematics and Applications' at Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris, entering in the first or second year depending on their background. They receive an excellence scholarship of €11,000 a year during the master's and a commitment of doctoral funding worth a minimum of about €82,800 gross over three years.

The call for 2027 opened on 21 October 2026 and closes on 24 January 2027. Because it is open to every nationality, it is an outstanding route for African women in mathematics into one of Europe's strongest mathematical communities.
opportunities.benefits: A master's excellence scholarship of €11,000 per year for one or two years, followed by three years of doctoral funding with a minimum total gross amount of about €82,800. A contribution to master's and PhD tuition is included.
requirements: Female applicant of any nationality
Completing a bachelor's degree or the first year of a master's at the time of application, preferably in mathematics
Intends to enrol in an eligible M1 or M2 of the 'Mathematics and Applications' master's at Paris-Saclay or IP Paris
Plans to continue to a PhD at EDMH
documents: Referee letters (submitted by referees by 31 January 2027)
opportunities.selection_process: An award jury makes a preliminary selection, then shortlisted candidates have a video interview in English or French.
opportunities.about_provider: The Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard brings together the mathematics departments and laboratories of Université Paris-Saclay, Institut Polytechnique de Paris and partner institutions. It funds students, researchers and programmes and runs the Hadamard Doctoral School of Mathematics (EDMH).
opportunities.how_to_apply: Check the list of eligible master's courses on the FMJH site, then complete the online Maryam Mirzakhani application form before 24 January 2027. Ask your referees to submit their letters by 31 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: The number of awards is not stated. Questions go to the FMJH contact email.
