opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mathematics students of any nationality entering the Paris-Saclay Mathematics and Applications master's may apply by 24 January 2027 for EUR 11,000 a year plus travel and housing support.
opportunities.description:
The Sophie Germain Master Scholarships fund talented students from around the world who join the Mathematics and Applications master's programme in the Paris-Saclay area, either at Université Paris-Saclay or at Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Around fifty scholarships are given each year, and selection is made without regard to where applicants come from.

The awards are run by the Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard (FMJH) and cover either the first (M1) or second (M2) year of the master's in one of the listed research-oriented courses. The 2027 Wave 1 call is reserved for students who are currently outside the Paris-Saclay institutions.

For African mathematics students the scholarship is a strong route into one of Europe's largest mathematics research clusters: it pays a living allowance, helps with registration fees and travel, and offers housing to first-time international students. English-speaking students can follow the English-taught Jacques Hadamard M1 tracks.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 11,000 net per year; a flat-rate contribution to university registration fees; for first-time international students, up to EUR 2,000 (depending on country) towards one return trip and visa costs, an offer of an individual studio in Orsay or Evry and a housing kit worth about EUR 100; access to French language courses.
requirements: Admission to one of the listed research courses of the Mathematics and Applications master's (M1 or M2) at Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris
Wave 1 is only for students coming from outside the Paris-Saclay institutions
Strong academic record in mathematics, shown by transcripts and references
Non-European students must obtain a French student visa and a Campus France file number
Cannot be combined with another excellence scholarship
documents: Transcripts for each year of the bachelor's and first year of master's (or equivalent)
Names and emails of two referees, who upload their letters
opportunities.selection_process: A jury appointed by the FMJH steering committee together with the heads of the master's programmes judges applications on academic criteria, mainly transcripts and recommendation letters. Results are announced about five weeks after the closing date.
important_dates: Results: about five weeks after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard is a research foundation that brings together the mathematics laboratories of the Paris-Saclay area. It runs graduate programmes and scholarships, including the Sophie Germain master's awards and the Maryam Mirzakhani doctoral scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the FMJH online scholarship form and, separately, apply for admission to the chosen master's through Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Give the names of two referees, who must send their letters by 31 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Students who do not speak French are pointed to the English-taught M1 Jacques Hadamard tracks. Contact: contact@fondation-hadamard.fr.

opportunities.description:
The Graduate Research School Scholarships (UQGRSS), which include the Australian Government Research Training Program, are the University of Queensland's main awards for research degrees. They support students doing a PhD, an MPhil or a research-focused professional doctorate at UQ, and both domestic and international applicants can compete.

The scholarship pays a tax-free living stipend and tuition for 3.5 years, with the chance of one extension, and international students also get single overseas student health cover. Round 1 of 2027 is open now, for students starting between the middle of 2027 and early 2028; two later rounds close in May and October 2027.

Because there is no separate scholarship form, the key step for African applicants is to find a UQ supervisor early, submit an expression of interest and get the enrolling school to support and endorse the full application before the closing date.
opportunities.benefits: A living stipend of AUD 39,220 per year tax free (2026 rate, indexed each year), tuition fees, and Single Overseas Student Health Cover for international students, for 3.5 years with one possible extension.

Full research-degree application once the advisor supports it

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Law graduates and researchers from any country can apply by 29 January 2027 for a paid 2027 AI law summer fellowship in Cambridge (UK) or a remote-first track with a Washington, DC convening.
opportunities.description:
The Institute for Law & AI (LawAI) runs paid summer research fellowships for people who want to work on the legal questions raised by advanced artificial intelligence. For 2027 there are two tracks. The EU Law fellowship runs from 28 June to 3 September 2027, mostly in person in Cambridge, United Kingdom, and starts with a Convening Week there on 5-9 July. The Legal Frontiers fellowship is remote-first and lasts ten weeks, from 14 June to 20 August 2027, with a Convening Week in Washington, DC on 21-25 June.

Fellows carry out a research project with guidance from LawAI staff, take part in seminars and meet others working on AI law and policy. Applicants from all countries are welcome, and prior AI research is not required.

The fellowship is a well-paid way for African law graduates and researchers with an interest in technology regulation to build a network and a publication record in a fast-growing field.
opportunities.benefits: EU Law track: GBP 1,000 per week (more for exceptional candidates), a GBP 7,000 relocation payment for fellows who move to Cambridge for the whole fellowship, travel for the Convening Week for those who cannot relocate, and the UK visa fee and Immigration Health Surcharge. Legal Frontiers track: a weekly subsidy of USD 1,800 (US-based) or GBP 1,000 (EU/UK-based), travel, accommodation and meals for the Washington Convening Week, and admission to the 2027 Workshop on Law-Following AI.
requirements: A background in law (degree, legal training or legal research) is preferred; Legal Frontiers also considers exceptional candidates from computer science, policy, economics, history, philosophy or psychology
EU Law track: EU law experience is desirable but not required
Legal Frontiers track: good understanding of law and policy in at least one of the US, EU or UK
Full-time availability for the whole fellowship period and attendance at the Convening Week
Right to work or a visa for in-person work (LawAI may sponsor case by case)
opportunities.selection_process: Step 1 is the online form. Step 2 is a recorded screening interview of about 20-30 minutes. Step 3 is a 30-45 minute research interview. Decisions are made by LawAI staff by the end of March 2027; AI tools may assist in reviewing applications.
important_dates: Applications close: 29 January 2027 (Legal Frontiers: 11:59 pm US Eastern time)
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute for Law & AI is an independent think tank that researches how law can help govern artificial intelligence safely. It runs fellowships, workshops and research programmes in the United States, the United Kingdom and Europe.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the application form on the relevant LawAI fellowship page. Applications for the EU Law track are reviewed on a rolling basis, so applying early helps.
opportunities.notes: Contact: programs@law-ai.org. The fixed relocation payment is taxable. The fellowship can be extended by up to five weeks on the EU Law track.

opportunities.title: Space Academy Ile-de-France Incoming Mobility Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Third-year bachelor's and master's students worldwide with a space-related project may apply by 29 January 2027 (or 28 May 2027) for up to EUR 1,200 a month to study or intern in the Paris region.
opportunities.description:
The Space Academy of Île-de-France offers incoming international mobility scholarships for students who want to come to the Paris region for space-related study or research. The scholarship gives a monthly living stipend either to follow one semester or one year of a master's programme belonging to the Academy, or to do a research internship in one of its laboratories while still enrolled at a university abroad.

The Academy is a France 2030 project that links eight Île-de-France institutions working in space science and engineering, including Université Paris-Saclay, Sorbonne Université, ONERA, Université Paris Cité, UPEC, UVSQ, Institut Polytechnique de Paris and PSL. The 2027 call has three deadlines; the first (30 October 2026) has passed, so the next one is 29 January 2027, followed by 28 May 2027.

The programme is open to third-year bachelor's and master's students worldwide, so African students in physics, engineering, Earth observation or related fields can use it to join a French space master's or gain lab experience in Paris.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly living stipend of up to EUR 1,200 for one semester or one academic year (master's study can be supported for up to two years if the student re-applies for M2). Tuition may be waived only under specific exchange agreements; research interns pay no tuition. Flights and travel are not covered, and an intern's total income including other grants must not exceed the stated amount.
requirements: Third-year bachelor's student or first/second-year master's student
Project must be exclusively linked to the space field
Master's route: must name a specific Academy master's programme, have the programme head's support, and not have studied at a French university before
Internship route: must be enrolled at a university abroad and have a supporting lab supervisor
PhD students are not eligible
documents: Support from the master's head or lab supervisor
All files merged into a single PDF named SPACE-IDF-IntMobility-Incoming2027-Form_StudentName.pdf
opportunities.selection_process: The Space Academy International Mobility Committee reviews applications first. Final approval also depends on the master's programme head, the host department and, for internships, the host laboratory. Answers are given about four weeks after each deadline.
important_dates: Response: about four weeks after each deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The Académie Spatiale d'Île-de-France is a French Government France 2030 project that coordinates space-related education across eight universities and research organisations in the Paris region. It also funds outgoing mobility and apprenticeships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the 2027 incoming call and form from the Academy's mobility page, complete it with your CV, transcript and statement, get the required support from the programme head or lab supervisor, and email the single PDF to mobility@academiespatiale.fr before a deadline.
opportunities.notes: Applications that do not name a specific master's programme are not eligible. The number of grants is not stated.

opportunities.title: CDU Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students with 95% or better in their last qualification can apply by 31 January 2027 (Semester 1) for a 50% tuition scholarship at Charles Darwin University.
opportunities.description:
The Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarships (VCIHAS) at Charles Darwin University reward international students with outstanding grades by paying half of their tuition fees for the full length of an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree. A limited number are awarded for each intake.

Charles Darwin University is based in Darwin in Australia's Northern Territory. For 2027 there are two rounds: Semester 1 (closing 31 January 2027) and Semester 2 (closing 4 July 2027). The scholarship has no living allowance, and scholars must keep a good GPA to keep it.

African students with excellent results can use it to halve the cost of an Australian degree; the same page also lists automatic awards such as the 30% CDU Global Merit Scholarship.
opportunities.benefits: 50% of tuition fees for the full duration of the course. No living allowance; the award cannot be transferred or refunded.
requirements: International fee-paying student starting in Semester 1 or 2, 2027 (the first intake offered)
At least 95% overall in the highest completed qualification
Meets CDU academic and English entry requirements
Not holding another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency
To keep it: GPA of at least 5.3, no failed units, and 40 credit points per semester
documents: CDU admission application (via StudyLink or SATAC) and its application number
VCIHAS application form with declaration and signature
Personal statement answering four questions (500 words or less on the form)
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are made on the overall score in the applicant's highest qualification and the quality of the supporting statement. Results are announced during Orientation Week.
opportunities.about_provider: Charles Darwin University is a public Australian university with campuses in Darwin and across the Northern Territory, known for its links with Asia and the Indigenous communities of northern Australia.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First apply to study at CDU through the international application process. Then submit the VCIHAS form using your application number, with a short statement on why you should be chosen, how you will be an ambassador for CDU, your extracurricular activities and how you will use your degree to help your community.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus EMship Master in Sustainable Ship and Offshore Design 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Engineering graduates (mechanical, electromechanical, naval architecture or marine technology) of any nationality can apply by 31 January 2027 for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship of EUR 1,400 a month for 24 months on the EMship master's.
opportunities.description:
EMship, the International Master in Advanced Design of Sustainable Ships and Offshore Structures, is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master coordinated by Ghent University in Belgium. The two-year, English-taught programme (120 ECTS) is delivered by seven universities in six countries: Ghent and Liège (Belgium), Galati (Romania), Rostock (Germany), Centrale Nantes (France), IST Lisbon (Portugal) and UPM Madrid (Spain).

Applications for the 2027-2028 intake are open. Erasmus+ scholarship holders have their tuition waived and receive EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months, intended to cover living costs including travel, visa, installation and rent. The consortium will award 95 scholarships over four cohorts: 60 open to all nationalities and 35 reserved for targeted regions, with no more than 10% of recipients from any one country.

African engineering graduates count as partner-country applicants. Self-funded places cost EUR 9,000 a year for partner-country students, with up to 20 high-potential self-funded students receiving a 50% discount.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus+ scholarship: full tuition waiver (covering enrolment, insurance and teaching) plus EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months. Self-funded fees: EUR 9,000/year (partner countries), EUR 4,500/year (programme countries); 50% discount for up to 20 high-potential self-funded students.
requirements: Bachelor's degree (at least 3 years / 180 ECTS) in mechanical engineering, electromechanical engineering, naval architecture, marine technology or a related field
Final-year students may apply; the degree must be obtained before the programme starts
Not eligible: STCW marine engineers and Bachelor of Science in Engineering Technology
English: IELTS Academic 6.5 (6.0 each), TOEFL iBT 92 (20 each), PTE Academic 62 (59 each), CAE/CPE 176 (169 each) or Trinity ISE II with distinctions; certificate no older than 2 years
No previous Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship
documents: Degree copy with certified English translation (legalised after selection)
Two reference letters emailed by referees to references@emship.eu
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are ranked on bachelor's GPA, an online test, background, CV, motivation and references. Top candidates have an online interview with a five-minute presentation and questions, and the Selection and Admission Board ranks scholarship candidates. Appeals are possible within 15 working days.
opportunities.about_provider: EMship is run by a consortium of European universities specialising in naval architecture and offshore engineering, coordinated by Ghent University and funded under the Erasmus+ Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Ghent University's OASIS online application form linked from emship.eu, uploading your documents and asking two referees to email their letters to references@emship.eu. Shortlisted candidates are invited to an online interview in March.
opportunities.notes: The 31 January deadline is stated without a year on the how-to-apply page; the site confirms that applications for 2027-2028 are open. Contact office@emship.eu with questions.

opportunities.title: IBSA Foundation Fellowships 2026-2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Biomedical researchers of any nationality under 40 (PhD students to postdocs) may apply by 31 January 2027 for one of seven EUR 32,000 one-year fellowships.
opportunities.description:
The IBSA Foundation Fellowships give young biomedical researchers a year of funding to carry out a research project in a host laboratory, university, hospital or research centre of their choice. The 2026 call offers seven fellowships in dermatology, endocrinology, fertility and urology, orthopaedics and pain medicine, and healthy ageing. Projects must start by 2027 and last 12 months.

The programme is run by the IBSA Foundation for scientific research in Lugano, Switzerland. It is open to researchers of any nationality under 40, from PhD students and residents to postdocs, who hold a degree in medicine, biology, pharmacy, biotechnology or bioengineering.

Alongside the fellowships, a separate Research Equity Prize of EUR 5,000 rewards the best project hosted in a developing country, including any African country, which gives African-based labs and researchers an extra chance of support.
opportunities.benefits: Each fellowship is worth EUR 32,000 gross (before tax), meant to cover salary and mobility costs for 12 months, paid half before the project starts and half by the end of 2027. It does not cover bench fees, overheads or consumables. The Research Equity Prize pays EUR 5,000 in one instalment.
requirements: Any nationality
Under 40 years old on the deadline
Degree in medicine, biology, pharmacy, biotechnology or bioengineering
PhD students, PhD holders, postdocs and medical residents may apply; holders of permanent positions such as professors may not
Must be based at the host institution for the whole grant
Project in dermatology, endocrinology, fertility/urology, orthopaedics/pain medicine or healthy ageing
documents: List of one to three best peer-reviewed publications
Project proposal entered on the online platform
Acceptance letter from the host institution (within one week of being notified as a winner)
opportunities.selection_process: The IBSA Scientific Board peer-reviews proposals for feasibility, originality and scientific value, along with the candidate's CV (especially research experience) and the suitability of the host lab. Projects carried out at an institution other than the candidate's home lab earn extra merit. Results usually come within three months of the deadline.
opportunities.about_provider: The IBSA Foundation for scientific research is a Swiss non-profit foundation in Lugano linked to the pharmaceutical company IBSA. It promotes biomedical research and science communication through fellowships, scholarships and events.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the proposal and the three documents as separate files on the foundation's application platform (ibsafoundation.poliresearch.com). Only online applications are accepted.
opportunities.notes: Winners must answer a yearly survey and acknowledge the foundation in publications. Contact: info@ibsafoundation.org, +41 58 360 10 00.

Southern Cross University marks International Women's Day each year with three scholarships of $5,000 for female students who are already enrolled at the university. Recipients must be studying full time in 2027 at the Coffs Harbour campus (including the National Marine Science Centre), Lismore or the Gold Coast, and must already have completed at least one full-time term on campus.

There is no nationality rule, so African women who are already enrolled at SCU as international students can apply. Each winner's introductory statement is shared publicly during the university's International Women's Day events.
opportunities.benefits: A one-year scholarship of $5,000. Three awards are available for 2027.
requirements: Female student
Currently enrolled and studying full time at SCU in 2027
Studying at Coffs Harbour (including the National Marine Science Centre), Lismore or Gold Coast
Has completed at least one full-time on-campus term
Excellent GPA
documents: Personal introductory statement of up to 200 words
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on academic merit and on the introductory statement. Selection takes place in the weeks after the closing date and can take up to a month.
important_dates: Selection: up to one month after closing
Statements shared: International Women's Day, March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Southern Cross University is a public Australian university with campuses in Lismore, Coffs Harbour and the Gold Coast in New South Wales and Queensland. It is known for marine science, environmental science, health and education.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form linked from the scholarship page before 31 January 2027 and include your 200-word introductory statement. Questions go to the SCU scholarships team by email or on 1800 72 4357.
opportunities.notes: Not open to prospective students who have not yet started at SCU. Your statement will be published if you win.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Residents aged 18-28 of Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe and other listed countries may apply by 31 January 2027 for a two-year environmental innovation fellowship with up to EUR 15,000 in project funding.
opportunities.description:
beVisioneers: The Mercedes-Benz Fellowship is a two-year programme for young people who want to turn an early idea for an environmental solution into a working project. The first year is an intensive, mostly online training year (at least 24 hours a month) in which fellows build a prototype with venture coaching, mentoring and project scholarships. The second year is an acceleration year with continued support and a cost-of-living stipend.

The fellowship is funded by Mercedes-Benz and run by The DO School Fellowships in Hamburg, Germany. It is delivered in English in a hybrid format and includes regional summits where fellows meet in person. Applications are now open for the 2027/28 fellowship year.

Eligibility depends on where you live, not your passport. In Africa, residents of Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zimbabwe can apply, alongside residents of Europe, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, Türkiye, the UK and the US.
opportunities.benefits: Project scholarships of up to EUR 15,000, available at the end of the first year; a cost-of-living stipend in the second year (amount not stated); innovation training, one-to-one mentoring and travel to regional summits.
requirements: Aged 18 to 28 on 31 January 2027
Resident in one of the listed countries (in Africa: Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda or Zimbabwe)
Strong command of English
Has identified an environmental problem to solve
Neither you nor a parent or guardian works for Mercedes-Benz
Able to commit at least 24 hours a month in year one
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on their written answers and their recorded interview video, which is also used to judge English ability. The number of fellows is not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: beVisioneers was launched in 2023 by Mercedes-Benz and is delivered by The DO School Fellowships gGmbH, a Hamburg-based organisation that trains young changemakers to launch social and environmental projects.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply on the beVisioneers DreamApply portal (applications.bevisioneers.world), answering the written questions and recording the video interview before the deadline.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students with a non-Dutch bachelor's who apply to an English-taught Radboud master's for 2027-28 and to the Radboud Scholarship Programme can be considered for €5,000.
opportunities.description:
The NL Scholarship at Radboud University in Nijmegen is a one-off award of €5,000 for students from outside the EU/EEA who start an English-taught master's programme. It is paid for jointly by the Dutch Ministry of Education and the university, and up to 32 awards are available for 2027-28.

It is a partial award, not a full scholarship, and can only be given together with the Radboud Scholarship Programme (RSP), so applicants must apply for both. Faculties judge candidates on academic excellence and ambition.

African students who hold a bachelor's degree from outside the Netherlands and are fully admitted to a regular English-taught master's (not an Erasmus Mundus or joint degree) can apply. The application must be in OSIRIS by 31 January 2027 and complete by 14 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: €5,000, awarded once for one year. It does not cover the full cost of study.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA passport and not eligible for the lower EU/EEA fee
Bachelor's degree obtained outside the Netherlands, with no previous Dutch education
Meet the English proficiency requirement
Full admission to an English-taught Radboud master's (not Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree)
Apply also for the Radboud Scholarship Programme
Full-time enrolment and compliance with visa rules
documents: Master's application in OSIRIS with the NL Scholarship indicated
opportunities.selection_process: Each faculty assesses academic excellence (grades, test scores, publications, relevance of the degree, standing of the university) and ambition (motivation, promise, life experience and extracurricular activities). Decisions are expected around mid-April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Radboud University is a public research university in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, with about 24,000 students. It offers many English-taught master's programmes and runs its own scholarship programme for talented non-EU students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your English-taught master's in OSIRIS and indicate the NL Scholarship by 31 January 2027, then make sure the application is complete by 14 February 2027. Apply for the Radboud Scholarship Programme at the same time, since the NL Scholarship cannot be awarded on its own.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants to Nova SBE's 2027/28 PhD programmes are automatically considered for four-year fellowships paying EUR 1,400 a month; apply by 31 January 2027.

Nova School of Business and Economics in Lisbon automatically offers its strongest PhD applicants a four-year research fellowship. For African graduates aiming at an academic or research career in economics or business, it is a funded doctorate at an internationally accredited European school. The same page also lists other funding sources for PhD students, such as FCT studentships, La Caixa INPhINIT and Camões Institute cooperation scholarships.
opportunities.benefits: A tax-free stipend of EUR 16,800 per year (EUR 1,400 per month), a 90% annual tuition waiver (worth about EUR 2,700), and from the second year a EUR 1,000 research allowance for conferences, for four years.
requirements: Apply to a Nova SBE PhD programme for the 2027/28 intake
Fellowships go to the top-ranked applicants
Renewal each year depends on satisfactory progress
documents: Nova SBE PhD online application (documents listed on the PhD admission page)
opportunities.selection_process: The top applicants to the PhD programmes are offered the fellowship automatically. Applicants may be invited to an online interview, and decisions are sent by email.
opportunities.about_provider: Nova SBE is the business and economics school of NOVA University Lisbon, Portugal, and holds AACSB, EQUIS and AMBA accreditation.

opportunities.title: Radboud Scholarship Programme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students admitted to an English-taught Radboud master's starting September 2027 may apply by 31 January 2027 for one of 32 tuition-reduction scholarships.
opportunities.description:
The Radboud Scholarship Programme helps highly talented students from outside the EU/EEA take a full English-taught master's at Radboud University in Nijmegen, the Netherlands. It is very selective: for 2027/2028 there are at most 32 scholarships spread across the faculties of Arts, Law, Management, Philosophy and Theology, Science and Social Sciences.

The scholarship does not pay living costs, but it cuts the tuition fee to the much lower Dutch statutory level and covers the costs of the visa and residence permit as well as health and liability insurance. It is funded from the university's Profiling Fund and lasts for the nominal length of the master's; the second-year grant requires all first-year courses to be passed.

Living costs are not covered.

opportunities.title: University of Glasgow Computing Science PhD Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a good computing degree, including international students, can apply by 31 January 2027 for Glasgow Computing Science PhD funding starting October 2027.
opportunities.description:
The School of Computing Science at the University of Glasgow funds PhD students who start in October 2027 or soon after through one competition that covers several scholarship schemes. Applicants are considered for whichever schemes suit them, including the College of Science and Engineering Graduate School Scholarships, College Scholarships, Excellence Bursaries and the part-time Minerva Scholarships.

Coverage differs between schemes. The Graduate School Scholarships pay fees (home or international) and a stipend for three years, while the Excellence Bursary for international students is a fee discount of GBP 10,000 a year. Stipends usually follow the UKRI rate, which is GBP 22,437 for 2027-28.

International applicants, including those from Africa, apply through the normal PhD admission system and simply select the university scholarship as their funding source. The school suggests PhD projects on its website, and contacting a potential supervisor first helps.
opportunities.benefits: Depending on the scheme: tuition fees (home or international) plus a stipend of GBP 22,437 for 2027-28 for three years (Graduate School Scholarships); home-level fees plus UKRI stipend (College Scholarships); a GBP 10,000 a year fee discount for three years for international students (Excellence Bursaries); or a five-year part-time Minerva post with home-level fees and pay of at least GBP 24,000 a year.
requirements: Upper second-class honours undergraduate degree (or equivalent) or a master's degree in computing science or a related field
Applying for a PhD in the School of Computing Science starting October 2027 or shortly after
Meets the University of Glasgow English requirements
documents: Documents listed on the university's before-you-apply page (transcripts, references, research proposal or statement)
opportunities.selection_process: Academic admission and scholarship applications are processed separately; scholarship decisions are confirmed with candidates around April 2027. The number of awards and detailed criteria are not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow is one of the UK's oldest universities and a member of the Russell Group. Its School of Computing Science is consistently ranked among the top ten in the UK.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the University of Glasgow postgraduate research application, and choose 'Univ of Glasgow Scholarship' as your funding source. Look at the school's suggested PhD projects and contact a supervisor before applying.
opportunities.notes: Contact: socs-pgr-enquiries@glasgow.ac.uk. The James McCune Smith scholarship listed on the same page is for Black UK-domiciled students only.

The scholarship application itself is short: an online form and a motivation letter of no more than 350 words, with no documents and no fee. The window is open from 16 January to 1 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee for the bachelor's or master's programme. Living costs are not covered.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: International and domestic first-year applicants to Centre College for Fall 2027 who want to study Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Latin or Spanish can apply for a renewable language scholarship of up to USD 5,000 a year on top of general merit aid.
opportunities.description:
Centre College, a private liberal arts college in Danville, Kentucky, offers Language Scholarships to incoming first-year students who want to pursue a language and its culture. The award is open to both international and domestic students entering in Fall 2027, and no major or minor in the language is required.

The scholarship is worth up to USD 5,000 a year, is renewable, and can be combined with Centre's general merit scholarships, which for international applicants are typically USD 15,000 to 30,000 a year and awarded automatically. Recipients must keep at least a 3.0 GPA in their language courses and are expected to study abroad.

For African students this is a way to reduce the cost of a US liberal arts education, especially combined with general merit aid. Applicants may even apply in their native language, but only one language scholarship can be held, and Spanish applicants must record a short video in Spanish.
opportunities.benefits: Up to USD 5,000 per year, renewable, stackable with general merit scholarships (USD 15,000-30,000 per year for international applicants). International students should plan for roughly USD 25,000 a year in remaining costs according to the college.

Complete Common App or Coalition App and all admission items
Only one language scholarship per student

opportunities.description:
The Hamburg Institute for Advanced Study (HIAS) offers residential fellowships that bring scholars and artists to Hamburg to work on their own projects in dialogue with partners in the city. The 2028-29 fellowship year runs from 1 October 2028 to 30 June 2029, and the preferred stay is at least three months.

Each fellow works with a 'tandem partner' at a Hamburg institution. Applicants only need to name a possible partner; prior contact is not required. HIAS values interdisciplinary profiles and aims for a diverse group of fellows.

The call is open to all nationalities, so African researchers and artists can apply. The deadline is 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET.
opportunities.benefits: Either a stipend paid to the fellow or partial reimbursement to the home institution for the cost of a teaching replacement (amount not stated). Office space is provided, and guesthouse accommodation may be available.

opportunities.selection_process: HIAS weighs the doctorate and publications (scholars) or exhibitions and performances (artists), interdisciplinary profile, prizes, English, fit of the project with Hamburg partners, and the diversity of the fellow group.
opportunities.about_provider: The Hamburg Institute for Advanced Study is an institute for advanced study founded by Hamburg's universities and cultural institutions. It hosts international fellows from the sciences, humanities and arts and links them with partners across the city.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers living in a low- or middle-income country, mainly nationals of DGD partner countries, with an ITM supervisor and a home-institute supervisor, can apply for 3 to 6 months of pre-PhD training in Antwerp.
opportunities.description:
The ITM-DGD Predoctoral Research Training Grants let promising early-career researchers from low- and middle-income countries spend three to six months at the Institute of Tropical Medicine (ITM) in Antwerp, Belgium, to prepare a PhD project. The training is not a degree; it is meant to build the skills and proposal needed to start doctoral research.

The grants are funded by the Belgian Directorate-General for Development Cooperation (DGD). At most five grants are available in the 2027 call, to be taken up between 15 June 2027 and 14 June 2028, preferably before the end of 2027.

Most eligible countries are in Africa, including Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda. Applicants need both an ITM supervisor and a supervisor at their home institute.
opportunities.benefits: A living allowance of €28 per day (up to 6 months in Antwerp), a housing allowance, a bench fee of €1,470 per month, a return ticket, insurance (€63 per month) and €200 for indirect travel costs. Grantees have student status, not employee status.
requirements: Primary residence in a low- or middle-income country
Nationality of a DGD-eligible country (a limited number of grants for other LMIC nationals)
Formal supervisor at ITM and at the home institute
Early-career researcher with strong potential for PhD research
Not a dual national of a high-income country
No more than one year of employment in a high-income country in the three years before 1 February 2027
Never on the ITM payroll
documents: CV with master's and postgraduate transcripts and current employment
Letters of support from both supervisors
opportunities.selection_process: The ITM PhD Committee evaluates applications, followed by a decision by the ITM Management Committee. Proposals limited to a single course are not considered a good fit.
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp is one of the world's leading institutes for research, training and services in tropical medicine and global health. It has long-standing partnerships with institutions in Africa, Asia and Latin America.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree on a training plan with an ITM supervisor and your home supervisor, then complete the application form from the ITM website. Email the full application to the ITM contact named in the call before 1 February 2027, 17:00 Belgian time.
opportunities.notes: At most 5 grants. ITM also offers DGD postdoctoral and sandwich PhD grants with March and September deadlines.

The New England Regional Fellowship Consortium (NERFC) is a group of 29 libraries, archives and historical societies coordinated by the Massachusetts Historical Society. Each year it funds researchers to work in the collections of several member institutions.

opportunities.description:
New York University's Center for the Study of Africa and the African Diaspora (CSAAD) offers a pre-doctoral research fellowship for the 2027-28 academic year. It is designed for PhD candidates who have reached the writing phase of their dissertation and need a year of focused time to complete it.

The fellow is based at CSAAD's offices at 20 Cooper Square in Manhattan for the full academic year and joins the intellectual life of a centre dedicated to Africa and the African diaspora. Projects must be in the humanities or social sciences and must deal with Africa or its diaspora.

The page sets no nationality restriction, so African doctoral candidates enrolled at universities in Africa or elsewhere can apply. The fellowship offers a stipend, health insurance and a base in New York to finish writing.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of US$30,000 and health insurance for the 2027-28 academic year.
requirements: PhD candidate in the dissertation-writing phase
Field in the humanities or social sciences
Dissertation research on Africa or the African diaspora
Must disclose any other fellowship support for 2027-28
Able to be in residence at NYU in New York for the academic year
documents: Statement of other fellowship support for 2027-28
One recommendation letter emailed to csaad@nyu.edu
opportunities.selection_process: CSAAD reviews the applications; the page does not describe further stages or the number of awards.
opportunities.about_provider: CSAAD is a research centre at New York University that supports scholarship, teaching and public programmes on Africa and the African diaspora. It hosts pre-doctoral and post-doctoral fellows each year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form linked as 'Apply here' on the CSAAD fellowship page and upload the letter, summary, chapter, CV and support statement. Ask your referee to email the recommendation letter to csaad@nyu.edu before the deadline.

opportunities.description:
The International Merit Scholarship is a tuition reduction offered by ACAP University College to new international students who enrol in one of its eligible bachelor's or master's courses. For the Trimester 2, 2027 intake it takes 20% off the published tuition fees, spread evenly across all the units of the course.

ACAP teaches in Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney, and the award applies to courses in psychology, counselling, social work, management and criminology. It can run for the full normal length of the course: up to four years (12 trimesters) for a bachelor's degree and up to two years (6 trimesters) for a master's degree of full-time study.

The official page places no limit on nationality, so African students who apply to ACAP as international students can compete. Candidates are judged on their academic record and on a written statement about leadership, community contribution and their future goals.
opportunities.benefits: A 20% reduction on published tuition fees, applied evenly to every unit needed to complete the course, for up to 12 trimesters (bachelor's) or 6 trimesters (master's) of full-time study. Only one scholarship, bursary or discount can apply to a unit; if several apply, the highest one is used.
requirements: Be a new international student
Hold an offer for an eligible ACAP course starting in Trimester 2, 2027
Assessment considers completion of an Australian university degree at AQF level 7 or above with a minimum GPA of 80% (check the scholarship policy for how this applies to you)
Submit a written statement on leadership, community contribution, personal development and future impact
Study full time
documents: Written statement (leadership examples, skills, career goals, challenges overcome)
Evidence of completed degree and GPA
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed against two criteria: the academic record (degree level and GPA) and the written statement describing leadership, contribution to the community, personal growth and the impact the applicant hopes to have.
opportunities.about_provider: ACAP University College is an Australian higher education provider, part of the Navitas group, that specialises in applied professions such as psychology, counselling, social work, criminology and management. It runs campuses in five Australian cities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First apply to ACAP as an international student for an eligible course. Then complete the International Merit Scholarship online form linked from the scholarship page before 12 February 2027 and attach your written statement. Read the scholarship policy linked on the page before applying.
opportunities.notes: The award is a fee reduction, not a cash payment. It cannot be combined with another ACAP discount on the same unit. Phone enquiries: 1800 039 139.

opportunities.title: Beit Strathclyde (BStrath) Engineering Master's Scholarship 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals and residents of Malawi, Zambia or Zimbabwe with a good engineering degree and an offer for a one-year engineering master's at Strathclyde in 2027/28 can apply.
opportunities.description:
The Beit Strathclyde (BStrath) Scholarship is a full award for one-year taught master's study in the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Strathclyde in Glasgow. It is run jointly by the university and the Beit Trust, and one scholarship is offered for the 2027/28 academic year.

The award covers the whole cost of the course, including tuition and living costs, for the one-year programme. Eligible departments are Architecture; Biomedical Engineering; Chemical and Process Engineering; Civil and Environmental Engineering; Design, Manufacturing and Engineering Management; Electronic and Electrical Engineering; Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering; and Naval Architecture, Ocean and Marine Engineering.

The scholarship is aimed at future leaders from Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe, the three countries the Beit Trust serves. Applicants are expected to return home after their studies and use what they have learned for the benefit of their country.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees; a living allowance; UK visa and Immigration Health Surcharge, TB test and biometrics costs; arrival, laptop and departure allowances; and economy return flights. Dependants are not funded.
requirements: National and permanent resident of Malawi, Zambia or Zimbabwe at the time of application
A good engineering degree from a recognised university (Distinction or Upper Second preferred)
An offer for a one-year taught master's in one of the eight eligible Strathclyde engineering departments for 2027/28
International fee status
About three years of work experience is a guide
Commitment to return home after the course
Must not have started the course already
documents: Offer letter from the University of Strathclyde
Personal statement of up to 300 words on how the study will benefit your country
Three references (academic, character and employer if applicable)
opportunities.selection_process: The Beit Trust selects on merit and eligibility, looking at degree results, work experience, leadership potential, commitment to return home and the relevance of the course. Shortlisted candidates are usually interviewed in person in April in Lusaka, Harare or Blantyre.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Strathclyde is a public technological university in Glasgow, Scotland, with a large engineering faculty. The Beit Trust is a UK charity that has supported education and development in Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe for over a century, including postgraduate scholarships at partner universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Secure an offer for an eligible Strathclyde engineering master's first. Then complete the Beit Trust online application form in one sitting, uploading all documents at once, between 1 December 2026 and 12 February 2027. Referees can also send forms to the Beit Trust scholarships email address.
opportunities.notes: Only one award is available. You can submit only one Beit Trust application and cannot save and return to the form. Strathclyde contact: Robert Graham. Late applications are not processed.

The scholarship rewards academic and personal merit rather than financial need. Applicants answer three short questions in the Bath Application Tracker after receiving an offer, and their answers are read alongside their UCAS academic profile.

opportunities.selection_process: A competitive review of the three written answers and the applicant's UCAS academic profile, based on academic and personal merit. Each applicant is considered once.
important_dates: Outcomes: before the May 2027 UCAS reply deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Bath is a public research university in south-west England, known for engineering, management, science and sport. It is consistently ranked among the leading UK universities for student experience.

ISCB UK 2027, the UK meeting of the International Society for Computational Biology, will be held at the University of Strathclyde in Glasgow from 20 to 22 April 2027 under the theme "Biology in the Age of AI". The organisers are inviting abstracts for talks and posters, and the first day includes a student symposium for PhD students and postdocs.

Topics include artificial intelligence and machine learning in biology and medicine; bioinformatics infrastructure, training and community; genomics, evolution and multi-omics; structural, molecular and systems biology; translational and precision medicine; and emerging areas of computational biology.

The call is open to anyone, so African bioinformaticians and data scientists can use it to present work to a European audience. Note that presenters must register and pay to attend, and the call does not mention travel grants or fee waivers.

Student symposium option for PhD students and postdocs

Printed poster up to 46 x 46 inches, or a PDF poster and 5-7 minute video for the virtual hall, if accepted

opportunities.description:
The KI Global Master's Scholarship is Karolinska Institutet's own award for international students who must pay tuition fees to study on one of its master's programmes in Stockholm. It removes the tuition fee bill for the programme, which is often the biggest obstacle for students from outside the EU/EEA, including applicants from African countries.

opportunities.description:
The CYD Doctoral Fellowships fund PhD research on cyber-defence topics at the Cyber-Defence (CYD) Campus, the research centre of the Swiss federal defence administration. Fellows work under a professor at a Swiss university while being linked to the CYD Campus, which has sites on the EPFL and ETH Zurich premises and in Thun.

The fellowship lasts four years, with a possible one-year extension, and pays the doctoral salary plus money for research costs and conferences. The upcoming 15th call opens on 3 December 2026 and its first-stage deadline is 25 February 2027 (17:00 CET).

There is no nationality or age restriction, which makes it a real option for African computer scientists, engineers and mathematicians who want to do a funded PhD in Switzerland on security, privacy, cryptography or related fields.

requirements: Open to all nationalities, no age limit
Enrolled in or accepted into a doctoral programme at a Swiss higher education institution
Endorsement by a supervising Swiss professor at Stage 2
Excellent academic record (strong grade transcripts)
Project must link the CYD Campus with at least one Swiss higher education institution
All documents in English
Preference for candidates who have not yet started or are at the start of their PhD
opportunities.selection_process: Stage 1 pre-proposals are reviewed by a CYD Campus committee chaired by the CYD Director for fit and quality. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed by a prospective CYD mentor, and only mentor-endorsed candidates move to Stage 2. A committee of three to five members chaired by the CYD Director makes the final decision, with academic excellence as the main criterion.

opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 3,000 per month for one to three months, paid after arrival. The stipend is taxable.

Residency of four to twelve consecutive weeks between 1 June 2027 and 31 May 2028

opportunities.title: APS-Voltaire Foundation 1776 Fellowships in Enlightenment Studies 2027
opportunities.provider: American Philosophical Society and Voltaire Foundation (University of Oxford)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders, advanced PhD candidates and independent scholars of any nationality researching the Enlightenment can apply by 1 March 2027 for research stays in Philadelphia and Oxford.
opportunities.description:
The 1776 Fellowships in Enlightenment Studies are a joint programme of the American Philosophical Society (APS) in Philadelphia and the Voltaire Foundation at the University of Oxford. Each year two fellows spend up to a month at each institution (and may stay longer) to research Enlightenment ideas, how they spread and how they were used.

Fellows work in the APS library and archives and in Oxford's collections, with the Voltaire Foundation as their base there. The programme marks the shared transatlantic history of the Enlightenment that shaped both institutions.

The call is open to scholars of any nationality, so African historians, philosophers and literary scholars working on the Enlightenment, its global reach or its critics can apply. It is especially useful for early-career researchers who need access to archives in the US and UK.
opportunities.benefits: $5,000 from the APS and £4,000 from the Voltaire Foundation, to cover travel, living and accommodation costs for up to two months of research (about one month at each institution). Two fellowships.

opportunities.description:
The African Leadership Bridge Endowed Scholarship at the University of Texas at Austin supports undergraduates who did all or part of their secondary education in Africa and who need financial help. It was set up in 2023 with the African Leadership Bridge, a nonprofit that helps African students study in the United States.

The award is USD 5,000 for the 2027-2028 academic year together with a waiver of the non-resident part of tuition, which greatly reduces the cost of study for international students. Incoming first-year students are given preference.

Applications for autumn 2027 are accepted from 1 February to 1 March 2027 through UT's LASSO scholarship system.
opportunities.benefits: USD 5,000 for the academic year (USD 2,500 each in autumn and spring) plus a waiver of the non-resident portion of tuition. It is a one-time award, not guaranteed in later years.

All or part of preparatory education completed in Africa
Preference for incoming first-year students

opportunities.description:
BI Norwegian Business School offers the Future African Leader Scholarship to citizens of African countries starting a full-time master's programme at its Oslo, Bergen or Trondheim campus. It covers full tuition for up to two years and adds a living-cost stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester, as long as the student keeps up the required academic progress.

BI is a member of the Global Business School Network (GBSN), and this award is one of two scholarships it uses to support initiatives in Africa. Preference goes to candidates who study or studied at a GBSN member school in Africa, or who attended a GMAC Study in Europe event or a SEED Business School Festival event in person in Africa.

The scholarship is merit-based. Applicants are also considered automatically for BI's Presidential, Master International and Women in Finance and Tech scholarships, which improves the chances of some funding.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition for up to two years of a full-time master's, plus a living-cost stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester, subject to academic progression.
requirements: Citizen of an African country, not resident in Norway and not a domestic applicant by education background
Applying for a first master's degree, full-time, at campus Oslo, Bergen or Trondheim
Minimum overall GPA of 4.0 on the ECTS scale (BI converts international grades)
Strong GMAT or GRE scores (required for admission)
Not available for the BI-Luiss Joint Master in Marketing
Must submit a complete admission application and accept the offer of admission

Complete master's admission documentation (uploaded in the online application)
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are based on academic merit, not financial need. BI considers grades, GMAT/GRE scores, other academic achievements and extracurricular and personal achievements, and may apply institutional priorities such as programme, diversity, gender and partner schools. opportunities.eligibility_summary: Canadian and international PhD students in mathematics at an ISM member university in Quebec with a GPA of at least 3.5 can be nominated by their department.
opportunities.description:
The Institut des sciences mathématiques (ISM) is a consortium of Quebec universities that pools resources for graduate training in mathematics and statistics. Its Graduate Scholarships support excellent students doing a PhD at a member university, alongside matching funding from the host department.

Candidates do not apply to ISM directly. They send their file to their host department by 1 March 2027, departments rank their candidates, and ISM's director chooses the recipients. The award is open to both Canadian and international students, and departments are asked to seek a waiver of the higher international fee for foreign recipients.

For African mathematicians admitted to a PhD in Montreal, Quebec City or Sherbrooke, this adds to the departmental funding package.
opportunities.benefits: ISM pays up to CAD 10,000 a year, and the host department must add at least the same amount. Total funding from all sources is capped at CAD 34,000 a year. Foreign students may receive help obtaining a tuition differential waiver.
requirements: Registered (or admitted) full-time in a PhD programme at an ISM member university
Master's students are not eligible
Cumulative GPA of at least 3.5
Excellent academic record and research ability
Open to Canadian and international students
Paid work limited to 450 hours a year
documents: Two letters of recommendation, one from the current or future supervisor
opportunities.selection_process: Departments rank their nominees and send lists to ISM between 15 March and 1 June. The ISM director selects recipients with input from programme groups.

opportunities.about_provider: The ISM, hosted by the Université du Québec à Montréal, brings together the mathematics departments of Quebec universities including McGill, Concordia, Université de Montréal, Université Laval, UQAM and Sherbrooke.

opportunities.description:
The ITC Excellence Scholarship Programme is offered by the University of Twente's Faculty of Geo-information Science and Earth Observation (ITC) in the Netherlands. It gives partial funding to a small number of very strong applicants to its two-year master's programmes in Geo-information Science and Earth Observation, and in Spatial Engineering.

The scholarship pays EUR 25,000 in support and waives ITC tuition of EUR 33,180. Recipients still contribute EUR 17,500 themselves towards tuition, living allowances, insurance and the residence permit, and must show they can pay it.

Applicants must be nationals and residents of a listed country, which includes most African countries, and must already hold an admission letter before applying.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 25,000 in financial support plus a waiver of ITC tuition worth EUR 33,180 (total programme cost EUR 75,680). The student pays an own contribution of EUR 17,500 (tuition EUR 12,080, allowances EUR 3,750, insurance EUR 1,400, residence permit EUR 270).

Academic admission to an eligible ITC master's received before applying
Bachelor's degree from a recognised university outside the Netherlands
Academic results in the top 10% of the class
IELTS overall 6.5 or equivalent
First enrolment at the University of Twente and not eligible for Dutch study finance
No other UT or Dutch scholarship (except the NL Scholarship) and no full external scholarship
Able to pay the EUR 17,500 own contribution and meet Dutch visa rules
documents: Supporting documents listed in the 2027 rules and regulations
opportunities.selection_process: A limited number of awards go to the strongest eligible candidates who meet the top-10% academic standard. To keep the award in year two, students must earn at least 45 of 60 credits and stay in the top 10%.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality with an offer from St John's College, Cambridge, for an MPhil or PhD on the literature, history or culture of China before 1912 are considered.
opportunities.description:
The Louis Cha Scholarship is a postgraduate award at St John's College, Cambridge, funded by a gift from the novelist Dr Louis Cha (Jin Yong). It supports one student doing an MPhil or PhD on the literature, history or culture of early and dynastic China, up to 1912.

The scholarship covers the approved University fee and pays a maintenance grant, reduced where the student holds other funding. It runs for the length of the course, up to three years, for study starting in October 2027.

There is no separate form: applicants apply to Cambridge for their course, naming St John's as first-choice college, and the application must reach St John's before 1 March 2027. African scholars working on pre-modern China are eligible on the same terms as everyone else.
opportunities.benefits: The approved University composition fee plus a maintenance grant, which St John's currently sets at GBP 20,700 a year; both are reduced by any other funding held. The Cambridge funding database lists the total value as GBP 32,650 to 59,600 a year. One award.

St John's College named as first-choice college
Not already fully funded through another Cambridge college
Chosen on academic merit
No nationality restriction
documents: Cambridge postgraduate application (no separate scholarship form)
Annual research report once the award is held

Awards range from USD 1,500 a year up to full tuition for the highest scores, and the top students can also get a free double room in their first year. They renew for four years if the student keeps a 2.5 GPA and completes 15 credits each semester.

ACT or SAT taken before the deadline (SAT converted to ACT)

opportunities.description:
The Joan and Eugene Vanderpool Fellowship is offered by the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (ASCSA). It supports research on any aspect of the Athenian Agora, the ancient civic centre of Athens, from antiquity to the present day.

Family and friends of the Vanderpools set up the fellowship to honour the Agora Excavations, where Eugene Vanderpool worked for decades. Topics can include history, archaeology, literature, epigraphy, architecture, art history and the site's biodiversity.

The fellowship is open to all nationalities, so African classicists, archaeologists and historians can apply through the ASCSA online form by 15 March 2027.

Research on any aspect of the Athenian Agora, from antiquity to the present
Open to all nationalities

opportunities.eligibility_summary: African-domiciled passport holders with first-class-equivalent grades who hold or are seeking an offer for a one-year taught master's at Glasgow starting September 2027 can apply for a 75% tuition fee waiver.
opportunities.description:
The University of Glasgow African Excellence Award is a merit scholarship for outstanding students from across Africa who want to take a one-year, full-time taught master's degree at Glasgow in Scotland. The 2027/28 round is for the September 2027 intake and covers almost every subject the university teaches.

The award takes the form of a 75% reduction in tuition fees, which in most colleges is worth more than £20,000. Up to 16 awards are available, and shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview.

Applicants must live in Africa and hold a passport from an African country, have grades equivalent to a UK first-class degree, and set out a clear career or development plan. You can apply for the award before you have an offer, but you need an offer to be considered for interview.
opportunities.benefits: A 75% tuition fee waiver for one year of study. Examples given by the university: about £20,543 off in Arts and Humanities, £25,281 in Medical, Veterinary and Life Sciences, £26,111 in Science and Engineering and the Adam Smith Business School, and £21,206 in Social Sciences. The actual value depends on the fee in your offer letter.

Grades equivalent to a UK first-class honours degree
Holding or applying for an offer for a one-year full-time taught master's starting September 2027
International fee status
Clear career and/or development plan
Must meet the UKVI living-cost requirement
documents: Online scholarship application form, including your career or development plan
Offer for an eligible master's programme (needed before interview)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on academic excellence and their plans. Shortlisted candidates are invited to interview and contacted by 7 May 2027. Up to 16 awards are made.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow, founded in 1451, is one of the oldest universities in the English-speaking world and a member of the UK's Russell Group of research-intensive universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme at Glasgow, then complete the African Excellence Award form on the university's scholarship portal (linked from the award page). Questions go to student.recruitment@glasgow.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: Postgraduate diplomas and certificates are not eligible. The award cannot be combined with other Glasgow scholarships or discounts except the alumni discount; if you are offered more than one award, the lower one is withdrawn.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UTS recipients from listed least-developed and low-income countries (including many African countries) starting a UT master's can be nominated by their faculty; deadline 1 April 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Kipaji Scholarship Fund at the University of Twente (UT) in the Netherlands gives extra support of up to €12,000 to master's students who already hold a University of Twente Scholarship (UTS). It is meant for students from the least developed and low-income countries, and can turn a partial UTS into full support.

The fund was started by UT alumni and friends and is kept going by an annual fundraising campaign among staff and alumni. Students cannot apply for it directly: their faculty nominates them.

It is a strong option for students from eligible African countries such as Ethiopia, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania or Malawi who are competing for a UTS on a Twente master's programme. ITC master's programmes and current UT students are excluded.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students entering the first year of a Bocconi Bachelor's or Law programme in 2027-28 can apply, after enrolling, for a full tuition and fees waiver based on their family's economic situation.
opportunities.description:
Bocconi University in Milan runs the Bocconi4Access to Education scheme to make its degrees affordable for students from families with limited means. For the 2027-28 academic year it offers a waiver of 100% of Bocconi's ordinary tuition and fees to international students starting the first year of a Bachelor's or Law degree. Applicants who do not qualify for the full waiver are automatically considered for one of the university's other benefits.

The waiver is assessed mainly on the family's economic and asset situation under Bocconi's rules, rather than on a single requirement. It is renewable each year as long as the student meets the merit requirements, so it can fund a whole degree.

For African students admitted to Bocconi, this is one of the most valuable awards available in Italy, because it removes tuition entirely at one of Europe's leading business and economics universities. The application is only possible once the student has completed enrolment, so timing matters.
opportunities.benefits: A 100% waiver of Bocconi's ordinary academic tuition and fees, renewable each year if merit requirements are met. Students who miss the full waiver are considered for other partial benefits. The first tuition instalment is paid upfront and refunded by the end of December if the conditions are met.

The call is open to international students, including Africans, who compete at a high level: for example in the top two divisions of a national championship, a national (or youth national) team, or senior championships within the last 12 months.

opportunities.title: ERCIM Alain Bensoussan Postdoctoral Fellowship (deadline 30 April 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality who earned a PhD within the last eight years (or are finishing an outstanding PhD) can apply for a 12-month postdoc at an ERCIM member institute in a country other than their own.
opportunities.description:
The ERCIM "Alain Bensoussan" Fellowship Programme is the main postdoctoral scheme of the European Research Consortium for Informatics and Mathematics. Each fellowship places a young researcher for twelve months at one of the consortium's member institutes, which include national research centres such as CNR in Italy, CWI in the Netherlands, Fraunhofer in Germany, INESC in Portugal, NTNU in Norway and RISE in Sweden.

The programme runs two application rounds a year, and the next official deadline is 30 April 2027. Fellows work on research topics in computer science, information technology and applied mathematics that the host institutes list for each round, so applicants should check the expertise areas posted for the current round before choosing a host.

The scheme is open to PhD holders of every nationality, which makes it a realistic route into European research for African computer scientists and mathematicians. Its mobility rules mean that a fellow always moves to a new country and a new institution, and it can be held for at most two terms.
opportunities.benefits: Fellows receive a monthly stipend or a working contract from the host. Approximate net monthly amounts given for the latest round are EUR 2,240 at CNR (Italy), EUR 2,625 at CWI (Netherlands), EUR 3,000 at Fraunhofer (Germany), EUR 1,807 at INESC (Portugal, working contract), EUR 4,415 at NTNU (Norway) and EUR 2,925 at RISE (Sweden). Stipends do not include social insurance, so ERCIM pays for a Campus France health insurance. Travel is reimbursed up to EUR 500 per trip for two trips, and fellows can claim up to EUR 100 a month for research exchanges and up to EUR 100 a month for conference attendance when a paper is accepted.
requirements: Open to applicants of any nationality
PhD obtained within the eight years before the round's deadline, or in the final year of a PhD with an outstanding record (proof of the degree needed before the fellowship starts)
Research profile in computer science, information technology or applied mathematics matching a host's listed expertise areas
A host institute cannot take a candidate of its own nationality
You cannot be hosted by an institute where you worked for six months or more in the three years before the deadline
Maximum of two fellowship terms (one reselection)
documents: Detailed CV without sensitive personal data
opportunities.selection_process: Senior scientists from the consortium review each application. They judge the candidate's scientific expertise, the quality of their publications, the relevance of the proposed research agenda, the added value for the consortium and the candidate's earlier mobility and experience.
opportunities.about_provider: ERCIM is a European consortium of leading public research institutes in computer science and applied mathematics. It promotes collaboration between its members and runs the Alain Bensoussan Fellowship as its flagship programme for early-career researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register and apply through the ERCIM fellowship online system at fellowship.ercim.eu, choosing a host from the expertise areas listed for the round. Upload your CV, publication list and two papers, and give the contacts of two referees. The application guide on the same site explains each step.
opportunities.notes: Read the round's list of host expertise areas carefully, because applications are matched to hosts. Questions go to the ERCIM fellowship contact listed on the official site.

The Dingxin Scholarship is the University of Science and Technology Beijing's own award for international students. It is offered as a full scholarship, covering tuition, campus housing, a living allowance and comprehensive medical insurance, or as a partial scholarship that covers one or more of those items.

The 2027 call, published on 16 October 2026, accepts applications from 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027 for undergraduate (four years), master's (two to three years) and doctoral (four years) programmes starting in September 2027. Awards are reviewed every year and the study period cannot normally be extended.

USTB is one of China's leading universities for materials, metallurgy, mining, engineering and computer science, so the award is a strong option for African students in these fields. Graduate applicants are advised to apply first for the Chinese Government Scholarship High-Level Postgraduate Program at USTB, which can also lead to Dingxin consideration.
opportunities.benefits: Full scholarship: tuition, on-campus accommodation, a living allowance and comprehensive medical insurance. Partial scholarship: one or several of these items. The monthly allowance amount is not published in the notice.
requirements: Non-Chinese citizen holding a valid foreign passport
Good health
Bachelor's applicants: high-school graduate under 30
Master's applicants: bachelor's degree holder under 40
PhD applicants: master's degree holder under 45
Annual review of the scholarship
documents: Application materials listed in USTB's materials guide (uploaded in the portal)
Payment of the non-refundable application fee
Original documents to be shown at registration
opportunities.selection_process: USTB reviews applications after the window closes and announces admission and scholarship results by the end of June 2027. Admission letters and the JW202 visa form are sent by email in July 2027. Students who do not register on time lose the award.
important_dates: Results: by the end of June 2027
Admission letter and JW202 form: July 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Science and Technology Beijing (USTB) is a national key university in Beijing, known for engineering, materials science and metallurgy. Its International Student Center handles international admissions and scholarships.

Check the materials guide at isc.ustb.edu.cn for the list of documents for your level.
