opportunities.title: University of Regina International Student of Distinction Scholarship (Tier 1, Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students applying straight from high school to a University of Regina undergraduate degree for Fall 2027 with an average of at least 90% can be considered for Tier 1 housing and meal-plan support.
opportunities.description:
The International Student of Distinction Scholarship is the University of Regina's top entrance award for new international undergraduates. Instead of a tuition credit, it pays for life on campus: Tier 1 covers on-campus housing and a meal plan, worth about CAD 22,500 a year and around CAD 90,000 over four years.

The university has posted that Tier 1 places for the Winter 2027 and Spring/Summer 2027 intakes are already filled, so new applicants should aim for the Fall 2027 intake. The lower Tier 2 award, which covered housing only for students with averages of 85 to 89.99%, has been suspended for the 2027 academic year until further notice.

The award suits strong African secondary-school graduates who want to study in Saskatchewan, Canada, and who need help with the cost of living. It can be renewed for up to three further years (three and a half for Engineering) if the student keeps a full course load and good grades.
opportunities.benefits: Tier 1: on-campus housing plus a meal plan, valued at about CAD 22,500 a year (approximately CAD 90,000 over four years). It is not a tuition credit, so tuition must still be paid. Tier 2 (housing only, about CAD 11,250 a year) is suspended for 2027.
requirements: Applying directly from high school to a first undergraduate degree at the University of Regina
Fall 2027 intake (Winter and Spring/Summer 2027 places are filled)
Early conditional or final high-school average of at least 90% (converted) for Tier 1
Complete admission application and all supporting documents by 30 April 2027
Renewal: at least 24 credit hours per calendar year and a minimum university average of 80%
documents: Completed University of Regina undergraduate admission application
All supporting admission documents (transcripts and other items required for admission)
opportunities.selection_process: Students are considered on the basis of their converted high-school average once the admission application and supporting documents are complete. Places are limited and are filled intake by intake, so early, complete applications have the best chance.
important_dates: Fall 2027 application and documents deadline: 30 April 2027
Winter and Spring/Summer 2027 Tier 1 places: filled
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Regina is a public comprehensive university in Regina, Saskatchewan, Canada. Its UR International office supports international recruitment, admission and student services, and manages the university's international entrance awards.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission through the University of Regina online application and submit every required supporting document by 30 April 2027 for Fall 2027. There is no separate essay; eligible students are considered through the admission file. Then complete the housing application by 15 June.
opportunities.notes: The same page lists automatic awards for international undergraduates: an International Entrance Scholarship of CAD 12,000 over four years for averages of 83% or more, and an International Undergraduate Student Bursary of CAD 20,000 over four years for students who deposit two years of tuition before their study permit application. Contact: International.Recruitment@uregina.ca.

opportunities.title: XJTLU Entry Scholarship for Outstanding Academic Applicants (International Undergraduates, 2027 entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International undergraduate applicants whose results exceed XJTLU's entry requirements and who are offer-ready by a round deadline (final round 30 April 2027) can receive up to 50% off tuition each year.
opportunities.description:
Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU) in Suzhou, China, rewards strong international undergraduate applicants with an Entry Scholarship for Outstanding Academic Applicants worth up to 50% of tuition each year. International tuition is RMB 99,000 a year, so the top award is worth about RMB 49,500 annually.

The scholarship is merit-based and renewable each year if the student keeps up strong academic results. A Scholarship Panel meets several times during the admissions cycle, and applications are judged in five rounds between November 2026 and April 2027.

XJTLU teaches in English and awards University of Liverpool degrees alongside its Chinese degree, which makes it attractive for African students who want a UK-linked degree at a lower cost in a major Chinese city.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 50% of the tuition fee per year (international tuition is RMB 99,000 a year), renewable annually with strong academic performance. A separate 10% Early Bird tuition discount applies to applications, offers and deposits completed by 31 March 2027.
requirements: International undergraduate applicant
Academic results that exceed the standard entry requirements
Offer-ready (enough documents for a conditional or unconditional offer) by the round deadline
Applicants not offer-ready for a round cannot be reconsidered later in the year
documents: Academic transcripts (originals with English translations; final-year transcript can follow)
English test certificates if already taken
Online programme application with the Entry Scholarship section completed
opportunities.selection_process: A Scholarship Panel assesses applicants on academic merit at meetings held throughout the admissions year, round by round.
opportunities.about_provider: XJTLU is an international joint-venture university founded by Xi'an Jiaotong University and the University of Liverpool, based in Suzhou near Shanghai. It teaches in English and its graduates receive a University of Liverpool degree.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online for your undergraduate programme at xjtlu.edu.cn/en/apply and indicate your interest in the XJTLU Entry Scholarship in the relevant section. Upload enough documents to be offer-ready before the round deadline you are aiming for.
opportunities.notes: Late applications after 30 April 2027 are not considered. Applying in an early round gives more chances, as the panel meets through the year. XJTLU also lists master's and research scholarships.

opportunities.title: THUAS World Citizen Talent Scholarship for Master's Students 2027
opportunities.provider: The Hague University of Applied Sciences
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants from outside the Netherlands who are conditionally admitted to one of three THUAS master's programmes and have IELTS Academic 7.0 can compete with an essay, due 1 May 2027, for one of three EUR 5,000 awards.
opportunities.description:
The World Citizen Talent Scholarship is a one-time award of EUR 5,000 from The Hague University of Applied Sciences (THUAS). Up to three are given each year to international students starting a THUAS master's programme.

Only three programmes qualify: the Master in Business Administration, the Master in Financial Management & Control and the Master in International Communication Management. Candidates compete by writing an English essay of 600 to 800 words about being part of an international, multicultural community, and the deadline for the 2027 round is 1 May 2027.

The award is open to people from any country outside the Netherlands, including all African countries, and winners are expected to act as ambassadors for their programme during their studies in The Hague.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time scholarship of EUR 5,000. Up to three are awarded each year.
requirements: From outside the Netherlands and not living in the Netherlands
Enrolling for the first time in one of the three eligible THUAS master's programmes (Business Administration, Financial Management & Control, International Communication Management)
Conditionally accepted to the programme for the coming academic year
IELTS Academic overall score of at least 7.0
Has never applied for this scholarship before
documents: English essay of 600 to 800 words on being part of an international, multicultural community
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reads all essays and chooses the three best. AI tools may not be used to write the essay, and the jury's decision is final. Winners must be conditionally admitted and meet all enrolment conditions.
opportunities.about_provider: The Hague University of Applied Sciences is a Dutch university of applied sciences with a strongly international student body. It offers bachelor's and master's programmes taught in English with a practical, professional focus.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First apply for one of the three eligible master's programmes through THUAS's online application tool. Then write the essay and submit it through the form linked on the official scholarships page before 1 May 2027.
opportunities.notes: Read the scholarship regulations PDF linked on the page. THUAS also offers NL Scholarships for five other master's programmes, listed on its study finance page.

Undergraduates receive ¥80,000 a month and graduate students ¥100,000 a month for up to 12 months; students who start in September receive six months. Students continuing beyond a year may reapply.

People from anywhere, including Africa, can apply if they enrol at Ryukoku (as regular or exchange students) to study Buddhism and do not hold another major scholarship. The next window for new students starting in September 2027 is 15 April to 13 May 2027.

opportunities.benefits: A tuition fee reduction of up to £12,000. If the course fee is lower than £12,000, only the fee is covered and no cash is paid. One award.

opportunities.title: University of Nottingham Ningbo China Global Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time international students of any nationality with a UNNC offer for 2027 can apply by 31 May 2027 for a 100% or 50% first-year tuition scholarship.
opportunities.description:
UNNC offers competitive first-year tuition scholarships to full-time international students who hold an offer for 2027 entry. There are two tiers: the Provost International Excellence 100% Scholarship, which covers the whole of the first year's tuition, and the Emerging Leaders 50% Scholarship, which covers half.

The awards exist for both undergraduate and taught postgraduate students. On two-year master's courses the award still covers the first year only. Undergraduate candidates are judged mainly on their predicted grades (A-level, IB or high-school results) and postgraduates on their university GPA; English ability is not part of the selection.

Because UNNC teaches in English and awards a British university degree in China, the scholarships are an affordable route for African students to a UK qualification in Asia. No nationality is excluded.

Postgraduates: strong university GPA
No nationality restriction
documents: Scholarship application form (linked from the official page)
Personal statement of up to 500 words on extra-curricular, volunteer, work or community contribution
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are competitive. Undergraduate applicants are ranked mainly on predicted grades and postgraduate applicants on their university GPA, with the statement on wider contribution also considered. English ability is not used in selection.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC) is a campus of the UK's University of Nottingham in Ningbo, Zhejiang province, and was the first Sino-foreign university approved in China. It teaches in English and awards University of Nottingham degrees.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a place at UNNC and receive an offer. Then submit the separate scholarship application, with the form and statement, through the UNNC Application Hub (https://oaas.nottingham.edu.cn/) by 31 May 2027.

opportunities.title: Hagan International Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-US citizens aged 24 or under who have never studied in the US, hold a foreign bachelor's and are starting a first graduate degree at a US institution in Fall 2027 with substantial financial need can receive up to USD 30,000.
opportunities.description:
The Hagan International Scholarship is a need- and merit-based award from the Hagan Scholarship Foundation for international students starting their first graduate degree in the United States. For the 2027-2028 academic year it supports students who are not US citizens and who have never studied in the US, beginning graduate study in Fall 2027.

The scholarship pays up to USD 7,500 per semester, with a maximum of USD 30,000, for up to four consecutive fall and spring semesters. It is limited to tuition, required fees, books and supplies, after subtracting other free financial aid. Recipients also attend a free workshop on investing and retirement planning, and there is no application fee.

For African graduates with strong results and real financial need, this is one of the few private US awards that is open to students who have never been in the US. Applications open on 15 January 2027, and applicants need an acceptance letter and a graduation plan approved by their US department.
opportunities.benefits: Up to USD 7,500 per semester and USD 30,000 in total, for up to four consecutive fall and spring semesters, covering tuition, required fees and required books and supplies (less other free aid). Free workshop on investing and retirement planning. No application fee.
requirements: Not a US citizen
Not older than 24 on the submittal deadline
Never attended graduate school or studied in the United States
Undergraduate degree from a foreign institution awarded before Fall 2027
First-time graduate student enrolling at a US institution in Fall 2027
Fluent in English
Substantial financial need
240 hours of supervised paid work between 1 January and 1 September 2027 before the fall payment
Keep a 3.25 GPA each semester and a 3.50 cumulative GPA after the first semester
documents: Graduation Plan approved by the Department Chair
Parent's passport or government photo ID
Parents' financial statement on the HSF form
opportunities.selection_process: The foundation selects recipients on financial need and merit from the submitted documents. Decisions are final and cannot be appealed.
important_dates: Submittal deadline: 1 June 2027 (application page states 15 June 2027)
Awards announced: by 1 July 2027 (application page: by 15 July 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: The Hagan Scholarship Foundation is a US charitable foundation established in 2008 that funds high-achieving students with financial need. It reports having awarded 6,920 scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: From 15 January 2027, create a username and password on the Hagan application page and complete the online application. Upload the acceptance letter, approved graduation plan, transcript, passport copies and the parents' financial statement before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Apply as early as possible: the foundation's own documents give two different deadlines (1 and 15 June 2027). The work-hours requirement must be met before the fall payment is released.

Open to all countries

opportunities.title: IESEG International Merit-Based Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a business or management bachelor's admitted to the Master Cycle of IESEG's Grande Ecole Program can receive up to 30% off tuition on merit, plus early-bird and partner discounts (capped at 50% in total).
opportunities.description:
IESEG School of Management, with campuses in Lille and Paris, offers merit-based tuition reductions to applicants admitted to the Master Cycle of its Grande Ecole Program, a master's-level programme in management. The reduction can reach 30% of tuition and is decided from the whole application: academic results, the rigour of previous studies, motivation, extracurricular activities and professional experience.

Two further discounts can be added: a 10% early-bird reduction for applications submitted before 1 March 2027 and a 10% reduction for students from partner institutions. All financial aid combined is capped at 50% of tuition. Tuition for 2026-2027 was EUR 13,200 and the application fee is EUR 100.

Admission runs in rolling sessions. The first session closed on 1 November 2026, the next closes on 1 December 2026 and the final session (Session 9) closes on 15 June 2027. African applicants benefit most by applying early, before 1 March 2027, to stack the early-bird discount with a merit award.
opportunities.benefits: Merit-based tuition reduction of up to 30%; early-bird reduction of 10% (apply before 1 March 2027); partner-institution reduction of 10%; total aid capped at 50% of tuition (2026-27 tuition EUR 13,200).
requirements: Bachelor's degree in management, business or a related field from a recognised university
Strong academic performance
English: IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 85, TOEIC (4 skills) 850, Duolingo 115 or Cambridge B2 (native speakers and those with two years of English-taught study are exempt)
GMAT/GRE optional
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored out of 20: application file (8), English written test (2), interview (8) and English interview (2). Merit reductions are based on the overall profile.
opportunities.about_provider: IESEG School of Management is a French business school with campuses in Lille and Paris. It holds the AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS accreditations.

opportunities.title: Lingnan University Entrance Scholarships for Non-local Undergraduates 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-local applicants with international qualifications who apply to Lingnan's UGC-funded first-year programmes are considered automatically for full, full-tuition or half-tuition scholarships.
opportunities.description:
Lingnan University in Hong Kong automatically considers applicants to its government (UGC)-funded first-year undergraduate programmes for entrance scholarships. There are three levels: a Full Scholarship covering tuition, hostel and part of academic and living costs; a Full-tuition Scholarship; and a Half-tuition Scholarship. Each can be renewed for the normal length of the degree, subject to an annual review.

Non-local students, meaning those who will study on a student visa or entry permit, pay HK$205,000 a year in tuition for 2027-28, so these scholarships make a large difference. There is no separate scholarship form: applying for admission is enough.

Lingnan is Hong Kong's liberal arts university, with small classes and a strong residential culture, which makes it a good fit for African students looking for a broad, English-taught education in Asia.
opportunities.benefits: Full Scholarship (tuition, hostel and partial academic and living expenses), Full-tuition Scholarship, or Half-tuition Scholarship; each renewable up to the normal study period subject to annual review. For reference, non-local tuition for 2027-28 is HK$205,000 a year.

Recognised international qualification (e.g. IB, GCE A-level/IAL, national curricula on Lingnan's list)
English: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall (one skill retake accepted) or another listed test
Applying to a UGC-funded first-year programme (self-financed programmes are not covered)
documents: Secondary school results / transcripts (IB, SAT, AP and ACT results sent by the exam board)
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarships are awarded on merit to applicants for UGC-funded first-year programmes, who are considered automatically when their admission application is assessed. Awards are reviewed annually for renewal.
important_dates: Final Round for non-local applicants: 30 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Lingnan University is a public liberal arts university in Tuen Mun, Hong Kong. It is known for whole-person education, small classes and a residential campus.

opportunities.description:

Self-funded with overseas fee status
Not PGDip/PGCert, Erasmus Mundus/Crossways, online or distance learning, or a higher clinical fee course
Accept the offer by 4pm UK time on 6 July 2027

opportunities.notes: The scholarship is forfeited if you withdraw; it is reinstated after approved compassionate leave.

opportunities.title: ECU Africa International Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Citizens of Mauritius and South Africa starting an eligible ECU degree in 2027 get 20% off tuition.

opportunities.title: ANU International Achievement Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students starting a degree at ANU who meet the entry bar (selection rank 85 or postgraduate GPA 5.5 of 7) and have no tuition sponsor get 20 to 50 percent off tuition automatically.

opportunities.title: Audencia International Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants admitted to Audencia's bachelor's, master's or MBA programmes are considered automatically for partial tuition waivers, with extra early-application discounts until 31 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
Audencia Business School in Nantes, France, offers partial tuition waivers to international applicants admitted to its programmes for the fall intake. Scholarships are assessed during admission, so there is no separate application.

There are several types. Early Application awards give 10% off master's and first-year bachelor's tuition for applications before 31 December 2026 and 5% before 31 January 2027 (15% and 10% for the International MBA). Solidarity Scholarships, based on financial need, and Excellence Scholarships, based on academic merit, are worth up to 30% for all programmes, and a Project-based Scholarship of up to 30% exists for the International MBA.

For African students, applying before the end of December gives the best chance of combining an early discount with a merit or need award, since places and funding are allocated on a rolling basis while money lasts.
opportunities.benefits: Partial tuition waivers: Early Application 10% (by 31 Dec 2026) or 5% (by 31 Jan 2027) for master's and first-year bachelor's; 15%/10% for the International MBA; Solidarity (need-based) up to 30%; Excellence (merit) up to 30%; MBA Project-based up to 30%. Example tuition: MSc 1 year EUR 19,900; 2-year MSc EUR 29,800; Master in Management EUR 38,250; plus EUR 500 service fee per year.
requirements: International applicant (scholarships are for international applicants only)
Admitted to an Audencia programme for the fall intake and not yet started
Excellence award: strong academic merit
Solidarity award: demonstrated financial need
Only one scholarship in addition to the Early Application discount
documents: Standard Audencia programme application (no separate scholarship form)
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarships are assessed as part of the admission review, based on academic merit or financial need, and allocated on a rolling basis subject to available funds.
important_dates: Early Application (10%/15% MBA): apply before 31 December 2026
Early Application (5%/10% MBA): apply before 31 January 2027
Other scholarships: rolling, while funds last
opportunities.about_provider: Audencia is a French business school based in Nantes that offers bachelor's, master's (Master in Management and MSc) and MBA programmes. It runs an international admissions team and a scholarship scheme reserved for international applicants.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online to your chosen Audencia programme; scholarships are considered automatically with the admission file. Apply before 31 December 2026 for the largest early discount. Contact international@audencia.com with questions.
opportunities.notes: Early Application and the MBA project-based award cannot be combined. Funding is limited and allocated on a rolling basis.

opportunities.title: Australian Institute of Music International Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students with an offer to start an AIM course in 2027 can apply before their course begins for a tuition reduction of up to 10%.
opportunities.description:
The Australian Institute of Music (AIM) offers an International Scholarship to overseas students who begin a course with it in 2027. AIM is a specialist music and performing arts college with campuses in Sydney and Melbourne.

The scholarship reduces tuition by up to 10% for the full length of the course, and it can only be awarded before the course begins. AIM takes students in February, May and September 2027, so applicants should arrange the scholarship as soon as they hold an offer.

The page sets no nationality restriction, so African students planning to study music in Australia can use it to lower their fees, but they will still need to fund the rest of their tuition and living costs.
opportunities.benefits: A tuition reduction of up to 10% for the full duration of the course. No other costs are covered.
requirements: International student starting an AIM course in 2027
Must have applied to AIM and received an AIM Offer Letter
Award must be confirmed before the course begins
Must pass all classes to keep the award
important_dates: Scholarship must be awarded before course commencement
opportunities.about_provider: The Australian Institute of Music is a registered higher education provider (PRV12050, CRICOS 00665C) specialising in music and performing arts. It teaches at campuses in The Rocks, Sydney, and on King Street, Melbourne.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to AIM through its online application first. Once you receive your Offer Letter, email AIM a cover email, your music career plan and two reference letters, stating your start year, before your course begins.
opportunities.notes: Failing a class means losing the scholarship. The award covers at most 10% of tuition, so plan funding for the remainder and for living costs in Australia.

opportunities.title: Bipartisan Policy Center Internship Program, Spring 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Paid policy internship in Washington, D.C. for rising juniors, graduate students and recent graduates; non-US citizens need valid US work authorization.

opportunities.title: CDU Global Merit Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students starting their first full-time course at Charles Darwin University in 2027 (TAFE, bachelor's or coursework master's) automatically receive 30% off tuition for the whole course.
opportunities.description:
The CDU Global Merit Scholarship is Charles Darwin University's automatic tuition discount for international students who begin their first course at CDU in 2027. It applies to full-time award study in TAFE, undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programmes.

The scholarship reduces international tuition by 30% for the entire duration of the course, and the university offers multiple awards. It is granted automatically to eligible students, at the university's discretion. To keep it, students must maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 4.0 (on CDU's 7-point scale) and progress on time.

For African students considering northern Australia, this can be a significant saving. Note the exclusions: the Bachelor of Nursing, the Doctor of Philosophy, the Master of Research, English for Academic Purposes, Study Abroad and several health and certificate or diploma courses are not covered.
opportunities.benefits: 30% reduction of the international tuition fee for the full duration of the course. It cannot be exchanged for cash or any other benefit.
requirements: International student on a student visa or other eligible visa
Starting a first course at CDU in 2027 (returning graduates may qualify for a higher-level course)
Full-time award study in an eligible TAFE, undergraduate or postgraduate coursework course
Not in an excluded course (e.g. Bachelor of Nursing, PhD, Master of Research, EAP, Study Abroad)
Maintain cumulative GPA of 4.0 or above and on-time progress to keep the award
documents: Standard CDU course application documents (no separate scholarship documents listed)
opportunities.selection_process: The award is applied automatically to eligible students, at the university's discretion; there is no separate competition.
opportunities.about_provider: Charles Darwin University is a public dual-sector university based in Darwin in Australia's Northern Territory, with further campuses including Alice Springs and Sydney. It offers vocational (TAFE), undergraduate, postgraduate and research programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible CDU course for a 2027 start. The scholarship is applied automatically if you qualify; questions go to scholarships@cdu.edu.au or international@cdu.edu.au.
opportunities.notes: Cannot be combined with any other CDU tuition discount and is non-transferable. Cancelling, transferring or changing course can mean repaying 30% of the published fee for each study period attempted.

opportunities.title: CQUniversity International Research Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students starting a research degree (research master's or PhD) at CQUniversity, or CQU coursework graduates moving into research, automatically receive 25% off tuition.
opportunities.description:
The CQUniversity International Research Scholarship is a tuition discount for international students who begin a Higher Degree by Research at CQUniversity Australia, meaning a research master's or a doctorate. It also covers graduates of CQU's own postgraduate coursework programmes who decide to continue into a research degree.

The award takes 25% off tuition fees and lasts for the whole length of the course. The university lists the number of awards as unlimited and shows the scheme as open now, with no closing date, so every eligible new international research student benefits.

For African researchers looking at Australia, this is a useful saving because nothing extra has to be submitted: the discount is applied once you are admitted to an eligible research programme and meet the academic and English entry rules.
opportunities.benefits: 25% off tuition fees for the full duration of the research course. The page lists no stipend or living allowance.
requirements: New international student (international fee-paying)
Admitted to a Higher Degree by Research course (research master's or PhD) at CQUniversity
Meet the academic entry requirements for the chosen research course
Meet CQUniversity's English language requirements
Alternatively, a graduate of a CQU postgraduate coursework degree applying to start research
documents: Certified English translations of any documents not in English
opportunities.selection_process: There is no separate competition: every applicant who meets the eligibility rules is considered automatically, and the outcome can be checked in the university's iStart applicant portal.
important_dates: Status: open now (no closing date stated)
opportunities.about_provider: CQUniversity Australia is a public university with campuses across Queensland and other Australian states. It offers coursework and research degrees and recruits international students into its Higher Degree by Research programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to your chosen CQUniversity research degree with certified transcripts and certificates. No separate scholarship form is needed; eligible students are assessed automatically, and if you use an education agent, the agent is told the result.
opportunities.notes: Number of awards is unlimited. Read the scholarship's terms and conditions on the CQU website before accepting an offer.

opportunities.title: DAAD Heilbronn AI Fellowship 2026/2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International final-year PhD candidates or postdocs within five years of their PhD can spend 1 to 12 months at Heilbronn AI institutes on a EUR 2,800 monthly stipend plus travel and insurance.

opportunities.title: Deakin Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students starting a Deakin undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree with strong prior results can apply for a 50% or 100% tuition award.

opportunities.title: EMBO Scientific Exchange Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Life scientists of any nationality with at least a year of graduate research, working in an EMBC member state or partner country (Chile, India, Singapore, Taiwan), can get travel and subsistence for a 7-90 day lab visit; apply at least 30 days ahead.
opportunities.description:
EMBO Scientific Exchange Grants pay for short research visits between laboratories so that scientists can learn new techniques and start collaborations. The visit can last from seven days to three months and must be between labs in EMBC Member States or EMBO's global partner countries (Chile, India, Singapore and Taiwan), but not between two labs in the same country.

The grant covers travel and subsistence for the researcher only, with daily rates that depend on the country visited. There is no deadline: applications are accepted all year, but must arrive at least 30 days before the visit starts, and EMBO advises applying about three months ahead.

Eligibility depends on where you work, not your passport. African scientists qualify if they are working at an institute in an EMBC Member State or partner country (or are funded by JST programmes), for example as PhD students or postdocs in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Travel costs and subsistence for the fellow (country-dependent rates) for visits of 7 days to 3 months. Not covered: dependants, courses, conference travel, bench fees, overheads and visa costs.
requirements: Active researcher with at least one year of graduate-level research experience (or equivalent) at submission
Working at an institute/university in an EMBC Member State, EMBC/EMBO global partner (Chile, India, Singapore, Taiwan) or funded by JST programmes
Visit to a lab in a different country, for 7-90 days
No visits to former supervisors/colleagues or labs with a prior collaboration
Return to the home lab for at least six consecutive months afterwards
documents: Signed English letter from the home institution confirming your return
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by EMBO against its selection criteria (see the selection page); applicants should allow about three months for a decision.
important_dates: Submit at least 30 days before the visit starts (three months recommended)
opportunities.about_provider: EMBO, the European Molecular Biology Organization, is an organisation of leading life scientists that supports research and researchers through fellowships, grants, courses and conferences. Its funding is provided through the European Molecular Biology Conference (EMBC) member states.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the EMBO guidelines for applicants, then register and apply through EMBO's online application system (applications.embo.org). Arrange two referees and a confirmation from the host lab before submitting.
opportunities.notes: Extensions of up to three more months are possible, but EMBO funds only the first three months. Workshops, courses and symposia are not eligible.

opportunities.title: ESSEC Master in Management Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants admitted to ESSEC's Master in Management for the 2027 intake are automatically considered for a EUR 10,000 ESSEC Scholarship based on the quality of their application.
opportunities.description:
ESSEC Business School's Master in Management (MiM) is its flagship Grande École programme, leading to a French state-recognised master's degree. It can be taken on the Paris-Cergy, Singapore or Rabat campuses, either as a one-year Intensive track (Cergy only, for applicants with professional experience) or a two-to-three-year Flexible track.

International applicants to the 2027 intake are automatically reviewed for the ESSEC Scholarship worth EUR 10,000, with no separate form: the decision is based on the overall strength of the admission file. Scholarship holders also pay a reduced deposit of EUR 500 instead of EUR 6,000 when they accept their place.

For African applicants the award reduces but does not remove the cost of a programme whose tuition ranges from EUR 25,500 to EUR 39,400 a year. Applying in an early round is advisable, especially for those who also want ESSEC to nominate them for France's Eiffel Excellence scholarship.
opportunities.benefits: ESSEC Scholarship of EUR 10,000 for international applicants, plus a reduced acceptance deposit of EUR 500 (instead of EUR 6,000). For reference, 2027 intake fees: Intensive track EUR 39,400 tuition (EUR 43,580 total); Flexible track EUR 25,500 per year (EUR 57,490 total).
requirements: International applicant to the MiM 2027 intake (no nationality restriction for the ESSEC Scholarship)
Management test: GMAT or GRE (valid 5 years) or TAGE MAGE (valid 2 years); GMAT Quant-only not accepted
English: IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 95, TOEIC L&R 850 or Cambridge B2 First 175, unless you studied full-time entirely in English for at least 3 years
Intensive track: at least 6 months of professional experience before joining
Flexible track: at least 8 months of professional experience completed during studies
Documents in English or French, or certified translations
documents: Two recommendations (ideally one academic and one professional)
English test result or exemption proof
opportunities.selection_process: Files are assessed on application quality, academic record, management test score and motivation. Shortlisted candidates take a 45-minute video interview in English. Scholarship decisions are made automatically together with the admission decision.
important_dates: Applications in several rounds for the 2027 intake (dates not published on the programme page)
Deposit due within two weeks of the admission result
Final diploma due by mid-December of the start year
opportunities.about_provider: ESSEC Business School is a French business school with campuses in Paris-Cergy, Singapore and Rabat. Its Master in Management was ranked 10th worldwide by the Financial Times in 2025.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on ESSEC's online application portal (essec.myapply.online), choose the MiM track and campus, upload the documents and pay the EUR 180 fee. You may apply only once per programme per academic year, and the application cannot be edited after submission. No separate scholarship application is required.
opportunities.notes: ESSEC nominates eligible non-French applicants under 30 for the Eiffel Excellence scholarship (EUR 1,181 a month); apply in the first round to be considered. Campus choice is final once your application is validated.

opportunities.title: Global Excellence Scholarship – QMBS, SEF & CCLS (January 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Overseas-fee students with a UK first-class degree or equivalent who hold an offer for an eligible January 2027 business, finance or law master's at Queen Mary automatically get GBP 7,000 off tuition.
opportunities.description:
Queen Mary University of London offers Global Excellence Scholarships worth GBP 7,000 to high-achieving international students who start an eligible taught master's in January 2027. This version of the award covers programmes in the School of Business and Management (QMBS), the School of Economics and Finance (SEF) and the Centre for Commercial Law Studies (CCLS).

Eligible courses include the MSc Finance and Banking, MSc Management, MSc Marketing and a range of LLMs, such as Commercial and Corporate Law, International Business Law, Intellectual Property Law, Comparative and International Dispute Resolution and Technology, Media and Telecommunications Law. The amount is deducted from tuition at enrolment and there is no limit on the number of awards.

For African applicants with first-class results, this is an automatic saving: there is no separate form, and awards are allocated on a rolling basis to offer holders who meet the criteria.
opportunities.benefits: GBP 7,000 tuition fee reduction, applied at enrolment for January 2027 entry; cannot be deferred to later years.
requirements: UK first-class bachelor's degree or overseas equivalent
Offer for an eligible full-time taught master's starting January 2027 (QMBS, SEF or CCLS)
Overseas fee status (must remain overseas for the whole programme)
Not receiving another Queen Mary scholarship or tuition discount
Able to fund remaining tuition and living costs
documents: None for the scholarship (standard master's application only)
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: offer holders who meet the criteria are awarded on a rolling basis; the award is confirmed once the offer is unconditional firm and the student enrols. No feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants.
opportunities.about_provider: Queen Mary University of London is a research-intensive member of the Russell Group based in east London. It runs Global Excellence Scholarships for international postgraduate students across its faculties.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible January 2027 master's at Queen Mary. Eligible offer holders are considered automatically; make your offer unconditional and enrol to receive the reduction. Contact globalengagement@qmul.ac.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: Unlimited awards. Pre-master's programmes and Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry courses are excluded (FMD has its own scheme). Partially funded students can still qualify.

opportunities.title: Guelph International Doctoral Tuition Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time international PhD students at the University of Guelph admitted with an average of at least 80% (A-) automatically receive CAD 12,500 a year for up to four years.
opportunities.description:
The International Doctoral Tuition Scholarship (IDTS) is an automatic award from the University of Guelph's Office of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies in Ontario, Canada. It is designed to close most of the gap between the international and domestic tuition that doctoral students pay.

Each award is worth CAD 12,500 per year for up to four years, paid in three equal instalments a year. Students who transfer from a master's into a doctorate can hold it for up to 12 semesters in total. No application is required: every international doctoral student who meets the conditions receives it.

For African applicants considering a PhD in Canada, this makes Guelph's doctoral fees close to domestic rates, provided their admission average is at least 80% (A-). Students admitted with a lower average can still become eligible after passing the qualifying exam, for the remainder of the four-year window.
opportunities.benefits: CAD 12,500 per year for up to four years (up to 12 semesters for master's-to-PhD transfers), paid in three equal instalments each year; it roughly covers the difference between international and domestic tuition.
requirements: International full-time doctoral student paying international tuition
Admission average of at least 80% (A-); lower averages become eligible after the qualifying exam
Maintain full-time registration and satisfactory progress
Residency status identified by the 14th class day
Not held with certain other scholarships or third-party funding (e.g. employer or home-government funding)
Ends if the student becomes a Canadian permanent resident or citizen
documents: None for the scholarship itself (standard PhD admission documents only)
opportunities.selection_process: No competition: every student who meets all the conditions receives the award automatically.
important_dates: Awarded automatically each year for up to four years
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Guelph is a public research university in Ontario, Canada, known for agriculture, veterinary medicine and life sciences. Its Office of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies administers internal awards with Student Financial Services, departments and colleges.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to a Guelph doctoral programme. Once admitted and registered full-time with international fee status, the scholarship is applied automatically. Questions go to the Graduate Program Assistant in your department.
opportunities.notes: Guelph also offers International Masters Tuition Scholarships (CAD 6,000 course-based, CAD 10,000 a year thesis-based), but these require a four-year honours degree from Guelph.

opportunities.title: HKUST RedBird PhD Award for International Students
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Outstanding international PhD applicants to HKUST get a HK$40,000 recruitment award, a first-year tuition waiver and HK$20,000 a year after that.

opportunities.title: IAEA Internship Programme (Vienna)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students aged 20+ with at least three years of university study, or graduates within one year of finishing a degree, can apply for 3-12 month IAEA internships in Vienna with a EUR 1,000 monthly stipend.
opportunities.description:
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) offers internships that give students and recent graduates practical work experience linked to their studies. Interns work mainly at the agency's headquarters in Vienna, Austria, for a period that is normally between three months and one year.

Full-time interns receive a stipend of EUR 1,000 per month, which the IAEA stresses is not a salary. Applications are made against specific internship vacancies posted on the IAEA job board, and the agency typically processes them six to nine months after a vacancy closes.

Fields range from nuclear science and engineering to law, communication, IT and administration, so African students in many disciplines can find a relevant posting. Working English is essential, and another UN language is an advantage.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of EUR 1,000 per month for full-time interns (not a salary). The page does not mention travel or insurance.
requirements: At least 20 years old
At least three years of full-time university study towards a first degree, or within one year of finishing a bachelor's, master's or doctorate
Study discipline relevant to the vacancy
Working oral and written English (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish an asset)
Not previously an IAEA intern
documents: Online application for a specific internship vacancy (all mandatory questions answered)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed per vacancy, usually six to nine months after the vacancy's closing date; only selected candidates are contacted with next steps.
important_dates: Deadlines: set by each internship vacancy on the IAEA job board
opportunities.about_provider: The IAEA is the United Nations-family organisation for cooperation in the nuclear field, promoting the safe, secure and peaceful use of nuclear technology. It is based in Vienna, Austria.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Search the IAEA job board for internship vacancies in your field, create a profile and apply to a specific posting, answering all mandatory questions and uploading two signed recommendation letters. Track your status under 'My Jobpage'.
opportunities.notes: Apply as soon as a relevant vacancy appears; processing is slow, so plan many months ahead.

opportunities.title: ISTA Year-Round Scientific Internships
opportunities.provider: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's and master's students or recent graduates in science, maths or computer science from any country can arrange a paid 2-12 month internship (min. EUR 1,583/month) at ISTA year-round.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) offers paid scientific internships throughout the year in its research groups at Klosterneuburg, just outside Vienna. Students and recent graduates can join a lab for anything from two months to one year.

Interns are employed by ISTA on a contract paying at least EUR 1,583 gross per month. There is no central deadline: you contact a research group leader directly, ideally four months before you want to start, and the group decides whether to take you on.

The programme is open to all nationalities, and English is ISTA's working language, so African bachelor's and master's students in the natural sciences, computer science or mathematics can gain hands-on research experience at a top European institute.
opportunities.benefits: An employment contract with a minimum salary of EUR 1,583 gross per month. Housing in ISTA apartments may be available for a fee. No separate travel grant.
requirements: Current student or recent graduate of a bachelor's or master's in natural sciences, computer science, mathematics or a related field
Available for at least 2 months (up to 1 year)
Good English
Not employed or funded elsewhere during the internship
Non-EU interns need an Austrian visa/residence permit; eligibility is reviewed under ISTA's research security policy
opportunities.selection_process: Research group heads or staff scientists choose interns, subject to available salary funding and approval by Academic Affairs. Not all groups take interns, and only selected candidates receive a reply.
important_dates: Apply at least 4 months before your desired start
Portal registration completed at least 2 months before start
opportunities.about_provider: ISTA is an international research institute in Klosterneuburg, Austria, dedicated to basic research in the natural sciences, mathematics and computer science. It runs a graduate school and does not charge application fees for any programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Browse ISTA's research groups and staff scientists, then email the group leader whose work interests you with a short motivation, your CV and possible dates. If they are interested, they will invite you to complete the application portal.
opportunities.notes: Incomplete applications are not processed. People affiliated with EU-sanctioned institutions in the past 12 months are not eligible. Admin questions go to predoc@ista.ac.at.

opportunities.title: International Student Support Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students with an offer for a UniSQ degree starting in 2027 automatically receive 10% off tuition for the whole degree.
opportunities.description:
The International Student Support Scholarship 2027 is an automatic 10% tuition reduction from the University of Southern Queensland (UniSQ) in Australia. It applies to new international students in all fields and at all levels, undergraduate, postgraduate and research, who receive an offer for an eligible award degree starting in the 2027 teaching year.

The reduction lasts for the length of the degree shown in the offer letter. There is no application and no extra selection criteria, and the scheme stays open across all 2027 study periods. It covers on-campus, external and online study, but not non-award programmes or programmes delivered by offshore or online partners.

African applicants should note that UniSQ accepts applications from Africa only through its official representatives (agents). For Trimester 1 2027, the recommended last date to apply is 12 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: 10% reduction of tuition fees for the duration of the degree as stated in the offer letter. No application fee for UniSQ applications.
requirements: New international student
Offer for an eligible UniSQ award degree starting in the 2027 teaching year
Meet the academic and English language entry requirements
Not combined with any other UniSQ tuition scholarship
Applicants from Africa must apply through a UniSQ representative
documents: English proficiency evidence (if from a non-English-speaking country)
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic at admission: there are no selection criteria beyond eligibility.
important_dates: Trimester 1 2027: apply by 12 December 2026, accept by 21 December 2026, start 15 February 2027
Trimester 2 2027: apply by 22 March 2027, start 31 May 2027
Trimester 3 2027: apply by 5 July 2027, start 13 September 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Southern Queensland (UniSQ) is a public Australian university with campuses in Toowoomba, Springfield and Ipswich and a large online student body.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your UniSQ degree through a UniSQ representative (required for applicants from Africa), who submits via the OMEGA online system. Processing takes about 14 days for undergraduate and postgraduate applications, and the 10% reduction is shown in your offer.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship does not transfer if you defer. The listed application dates are recommended dates; late applications may be delayed.

opportunities.title: KAIST International Student Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Tuition and monthly stipend for international master's and PhD students admitted to KAIST.

opportunities.title: KAUST Visiting Student Research Program (VSRP) Internship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Third-year-plus undergraduates and master's students in STEM with GPA 3.5+ can do 2 to 6 month research internships with housing, airfare and a USD 1,000 monthly stipend.

opportunities.title: Lancaster Undergraduate International Excellence Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International fee payers with A*AA or equivalent who make Lancaster their firm UCAS choice automatically receive a GBP 3,000 annual tuition reduction.

opportunities.title: Leakey Foundation Emergency Fund for Primate Field Research
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Leaders of long-term primate field projects with at least 10 years of behavioural data, from any country, can apply year-round for up to $25,000.

opportunities.title: Leakey Foundation Joan Donner Field School Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students from countries with limited academic resources can receive up to $2,000 toward human-origins field school tuition, with the application submitted by the field school director.

opportunities.title: Luther College Academic Merit Scholarships for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Luther College in Iowa are automatically considered for renewable merit scholarships of up to USD 39,000 a year, with best chances by 1 January or 1 March.
opportunities.description:
Luther College, a liberal arts college in Decorah, Iowa, USA, automatically considers every international first-year applicant for academic merit scholarships worth up to USD 39,000 a year, renewable through the fourth year of full-time study.

The awards are based on academic performance, predicted exam results and the whole admission file. Even with a large award, Luther expects families to contribute a substantial share, often half or more, of the estimated USD 78,655 yearly cost for 2027-28, and need-based aid is limited.

For African students, applying by the 1 January Early Action date or the 1 March Fall priority date gives the best chance of merit funding at a small US college.
opportunities.benefits: Merit scholarships of up to USD 39,000 per academic year, renewable through the fourth year. 2027-28 costs for reference: tuition USD 57,160, room USD 6,430, meals USD 7,170, fees USD 3,195 (total about USD 78,655 with personal costs).
requirements: International first-year undergraduate applicant
Strong academic record and predicted exam results
English proficiency if not from an English-medium school: IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 80 (old scale) or 4 (new scale), Duolingo 115 or TOEFL Essentials 8.5
SAT/ACT optional
documents: Certified secondary school transcripts and school-leaving results
Signed 2027-2028 ISAFA financial aid form with certified bank or wage statements
opportunities.selection_process: Merit awards are decided automatically from the admission file; admissions staff interview applicants as a final step.
important_dates: Early Action deadline: 1 January (decision by 1 February)
Later applications considered while space and aid remain
opportunities.about_provider: Luther College is a private liberal arts college in Decorah, Iowa. For 2026 entry it received 718 international applications, admitted 166 and enrolled 37 students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application with your transcripts, recommendations and English results, and submit the ISAFA form with financial documents. Merit scholarships are considered automatically.
opportunities.notes: Plan to fund a significant part of the cost yourself; on-campus jobs pay about USD 1,700-3,800 a year. Contact worldadmissions@luther.edu.

opportunities.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Talented young people from underrepresented backgrounds at secondary, undergraduate or master's level apply through partner institutions, each of which sets its own deadline.

opportunities.title: Mitacs Globalink Research Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Senior undergraduates, graduate students and postdocs at universities abroad can apply year-round, with a Canadian host professor, for CAD 6,000 per 12-24 week research stay in Canada.
opportunities.description:
The Mitacs Globalink Research Award (GRA) funds research stays between Canada and other countries for senior undergraduates, graduate students and postdoctoral fellows. A student at a university abroad can come to Canada (or a Canadian-based student can go abroad) to work on a project jointly supervised by a home professor and a host professor.

Each internship unit is worth CAD 6,000 and covers a stay of 12 to 24 weeks; two units fund either one 24-48 week project or two shorter ones. The money goes towards the intern's travel, accommodation, research costs and a stipend.

Applications are taken on an ongoing basis, ideally at least 16 weeks before the planned start, so African students enrolled at their home universities can use it for a funded research visit to a Canadian lab once a Canadian professor agrees to host them.
opportunities.benefits: CAD 6,000 per internship unit (12-24 weeks), or CAD 12,000 for two units, to cover travel, accommodation, research expenses and a stipend for the intern. The host supervisor is not funded.
requirements: Full-time senior undergraduate (past second year), graduate student or postdoc (PhD within 5 years) registered at an eligible institution throughout the award
Joint supervision by a home professor and a Canadian (or host) professor at eligible universities
Project not at an institution where you previously earned a degree, and not in your country of citizenship
Aged 18 or over and able to meet visa requirements
Lifetime limit of two GRA units
documents: Online GRA application completed by all participants
Mitacs pre-departure form and confirmed project dates
opportunities.selection_process: An interdisciplinary team reviews proposals on research quality, benefits to industry, society and Canada, and the opportunities for the intern. Applications are also checked for research security and conflicts of interest. Outcome letters usually come 10-12 weeks after submission.
important_dates: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
Apply at least 16 weeks before the planned start
Projects must start within one year of the outcome letter
opportunities.about_provider: Mitacs is a Canadian not-for-profit organisation funded by the Government of Canada and the provinces and territories. It builds research and innovation partnerships between universities, industry and international partners.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a host professor yourself (Mitacs does not match interns), then contact your local Mitacs Advisor for the application portal link. Each participant completes their section, the Canadian university signs, and the application is submitted at least 12-16 weeks before the start date.
opportunities.notes: You cannot travel until you hold both the outcome letter and the award letter. Allow 1-3 weeks for the Canadian university's signature.

opportunities.title: Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students

opportunities.title: NUS Research Scholarship

opportunities.title: Nipissing University Guaranteed Entrance Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Secondary-school leavers, including international students, entering Nipissing with an average of 80% or more.
opportunities.description:
Nipissing University in North Bay, Ontario, gives guaranteed entrance scholarships to students who apply straight from secondary school, and international applicants are included. There is no separate application: every eligible new student is considered automatically on the basis of their admission average, for September or January entry.

The award is renewable, so a strong average can reduce tuition for the whole degree as long as the student keeps up their grades and course load. For African school-leavers comparing Canadian options, it is a predictable, merit-based discount rather than a competition.
opportunities.benefits: Based on the 2026-27 table: an average of 95% or more earns free tuition at the domestic rate (worth over $24,000 in total); 90-94% earns $2,500 a year; 85-89% earns $1,500 a year; 80-84% earns $1,000 a year.
requirements: Applying directly from secondary school for September or January entry
Canadian and international applicants are both considered
Admission average of at least 80%, based on the best six Grade 12 (4U/4M) courses or the IB score as of 30 June
Not in Consecutive Education, the Commerce/BBA college-partnership or Nursing Scholar Practitioner programmes
Renewal requires the set cumulative GPA and 24 credits each year
documents: None beyond the normal undergraduate admission application
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: the award level is set by the admission average, with no separate application or competition.
opportunities.about_provider: Nipissing University is a public, primarily undergraduate university in North Bay, Ontario, known for small classes and its education and liberal arts programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission to Nipissing as a secondary-school applicant; the scholarship is assessed automatically from your grades. January entrants must take 9 credits in the winter term, and their payment is deferred to September.
opportunities.notes: The official page gives no deadline; the listing's 13 and 20 November dates are not on it, so this entry is marked rolling. The amounts shown are from the 2026-27 table and may be updated for 2027 entry.

opportunities.title: OECD Internship Programme (Paris)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Paid one- to six-month internships in Paris for master's and PhD students, open year-round to applicants worldwide.

opportunities.title: Pulitzer Center Gender Equality Reporting Grant

opportunities.title: Pulitzer Center Reporting (Travel) Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Staff and freelance journalists of any nationality can apply on a rolling basis for travel grants, usually $5,000 to $15,000, for international reporting projects with a distribution plan.

opportunities.title: Seattle Pacific University Merit Scholarships for International First-Year Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted as first-year students for the fall term are automatically considered for SPU's renewable merit scholarships worth roughly USD 20,000-30,000 a year; there is no need-based aid for international students.
opportunities.description:
Seattle Pacific University (SPU), a private Christian university in Seattle, Washington, gives merit scholarships to incoming first-year students, and international students are eligible for most of them. There is usually no separate scholarship application: every admitted student is reviewed for merit awards at the moment of admission, based mainly on the cumulative unweighted secondary school GPA.

The largest awards are the SPU Merit Scholarships and the Faith for the Future Merit Scholarship, and both are renewed automatically for up to four years if the student keeps meeting the academic and full-time enrolment conditions. Smaller stackable awards exist for Christian leadership, alumni families, church matching and engineering. The top Distinguished Scholar full-tuition award is not open to international students.

For African applicants this means a substantial, predictable tuition discount at a US university that charges the same tuition to international, in-state and out-of-state students. Students should plan for the remaining costs themselves, because SPU does not offer need-based aid or full rides to international students and proof of funds is required before an I-20 is issued.
opportunities.benefits: Renewable merit scholarships (published 2026-27 amounts): SPU Merit Scholarships USD 20,100-30,400 per year; Faith for the Future Merit Scholarship USD 25,400-30,400 per year. Awards renew for up to 4 years. Possible add-ons: Christian Leader Award USD 1,500 (first year), Alumni Legacy USD 2,000, Church Match up to USD 500, Engineering Scholarship USD 5,000 for incoming engineering freshmen (international eligibility for add-ons not stated). No need-based aid and no full-ride awards for international students.
requirements: Admitted as a new first-year student for the fall term
International students are eligible for most merit awards (not the Distinguished Scholar award)
Award level depends on cumulative unweighted GPA
Faith for the Future: unweighted GPA 3.0 or higher plus faith or service involvement, a Christian high school, or a parent in full-time ministry
English proficiency test if English is not the first language
SAT/ACT not required for international students
Full-time enrolment (at least 12 credits) and academic progress to renew
documents: English proficiency results if English is not your first language
Proof of funds after admission, before the I-20 is issued
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants receive a holistic academic review covering GPA, course rigour, grade trends, any test scores, activities and fit. All admitted students are considered for merit scholarships automatically when they are admitted; the GPA largely sets the award band. SPU may arrange an interview (Zoom possible) where circumstances are unusual.
important_dates: Early Action (and Distinguished Scholar consideration): 1 November
Scholarship consideration: apply by the regular admission deadline
opportunities.about_provider: Seattle Pacific University is a private Christian university in Seattle, Washington. It charges the same tuition to in-state, out-of-state and international undergraduates and bases its first-year merit awards on unweighted cumulative GPA.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for first-year admission to SPU as an international student by the regular admission deadline; no separate scholarship form is needed for most awards, as you are considered when admitted. Some awards, such as fine arts scholarships, require their own application. After admission, submit proof of funds so SPU can issue the I-20.
opportunities.notes: Amounts and rules can change at the university's discretion; the figures above are the 2026-27 published values. Government aid and need-based aid are not available to international students.

opportunities.title: Trent University International Entrance Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International undergraduate applicants to Trent University with a final average of 80% or more are automatically considered for renewable awards of CAD 2,500-5,500 a year.
opportunities.description:
Trent University automatically considers every international undergraduate applicant for its International Entrance Scholarships, renewable awards worth up to CAD 22,000 over four years. Trent has campuses in Peterborough and Durham (Greater Toronto Area), Ontario, Canada.

The value depends on your final high-school average converted to the Canadian scale: CAD 5,500 a year for 95-100%, CAD 4,500 for 90-94.9%, CAD 3,500 for 85-89.9% and CAD 2,500 for 80-84.9%. Students entering in Fall, Winter or Summer 2027 receive the award in two payments each year.

There is no separate application, so African students who apply for undergraduate admission with strong results get it automatically, and can also apply for Trent's larger Prestigious Scholarships.
opportunities.benefits: Renewable entrance scholarship per academic year: CAD 5,500 (average 95-100%, CAD 22,000 over four years), CAD 4,500 (90-94.9%, CAD 18,000), CAD 3,500 (85-89.9%, CAD 14,000) or CAD 2,500 (80-84.9%, CAD 10,000).
requirements: International fee-paying student on a Canadian study permit
Applying to a Trent undergraduate degree (not graduate or postgraduate certificate programmes)
Final high-school average of at least 80% (Canadian equivalent)
Meet admission requirements, including English proficiency
Renewal requires a full course load and at least an 80% average
documents: Trent undergraduate admission application with school transcripts and English proficiency proof (no separate scholarship form)
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: all international undergraduate applicants are assessed, and the amount is set by the final admission average.
important_dates: Payments: 50% in each of the first two terms of the year
opportunities.about_provider: Trent University is a public university in Ontario, Canada, known for small classes and a collegiate system. Its Trent International office supports students from around the world.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission through the Trent Applicant Portal; the entrance scholarship is assessed automatically and appears on your account statement near the start of your first term.
opportunities.notes: Trent's separate International Prestigious Scholarships (up to CAD 15,000 a year) need an application through the Applicant Portal, open 1 November to 15 February. Contact international@trentu.ca.

opportunities.title: Türkiye Scholarships Research Program
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders and doctoral candidates at the dissertation stage from any country can apply year-round for a 37,000 TL monthly stipend for 3-12 months of research in Türkiye.
opportunities.description:
The Türkiye Scholarships Research Program funds international researchers and academics to spend three to twelve months carrying out research with Turkish academics at leading universities in Türkiye. It is part of the Türkiye Bursları scholarship system run by the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB).

Applications are open all year and assessed in four rounds: January-March (results in April), April-June (July), July-September (October) and October-December (results in January). Researchers receive a monthly stipend of 37,000 Turkish lira, but must cover accommodation and other costs themselves.

The official page sets no nationality limit, so African PhD holders and doctoral candidates at the dissertation stage can use it for a funded research stay in Türkiye.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly stipend of 37,000 TL for the 3-12 month research stay. Accommodation and other expenses are not covered.
requirements: PhD holder, or PhD candidate at the dissertation stage
A research plan to carry out with academics at a Turkish university
Research stay of 3 to 12 months in Türkiye
documents: Online application on the Türkiye Scholarships application system (TBBS)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed in four periods each year, with results announced in April, July, October and January.
important_dates: Current round: October-December, results in January
opportunities.about_provider: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları) is the Turkish government's international scholarship programme, managed by YTB. It funds degree and short-term programmes for students and researchers from around the world.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the Türkiye Scholarships application system (tbbs.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr) and submit your research programme application; it will be assessed in the next round.
opportunities.notes: Budget for accommodation, which is not included. Türkiye Scholarships also runs a General Scholarship for degrees with an annual window of 10 January to 20 February.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students who meet the GPA and entry thresholds get 10% off tuition for their course.

opportunities.title: UCC College of Business and Law International Undergraduate Scholarship 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU students admitted to a full-time undergraduate programme in UCC's business school or law school for 2027/28 automatically receive EUR 2,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
University College Cork's College of Business and Law gives an automatic scholarship of EUR 2,000 per year to non-EU international students on full-time undergraduate programmes in Cork University Business School or the School of Law. The award is based on previous academic results and needs no separate application.

The scholarship is offered once to each eligible full-time international undergraduate and is awarded annually. It cannot be combined with any other UCC scholarship.

For African school leavers aiming for a business or law degree in Ireland, it is a modest but guaranteed reduction once they hold an accepted offer through UCC's application portal.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 2,000 per year towards costs for eligible non-EU undergraduates (cannot be combined with other UCC scholarships).
requirements: Non-EU international student
Full-time undergraduate programme in Cork University Business School or the School of Law
Accepted offer in the UCC application portal
Awarded on the basis of previous academic results
documents: None for the scholarship (standard undergraduate application only)
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic, based on previous academic results; no application or interview.
opportunities.about_provider: University College Cork is a public research university in Cork, Ireland. Its College of Business and Law includes Cork University Business School and the School of Law.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to an eligible undergraduate programme through the UCC application portal (ucc.elluciancrmrecruit.com/Apply) and accept your offer. The scholarship is applied automatically. Contact internationaloffice@ucc.ie with questions.
opportunities.notes: UCC also lists automatic international undergraduate scholarships in its science/engineering (SEFS) and arts/social sciences (CACSSS) colleges for 2027/28.
